title: DITA-OT Issue #3: Broken XPath expression in mappull.xsl

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3: Broken XPath expression in mappull.xsl
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1163523](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1163523), submitted by [jelovirt](/jelovirt)

Mappull.xsl contains

 <xsl:apply-templates select="@*[not(self::navtitle)]"/>

The principal node type for self axis is element, thus
"self::navtitle" will return an empty node-set for
@navtitle and @navtitle is selected by the expression
along with the other attribute nodes. The expression
should be rewritten to

 <xsl:apply-templates select="@*[not(name() =
'navtitle')]"/>

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1165072](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1165072), submitted by lmandel

The dita toolkit provides a property to register a footer to 
be included in each transformed dita file. The toolkit 
currently requires that the footer document be in the 
same location as the dita file. With dita files in multiple 
locations there must be multiple versions of the XHTML 
document. 

The toolkit should resolve the location of the footer 
XHTML document relative to either the source directory 
or the temp directory.

title: DITA-OT Issue #15: CSS file location should be relative to the root dir
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1173877](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1173877), submitted by nobody

The Dita Open Toolkit allow you to specify the location 
of a css file for the resultant HTML files. The css file 
location must be specified relative to the generated 
HTML files. As HTML files can appear at different 
relative locations within the same project the css file 
location shouldn't be relative to the resultant HTML files 
but should rather be relative to a constant location such 
as the root of the project.

For example, if my project is structured as

project/my.ditamap
project/component1/tasks/mytask1.dita
project/tasks/mytask2.dita

the css file location will be incorrect in one of the two 
dita files.

title: DITA-OT Issue #16: format attribute should be set to 'dita' for dita topic

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #16: format attribute should be set to 'dita' for dita topic
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1181950](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1181950), submitted by imagiczhang

In xsl files, DITAEXT is used for file extension name and 
can reasonably be set to 'dita' or 'xml'. However, in the 
format attribute, the only legal values when pointing to a 
DITA topic are "dita" and "DITA". This is true even if the 
extension of your DITA files is "xml". The DITA spec 
defines "dita" or "DITA" as the correct values for 
@format.

title: DITA-OT Issue #22: JavaHelp transform drops 2nd use of title
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1208902](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1208902), submitted by nodyad

The JavaHelp transform is given this requirement:
(a) control the navtitle from the DITAMAP and (b) call
a topic file more than once within a DITAMAP file. But
upon output, the Toc file produces no title for the
second instance.

Erik Hennum notes that this is a bug in his code. "The
intent was to use the Map as a BOM so you convert the
topic to XHTML only once. That should work
independently of the title retrieval. Apparently, the
code isn't getting the title from the file if it's not
generating the topic."

title: DITA-OT Issue #24: Add XML Schema processing to DITA-OT
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1220569](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1220569), submitted by easirois

Since the OASIS DITA specification defines a DTD and
XML Schema implementaiton of the DITA Architecture as
normative, DITA-OT should be able to process both DTD
and XML Schema validated instance documents. It
currently does not.

1- At leats two files will need to be updated.
PipelineReader.java and DITAWriter. Both of these file
must turn on DTD validation and XML Schema validation
features.

Both PipelineReader and DITAWriter should have the
following XML parser features turned on.

reader.setFeature("http://xml.org/sax/features/namespace-prefixes",
true); 
reader.setFeature("http://xml.org/sax/features/validation",
true); 
reader.setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/validation/schema",
true);

2- Also, since validation will be turned on we also
need to updated.
DTD - bookmap.mod
<!ELEMENT preface ((%divinfo;)?, (%topicref;)+)> should be

<!ELEMENT preface ((%divinfo;)?, (%topicref;)*)>

XML Schema - bookmap_mod.xsd
<xs:group ref="topicref" maxOccurs="unbounded" /> should be

<xs:group ref="topicref" minOccurs="0"
maxOccurs="unbounded" />

3- The bookmap XML Schemas should conform to the naming
convention established in the OASIS DITA specification.

title: DITA-OT Issue #27: extra "../" link generated by topicgroup
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1272687](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1272687), submitted by nodyad

Reported by Jen Linton.

I can replicate an apparent bug that Jen is getting
with the included source files. The messages about an
invalid "../" link seem related to each occurence of
the topicgroup element which has no href. 

My guess is that apparently the processing in DITA-OT
is falling through to topicref processing and thereby
expecting to find an href. Meanwhile, the relative
"../" path qualifier that would be generated for
content in a subdirectory still seems to be placed into

title: DITA-OT Issue #29: Index generation doesn't cope with multilevel well
content:
DITA-OT Issue #29: Index generation doesn't cope with multilevel well
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #29: Index generation doesn't cope with multilevel well
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1273816](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1273816), submitted by debbiep-sf

This is in the context of HTML help, but I imagine
other helps are the same.

If I have file1.xml containing
<indexterm>foo<indexterm>bar</indexterm></indexterm>
and I have file2.xml containing
<indexterm>foo<indexterm>baz</indexterm></indexterm>
then I would expect to see an index like

foo
- bar
- baz

Instead what I get is
foo bar
- bar
 foo baz
- baz

Upon commenting out these lines (which I can't fathom
why you'd want anyway) in
reader/IndexTermReader.java::characters():

 term.setTermName(new StringBuffer(term.getTermName())
 .append(Constants.STRING_BLANK).append(temp)
 .toString());

I get this, which is better:

foo
- bar
 foo
 -baz

but it still ought to collect those "foo"s. I figure
that this can be done in one of two places:
1. IndexTermReader::endElement()
2. IndexTermCollection::addTerm()

As a proof of concept, I had a go with sticking the
following code in as a third if-case in addTerm's for loop:

if (indexTerm.getTermName().equals(term.getTermName())) {
 int j = 0;
 int numSubTerms = term.getSubTerms().size(); //
always 1?
 for (; j < numSubTerms; j++) {
 indexTerm.addSubTerm((IndexTerm)
term.getSubTerms().get(j));
 };
 indexTerm.addTargets(term.getTargetList());
 break;
};

and it works (sort of) for top-level index terms (i.e.,
foo), but I didn't make it work for cases where the top
two or more levels are shared because the
IndexTermCollection code isn't re-entrant and I didn't
want to mess up the rest of the code too much. Doing
this recursively would make all three (including mine)
of addTerm()'s cases collapse into one case anyway, so
it might be worth doing.

A related problem is that situations like this
<indexterm>foo</indexterm>
<indexterm>foo<indexterm>bar</indexterm></indexterm>
need to be dealt with, and I am not convinced that my
approach does so.

title: DITA-OT Issue #32: multiple document($FILTERFILE,/) doesn't work (XALAN)
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1283644](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1283644), submitted by imagiczhang

When using XALAN as the xsl processing engine and 
we want to do flagging with ditaval file, there will 
probably be a programmer error reported by XALAN 
because it doesn't allow document($FILTERFILE,/) to 
be called repeatedly and frequently. XALAN will throw 
that exception if it founds the document tree of the 
$FILTERFILE is already in its cache. It's an XALAN bug 
but we can prevent invoking that bug by using a global 
variable to contain the document tree of the filter file.

title: DITA-OT Issue #33: Multilevel HTML Help popup shows filenames
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1297355](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1297355), submitted by debbiep-sf

If I have two DITA topics, and each contains an
<indexterm> that has the same top-level text:

file1.dita:
<indexterm>general<indexterm>specific1</indexterm></indexterm>
file2.dita:
<indexterm>general<indexterm>specific2</indexterm></indexterm>

and I generate HTML Help from this, when I double-click
on the word "general" in the index pane of the Windows
help viewer, up pops a dialog box asking me if I want
specific1 or specific2. (This is normal for Windows
HTML Help.) But what it lists isn't the topic titles
from file1.dita and file2.dita, rather, the filenames
themselves.

This is because of the following in the generated .hhk
file:

<li> <object type="text/sitemap">
<param name="Name" value="grass">
<param name="Name" value="concepts/lawnmower.html">
<param name="Local" value="concepts/lawnmower.html">
</object>

The "Name" param needs to have a value that is the
topic's (search) title. This would be better:

<li> <object type="text/sitemap">
<param name="Name" value="grass">
<param name="Name" value="Mowing the Lawn">
<param name="Local" value="concepts/lawnmower.html">
</object>

title: DITA-OT Issue #47: filtered-out indexterms leak into index through dita.list
content:
DITA-OT Issue #47: filtered-out indexterms leak into index through dita.list
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #47: filtered-out indexterms leak into index through dita.list
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1326439](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1326439), submitted by debbiep-sf

The problem: Although <topicref> entries in ditamap
files can be excluded through the ditaval/filtering
mechanism, any <indexterm> entries inside these topics
are still included in the index.

Probable reason: The dita.list file contains a list of
topics pulled from all maps. This is done before
filtering, so it may contain topics that are,
ultimately, filtered out through a ditaval file.

Index creation in DitamapIndexTermReader reads the list
of topic files from dita.list and then parses the
indexterms it finds. But since dita.list is made prior
to filtering, some indexterms are included that end up
pointing to topics that don't exist in the final output.

The Microsoft HTML Help compiler helpfully adds back
into the compiled help file any files that are
referenced in the index.hhk file but not mentioned in
the .hhp file, so these filtered-out topics end up back
in the help file anyway.

title: DITA-OT Issue #50: Mapref function does not work for maps in another directory
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1333481](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1333481), submitted by [robander](/robander)

When a topicref points to a map in another directory,
not all of the paths in that new map are updated. In
the zip below, the first mapref goes to a topic in the
directory "subdir/". Inside that map, there are several
references.

The XSL passes the $remaining-path variable to topicref
elements in the other file. This works for the top
level topicrefs. However, topicrefs do not pass this
variable to their children. So, if my target map in
subdir/ has this:
<topicref href="file1.dita">
 <topicref href="file2.dita"/>
</topicref>

only file1.dita will be updated with relative path
information.

It looks like the fix is to pass $relative-path to

title: DITA-OT Issue #51: Mappull pre-processor adds empty href value
content:
DITA-OT Issue #51: Mappull pre-processor adds empty href value
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #51: Mappull pre-processor adds empty href value
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1337738](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1337738), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The mappull pre-processor adds an empty href value to
topicref-based elements that do not have an href
specified. The match statement for topicrefs looks like:
match="topicref"
 when format=ditamap
 apply-templates on the map
 otherwise
 copy this element

The section that copies the current topicref begins with:
 xsl:copy
 <!--copy existing explicit attributes-->
 <xsl:apply-templates
select="@*[not(local-name()='href')]"/>
 <xsl:attribute name="href">
 ....
 /xsl:attribute

The href attribute should only be generated if @href
already exists. Otherwise, downstream processes that
use @href may generate errors. For example, if I have a
<topicgroup> element in my map, the empty href is
added, which results in <tocitem text=""> in my
JavaHelp output.

The revised XSL should have an xsl:if statement:
 xsl:copy
 <!--copy existing explicit attributes-->
 <xsl:apply-templates
select="@*[not(local-name()='href')]"/>
 <xsl:if test="@href">
 <xsl:attribute name="href">
 ....
 /xsl:attribute
 /xsl:if

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1357139](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1357139), submitted by imagiczhang In dita spec, if a value is set to selective attribute and no rule in ditaval file is specified for this attribute value, the default action is to include this element in the final output. But currect default action is that no action will be taken to this element if there is another selective value that is set to this element which is specified to be excluded, then the element will be excluded. For example,

This is a test

if we set "audience=a" to be excluded and no rules is specified for "audience=b", then currectly this paragraph will be excluded from the output. But the spec. says that because the default action for "audience=b" is include this paragraph should be included.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1363055](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1363055), submitted by [robander](/robander)

With OASIS DITA it is possible to leave off the body
element in a topic. Some of the XSL still relies on the
body element to work. Specifically, the shortdesc
content is generated from inside of the body. If there
is no body element, the shortdesc is not generated.

The XSL template for the shortdesc element in
dita2htmlImpl.xsl should be updated to:
<xsl:template match="*[contains(@class,'
topic/shortdesc ')]">
 <xsl:if
test="not(following-sibling::*[contains(@class,'
topic/body ')])">
 <xsl:apply-templates select="." mode="outofline"/>
 /xsl:if
/xsl:template

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1366843](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1366843), submitted by prescod

It seems that the DITA toolkit does not generate
correct internal-destination links in FO. The algorithm
for creating the href attribute is much more simple
than the range of possibilities DITA allows. This
problem can be reproduced just by generating the PDF
version of the DITA language reference. There are
several problems with the href generation algorithm but
one in particular is that it expects that the "id" will
be on the root element but DITA allows a "dita" element
that wraps the root element.

title: DITA-OT Issue #63: The dita2docbook transformation lacks support for args.xsl
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1368403](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1368403), submitted by dcramer

args.xsl not supported for the dita2docbook
transformation if you use a map. See the following from
 ditatargets.xml:

<!-- Build DocBook output from ditamap -->

<target name="dita.map.docbook"> 
 <mkdir dir="${outputDir}" />
 <xslt processor="trax"
 in="${inputDir}${file.separator}${inputMap}"
 out="${outputDir}${file.separator}${mapRoot}.xml"

style="${dita.script.dir}${file.separator}map2docbook.xsl">
 <param name="outputdir" expression="${outputDir}" />
 <xmlcatalog refid="dita.catalog" />
 </xslt>
</target>

Should be something like:

<!-- Build DocBook output from ditamap -->

<target name="dita.map.docbook"> 
 <condition property="args.xsl"
value="${dita.script.dir}${file.separator}map2docbook.xsl">
 <not>
 <isset property="args.xsl"/>
 </not>
 </condition>

 <mkdir dir="${outputDir}" />
 <xslt processor="trax"
 in="${inputDir}${file.separator}${inputMap}"
 out="${outputDir}${file.separator}${mapRoot}.xml"
 style="${args.xsl}">
 <param name="outputdir" expression="${outputDir}" />
 <xmlcatalog refid="dita.catalog" />
 </xslt>
</target>

title: DITA-OT Issue #66: docbook/topic2db.xsl - better linking support
content:
DITA-OT Issue #66: docbook/topic2db.xsl - better linking support
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #66: docbook/topic2db.xsl - better linking support
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1385654](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1385654), submitted by efh

In the current DITA-2-DocBook transform, the treatment
of linking elements (in particular, <link> and <xref>)
requires some enhancement.

First, the transformat distinguishes between local
links (which convert to DocBook <xref>) and remote
links (which convert to DocBook <ulink>) only for the
DITA <xref> element and not for the DITA <link> element.

Second, the expression for distinguishing remote links
should probably resemble the following:

 and (
 (@format and @format!='dita' and @format!='DITA') or
 (@scope and @scope!='local' and @scope!='LOCAL'))

The expression for distinguishing local links should
probably resemble the following:

 and
 (not(@scope) or @scope='local' or @scope='LOCAL') and
 (not(@format) or @format='dita' or @format='DITA')

Third, local links should be emitted using the id of
the link target in the generated DocBook.

The following rule processes a DITA <link> element with
a local target where the id of the referenced topic is
the id in the generated DocBook document:

<xsl:template match="*[contains(@class,' topic/link ') and
 (not(@scope) or @scope='local' or @scope='LOCAL') and
 (not(@format) or @format='dita' or @format='DITA')]">
 <xsl:variable name="linkID">
 <xsl:call-template name="getLinkID"/>
 /xsl:variable
 <listitem>
 <para>
 <xref linkend="{$linkID}">
 <xsl:call-template name="setStandardAttr">
 <xsl:with-param name="IDPrefix" select="'xref'"/>
 /xsl:call-template
 </xref>
 </para>
 <xsl:apply-templates select="*[contains(@class,'
topic/desc ')]"/>
 </listitem>
/xsl:template

<xsl:template name="getLinkID">
 <xsl:param name="href" select="@href"/>
 <xsl:variable name="hasID" select="contains($href,'#')"/>
 xsl:choose
 <xsl:when test="$hasID">
 <xsl:value-of
select="translate(substring-after($href,'#'),'/','_')"/>
 /xsl:when
 xsl:otherwise
 <xsl:value-of
 select="document($href, /)/*[contains(@class,'
topic/topic ')]/@id"/>
 /xsl:otherwise
 /xsl:choose
/xsl:template

While this rule is an improvement, a better approach to
both ids and linking would handle the case where two
topics in different files have the same id. One
approach might be to use the relative path to the file
in the generated id (substituting underscores for the
path separator slash and other invalid characters). 
Another approach would be to append a unique generated
number to the supplied id.

title: DITA-OT Issue #71: Note template for XHTML should be easier to override

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #71: Note template for XHTML should be easier to override
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1405184](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1405184), submitted by [robander](/robander)
Currently it is difficult to override one part of the note template (for example, the output for note with type="caution"), because to override one small part you must override the entire thing. It would be much easier to change the output for one type of note if we broke the template apart. Instead of this: match="note" if type="note", call-template note if type="tip" generate a tip if type="fastpath" generate fastpath ...
We should have this: match="note" if type="note", call-template note if type="tip", call-template tip if type="fastpath", call-template fastpath ...
This will allow users to easily change the presentation for a single type of note, without overriding the others.
The attached XSL moves each section into a named template. It also contains the spacing fix from problem ID 1405169. This code cannot be used on its own, it is meant to replace the named "note" template and the match="*[contains(@class,' topic/note ')]" template in dita2htmlImpl.xsl

title: DITA-OT Issue #73: XHTML processing for <alt> is incomplete
content:
DITA-OT Issue #73: XHTML processing for <alt> is incomplete
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #73: XHTML processing for <alt> is incomplete
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1407454](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1407454), submitted by [robander](/robander)

Inside the image template, the contents of the alt
element are retrieved using xsl:value-of/. This is a
problem because it misses extra text that may be
generated with some elements, and it also pulls in any
index terms or other content that should be removed. We
should process the contents, but we should do it with
mode="text-only" because the contents go into an attribute.

We should fix this by changing the value-of to
<xsl:apply-templates select="*[contains(@class,'
topic/alt ')]" mode="text-only"/>

We should also add a default rule for the alt element.
One user tried to override the image element, and
processed the alt element with apply-templates. There
is no rule for the alt element, so this used the
topic.undefined_element template.

We should include this template so that there is
default processing for the alt element:
<xsl:template match="*[contains(@class,' topic/alt ')]">
 <xsl:apply-templates select="." mode="text-only"/>
/xsl:template

title: DITA-OT Issue #75: <desc> element is not handled inside xref for XHTML
content:
DITA-OT Issue #75: <desc> element is not handled inside xref for XHTML
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #75: <desc> element is not handled inside xref for XHTML
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1408477](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1408477), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The OASIS-approved DTDs for DITA added the <desc>
element to the content model of <xref>. It is supposed
to function the same way as the <desc> element inside
of a link; for XHTML, it should provide hover-help
using the title attribute on the link. Currently, it
falls to the topic.undefined_element rule, and
generates broken output.

We should add this to the xref rule:
 <xsl:if test="*[contains(@class,' topic/desc ')]">
 <xsl:attribute
name="title"><xsl:apply-templates
select="*[contains(@class,' topic/desc ')][1]"
mode="text-only"/>/xsl:attribute
 /xsl:if

In addition, the code uses the href attribute as
fallback unless an element is specified; when only the
desc is specified, we still need to fall back to the
href value.

title: DITA-OT Issue #76: Short description is not retrieved for <xref> element
content:
DITA-OT Issue #76: Short description is not retrieved for <xref> element
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #76: Short description is not retrieved for <xref> element
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1408487](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1408487), submitted by [robander](/robander)

This is related to bug #1408477 but the severity is not
as high.

The <xref> element supports the <desc> element as a
child. If the <desc> element is not specified, the
short description of the target should be retrieved, in
the almost same way that it is retrieved for links
today. The main change is that xref may target an
element within a topic, which is not supported for link
elements.

The desc element in xref is supposed to be processed as
follows:
- If it is specified, keep the specified value
- Else if the target is an element within a topic, and
 that element has a <desc> child, use that <desc> child
- Else if the target is a specific topic, use the
 shortdesc for that topic
- Else if the target is a file, use the shortdesc for
 the first topic in that file

The following changes are needed to fix processing of
the desc element in topicpull.xsl:
- Remove the line that skips shortdesc processing for
 the xref element
- When we call apply-templates with
 mode="getshortdesc", we must also pass the $elemid
 value as a parameter
- Allow the mode="getshortdesc" template to match xref
 as well as link, and catch the $elemid parameter
- If $elemid!='#none#', try to copy the contents of the
 target's <desc> element

The PDF TOC generated by xsl/dita2fo-shell.xsl fails 
to generate page numbers, making the TOC useless.

unique and predictable IDs for all merged topics... 
Is there any practical limitation on the size of IDs 
that makes the "predictable" part impossible to 
implement?

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1421147](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1421147), submitted by debbiep-sf

If I nest topicrefs:

<!-- subdir/component.ditamap -->

<map title="component">
 <topicref href="topic1.xml">
 <topicref href="topic2.xml"/>
 </topicref>
</map>

and use the above map in another map, from a different
directory:

format="ditamap"/>

title: DITA-OT Issue #82: @colname renaming needs to apply to @namest and @nameend
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1422182](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1422182), submitted by debbiep-sf The following table has a span in its second body row. It renders correctly when the column name attributes are "col1", "col2", ... (likewise the span attributes on ). First Second First Only Second Only This should span both columns.
but change them (all) to anything else and it will fail to span columns correctly. This appears to be because of code in /src/org/dita/dost/writer/DitaWriter.java which renames @colname back to "col1", ... but does not attempt to rename @namest or @nameend similarly. End result: the information about the span is lost. Either the @colname renaming needs to apply to @namest and @nameend as well, or it needs to be removed. (The current workaround is for me to name columns "col1", "col2", ... in my tables; this seems to work because it causes the DitaWriter rewrite to be a no-op.)

content: Converted from [SourceForge issue 1427808](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1427808), submitted by [robander](/robander) There are several places in rel-links.xsl that create XHTML links. Some users have expressed a desire to add attributes to based on their own criteria; in order to do this, they must override every template that creates links. We should make this much simpler by moving the attribute creation to easily override-able templates. Every tag gets about the same thing: call-template name="href" call-template name="commonattributes" check @scope to see if it is external do additional processing (@title, link text, etc) We should replace those first three items with a call to a named template "add-linking-attributes". We cannot move @title processing here, because it varies based on context. The template should look like this: ... call href ... /xsl:call-template ... process scope attribute (done in 5 places today) /xsl:template /xsl:template

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1429400](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1429400), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The FO code currently checks to see if links are to
DITA files (treat as an internal link); or, if they are
HTML (treat as an external link); otherwise, generate
an error and do not generate a link. This is done by
checking the format attribute. We should allow any
unknown values in the format attribute to create
external links, rather than generating an error.

This needs to be fixed in the following two templates:
 <xsl:template match="*[contains(@class,' topic/xref
')][not(@href='')]">

 <xsl:template match="*[contains(@class,' topic/link
')][not(@href = '')]">

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1454835](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1454835), submitted by iafanasyev

files that are not directly referenced from within 
ditamap, but from conref only.

ditamap. This is a single link in ditamap. The topic

title: DITA-OT Issue #93: utf-8 not capitalized
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1456430](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1456430), submitted by jlevita

Per the discussion on the [Derby project developer's list here](http://mail-archives.apache.org/mod_mbox/db-derby-dev/200603.mbox/ajax/%3c54ac72d70603211655g57e3a756mfe1be1f6f49dc091@mail.gmail.com%3e).

The Derby community believes that the "utf-8" values throughtout the DITA toolkit XSL files should be modified to be uppercase "UTF-8". Otherwise, case-sensitive browsers (almost all of them) misinterpret the lowercase value, and display utf values incorrectly, such as trademarks and copyright tags. As an example, look at how the (TM) portion of Java(TM) is mangled on these Derby documentation html pages:
- http://db.apache.org/derby/docs/dev/getstart/cgsintro.html
- http://db.apache.org/derby/docs/dev/adminguide/cadminappsthenetworkserverandjvms.html
- http://db.apache.org/derby/docs/dev/adminguide/tadminapps811695.html

title: DITA-OT Issue #95: FO gen-toc does not work right for ditamaps and bookmaps
content:
DITA-OT Issue #95: FO gen-toc does not work right for ditamaps and bookmaps
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #95: FO gen-toc does not work right for ditamaps and bookmaps
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1457552](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1457552), submitted by nodyad

(reported by Don Day for user ):

The current dita2fo-shell_template.xsl is not a best
practice of DITA overrides for books. To fix this
properly, rather than using the "isBookmap" mode, I
suggest that we do the hard work of separating the
bookmap-specific code out of that file and turn it into
a proper bookmap override file (import dita2fo-shell
and then let the new defs override the ditamap-specific
defs). Then we can make the toc generator in each set
of code do the right thing for its expected content.

ditamaps have no hint of "chapter" or "appendix" etc.,
so the ToC for a ditamap should create a simple
hierarchy. It should be triggered by the
"//map/*[contains(@refclass,' map/topicref ')]"
selector for first-level headings, and equivalent
nested paths for 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th levels (and so
on). This will produce a regular hierarchical ToC
representing the map's structure. Reltables are
currently ignored as map-aggregated content.

bookmaps have refclass attributes that specifically
identify the bookish intent of these specialized
topicrefs, triggered by the
"//bookmap/*[contains(@refclass,' bookmap/preface ')]"
selector for preface, then a peer sequence each for '
bookmap/chapter ' and ' bookmap/appendix '.

A common fix needs to be applied to the design pattern
for EACH set of code that generates a page number. See
this example:

title: DITA-OT Issue #95: FO gen-toc does not work right for ditamaps and bookmaps
content:
select="//bookmap/_[contains(@refclass,'
bookmap/preface ')]">
 <xsl:variable name="id-value">
 xsl:choose
 <xsl:when test="@id">
 <xsl:value-of select="@id">/xsl:value-of
 /xsl:when
 xsl:otherwise
 <xsl:value-of
select="generate-id()">/xsl:value-of
 /xsl:otherwise
 /xsl:choose
 /xsl:variable
 <fo:block text-align-last="justify"
margin-top="6pt" margin-left="4.9pc">
 <fo:inline font-weight="bold">
 <xsl:value-of select="_[contains(@class,'
topic/title ')]"/>
 /fo:inline
 <fo:leader leader-pattern="dots"/>
 <fo:page-number-citation ref-id="{$id-value}"/>
 /fo:block
 <xsl:call-template name="get-tce2-section"/>
 /xsl:for-each

In this chunk, the <xsl:variable name="id-value">
structure is new, and needs to be added to EACH chunk
that generates a page number. Then later in the chunk,
the <fo:page-number-citation ref-id="{$id-value}"/>
field uses the value created by that variable code to
create a proper page link to the corresponding topic.

Appropriate generated text needs to be generated for
"Chapter" and "Appendix" prefixes, and a counter for
the incrementing number needs to be added both to the
toc generator and to the actual heading generated for
the Bookmap-specific override. Headings in a regular
ditamap do not take any form of generated heading or
numbering.

Converted from [SourceForge issue 1459790](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1459790), submitted by debbiep-sf

href="file.xml") the links from maplinks.unordered are

never included.

Solution: add

as in the attached patch.

title: DITA-OT Issue #106: Map2PDF crashes if a topic is referenced more than once
content:
DITA-OT Issue #106: Map2PDF crashes if a topic is referenced more than once
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #106: Map2PDF crashes if a topic is referenced more than once
content: Issue #106 is closed with labels none. Retrieval signals: error, crash, map, pdf.

title: DITA-OT Issue #106: Map2PDF crashes if a topic is referenced more than once
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1461966](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1461966), submitted by dafletcha

There are several routines in the dita2fo*.xsl files 
that try to copy through an existing @id value, if an 
@id exists (otherwise generate-id() is used). But if 
a topic is referenced more than once in a ditamap, 
reusing its @id causes a non-unique ID error.

I've written some code that solves the problem by 
reusing only the first occurrence of any particular 
@id value. If subsequent matching @id's are found, 
they are not passed: generate-id() is used instead. 

(in any template that selects an element with the @id 
attribute...)
xsl:variable
 xsl:choose
 <xsl:when test="@id and generate-id()=generate-id
(//*[@id=current()/@id][1]">
 <xsl:value-of select="@id"/>
 /xsl:when
 xsl:otherwise
 <xsl:value-of select="generate-id()"/>
 /xsl:otherwise
 /xsl:choose
/xsl:variable

(in any template that selects the @id attribute 
itself...)
xsl:variable
 xsl:choose
 <xsl:when test="generate-id(parent::*)=generate-id
(//*[@id=current()][1]">
 <xsl:value-of select="."/>
 /xsl:when
 xsl:otherwise
 <xsl:value-of select="generate-id(parent::*)"/>
 /xsl:otherwise
 /xsl:choose
/xsl:variable

I think there's just one routine in the system where 
this fix (or one like it) _must_ be implemented. It's 
in dita2fo-subroutines and it reuses @id's if they 
exist so that links to those @id's will not break. 
I've attached the new code for that routine here. 

However, there are other places where we reuse @id's 
where _either_ this fix could be implemented _or_ we 
could decide it's not necessary to reuse existing 
@id's. See my comments in this bug report: 
http://sourceforge.net/tracker/index.php?
func=detail&aid=1409960&group_id=132728&atid=725074

Until it's decided what to do about these other @id 
handlers, these dupe ID errors will continue.

title: DITA-OT Issue #107: TROFF output is not usable
content:
DITA-OT Issue #107: TROFF output is not usable
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #107: TROFF output is not usable
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1463756](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1463756), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The troff output is missing code for a significant
number of elements. It also does not include overrides
for the specializations.

Today the transform calls step1.xsl followed by
step2.xsl. As with other output transforms, it should
be calling a shell, which imports the base code and
specialization overrides. So, instead of calling these two:
xsl/troff/step1.xsl
xsl/troff/step2.xsl

we should be calling these:
xsl/troffstep1_shell.xsl
xsl/troffstep2_shell.xsl

These shells should be in the main XSL directory (as
with other shell programs), but the actual transform
code should all remain in the troff/ subdirectory.

The attached code fixes a large number of bugs in the
current version, and includes support for the
specializations. The files are organized as described
above. The only elements from the base OASIS document
types that still need to be implemented are tables and
syntax diagrams.

title: DITA-OT Issue #116: Syntax code makes overrides difficult
content:
DITA-OT Issue #116: Syntax code makes overrides difficult
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #116: Syntax code makes overrides difficult
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1473029](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1473029), submitted by [robander](/robander)

There are several templates in syntax-braces.xsl that
use priorities, which prevents our override from
working. Our code for elements outside of syntax
diagrams uses no mode and no priority; this code is not
used, because the priorities in syntax-braces.xsl are
used instead.

Our own syntax diagram code uses a mode for elements
within a syntax diagram. This allows us to have two
templates for <kwd> without using priorities, and
without conflicts. I would suggest doing this for the
syntax-braces code. Use mode="syntax-braces" when
processing <syntaxdiagram> and when processing
syntax-related children (the mode would not be used
when processing the contents of the title element). 

The following elements use priorities:
fragref: there is no other fragref template, so
priority="100" should not be needed, even without the mode.

var: There are 2 templates for var inside
syntax-braces.xsl. The first has priority="51" and the
second has no priority, so the second never fires. We
should just include one template that does what we want.

kwd: The kwd template has priority="3" in
syntax-braces.xsl. By processing syntax contents with
modes, we can remove this.

title: DITA-OT Issue #119: Image in xref will not create correct link
content:
DITA-OT Issue #119: Image in xref will not create correct link
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #119: Image in xref will not create correct link
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1484055](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1484055), submitted by [robander](/robander)

When an xref element contains an image, the image is
discared in XHTML output. Instead, the href value is
used. For example:
<xref href="http://www.ibm.com" format="html"><image
href="../image/carwash.jpg"/></xref>

In this case, the link text is "http://www.ibm.com".
The image does not appear.

The coding should work like this:
- If there is no text content, and no element content,
 use the href value
- If the only content is the <desc> element, use the
 href value
- If there is (*[not desc] | text()) then use all
 content except for <desc>

The desc element is always added to the link as a title
attribute.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1486791](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1486791), submitted by dafletcha

The gen-toc subroutines in dita2fo-shell only select 
topics (*[contains(@class,' topic/topic ')]). But I 
think titled sections should also appear in PDFs.

This match will catch both topics and titled sections:

_[contains(@class,' topic/topic ')]|_/_[contains
(@class,' topic/section ')][_[contains(@class,' 
topic/title ')]]

This same match could also be used in the 
mode="outline" template that builds Adobe's TOC 
navigator.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1505172](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1505172), submitted by debbiep-sf

The FO image extension option, defaulting to .jpg, is
causing grief among users who rightfully don't expect
this behaviour. It isn't even useful because the
Toolkit doesn't convert image formats anyway, resulting
in a GIF with a ".jpg" extension.

We should at least (a) default to this option being off
and all image extensions being unmolested by the
toolkit, and preferably (b) deprecate the option and
remove it from a later version.

title: DITA-OT Issue #128: dost.jar relies on the incorrect behavior of Xerces
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1530443](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1530443), submitted by hussein_shafie

DITA OT 1.2.2, any OS, any version of Java.

--> I've finished integrating the DITA Open toolkit in
XMLmind XML Editor (XXE).

This is done by:
- Embedding ant in the DITA add-on for XXE.
- Bundling a minimal copy of the DITA OT with the DITA
 add-on for XXE.

This means that, ant, running as a thread in XXE,
``inherits'' many things from XXE and notably, its XML
parser (which is not Xerces).

--> The most severe problem I've found may be described
as follows:

The following classes
src/org/dita/dost/writer/DitaWriter.java,
DitaLinksWriter.java, DitaIndexWriter.java implements
org.xml.sax.ext.Lexicalhandler.

They assume that character entities such as "<",
"'", "&" are reported through the
By doing this, these classes do not care escaping the
following characters "<", "'", "&", etc, when needed to.

Therefore, when used without Xerces, these classes
often create non-well-formed XML files.

--> Please find attached to this email a complete
description of what I had to do to make dost.jar work
with an XML parser other Xerces. (There are problems
_other_ than the above one.)

If you want a patch file, just tell me.

title: DITA-OT Issue #129: topicref @id incorrectly uses NMTOKEN type
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1541055](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1541055), submitted by dafletcha
The langspec for topicref states the its @id uses type "ID", but it doesn't. Although this is an inaccuracy in the doc, I think it's really a bug in the schema. Because topicref @ids are meant to be referenced without scoping, the are assumed to be unique within a map. The only way to ensure this is by using the "ID" datatype.

title: DITA-OT Issue #130: CommandLineInvoker is unfriendly towards spaces
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1545038](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1545038), submitted by debbiep-sf
CommandLineInvoker.startAnt() builds an ant command line in a string, then invokes exec(String) to start ant. This is unfriendly towards shell metacharacters such as space, and could become an injection point for an SQL-injection-like attack.
This code should be changed to use exec(String[]) to bypass shell argument splitting and metacharacter interpretation.

title: DITA-OT Issue #131: XHTML index links should go to the topic
content:
DITA-OT Issue #131: XHTML index links should go to the topic
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #131: XHTML index links should go to the topic
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1548154](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1548154), submitted by [robander](/robander)

When an index entry appears in a sub-topic, the index
reference should point to that sub-topic. For example,
if an entry appears in the file test.dita, in the
prolog of a topic with ID="test", a reference in the
index should go to test.html#test.

If a map references a specific topic, and includes an
index term, that index should point to the specific
topic. For example, in this map:
<topicref href="test.dita">
 ...<indexterm>one</indexterm>
</topicref>
<topicref href="test.dita#root">
 ...<indexterm>two</indexterm>
</topicref>
<topicref href="test.dita#sub-topic">
 ...<indexterm>three</indexterm>
</topicref>

The term "one" should go to test.html or test.html#root
(the root topic).
The term "two" should go to test.html#root
The term "three" should go to test.html#sub-topic

Currently, in HTML Help output, all of these go to
test.html.

For JavaHelp output, all three go to target="test",
which is ok because no other target is defined in the
JavaHelp mapping file.

title: DITA-OT Issue #132: Spaces dropped from index terms
content:
DITA-OT Issue #132: Spaces dropped from index terms
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #132: Spaces dropped from index terms
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1548180](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1548180), submitted by [robander](/robander)

Index terms do not preserve spaces, which means that
XML editors are free to wrap text within terms. A
newline inside an index term should be treated the same
as a space.

In the generated HTML Help and Java index files, index
terms are dropped entirely. So, this term:
......<indexterm>Test
entry</indexterm>

will show up in the index as "Testentry". It should be
merge with the term
<indexterm>Test entry</indexterm>

In the sample files attached, the following index terms
are generated:
BanningBocce
 church regulation
Banning Bocce
 governmentregulation
...
World-widepopularity

The index should be formatted like this:
Banning Bocce
 church regulation
 government regulation
...
World-wide popularity

title: DITA-OT Issue #133: Sections should not jump to <h4> for Accessibility reasons
content:
DITA-OT Issue #133: Sections should not jump to <h4> for Accessibility reasons
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #133: Sections should not jump to <h4> for Accessibility reasons
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1548189](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1548189), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The W3C's Web Content Accessibility Guidelines advise
against jumping more than one heading level - that is,
an XHTML file should not jump from <h1> or <h2> to
<h4>. Instead, it should go h1 to h2, and h2 to h3.

Section headings in DITA should determine the level of
the current topic heading, and then go one deeper (with
a maximum of h6). The attached file contains updates
for the following XSL templates in dita2htmlImpl.xsl:

<xsl:template name="sect-heading">

<xsl:template match="*[contains(@class,' topic/section
')]/*[contains(@class,' topic/title ')]"
name="topic.section_title">

For reference, the WCAG guideline is here:
http://www.w3.org/TR/2006/WD-WCAG20-TECHS-20060427/Overview.html#H42

title: DITA-OT Issue #138: Conref on index term in map does not work
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1556417](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1556417), submitted by [robander](/robander)

In the pre-processor today, index terms are copied from
the map to topics. This is so that the terms are
available locally when processing those topics -- they
can appear as XHTML keywords metadata.

This does not work when conref is specified on an index
term. For example, this value will be copied from a map
to the topic:
<indexterm conref="#idx"/>

The value cannot be resolved after it is moved to the
topic, because conref="#idx" is invalid on an indexterm
in a topic. So, this generates a warning, and the index
term is lost.

There are a few ways this can be changed, but some are
easier than others. Here are some possibilities:
1. Do not copy values from the map to the topic until
 after conref.xsl runs. This probably means an
 additional step after conref. This is the best
 solution, because eventually we expect to copy
 additional metadata from the map to topics, and the
 same problem with conref will occur. That could be done
 in the same new step.
2. Workaround: Do not copy terms that use @conref into
 topics. Update the index module to get terms from both
 the map and the topic. This might be easier to support,
 but it means some index terms will not be available
 when processing topics.
3. Workaround: Do not copy terms that use @conref into
 topics. Warn users that these will not be supported
 until the next release. This is not a good solution,
 but is better than the current warning about invalid
 conref values.

The attached sample file includes the term "Map term in
both topics". This term should be in the index for both
DITA Topics. It only appears for the first topic today.

title: DITA-OT Issue #140: Flag is confusing when a list is mixed with text
content:
DITA-OT Issue #140: Flag is confusing when a list is mixed with text
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #140: Flag is confusing when a list is mixed with text
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1562518](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1562518), submitted by [robander](/robander) When a list appears next to text, and that list is flagged, the flags appear at the end of the text. When a list is on its own, the flags appear before it, and are not mixed with the previous content. For example, when a topic contains this:

text

  1. item

If the list is flagged, that flag will appear with the paragraph text. When the list is outside of the paragraph, it is easier to tell that the flag belongs to the list. Ideally, when a flag is generated for lists, and the list comes after a text node, there will be a
before the flag. If there are multiple flags, there should only be one
before all of the flags.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1563093](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1563093), submitted by [robander](/robander)

When I have an incorrect type value on a topicref, the
console shows this message:

Pull the navtitle and topicmeta from topics to ditamap...
 [xslt] [DOTX019W][WARN]: The type attribute on a
topicref element does not match the target topic. The
type attribute was set to 'concept', but the topicref
points to a more specific 'topic' topic. This may cause
your links to sort incorrectly in the output. Note that
the type attribute is inherited in maps, so the value
'concept' may come from an ancestor topicref. Check and
make the type of topicref match with the actual type of
topic.

The message does not indicate where the problem exists,
so it is hard to find. The log contains both the
message and the debug information.

If the message is going to appear on the command
screen, then it should contain the debug information
with the message. Otherwise, the message should only
appear in the log.

I am opening a related RFE to provide a message at the
end of a build, that says whether there were warnings
or errors during the process.

title: DITA-OT Issue #142: Should use CSS to honor rowsep and colsep in table entries
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #142: Should use CSS to honor rowsep and colsep in table entries
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1563665](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1563665), submitted by [robander](/robander)

If rowsep or colsep is set to 0 in an entry, on a
colspec, or on a row, the value is ignored in the XHTML
output. If we add the code below to the start of the
"doentry" template in dita2htmlImpl.xsl, and update the
CSS accordingly, the colsep and rowsep values will be
honored.

The OASIS Exchange table model says that rowsep and
colsep are not evaluated in the last row or column -
the attached code does not do a very robust check for
this (it does not check for spanning).

Currently, we honor colsep=0 and rowsep=0 on the table
or tgroup. If an entry then uses colsep=1, we do not
turn the column border back on. My quick tests did not
show a way to turn this back on with CSS, and have it
work well in all broswers (Firefox and IE would not
work the same). So I have not included that in the CSS
until a better method can be found. Suggestions are
welcome...

The updated XSL code for the "doentry" template, and
the updated XSL values, are included in the attached file.

title: DITA-OT Issue #143: Xref to footnote is not resolved correctly

title: DITA-OT Issue #143: Xref to footnote is not resolved correctly
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1567117](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1567117), submitted by [robander](/robander)

Cross references to a footnote do not resolve correctly
today. If I have this in a source file:
<fn id="local">This is my footnote</fn>
....
<xref href="#topic/local"/>

the xref should create a footnote-style link, using the
number of that footnote. The link today uses link text
"#topic/local" and there is a warning about unresolved
link text.

When the type attribute is specified in the source
file, the link text uses the correct footnote number.
However, the link is not superscript like other
footnotes. The link should be superscript.

Note that at present, the design for footnotes is to
NOT generate a number for the footnote itself, when an
ID is specified. When the footnote has an ID attribute,
it will only generate a number in the content when it
is referenced.

When you process a ditamap with nested maps (using

problem.

title: DITA-OT Issue #150: 1.3 Ant scripts change the basedir for the FO Plugin
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1576684](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1576684), submitted by nodyad

This bug was publicly reported by Bob Beims, and later
identified more specifically by Chris Wong in this note:
http://tech.groups.yahoo.com/group/dita-users/message/3831 

Chris Wong reported:
"You are right, the FO Plugin mixes up dita.dir and
basedir."

"Looks like I was naive about DITA OT 1.3 compability
when I packaged the FO Plugin for DITA OT 1.2.2. The
Ant scripts change the basedir for the FO Plugin, which
confuses it. I'll have to update the Ant scripts to
work with DITA OT 1.3."

Some users have reported failure with the Java command
line workaround mentioned there. This might be still
related to the root bug being present in intermediate
Ant that is called by Java.

The OT Team should inspect the refactored Ant scripts
to see if the refactoring affected the previous "API"
that the FO Plugin was relying on. If so, the OT Team
should assess whether this is a strategic breakage that
needs to be documented so that Chris can modify his Ant
script accordingly, or something that can be patched
for normal interfacing to existing plugins. 

I suspect that this bug will affect the Mekon Plugin as
well. Someone from the Mekon support team should test
the plugin against the new 1.3 base code.

If I use the mapref feature:

<!-- one.ditamap -->

<bookmap>
 <title>Book <q>one.ditamap</q></title>
 <topicref href="two.ditamap" format="ditamap"/>
 <!-- -->
</bookmap>

<!-- two.ditamap -->

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1584187](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1584187), submitted by debbiep-sf

topicmerge.xsl does not correctly handle a `<title>` element child of `<bookmap>` per the OASIS DITA 1.1 draft. The title tags are lost, leaving text content as a child of `<bookmap>`.

A fix is to add this template to topicmerge.xsl:
<xsl:template
 match="/*/*[contains(@class,' topic/title ')]">
 <xsl:apply-templates select="." mode="copy-element"/>
</xsl:template>

title: DITA-OT Issue #154: Conref domain checking is sub-par
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1588039](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1588039), submitted by [robander](/robander) Currently, if topic A with one domain tries to conref from topic B with five domains, the conref will not work. It will generate an error, because topic B allows elements that are not valid in topic A. This is technically valid, but it is not what we should be doing. We should generalize any invalid domain elements when resolving conref, and we should not generate the domains message (012). The conref code should do this: Conref between 2 matching elements should work, even if they are in topics with different domains. If no domain elements are nested within those elements, everything is fine. If there _are_ domain elements, we should generalize the elements as necessary. For example, assume topic A uses this:

If topic A does not allow the higlighting domain, but the target paragraph contains a element, that element should be generalized to . If topic A _does_ allow the highlighting domain, then the element is pulled in without a change. To accomplish this, we only need a couple of changes in the code: 1. Set a variable with the domains attribute for the original file - $ORIGINAL-DOMAINS 2. When domain elements are processed today, they are copied through. Instead, we should compare the class attribute to the $ORIGINAL-DOMAINS. If the domain is not allowed, the element name should be changed (generalized) to a value that is valid in the original topic. 3. Remove the code that warns about domain mis-matches. The attached code is an updated version of the conrefImpl.xsl file that shipped with DITA-OT1.3 -- it generalizes domain elements as needed, and removes the check for matching domains. The new code is in these two templates:

an existing project that worked fine under
dita-ot1.2.2. However the 1.3 output .chm file would
not open, although the build was successful.

On looking through the XSLTs, I found a discrepancy
between the 1.2.2 map2hhc.xsl and the 1.3 version.

closing tag), fixed the problem.

In a follow up, another member of DITA user's reported
a problem with their output file. I pointed them to my
fix, which they tried, and this also resolved the issue
for them.

title: DITA-OT Issue #162: Poor organization in mappull makes overrides difficult
content:
DITA-OT Issue #162: Poor organization in mappull makes overrides difficult
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #162: Poor organization in mappull makes overrides difficult
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1614241](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1614241), submitted by [robander](/robander)

Most of the functional code in mappull is located in just a few templates: the topicref match (about 350 lines), get-stuff (also over 350), and getmetadata (approaching 200). In order to override any of these templates, all of the code must be copied into the override, which is not very user-friendly or manageable.

The current code also makes it very difficult to selectively inherit attributes, which will probably be possible in the near future. For example:
- Selectively turn off inheritance for a specific attribute (there may be a valid reason to say that attribute A should never inherit)
- Turn off inheritance for a specific attribute on a given element (on the new topicThing element, do not inherit @audience)
- Turn off inheritance for all attributes on a given element (on the new topicOtherThing, use only attributes that are specified locally)
- Skip an element when inheriting (if topicThing is an ancestor, ignore it when inheriting @type)

All of these are possible with some simple reorganization in mappull. The plan to implement this primarily involves breaking down the large templates, such that:
- Variables specific to a template that are not used can be removed
- Create templates for common code that sets attributes (this eliminates the need for many variables)
- Use templates with modes to set many values - for example, use mode templates to set variables, get the type, and find the navtitle, rather than evaluating everything within get-stuff.
- Make the "inherit" template into a simple recursive template, rather than doing all evaluation in one template (allows the selective inheritance mentioned above).

title: DITA-OT Issue #168: Some topic/element names cause NullPointerException
content:
DITA-OT Issue #168: Some topic/element names cause NullPointerException
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #168: Some topic/element names cause NullPointerException
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1629216](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1629216), submitted by paul_cpwr

During processing, the org.dita.dost.reader.startElement method looks at each element's class attribute to see if it includes the string constant "topic/topic" anywhere in its value. If it does, it collects the value of the domains attribute, which is present on top-level elements, and calls org.dita.dost.util.getExtProps. 

Here's how you can get into trouble:
- You specialize topic to create my-topic.
- In my-topic.mod, you specialize an element to create topic-data.

The result is that the class attribute for the topic-data element has a value something like the following:
- topic/para my-topic/topic-data

When the OT parses the topic-data element, it finds the string "topic/topic" and assumes it is looking at a top-level element. It then calls getExtProps with the value of the domains attribute on the topic-data element. The getExtProps method then attempt to operate on a null and throws the NullPointerException.

The proper solution is to make the indexOf testing for constants in attribute values more robust. The quick-and-dirty solution is to add a leading space to the constants used to test the class attribute values.

title: DITA-OT Issue #169: topicpull breaks specializations of xref
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1637564](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1637564), submitted by debbiep-sf

topicpull.xsl helpfully adds target title text and a <desc> child to
any xref element that it can resolve.

This works fine for vanilla xrefs, but it breaks the programming domain <fragref> element (class "+ topic/xref pr-d/fragref ") because fragref doesn't allow a <desc> element as a child. So the resulting document is invalid.

You also can't turn this behaviour off because <fragref> doesn't have a @scope attribute for you to set to "peer". Not that I'd want to, because I still want topicpull to pull the target title text.

topicpull should probably do the shell-override thing to let a fragref-friendly version omit the <desc> for this particular specialization. But the templates in topicpull.xsl are really long, making overriding do an unreasonable amount of copy-and-paste.

title: DITA-OT Issue #170: Xref : topicpull : the spectitle not used as linktext
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #170: Xref : topicpull : the spectitle not used as linktext
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1639344](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1639344), submitted by nquaine

Xref to section with a spectitle: topicpull doesn't take the spectitle as linktext.

Topicpull uses the title of a section to create the linktext of an xref pointing to this section. 

But if a section doesn’t have a title, but only a spectitle, no linktext is created, and the toolkit produces the following error:

[DOTX032E][ERROR]: Unable to retrieve link text from target: '../blabla/myfile.dita#id-my-topic/id-new-section'. Make sure the link type matches the target, the ids for topic and element are correct, and that the target has a title. If the target is not accessible at build time, or does not have a title, give the link text as content of the xref element.

This message is asking to “Make sure that the target has a title”. But the spectitle should be an alternative for the title, if the latter doesn’t exist.

A solution like the following code could be implemented in topicpull where the linktext is created (there is more than one location).

For example: 
<xsl:template mode="getlinktext" …
<xsl:choose>
 <xsl:when test="//*[contains(@class, classval)][@id=$topicid]/*[contains(@class, ' topic/title ')]">
/xsl:when

------ end of changes

xsl:otherwise
 <!—if no title nor spectitle, process with href or error -->
/xsl:otherwise
…
/xsl:template

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1643155](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1643155), submitted by debbiep-sf

The XSL stylesheet map2htmtoc.xsl generates an HTML table of contents.

The user is able to specify the (X)HTML filename suffix for a build using the ${out.ext} ant property. This is sometimes required, in order to associate an XHTML document as an XML document rather than an HTML document.

Strict renderers (Safari appears to be one) will not accept HTML when the file is tagged by its extension as being an XML file. They cannot open a ToC generated from map2htmtoc.xsl if the filename has a suffix of ".xml".

title: DITA-OT Issue #177: Invalid hdr/ftr arg value causes build failure
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #177: Invalid hdr/ftr arg value causes build failure
content: Issue #177 is closed with labels none. Retrieval signals: error, exception, map, html, dita-ot, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #177: Invalid hdr/ftr arg value causes build failure
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1652892](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1652892), submitted by easirois

The parameter args.ftr/args.hdr is expecting a proper URL, using the file:/ protocol, instead of a filename starting with D:. 

This is the case for build_demo.xml, the current sample demo builds fail. If we change the following parameter declaration from <param name="args.ftr" value="${dita.doc.langref.dir}${file.separator}langref-footer.html"/> to 
<param name="args.ftr" value="file:/${dita.doc.langref.dir}${file.separator}langref-footer.html"/>

 I think for any parms where we expect a relative or absolute reference to a file we should test for it's existence before starting starting to process the map/topics. In this case, the user had to go 3/4 of the build process before he got an error message. And the following error is cause by the Xalan/SAxon getting a malformed URL. 

The actual cause of the error is only revealed when setting the -d flag on the Ant process.

Caused by: javax.xml.transform.TransformerException: Malformed URL D:\eclipse3.3M2\eclipse\workspace\dita-ot-schema-1.3.1\doc\langref\langref-footer.html(base file:/D:/eclipse3.3M2/eclipse/workspace/dita-ot-schema-1.3.1/temp/alt.dita)
at org.apache.xml.resolver.tools.CatalogResolver.resolve(Unknown Source)
at org.apache.xml.resolver.tools.CatalogResolver.resolve(Unknown Source)
... 57 more
Caused by: java.net.MalformedURLException: unknown protocol: d
at java.net.URL.<init>(URL.java:608)
at java.net.URL.<init>(URL.java:498)
... 59 more

The toolkit should be catching these types of errors from the start and not starting the build if the build can't find files. 

We can test for the existence of a file using XSL via boolean(document()) wrapped in an if block. As well, this fix should also include a number of test cases checking for valid/invalid absolute/relative URLs

Eric

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1663976](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1663976), submitted by debbiep-sf

Line 2810-2815 of dita2htmlImpl.xsl:

<!-- if the element has a compact=yes attribute, assert it in XHTML form -->

<xsl:template match="@compact">
 <xsl:if test="@compact = 'yes'">
 <xsl:attribute name="compact">compact/xsl:attribute<!-- assumes that no compaction is default -->
 /xsl:if
/xsl:template

<!-- if the element has a compact=yes attribute, assert it in XHTML form -->

<xsl:template match="@compact">
 <xsl:if test=". = 'yes'">
 <xsl:attribute name="compact">compact/xsl:attribute<!-- assumes that no compaction is default -->
 /xsl:if
/xsl:template

title: DITA-OT Issue #182: Plugins adding to classpath break when basedir != dita.dir
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1676968](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1676968), submitted by debbiep-sf

Background:

build_template.xml has this section to add jar files to the classpath:
 <path id="dost.class.path">
 <dita:extension id="dita.conductor.lib.import" behavior="org.dita.dost.platform.ImportAction" xmlns:dita="http://dita-ot.sourceforge.net"/>
 <pathelement location="${dita.dir}${file.separator}lib${file.separator}dost.jar"/>
 </path>

A plugin declares its need to add a path element thusly:
 <feature extension="dita.conductor.lib.import" value="fo.jar" type="file"/>

Leaving this in build.xml:
 <path id="dost.class.path">
<pathelement location="demo/fo/fo.jar"/>
 <pathelement location="${dita.dir}${file.separator}lib${file.separator}dost.jar"></pathelement>
 </path>

Problem:

The pathelement location is relative to basedir, not relative to build.xml itself. When basedir != dita.dir, this fails to add the path element to the classpath when running a transform. Sample error message with ant -d:
 dropping C:\Documents and Settings\deborah\Desktop\svg-dita\samples\mathml\demo\fo\fo.jar from path as it doesn't exist

One solution:

Prefix the generated element with literal "${dita.dir}/" in ImportAction.getResult().

title: DITA-OT Issue #183: Non-DITA file is treated as DITA in pre-process
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1677620](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1677620), submitted by [robander](/robander)

I have a couple of topicref elements in my file that 'forgot' to set the format attribute:
<topicref href="file.html"/>
<topicref href="book.pdf"/>

The pre-process step that converts all DITA references to the same extension also changes the extension on these. The rest of the process then generates invalid messages about file.xml and book.xml. Even worse, if I already have "file.dita" or "book.xml" in my information, those will be used.

We should only change .dita or .xml extensions to the common DITA extension, and we should only change these when format is not set, when format="dita", or when format="DITA".

If the extension is left unchanged, there are already messages in place that will instruct the user how to fix the problem. Those messages do not appear today because the href is changed.

 <xsl:number count="*/fig/title" level="any"/>
 <xsl:number count="*/table/title" level="any"/>

This needs to be made specialization aware. However, just updating this to use class attributes is really not good enough, because it is not possible to leave some specializations out of the count.

For example, I do not want to include syntax diagrams with other figures in the count; I wish to number those independently. When I use xsl:number or the count() function, there is no way to select which figures to leave out of the count.

The solution seems to be to process preceding elements in order to determine the count. This change needs to be made in topicpullImpl.xsl and in dita2htmlImpl.xsl. The code needs to do something like this (with corrected syntax):
 <xsl:variable name="fig-count">
 <xsl:apply-templates
 select="self::*"
 mode="count-fig"/>
 /xsl:variable
...
<xsl:template match="*" mode="count-fig">
 <xsl:param name="figcount">0/xsl:param
 xsl:choose
 <xsl:when test="preceding::*[ fig[title] ]">
 <xsl:apply-templates
 select="preceding::*[ fig[title] ]"
 mode="count-fig">
 xsl:with-param figcount + 1/xsl:with-param
 /xsl:when
 xsl:otherwise figcount + 1 /xsl:otherwise
 /xsl:choose
/xsl:template

This would allow me to add a syntaxdiagram override, so that syntax diagram is not counted with normal figures. Other figure specializations would continue to be counted.

title: DITA-OT Issue #186: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError for map with many references
content:
DITA-OT Issue #186: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError for map with many references
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #186: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError for map with many references
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1693223](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1693223), submitted by vancouverizer

There seems to be a fundamental issue with the way the OT has been designed. The OT launches a single Java process that handles everything.

Unfortunately, a 32bit Windows machine is able to allocate a maximum of 2Gb for any single process. When generating output using the OT the memory used by the Java process that handles generation may easily grow beyond this size. This is particularly true of the memory intensive output types such as CHM or PDF, though all output types will suffer from this issue given a large enough map/topics.

The average user generating output from a map referencing a few hundred topics may never hit this limit, particularly if those topics are "small". However, it is not uncommon for documentation (for complex software) to contain many hundreds or even thousands of topics and if those topics are on the "large" side (= a few full "pages" of content) the 2Gb is easily reached. If those topics also reference images the memory usage may also increase, reducing the number of topics needed to hit the limit.

It may be useful to see how quickly this can occur so I am attaching a set of VBScript files that can be executed on a Windows box to generate a "test suite" for testing the limits of the OT. Instructions:
1. Save attached zip file and unzip to an EMPTY (!) folder.
2. Run the two VBS files. One generates a single map file containing 2000 topic references. The second generates the 2000 topics that are referenced by the map. See readme.txt for descriptions on how to modify the VBS to generate different numbers of topic files and references in the map file.
3. Set ant_opts to use as much memory as your system can dish out: -Xmx####m (possibly also -Xms####m).
4. Generate output using the map you generated in step 2.
5. Monitor Java process memory and CPU usage using Windows Task Manager or another monitor.

Repeat steps 2 to 5 after modifying the VBS files so that they generate a larger map and more topics, or simply larger topics or both, then repeat steps 3 and 4 until you hit the limit.

To truly test this as described you would need a machine with (about) a minimum of 3Gb of RAM -- 1Gb for Windows and other miscellaneous processes and 2Gb that can be dedicated to generating output.

We may wish to blame this on the OS, however, many users may not be able to move to a 64bit version of Windows (or other OS) and so I believe it is worth looking into ways to resolve this. That also assumes that the 7152Gb-per-process limit of a 64bit Windows release is enough (perhaps when the OT supports output to MPEG movies that limit will be hit ;-) But seriously, making this type of assumption is not good programming - remember Y2K.

It is not known whether this affects other operating systems. This bug as submitted is specifically for Windows.

Links:
http://msdn.microsoft.com/msdnmag/issues/01/12/XPKernel/
http://forum.java.sun.com/thread.jspa?threadID=553939&messageID=2712071

Brainstorming:

Break up the generation steps (somehow) so that each one runs in a separate Java process (perhaps using a .bat file or some other method).

In theory, this might actually improve performance -- stopping one process after it has completed its OT generation step before launching the next one could free up any memory allocated to the first Java process. Right now the single process just continues to grow, only freeing up memory when it has completed.

Making this change might help other users of the toolkit that are not worried about hitting any limit by speeding things up (this assumes that addressing and finding things in such a large block of memory wastes time, testing may be necessary in that case).

It might also reduce the number of people that need to fiddle with ant_opts for allocating Java memory. This seems to be an issue that many users of the OT run into (search a few forums and you'll find many questions about this). It would be nice if this "just works" with the defaults for more people and this might help.

Allowing each step in the generation process to complete might allow for easier debugging (?)

I assume it would not be good to run any of the generation steps in parallel as then one process would be "robbing" overall system memory from other Java processes (or would it?)

title: DITA-OT Issue #188: Image from different folder levels fail to appear
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1699602](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1699602), submitted by su-laineyeo

If a topic links to two image files residing in two different folders, it often happens that one image appears and the other one doesn’t. Images from the highest-level folder appear, and images from lower-level folders usually do not appear. This bug can cause the disappearance of images that reside right beside the topic file. 

To reproduce this bug:
1) Insert an image into a topic, and generate HTML output from the map to verify that the image appears.
2) Insert a second image, resideing in a higher-level folder than the first image file, into the same topic. Generate HTML output from the map again.

Result: The second image appears in output. The first one fails to appear.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1699607](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1699607), submitted by su-laineyeo

If a topic includes a <xref> or <image> with a target that does not exist, output displays the path of the href. No warning is generated. In some cases, this problem occurs if the target topic exists but is not in the current map file. 

If the target of a reference cannot be found, output should show the <xref> element content or the <image> alt text in lieu of the target, and provide a warning in the error log.

title: DITA-OT Issue #193: Font name "Monospaced" should "monospace"
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1710236](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1710236), submitted by drmacro

The FO generated contains this markup:

<fo:block background-color="#f0f0f0"
 font-family="Monospaced"

"Monospaced" should be either "monospace" (the built-in generic font name) or "Monospaced, monospace" if "Monospaced" is the name of a font that is expected to be available (but "monospace" should be sufficient).
