title: DITA-OT Issue #194: referencing specific <step> numbers in a task
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1710261](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1710261), submitted by ig88

I posted this question to the DITA-OT, and it was suggested posting it as a bug report. 

In a task, I want to reference a specific <step> and have the Toolkit display the corresponding step number in the output. If the step order changes, the Toolkit should automatically update the step number w/o manual intervention. (Prompting users to skip to specific step numbers is typical in complex task instructions.)

Example:

<step> 1. <cmd> if "Yes", go to Step <xref href=#thisdoc/yes-response>_</xref>, if "No", go to Step <xref href=#thisdoc/no-response>_</xref></cmd>. 

<step> 2. <cmd id="no-response"> some text </cmd></step>

<step> 3. <cmd id="yes-response"> some more text </cmd></step>

In the output, step numbers "2" and "3" should display in <step> 1 (see the underscores), but currently they do NOT (instead, the output displays the href address). 

Excerpt from posting on DITA-OT Yahoo group: 
"[...] the Toolkit should be generating at least the number for the indicated step (ie, a linked "3" for the third step, and so forth). Rather than your having to write any kind of override, please submit a reproducing sample for version 1.3.1 in a bug report to the DITA Open Toolkit's bug tracker page so that the maintenance team can take a look at it." 

Thanks for your consideration, Todd

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1728700](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1728700), submitted by debbiep-sf

GenMapAndTopicList does not reset the filter map back to null when there is no ditavalFile.

This matters when GenMapAndTopicList is called multiple times in one JVM, as happens in builds that produce several outputs. It was noticed in the DITA-OT User Guide garage hierarchy sample files, which builds four targets, only the second of which has filtering in it. The third and fourth targets inadvertently retain the second target's filtering.

The cause appears to be around line 400 of GenMapAndTopicListModule.java, which sets FilterUtils.filterMap (a static member) only when ditavalFile is specified, but does not (re-)null it when datavalFile is unspecified.

The attached patch makes the problem go away in the user guide sample files.

title: DITA-OT Issue #201: DitaLinksWriter and DitaIndexWriter use bad class attributes

title: DITA-OT Issue #201: DitaLinksWriter and DitaIndexWriter use bad class attributes
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1729039](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1729039), submitted by paul_cpwr
When evaluating class attribute values, it is common to do look for strings like "topic/topic". Programatically, we need to prefix and suffix this string with a space to prevent accidentally finding "topic/topic" inside a class attribute like "codex-topic/topic-title".
The DitaIndexWriter and DitaLinksWriter classes both contain hardcoded evaluations of class attribute values the do not use the leading and trailing spaces.
Ideally, these references should use the corresponding property in the Constants class.

It appears that the use of topichead is not supported for pdf2 output using the FO plug-in. A topichead's navtitle value does not appear in the bookmarks, the table of contents, or the body content. Is this a known issue? I didn't see a bug for it in the DITA-OT project on SourceForge.

title: DITA-OT Issue #203: Wrong encoding on RTF stylesheet
content:
DITA-OT Issue #203: Wrong encoding on RTF stylesheet
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #203: Wrong encoding on RTF stylesheet
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1732205](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1732205), submitted by hypersire

Deborah Pickett on the Yahoo DITA user's group asked me to submit this bug if her fix worked, which it did. She summarized it nicely:

"The XSLT is producing UTF-8 output, but RTF insists on its input being in Latin-1 (it's in the RTF spec). A UTF-8 non-breaking space U+A0 becomes the bytes C2 A0, which is interpreted in Latin-1 as A-circumflex + non-breaking-space."

In the file "dita2rtf.xsl", 

<xsl:output method="text" encoding="UTF-8">/xsl:output

simply needs to be changed to:

<xsl:output method="text" encoding="latin1"/>

and problem solved !

title: DITA-OT Issue #207: pretty.xsl is broken
content:
DITA-OT Issue #207: pretty.xsl is broken
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #207: pretty.xsl is broken
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1733264](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1733264), submitted by obecker

Version 1.3.1

pretty.xsl doesn't work.
The condition 
 generate-id(.)!=($class or $space)
always evaluates to false. This results in removing every attribute on all elements.

That's because
 ($class or $space)
is a boolean expression, thus the values of $class and $space will be converted to booleans. At least $class (that stems from generate-id(@class)) is a non-empty string, so its boolean value is true, thus ($class or $space) is true.
That means generate-id(.) must be converted to a boolean before comparison, which results also in the value true.
So the above condition becomes
 true != true
which is false.

The correct predicate for removing class and xml:space attributes is
generate-id(.)!=$class and generate-id(.)!=$space

BTW: the comment in normalize.xsl is incorrect. It says indentation is enabled, but it is not. Also it mentiones (for whatever reason) the buggy predicate from pretty.xsl. I think this reference to the predicate could be completely removed.

Best regards,
Oliver

title: DITA-OT Issue #208: Idiom plugin requires units to be specified for SVG images

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #208: Idiom plugin requires units to be specified for SVG images
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1733878](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1733878), submitted by su-laineyeo

It is possible, using the Idiom plugin, to have SVG 1.1 (but not 1.0) images display in PDF output. 

There is a quirk in that if the DITA <image> element referencing an SVG file does not give units, output is not assumed to be in pixels. If units are not specified, they should be assumed to be pixels (http://wiki.oasis-open.org/dita/Graphic_scaling_improvements). I.e. the following elements should yield exactly the same results:

<image href="arrows.svg" width="100" height="100"></image>

<image href="arrows.svg" width="100px" height="100px"></image>

Using the 1.4 M5 code, if I have href= values of the form:

title: DITA-OT Issue #215: Chunk "to-content" on map not implemented
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #215: Chunk "to-content" on map not implemented
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1770571](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1770571), submitted by drmacro

The 1.4 M5 code does not implement the behavior for chunk="to-content" as specified in the 1.1 arch spec, namely:

"When specified on the map element, creates a single document that contains all the topics referenced by the map."

For example, given this starting map:

<map>
 <topicref href="topic1.xml" chunk="to-content">
 <topicref href="topic2.xml/>
 </topicref>
</map>

I get a single output HTML chunk for topic1.xml and topic2.xml.

However, if I move the chunk= attribute from the topicref to the map, I get individual HTML files for each of topic1.xml and topic2.xml. However, per my reading of the spec, the result should be identical in both cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #216: Inappropriate Message 018 On type= value
content:
DITA-OT Issue #216: Inappropriate Message 018 On type= value
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #216: Inappropriate Message 018 On type= value
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1771123](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1771123), submitted by drmacro

The DITA spec is clear that the type= value simply needs to reflect a type in the class hierarchy of the target. In particular, if the type= value is a generalization of the specialized type, then it's fine.

However, the mappull XSLT issues message 018 when, for example, the type= value is "topic" and the target topic is a specialization. In this case there should be no message, as indicated by this language from the 1.1 language reference (under "Using type on a linking element"):

"Applications may, but need not, issue a
warning when the specified or inherited type attribute value does not match the target (or a
specialization ancestor of the target)."

The only conditions under which a message should be emitted is when the specified type is not in the class hierarchy of the target topic, e.g., I specify type="concept" but the target topic is of type "topic" or of type "task".

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1771802](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1771802), submitted by drmacro

Given a map like this:

<map>
 <topicref
 chunk="to-content"
 href="205-15.xml"
 navtitle="Overall">
 <!--Topic/Subtopic/section-->
 <topicref
 href="00/205-15-00.xml"
 navtitle="Status">
 <topicmeta>
 <searchtitle>Status</searchtitle>
 </topicmeta>
 <!--Topic/Subtopic/section/subsection-->
 <topicref
 href="00/topic-205-15-00-subsect-01.xml"
 navtitle="General"/>
 </topicref>
 </topicref>
</map>

Using the 1.4 M5 code, I get a single chunked output HTML doc but I also get HTML pages for the individual topics below the chunking topic.

The generated navigation pane includes links to those individual HTML pages as does the big HTML chunk.

That's clearly not right: if the topics are chunked they should not also generate individual pages and any navigation links should be to the location of topics in the resulting chunk, not their individual HTML pages (which shouldn't be generated at all).

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1806666](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1806666), submitted by debbiep-sf
There is no glyph for this character in the default fonts which the fo plugin uses (Arial, Helvetica). The FO processor either omits the character or uses a character-missing glyph. Either makes the menucascade look wrong to the user. This is bad from the perspective of making the FO plugin "just work".
Suggestion: Change the default. Use a more general character (e.g., >) or make the character used configurable. Users who want something fancier will be willing to write overrides to produce the desired output.

title: DITA-OT Issue #232: Merge doesn't normalize filenames
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1806728](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1806728), submitted by debbiep-sf

The Java topicmerge code treats files
 y
 a/../y
 a/b/../../y
all as different files, so that y ends up multiple times in the merge output. This is almost never what the user wants. All should be normalized to y.

Calls to StringUtils.removeRedundantNames() should be inserted in places to prevent this.

title: DITA-OT Issue #233: FO topicmerge needs to discard reltables
content:
DITA-OT Issue #233: FO topicmerge needs to discard reltables
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #233: FO topicmerge needs to discard reltables
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1807277](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1807277), submitted by debbiep-sf

The FO topicmerge XSL currently processes the <reltable> element and its descendants, causing the topics referenced inside the reltable to appear at the end of the merged output. The topicrefs in the reltable are usually already in the main map hierarchy, so there is no need to include them again. (It looks particularly bad when processing a bookmap.)

A template like this which discards the entire reltable should be included in topicmerge.xsl:
 <xsl:template
 match="*[contains(@class, ' map/reltable ')]"
 mode="build-tree"/>

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1807808](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1807808), submitted by debbiep-sf
TopicMergeModule.java optionally lets users append an XSLT process to the result of the topic merge (the FO plugin uses this).
Line 93 puts the output of this transformation in StreamResult(out). Since out is a String, it is treated as a URL (see javadoc for StreamResult). However, it needs to be a file, since it may contain backslashes as directory separators (as the FO plugin does).

title: DITA-OT Issue #239: Invalid property in fo:table-body
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1815571](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1815571), submitted by tmakita

Dear developers,

I have installed FO-Plugin to DITA OT1.4. If I enter following command,

java -jar lib/dost.jar /i:samples/taskbook.ditamap /transtype:pdf2

The result topic.fo contains following tables.

<fo:table table-layout="fixed" width="100%">
...
<fo:table-body page-break-after="always">
...

In XSL1.1, "page-break-after" is the short-hand. It is divided into two properties.

break-after="page"
keep-with-next="auto"

If you see XSL1.1 fo:table-body properties, you will find that there is _NO_ break-after propety. So that specifying page-break-agter to fo:table-body is invalid.

Stylesheet sholud add page-break-after="always" to fo:table. Because fo:table allows break-after property.

Regards,

tmakita

title: DITA-OT Issue #240: XHTML processing add   in output files.
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #240: XHTML processing add   in output files.
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1819663](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1819663), submitted by easirois

The dita2htmlImpl.xsl file adds &nbsp: when cells in a table are empty. This causes a parsing issue when viewing those topics in Eclipse Help 3.3. 

The underlying HTML parser in the new Eclipse Help architecture actually parses all of the XHTML content. Since   is not defined in the XHTML DTD. The parser thorws the errro below.

The following line of code is the culprit:
<xsl:when test="not(*|text()|processing-instruction())">
 <xsl:text disable-output-escaping="yes">&nbsp;/xsl:text <!-- nbsp --> 
 /xsl:when

It should be:
<xsl:when test="not(*|text()|processing-instruction())">
 <xsl:text disable-output-escaping="yes">&#xA0;/xsl:text <!-- nbsp --> 
 /xsl:when

The fix should remove all instances of   in the XHTHL since it produces sources files that are not valid.

Eric

title: DITA-OT Issue #242: Empty <fo:inline> element ids are ignored by FOP 0.94
content:
DITA-OT Issue #242: Empty <fo:inline> element ids are ignored by FOP 0.94
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #242: Empty <fo:inline> element ids are ignored by FOP 0.94
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1822157](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1822157), submitted by tashid

DITA OT 1.4 produces empty fo:inline elements to add TOC references for sections.

The latest Apache FOP ignores fo:inline elements with no content, because they occupy no space on the page.[1] See

http://issues.apache.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=42748

Patch to work around in 
xsl/xslfo/dita2fo-subroutines.xsl 

 43c43
 < <xsl:variable name="afill">/xsl:variable

---

> <xsl:variable name="afill">​/xsl:variable
> 56c56
> < <xsl:variable name="afill">/xsl:variable
> ---
> 
> <xsl:variable name="afill">​/xsl:variable

and in xsl/xslfo/dita2fo-titles.xsl

192c192
 < <fo:inline id="{generate-id(parent::*)}">/fo:inline

---

> ```
> <fo:inline id="{generate-id(parent::*)}">​</fo:inline>
> ```

Could someone with greater knowledge of DITA-OT innards suggest a more acceptable patch? Perhaps the inline should encompass the whole title, or the id should be placed on the containing title block?

[1] Though ​ occupies no space either, it seems to count as content for the purposes of FOP.

title: DITA-OT Issue #246: Empty end-range indexterm causes eclipse error
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1832800](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1832800), submitted by craig_sandvik

According to the language spec for indexterm, an end range entry should be empty. As in:
<indexterm end="level-3-pecorino"/>

If you use these in an eclipse build with DITA-OT 1.4.1, you get the error:
[pipeline] [DOTJ014W][WARN] The indexterm element does not have any content. Setting the term to ***. Please add content to the indexterm.

You also get a '***' entry in the eclipse index. The eclipse build should probably ignore end entries, or perhaps treat them the same as if they were an occurrence of the equivalent start entry.

Converted from [SourceForge issue 1839765](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1839765), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The index-sort-as element in DITA 1.1 is not properly evaluated when generating indexes. The contents of the element should be used as the key for sorting. For example:

<indexterm>Open</indexterm>
<indexterm>Closed</indexterm>
<indexterm>123
 <index-sort-as>One Two Three</index-sort-as>
</indexterm>

Should sort as
- Closed
- 123
- Open

because "One Two Three" is used as the value to sort 123.

Also, the contents of the <index-sort-as> element should not appear in the index.

title: DITA-OT Issue #252: Need to clean up doc/ directory (remove invalid items)
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1841175](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1841175), submitted by [robander](/robander)
The doc/ directory in the toolkit contains outdated and possibly incorrect material. The directory should be examined, and incorrect material should be updated or removed in the next release.
For example, the doc/ directory ships the source files for the DITA 1.1 language reference. However, it also ships ditaref-book.chm and ditaref-book.pdf, which were built with the DITA 1.0 language specification. We should update these or remove them.
There is also a ditaot13_doc directory. If this information is specific to DITA-OT 1.3 then it should be removed from later versions. If it is not specific then it should be updated.
All of the files in the directory should be examined to determine if they are valid.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1843693](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1843693), submitted by [robander](/robander)

I have a topic with an <xref> that used incorrect syntax:

<xref href="#sectionid">Link to section</xref>

The <xref> should have had included the topic ID in the href attribute:
<xref href="#topicid/sectionid">Link to section</xref>

The PDF2 build generated this error message:
 [java] WARNING: unresolved internal destination: 'unique_193'

I'm not sure where this problem needs to be addressed; it could be in the merge program, or it could be in the PDF2 process that evaluates the merged file and generates this message. It would probably be best to generate the message during the merge program, because at that point the href is converted to something that we know is invalid. The code can determine that there is no target for #sectionid.

title: DITA-OT Issue #257: PDF2: Non-DITA link broken unless marked external

content: Issue #257 is closed with labels bug. Retrieval signals: error, xref, map, pdf, html.

title: DITA-OT Issue #257: PDF2: Non-DITA link broken unless marked external
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1844429](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1844429), submitted by [robander](/robander)

Encountered using doc\DITA-changes.xml in the toolkit. This xref element is broken in the PDF2 output:

<xref href="http://www-106.ibm.com/developerworks/xml/library/x-dita6/x-dita_downloads.html" format="html">DITA Downloads</xref>

XEP fails quietly - the output looks like a link but is not. FOP fails loudly with an error.

It looks like the code assumes this link is internal to the map. Local HTML links are typically still part of the information set; external ones are part of some other information set. For XHTML output, links to local HTML open in the same window, links to external HTML will open in a new window. I would expect the link to an HTML file to work for PDF whether it is scoped as local or external, though both would have to open up an external browser window.

Today the FO file contains this xsl:fo code for the sample above:
<fo:basic-link color="blue" font-style="italic" internal-destination="">DITA Downloads/fo:basic-link

If I add scope="external" onto the xref, the link becomes valid:
<fo:basic-link color="blue" external-destination="url(http://www-106.ibm.com/developerworks/xml/library/x-dita6/x-dita_downloads.html)" font-style="italic">DITA Downloads/fo:basic-link

title: DITA-OT Issue #258: Table cell spanning fails if another table embedded

title: DITA-OT Issue #258: Table cell spanning fails if another table embedded
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1846993](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1846993), submitted by iggraham

I've inserted one table inside another, and the outer table has cells which span columns. Unfortunately DITA is incorrectly preprocessing the table so that the column spanning doesn't work in subsequent rows.

The problem is that in the preprocessor's output the entry/@nameend attribute is being assigned the name of the wrong column(the same as @namest), eventually resulting in the HTML containing @colspan="1" when it should really be 2.

I've attached a sample DITA topic that illustrates the bug, which is very obvious when viewing the HTML output in a browser. Only the second row is spanning as it should. Rows 4 and 6 should too.

The table had worked fine until I embedded the inner table in one cell.

I discovered the problem after overriding the processing of <dl compact="yes"> to create a two-column table instead of HTML <dl>.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1848313](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1848313), submitted by debbiep-sf
When using a ditaval file, flagging is done by the XSLT (e.g., dita2htmlImpl.xsl for the xhtml transtyle). The path to the ditaval file is incorrectly being sent to the XSLT as a filesystem path, not a URL. Errors like this ensue:
[xslt] file:/M:/dap_vobwork/ttutil/build/dita-ot/1.3.1/xsl/xslhtml/dita2htmlImpl.xsl:132: Error! java.io.FileNotFoundException: \mpi.ditaval (The system cannot find the file specified) Cause: java.io.FileNotFoundException: \mpi.ditaval (The system cannot find the file specified)
Suggested solution: turn the file path into a URL using the Ant <makeurl> task, and pass the URL to the XSLT. Perhaps some code to force the URL to be absolute (which is the root cause of the above quoted error) would also help.

title: DITA-OT Issue #260: gen-list wants class on <foreign> descendants
content:
DITA-OT Issue #260: gen-list wants class on <foreign> descendants
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #260: gen-list wants class on <foreign> descendants
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1848355](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1848355), submitted by debbiep-sf

The gen-list pipeline complains if an element has no class attribute, but this is not appropriate for descendant elements of <foreign>. <foreign> elements and their subclasses may contain any well-formed XML content. They need not have a DITA class attribute, and often won't, particularly if they are from a foreign vocabulary like MathML.

The warning should be suppressed for any element that is a descendant of *[contains(@class, ' topic/foreign ').

title: DITA-OT Issue #261: <shortdesc> for chapter should not be suppressed
content:
DITA-OT Issue #261: <shortdesc> for chapter should not be suppressed
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #261: <shortdesc> for chapter should not be suppressed
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1848978](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1848978), submitted by roxvillerooster

When you use a topic in the <chapter> element of a bookmap (e.g., <chapter href="concepts/con_about_aca_tables.xml">) and then generate your PDF2 output, why is the topic's <shortdesc> element not shown on the chapter page in the PDF? The contents of the <body> is shown in the output, but not the <shortdesc>. 

Quoting Robert Anderson:
"It doesn't really make sense to
me that, by marking a topic as the start of the chapter, information that
would otherwise appear now does not. The shortdesc (if specified) fulfills
the same purpose that it does in other topics, right? It provides more
information about the rest of that topic, and should be used for hover help
in links to that topic (when such a thing is available). Given that it
appears in every other situation, I don't quite understand why this would
be an exception."

See http://tech.groups.yahoo.com/group/dita-users/message/7448
for more.

Can you give us a switch or a bit of XSL that we can insert so that the <shortdesc> behaviour can always be the same?

In demo/fo/xsl/fo/commons.xsl there is the XSL that controls the chapter page for the bookmap.
It seems to me that, right after createMiniToc is called, there needs to be a line that says "bring in the shortdesc".

title: DITA-OT Issue #264: args.css requires dummy file
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1852808](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1852808), submitted by davemcg

The goal is to create XHTML that will use an existing CSS on a web server by using the args.csspath and args.css properties in the Ant build script.

When generating XHTML using OT 1.3.1 or 1.4, a CSS link for the user-defined CSS is not being generated in the output if a CSS file with the same name does not exist locally. 

Note that the local file need not be a valid CSS file, just named as specified in the args.css property.

For example, given the following properties:
<property name="args.csspath" value="http://www.foobar.net/css"/>
<property name="args.css" value="myStyles.css"/>

If a file named "myStyles.css" does not exist locally relative to the Ant script, the output only contains the default:
<link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="http://www.foobar.net/css/commonltr.css"/>

If I then create a dummy myStyles.css file and resubmit the build, the results are correct:
<link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="http://www.foobar.net/css/commonltr.css"/>
<link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="http://www.foobar.net/css/myStyles.css"/>

Either this should be fixed, or the DITA-OT docs should be updated to indicate that a dummy file is required in this scenario.

title: DITA-OT Issue #273: XHTML: colsep in last column when @frame=none
content:
DITA-OT Issue #273: XHTML: colsep in last column when @frame=none
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #273: XHTML: colsep in last column when @frame=none
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1873401](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1873401), submitted by debbiep-sf

(And ditto rowsep in last row.)

In dita2htmlImpl.xsl, the "doentry" template assigns a class (nocellnorowborder row-nocellborder cell-norowborder cellrowborder) to a table cell, correctly ignoring the @colsep on the last column, and the @rowsep on the last row.

However, it forces the cell's right and bottom borders to be solid rather than missing, because of these lines:

<xsl:when test="not(../following-sibling::*)">1/xsl:when
...
<xsl:when test="not(following-sibling::*)">1/xsl:when

These borders will merge into the table's frame if the table has a frame, but if the table's frame is off (frame="none") then the cells in the last column and the last row combine to give a partial table frame anyway. You end up with a table whose right and bottom edges are visible.

The "1" in both of the above lines of XSLT should instead be "0". This will not affect tables that have frames because those tables are faked in the XHTML transform by nesting the entire table in a one-cell, bordered, table.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1897358](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1897358), submitted by m_minderbinder

I am using Dita OT 1.4.1 on Windows XP to generate a
series of HTML Help (CHM) projects, each with their own ditamap and which consume topics from a common directory.

I have an ANT build script that has a target to build
each project and an additional "build-all" target that
calls each individual target in sequence to generate
the CHM files.

If I call each target individually, the indexes (HHK
file) generates as they should. If I call the
"build-all" target, then the first index is compiled
correctly, but each successive HHK file contains all
index entries of the preceding files in addition to
its own (B contains A, C contains A&B etc). The topics
for the errant index entries are not present in the
CHM, only the keywords.

The following has been suggested on the DITA mailing list:

The generate-HHK code is part of the Java part of DITA-OT. It's quite possible that the hash table for old index entries is not being cleared out between iterations. This seldom comes up because most
people generate only one CHM per run of DITA-OT.

Example:

Map contains:
<topicref href="one.dita" chunk="to-content">
 <topicref href="two.dita" chunk="to-content"/>
</topicref>

one.dita contains:
<topic id="foo">
...
</topic>

two.dita contains:
<topic id="foo">
...
</topic>

Chunked result is
<topic id="foo">
...
 <topic id="foo">
 ...
 </topic>
</topic>
which is invalid (a topic ID is duplicated within the same file).

Chunking should rewrite ids (and track the mapping of the rewritings) when it chunks topics to-content to prevent the creation of invalid result topics.

title: DITA-OT Issue #286: maplink is unawareof chunk to-content
content:
DITA-OT Issue #286: maplink is unawareof chunk to-content
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #286: maplink is unawareof chunk to-content
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1897551](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1897551), submitted by debbiep-sf

The maplink preprocessing stage needs to ignore sections of the map that have undergone to-content chunking.

After chunking, a map contains entries like:

<topicref chunk="to-content" href="one.dita">
 <topicref href="one.dita">
 <topicref href="one.dita">
 <topicref href="one.dita">
</topicref>

When maplink runs it dutifully walks this structure and decides that one.dita is the parent of one.dita (among other nonsense relationships). This produces odd related links in (at least the HTML) output.

maplink should detect chunk="to-content" sections and skip them when it generates maplinks.unordered.

title: DITA-OT Issue #288: HTML titles should be space-normalized for CHM consumption
content:
DITA-OT Issue #288: HTML titles should be space-normalized for CHM consumption
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #288: HTML titles should be space-normalized for CHM consumption
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1898451](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1898451), submitted by debbiep-sf

The HTML <title> element's content is used in MS HTML Help as the topic title displayed in the search results tab when the user does a full-text search.

HTML user agents such as browsers are smart about whitespace in the title, and collapse multiple spaces into one for display in the browser. The HTML Help viewer HH.EXE is not so smart. If a title in DITA is

<title>
 Opening
 a file
</title>

then the four spaces between "Opening" and "a" will be visible in the search results tab when this topic is searched for.

Judicious use of normalize-space() on titles should eliminate this problem for HTML Help, and should have no effect on other uses of HTML.

title: DITA-OT Issue #306: FO 1.4.2 doesn't fail correctly when called from Ant
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1930201](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1930201), submitted by esroberts

The fo plugin (pdf2) does not behave correctly when there are errors in then PDF transform (OT 1.4.1, fo-plugin 1.4.2). Specifically, if there is an error encountered, an exception may be thrown but the build finishes with 'BUILD SUCCESSFUL', which shouldn't be the correct behavior. It should instead result in 'BUILD FAILURE'. Here is reproducible output from a failed build:

---snip---
transform.fo2pdf.xep:
 [java] EXCEPTION: Failed to create image file:/C:/Sandbox/doc/Borland-DITA/
DITATest/trunk/out/Graphic/swcarchitecture.gif of type null
 [java] Java Result: 1

transform.fo2pdf.fop:
 [delete] Deleting 3 files from C:\Sandbox\doc\Borland-DITA\DITATest\trunk\tem
p

topic2pdf2:

dita2pdf2:

BUILD SUCCESSFUL
Total time: 24 seconds
Press any key to exit...

---snip---

Obviously, the EXCEPTION and Java Result: 1 should trigger a failure. In demo/fo/build.xml around line 249, the failonerror attribute for the <java> task that calls com.idiominc.ws.opentopic.fo.xep.Runner is currently set to 'false'. If I change it to failonerror="true" PDF2 builds fail like they should. 

<target name="transform.fo2pdf.xep" if="use.xep.pdf.formatter">
 <java classname="com.idiominc.ws.opentopic.fo.xep.Runner" resultproperty="errCode" failonerror="false" fork="true" maxmemory="256m">
 <arg line='"${inputFile}" "${outputFile}" failOnError=${xep.failOnError}'/>
 <classpath refid="xep.class.path"/>
 <sysproperty key="com.renderx.xep.CONFIG" value="${xep.config.file}"/>
 </java>
 <condition property="xepExitedOnError" value="true">
 <not>
 <equals arg1="${errCode}" arg2="0"/>
 </not>
 </condition>
 </target>

Also, the ${xep.failOnError} parameter passed to the Runner class doesn't seem to do anything. I've verified that this value is true in my test scenarios but it doesn't seem to fail like it should.

I've attached a patch for build.xml that fixes the failonerror problem

title: DITA-OT Issue #317: Link generation is disabled for bookmaps
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1951879](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1951879), submitted by hmichaud

Not sure if this should be a bug report or a feature request, but the ability to have links within a book deliverable is pretty crucial for us, so I'm filing it here.

Our particular use cases are:
- links that are driven out of the topic hierarchy in the TOC -- specifically, for the top-level topic of each chapter to link to all its child topics
- links that are driven from reltables -- to enable cross-references between topics without using hard-coded links.

When producing a PDF from a ditamap, these hierarchical links and reltable links are generated, but when producing a PDF from a bookmap, links do not get generated regardless of the "generate related links" setting. We would like to see the same link generation behavior for bookmap processing as for ditamaps.

My team's DITA topic files include a mix of formats for local cross-references. We used a set of XSL stylesheets to convert legacy documentation to DITA XML. The local cross-references in these files do not include the file name.

For example:
<xref href = "#i120663"></xref>

We're currently authoring topic files using FrameMaker, which inserts local file names automatically.

For example:

The FO 1.4.2 plugin seems to handle these two formats differently. The plugin inserts the "on the page" text automatically for local cross-references that include the file name. But the plugin does not insert the "on the page" text if the cross-reference does not include the local file name.

Including the page numbers is a handy feature. I'd prefer to see the page numbers inserted automatically in all cases, if possible.

I've been studying the demo/fo/xsl/fo/links.xsl file, but haven't figured out where to override the default behavior to insert page numbers regardless of whether the local file name is or is not provided.

Thanks,
Mark

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1954463](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1954463), submitted by roxvillerooster

Hi all,

The problem in short, is that, when I build multiple PDFs using OT 1.4.1 and FO 1.4.2, conditional processing (filtering) is getting confused and this results in incorrect output.

Here's my team's situation:

Currently we use
 \* OT 1.2.2
 \* FO 1.2.1
 \* DITA 1.0 
 \* XEP 4.9

We are planning to move to
 \* OT 1.4.1
 \* FO 1.4.2
 \* DITA 1.1

XMetaL is primarily used as an authoring tool. We have a nightly Ant build process that builds all our deliverables (PDF2, tocjs and xhtml). In troubleshooting this problem, I have done everything to ensure that the problem I am experiencing is not a product of our own nightly build process.

Here's how everything works under our current environment:

I have two variations of a user guide, one for implementation X and one for implementation Y.
I have separate bookmaps for X and Y because each book has different content requirements.

Here's how the dir looks:

|--projectA

 |--ant_scripts

title: DITA-OT Issue #320: Conditional processing multiple PDFs in the same JVM
content:
|--concepts |--composite |--images |--references |--static content |--support |--tasks |--topics bookmapX.ditamap bookmapY.ditamap [other submaps are also here] Both of these bookmaps are stored in the same directory (projectA). The X and Y deliverables share many of the same topics. In these topics it is typical for me to use the select attribute product. If the

or is intended for the X deliverable, I set product="X"; if the element is only used for the Y deliverables, I set product="Y". When I build my outputs, I point to the ditaval files. For deliverable X, I use a ditaval that says include all elements where product="X" and exclude all elements where product="Y"; for deliverable Y, the exclude and include rules are flipped. When I use OT 1.2.2 and FO 1.2.1, I get the results I want. I can generate deliverable X or deliverable Y separately (each one has its own JVM). The documents are conditionally processed correctly. Perfect! When I generate both PDFs in the same JVM, conditional processing problems arise. Here's what I have tested: I have installed a fresh OT 1.4.1 toolkit with FO 1.4.2. When I build deliverable X separately or deliverable Y separately, they build fine and filtering is done correctly. BUT when I try to build deliverable X and Y at the same, the filtering gets confused and no warning is given that this has happened. Yikes! This first deliverable (e.g., X) that gets built is filtered correctly but the second deliverable (e.g., Y) is not. During the build of Y, the OT or FO tries to conditionally process the content correctly (i.e., from the log, it appears the correct ditaval is being used) but it gets confused. The PDF output for Y is filtered using the ditaval for X. That's very bad! The order of the deliverables does not seem to matter. If the Y deliverable is built before X, the output for X will be filtered as if it were Y. The only reason I discovered this as early as I did was because I had conditionalized two elements, one for X and one for Y. When I built both outputs together, the log for the second deliverable stated that it could not find the image file that was contained in the (i.e., Java result 1 error). Here's the error from the debug log:

title: DITA-OT Issue #320: Conditional processing multiple PDFs in the same JVM
content:
[java] EXCEPTION: Failed to create image file:/C:/SVN_testing/OT141_content/DITA_XML/test_output/b2_pillar2/pdf/integrated/b2_pillar2/images/p2_only_workflow.jpg of type null

 [java] Java Result: 1
Setting project property: errCode -> 1

The image file that could not be found, p2_only_workflow.jpg, should be filtered out and, it seems, that the filtering is working to an extent because that file cannot be found. When I check the PDF output the image is missing (as the error indicated) but all the filtering is wrong.
There's no other error in the log that indicates that I have a problem with my filtering.

Has anyone else encountered this issue?

This error does not occur when I run the XHTML transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #322: OSGI Manifest for eclipsehelp transtype contains spaces.
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1956231](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1956231), submitted by easirois

When producing an OSGI manifest from the eclipse transtype using a DITA Map, the XSL is adding some extra spaces in front of the Bundle Headers in the OSGI manifest.

This extra space is preventing the Eclipse Information Center from loading the content plugins.

Sample:
Bundle-Version: 1.0
 Manifest-Version: 1.0
 Bundle-ManifestVersion: 2
 Bundle-Localization: plugin

It should be:
Bundle-Version: 1.0
Manifest-Version: 1.0
Bundle-ManifestVersion: 2
Bundle-Localization: plugin

The fix is to modify the variable newline xsl/map2pluginImpl.xsl. The should be no spaces between the carriage return and the end of closing xsl:text The current template is

<xsl:variable name="newline">
 xsl:text
 /xsl:text
/xsl:variable

It should be:

<xsl:variable name="newline">
xsl:text
/xsl:text
/xsl:variable

Eric

title: DITA-OT Issue #324: Eclipse Provider not propogated to plugin.properties
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1960477](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1960477), submitted by abeerends

I really appreciate the inclusion of a manifest.mf file in the eclipsehelp output. However, there is one problem. The plugin.properties file used by the manifest for localization does not have the correct provider. It shows the default (DITA) instead of what is provided.

On the dita-users mailing list, Eric Sirois added:
From the looks of it, the version and 
provider parameters are not passed to the 
dita.out.map.eclipse.plugin.properties and 
dita.map.eclipse.plugin.properties targets.

<param name="version"
expression="${args.eclipse.version}"
if="args.eclipse.version" />
<param name="provider"
expression="${args.eclipse.provider}"
if="args.eclipse.provider" />

---

On a related point, the provider listed in the plugin.xml is the provided value. But, once a manifest is in use, the plugin name, provider, id, and version should not be listed in the plugin.xml. The manifest has been the preferred way to list this information since Eclipse adopted the OSGi specification with version 3.0 in 2004.

title: DITA-OT Issue #327: Building PDFs using a single JVM: topicref confusion
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1979522](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1979522), submitted by roxvillerooster

I am using OT 1.4.2, FO 1.4.2, and XEP 4.9 to generate multiple PDF (i.e., PDF2) outputs in one batch Ant build.

Here's the problem:
Two different bookmaps contain a topicref to files called ref_summary_of_changes.xml. These are two very different reference topics that are named the same. As far as I am concerned, the file naming should not be a problem. Both topics are in different folder structures and have different IDs.

When I build the PDFs for these two documents in the same JVM, there's a problem.

But first, here's how the directories and files are set up:
|--projectA
 bookmapA.ditamap
 |--referencces
 ref_summary_of_changes.xml (this file is specific for deliverable A).
|--projectB
 bookmapB.ditamap
 |--referencces
 ref_summary_of_changes.xml (this file is specific for deliverable B).

If the PDF for bookmapA is built first, the correct ref_summary_of_changes.xml is used. But, when bookmapB is built as part of the same build process (i.e., in the same JVM), its output uses the ref_summary_of_changes.xml from projectA. No error is given. The log makes it look like the correct file is used, but the PDF output is dead wrong. Is this a a caching issue?
If bookmapB is built before bookmapA, the same type of error occurs - bookmapA is output using projectB's ref_summary_of_changes.xml file.

When I build these two bookmaps separately (i.e., in separate JVMs) the correct ref_summary_of_changes.xml file is used as expected. Both outputs are fine.

The two workarounds I know of are:
 \* Ensuring the files are not named the same thing (but this should be acceptable and is OK with others DITA outputs)
 \* Building the outputs in separate JVMs (e.g., using ant's exec task)

I would rather avoid these workarounds. I am beginning to wonder whether all my PDF outputs should be built in separate JVMs.

I think this issue is likely connected to issue 1954463.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2008317](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2008317), submitted by [robander](/robander)

I have a several megabyte file that consists of a series of small topics.

I have a map that references each individual topic, and chunks those topics to new files, with a file name provided in the copy-to attribute.

The current toolkit process creates a copy of the entire file for every chunk that will be created (one for each copy-to attribute). With debug information, these each go up to 20+ megabytes. It then runs topicpull on each of the 20+ megabyte files. Finally it chunks the files and discards all but the single desired topic from each file.

This causes the temporary directory to fill up with hundreds of 20+ MB files. The build eventually hangs because too much memory is used.

It would be better if the copy-to processing was aware of the chunk value, and only created a copy with the correct chunk. This way the topics in the temporary directory would each be manageable and the build would complete quickly.

Sample files are provided by the person who originally reported this bug to me - I've sent them to the developer responsible for this piece of code, as SourceForge does not allow me to attach a zip this large.

title: DITA-OT Issue #340: example or section title can be orphaned in PDF2
content:
DITA-OT Issue #340: example or section title can be orphaned in PDF2
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #340: example or section title can be orphaned in PDF2
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2010092](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2010092), submitted by craig_sandvik

If <indexterm> immediately follows a section or example title, the title can appear by itself at page end, with following text on next page. Apparently, the <indexterm> is emitted in an invisible fo container, and keeping the title and this invisible container together satisfies the keep-with-next constraint.

A workaround is to move the <indexterm> into the title wrapped in <ph>. 

A minimally invasive fix is to apply the workaround automatically when creating the MERGED.xml file. 
Add the following template to xsl/common/topicmerge.xsl:

 <!-- Move <indexterm> that is direct child of titled <section> or <example> into the title. -->
 <xsl:template match="*[(contains(@class, ' topic/section ') or contains(@class, ' topic/example ')) and *[contains(@class, ' topic/title ')] ]">
 <xsl:element name="{name(.)}">
 <xsl:copy-of select="@*"/>
 <xsl:element name="{name( *[contains(@class, ' topic/title ')][1] )}">
 <xsl:copy-of select="*[contains(@class, ' topic/title ')][1]/@*"/>
 <ph><xsl:copy-of select="*[contains(@class, ' topic/indexterm ')]"/></ph>
 <xsl:copy-of select=" *[1][contains(@class, ' topic/title ')]/(element() | text())"/>
 /xsl:element 
 <xsl:apply-templates select="( *[not(contains(@class, ' topic/title ')) and not(contains(@class, ' topic/indexterm '))] ) 
 | (*[contains(@class, ' topic/title ')][position() > 1]) 
 | text()" 
 />
 /xsl:element
 /xsl:template

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2027058](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2027058), submitted by robertnthomas

In org.dita.dost.reader.ChunkMapReader.java, map processing quits recursion when processChildTopicref receives a topichead as its node argument. The inner-most if statement ought to allow elements with topichead in their class attribute to call processTopicref(). The way the code is currently written, topicrefs that are descendants of topichead do not get processed.

I will attach a modified version ChunkMapReader that changes the inner-most if statements test such that topichead will be processed. The change to the test also requires a new entry in org.dita.dost.util.Contstants.java, so I will attach that file as well.

title: DITA-OT Issue #345: maprefImpl.xsl removes part of class attr from topichead
content:
DITA-OT Issue #345: maprefImpl.xsl removes part of class attr from topichead
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #345: maprefImpl.xsl removes part of class attr from topichead
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2027170](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2027170), submitted by robertnthomas

maprefImpl.xsl removes "mapgroup-d/topichead" from the topichead element's class attribute in some cases. This makes it impossible to consistently identify topichead from its class attribute in downstream processes.

You can reproduce this problem with the following DITA context:

mapA.ditamap:
<map>
 <topicref format="ditamap" href="mapB.ditamap"/>
</map>

mapB.ditamap:

<map>
 <topichead id="ego" navtitle="This topichead is a child of map">
 <topicref href="MyTopic.dita"/>
 </topichead>
</map>

temp/mapA.ditamap will contain the following line:
<topichead class="- map/topicref " id="ego"
 navtitle="This topichead is a child of map" [snip!] >

The class attribute should be:
class="+ map/topicref mapgroup-d/topichead "

The following code excerpt is responsible:

277 <!-- if the element is not at the top level of
 reference target, @class equals to $refclass -->
278 <xsl:when test="not(contains(@class,$refclass))">

Perhaps the original test fails because topichead is part of a domain specialization; specifically, the "+" at the beginning of its class attribute value is causing the contains() statement to not match $refclass which begins with a "-" rather than a "+". One possible fix would be to change the test to this:

278 <xsl:when test="not(contains(@class,substring($refclass, 3)))">

title: DITA-OT Issue #350: Conkeyref does not work with range

title: DITA-OT Issue #350: Conkeyref does not work with range
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2078586](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2078586), submitted by [robander](/robander)

Using the latest code from CVS - conkeyref only works for single targets. I have this in my DITA 1.2 task:

<step conkeyref="special/start"
 conref="default-task.dita#default-task/start"
 conrefend="default-task.dita#default-task/end">
 <cmd></cmd>
</step>

In this case, the following should happen:

1) If the key "special" is not defined, the range should go from default-task.dita#default-task/start to default-task.dita#default-task/end

2) If the key "special" is defined as "special-task.dita#sp", the range should go from special-task.dita#sp/start to special-task.dita#sp/end, because the key "special" replaces the topic identifier in the conrefend attribute.

3) If the key "special" is defined as "special-task.dita", then the range should go from the element with id="start" in the FIRST topic in special-task.dita, to the element with id="end" in the FIRST topic in special-task.dita. This is because a key that resolves to "special-task.dita" is the same as a reference to the first topic in special-task.dita.

With the latest code, #1 is working, but #2 and #3 are not. It appears that for #2 and #3, the conrefend is ignored, and only the start element is pulled in.

The latest draft of the DITA 1.2 Language specification has several examples of how this should work.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2220010](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2220010), submitted by [robander](/robander)

According to the DITA 1.2 specification, acronyms should be referenced using the <abbreviated-form> element, which should give a key that is defined for a glossary topic.

I have a sample where my glossary topics are defined with keys="ibm" and keys="un". I use these keys inside my topic.

When I build the output, I get 10 warnings about undefined keys. For example:
 [xslt] file:/C:/DITA-OT1.5/xsl/common/output-message.xsl:68:20: Warning! [DOTX058W][WARN]: No glossary id was found to be associated with key 'ibm'. Appropriate forms will be guessed from glossary entry contents by application contexts. Specify the glossary id when referring to a glossary in glossentry tag.The location of this problem was at (File = C:\DITA-OT1.5\abbrev\acronyms.dita, Element = abbreviated-form:1)

The output pulls in the acronym in all cases. However, in the first instance within an output file, it is supposed to pull in the surface form. In the attached sample, the surface form always appears on the title attribute of the link around the acronym. The first time it is referenced, the full surface form should appear in normal text, without any title attribute. After that, the acronym should appear as normal text, and the full term (from the glossterm element) should appear on the title attribute.

Sample files are attached. The files can be unzipped to the toolkit directory; run the batch file to produce the output.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2220736](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2220736), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The <term> element may use a keyref attribute to reference a target topic. When the term element does this and references a glossary topic, it should pull in the title of that topic (the glossterm element). Instead it is pulling in the content of glossAcronym. Only the abbreviated-form element (or specializations of abbreviated-form) should work with the glossAcronym element.

title: DITA-OT Issue #363: Extra files generated when many topics are chunked to one
content:
DITA-OT Issue #363: Extra files generated when many topics are chunked to one
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #363: Extra files generated when many topics are chunked to one
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2317681](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2317681), submitted by [robander](/robander)

According to the DITA 1.1 specification, when many source files are chunked into a single output chunk, a DITA process should not produce chunks for the files that are merged into the main file.

For example, see the description of each sample in the specification:
http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/v1.1/CS01/archspec/chunking.html

In the example for map1, parent1.dita includes content from ditabase.dita. The output process does this correctly. However, the description says that ditabase.dita should not be generated on its own, because the reference only moves some content into the parent. With the 1.5 Milestone 7 build, ditabase.html is produced with all of the content from ditabase.dita.

The results are similar for the rest of the samples in the specification.

NOTE: There are some incorrect values in the samples. In map2, the nested topicref should use href="ditabase.dita#Y1" instead of href="ditabase.dita". Several examples use the copyto attribute but this should be the copy-to attribute. I've included all of the corrected samples from the specification in chunkspec.zip. To run all of the samples, unzip the attachment to the toolkit directory, which creates a "chunk" sub-directory. In that file, run the batch file runall.bat.

title: DITA-OT Issue #365: Handle @font-family="inherit"

DITA-OT Issue #365: Handle @font-family="inherit"
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #365: Handle @font-family="inherit"
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2385466](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2385466), submitted by debbiep-sf

Two bugs, one in the FO plugin, one in RenderX XEP, prevent the use of @font-family="inherit".

In the FO plugin, fo/xsl/fo/i18n-postprocess.xsl does not treat the value "inherit" specially for the font-family attribute. Instead, it looks up the font called "inherit" in the font-mappings file, which of course does not exist. It should ignore this attribute because it does not constitute a change in the font family.

In RenderX XEP, @font-family="inherit" incorrectly tries to look for a font called "inherit", fails, and falls back to Helvetica. To work around this bug, the i18n-postprocess stylesheet should omit @font-family when it is equal to "inherit".

The attached patch fixes both of these issues.

title: DITA-OT Issue #368: Map contains wrong reference after chunking
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2414891](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2414891), submitted by [robander](/robander)

When I have this in my map:
<topicref chunk="to-content" href="concept1.dita" navtitle="Concept1">
 <topicref href="reference1.dita" navtitle="reference1"></topicref>
 <topicref href="task1.dita" navtitle="task1"></topicref>
</topicref>

The chunking module merges the nested topics into concept1.dita. That is good. At the same time the map is updated so that the "reference1.dita" and "task1.dita" references point to concept1.dita. They should point to the correct topics within that file, so that they still reference the same topic. After the merge, the map currently contains this:
<topicref chunk="to-content" href="concept1.dita" navtitle="Concept1">
 <topicref href="concept1.dita" navtitle="reference1"></topicref>
 <topicref href="concept1.dita" navtitle="task1"></topicref>
</topicref>

It should point to the topics for the updated values, using the ID of the topic:
<topicref chunk="to-content" href="concept1.dita" navtitle="Concept1">
 <topicref href="concept1.dita#reference1" navtitle="reference1"></topicref>
 <topicref href="concept1.dita#task1" navtitle="task1"></topicref>
</topicref>

The attached sample contains these files.

title: DITA-OT Issue #374: pdf2: topic title widowed due to fo:marker placed in separat
content:
DITA-OT Issue #374: pdf2: topic title widowed due to fo:marker placed in separat
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #374: pdf2: topic title widowed due to fo:marker placed in separat
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2521819](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2521819), submitted by craig_sandvik

In pdf2, the template processTopicTitle in fo/xsl/fo/commons.xsl emits fo:marker in a separate fo:block that follows the fo:block containing the title, as in (greatly simplified):
fo:block ... The Title ... /fo:block
fo:blockfo:marker... The Title .../fo:marker/fo:block

This can lead to the title being widowed at the bottom of the page, since keeping the marker block with the title satisfies keep-with-next constraints. The marker should probably be emitted in the same block as the title.

title: DITA-OT Issue #382: mapref: should not modify href if scope=external
content:
DITA-OT Issue #382: mapref: should not modify href if scope=external
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #382: mapref: should not modify href if scope=external
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2629256](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2629256), submitted by debbiep-sf

Line 272 of xsl/preprocess/maprefImpl.xsl:

<xsl:when test="$relative-path='#none#' or contains(@href,'://')">

Should be:

<xsl:when test="$relative-path='#none#' or contains(@href,'://') or @scope='external'">

Reason: external hrefs are outside the current document set and should not have the current relative path tacked onto them. Not all external URIs have "://" in them so the other test in the same condition isn't sufficient.

title: DITA-OT Issue #383: maplink: should not modify href if scope=external
content:
DITA-OT Issue #383: maplink: should not modify href if scope=external
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #383: maplink: should not modify href if scope=external
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2629271](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2629271), submitted by debbiep-sf

Line 298 of xsl/preprocess/maplinkImpl.xsl:

<xsl:when
 test="starts-with(@href,'http://') or starts-with(@href,'/') or
 starts-with(@href,'https://') or starts-with(@href,'ftp:/') or @scope='external'">

Should be:

<xsl:when
 test="starts-with(@href,'http://') or starts-with(@href,'/') or
 starts-with(@href,'https://') or starts-with(@href,'ftp:/') or @scope='external'">

Reason: external scope means that the href is not relative to the current document set. Not all absolute hrefs contain :/ or start with slash.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2661418](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2661418), submitted by jonri

The Idiom PDF2 plug-in generated a TOC with links, which allowed users to click an item in the TOC and go to the applicable section in the PDF.

I noticed in the DITA-OT1.4 M11 build that the TOC is generated, but without links.

Adding a linked TOC is beneficial in the following ways:

If a user has Adobe Acrobat Pro/Standard they can change the view of the PDF to not show the Bookmark list.

title: DITA-OT Issue #387: xref linktext pulls in too many titles
content:
DITA-OT Issue #387: xref linktext pulls in too many titles
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #387: xref linktext pulls in too many titles
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2662218](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2662218), submitted by tashid

When the root topic in a referenced file (i.e. <xref href="othertopic.dita" />) contains child topics, the title of its first child (and that child's first child, etc.,) is pulled in to the xref linktext as well as the root topic's own title.

This is due to the line in topicpull:getlinktext-firstinfile
<xsl:apply-templates
 select="document($file,/)//*[contains(@class, ' topic/topic ')][1]/*[contains(@class, ' topic/title ')]" mode="text-only"/>

The // means "select all descendants" so this returns every topic in position 1 with respect to its parent;
the line (and similar ones throughout) should be
<xsl:apply-templates
 select="document($file,/)/*[contains(@class, ' topic/topic ')][1]/*[contains(@class, ' topic/title ')]" mode="text-only"/>

this only applies to "firstinfile" and not to "otherfile" where // is correct as we are searching for a topic id.

Not tested on 1.5 (I'm still using 1.4.1) but topicpullImpl.xsl in the 1.5M11 release seems to use the same query. Apologies if this no longer applies for some other reason.

A topicref with @copy-to set produces a new copy of the topic in preprocess

A topicref with collection-type="sequence" and copy-to set on child

copy this way.

ZIP also describes code modifications to merge topics referenced by 
@copy-to.

title: DITA-OT Issue #409: Topicmeta searchtitles in map not used in topic
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2791345](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2791345), submitted by lakowalski1

To ensure my topics are reusable in different maps, I want to set the <searchtitle> for my topics in the map, rather than inside the topics themselves. Based on the DITA 1.1 spec about metadata inheritance between maps and topics, I tried using <topicmeta><searchtitle> in the hierarchy.map in the DOT samples. I ran some iterations and here are the results.

Iteration 1:
Test setting <searchtitle> inside the topic itself. Update changingtheoil.xml in samples/tasks to have:

<title>Changing the oil in your car</title>
<titlealts><searchtitle>LAK Search Title</searchtitle></titlealts>

Transform to eclipsehelp, and the output changingtheoil.html has inside it:

<link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="../commonltr.css"/>
<title>LAK Search Title</title>
</head>

Iteration 1 works to make the <title> in the output file match the <searchtitle> text.

Iteration 2: 
Remove the <titlealts><searchtitle> from the changingtheoil.xml file.

Update hierarchy.ditamap to use <topicmeta><searchtitle> to apply a different search title text to that topic:

<map title="Eclipse content aggregated by a map">
<topicref href="tasks/garagetaskoverview.xml" type="concept">
 <topicref href="tasks/changingtheoil.xml" type="task">
<topicmeta>
<searchtitle>Map Oil Search Title</searchtitle>
</topicmeta>
</topicref>
 <topicref href="tasks/organizing.xml" type="task"/>

Transform to eclipsehelp. Output file changingtheoil.html file has:

<link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="../commonltr.css"/>
<title>Changing the oil in your car</title>
</head>

The searchtitle text "Map Oil Search Text" is not found in the out directory. Iteration 2 does _not_ work to set the searchtitle using the <topicmeta><searchtitle> inside the map.

Iteration 3:
Try having both a <searchtitle> in the topic _and_ a different one in the map. Update changingtheoil.xml in samples/tasks to have:

<title>Changing the oil in your car</title>
<titlealts><searchtitle>LAK Search Title</searchtitle></titlealts>

Keep the hierarchy.ditamap from Iteration 2 to have the lines:
<topicref href="tasks/changingtheoil.xml" type="task">
<topicmeta>
<searchtitle>Map Oil Search Title</searchtitle>
</topicmeta>
</topicref>

Transform to eclipsehelp. This time, the searchtitle text that's set in two places (topic and map) seems to be ignored (!). Even though there is a <searchtitle> inside the topic file, and there is a <topicmeta><searchtitle> in the map, the output file uses the <title> from the topic file:

<link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="../commonltr.css"/>
<title>Changing the oil in your car</title>
</head>

---

For Iteration 2, I expected that the searchtitle text from the <topicmeta> in the map to be applied to the topic, unless there is a statement that it is not currently supported.
For Iteration 3, I would have expected that if there's no current support for using <topicmeta><searchtitle> in the map, that at least the <searchtitle> set inside the topic would be used. (That is, the results of Iteration 3 were completely unexpected to me.)

I looked inside the /temp directory after Iteration 3. For the changingtheoil.xml that's in /temp it has the following lines at the top:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?><?workdir /C:\DITA\DITA_OT15\DITA-OT1.5\temp\tasks?><?path2project ..\?><task xmlns:ditaarch="http://dita.oasis-open.org/architecture/2005/" id="changeoil" xml:lang="en-us" ditaarch:DITAArchVersion="1.2" domains="(topic task) (topic hi-d) (topic ut-d) (topic indexing-d) (topic hazard-d) (topic abbrev-d) (topic pr-d) (topic sw-d) (topic ui-d) (topic task strictTaskbody-c) " class="- topic/topic task/task " xtrf="C:\DITA\DITA_OT15\DITA-OT1.5\samples\tasks\changingtheoil.xml" xtrc="task:1">
<title class="- topic/title " xtrf="C:\DITA\DITA_OT15\DITA-OT1.5\samples\tasks\changingtheoil.xml" xtrc="title:1">Changing the oil in your car</title>
<titlealts class="- topic/titlealts " xtrc="titlealts:1" xtrf="C:\DITA\DITA_OT15\DITA-OT1.5\samples\tasks\changingtheoil.xml"><searchtitle class="- map/searchtitle " xtrc="searchtitle:1" xtrf="C:\DITA\DITA_OT15\DITA-OT1.5\samples\hierarchy.ditamap">Map Oil Search Title</searchtitle></titlealts>

I can see the "Map Oil Search" text from the <topicmeta> in the map inside the changingtheoil.xml file that's sitting in the /temp directory from this process. In some part of the process, it fails to carry through to the final output file.

Thanks for looking into this,
Lee Anne

title: DITA-OT Issue #413: CHM Index terms come out with extra spaces
content:
DITA-OT Issue #413: CHM Index terms come out with extra spaces
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #413: CHM Index terms come out with extra spaces
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2793836](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2793836), submitted by [robander](/robander)

If an index term contains multiple spaces, those spaces are all preserved in the HHK file used to produce an index for HTML Help. This is a side effect of the fix for bug 2010062, which caused spaces to be dropped when an index term had sub-elements: https://sourceforge.net/tracker2/?func=detail&aid=2010062&group_id=132728&atid=725074

The following sample uses underscores to represent spaces, because the HTML display will drop spaces. The problem now is that this:
<indexterm>
_____Hello
_____There
</indexterm>

Comes out in the HHK file as the term
"______Hello______There_"

The code that generates this index term should condense multiple consecutive white-space characters into a single space.

title: DITA-OT Issue #414: No Easy Way to Override/Extend HTML Navtitle Generation
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2794487](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2794487), submitted by drmacro

The current implementation for getting navtitles in the map2htmltoc.xsl makes it difficult to override or extend the processing. In addition, it is using value-of to get the content of <navtitle> elements, which is not good--will produce bad results for specializations of <navtitle> that include <ph> elements.

I think the correct implementation is to use a navtitle mode rather than a named template to construct the navtitle. That then allows easy extension and override via plugins.

I'm willing to attempt this fix nobody else wants to do it.

content: Issue #416 is closed with labels none. Retrieval signals: map, html, plugin, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #416: Leading slash breaks PLUGINS_ROOT usage for Eclipse help
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2796614](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2796614), submitted by lakowalski1

I don't know if this is really a 'bug' because the Language Reference on anchorref doesn't give an example that actually works in Eclipse, I believe that putting a leading slash in the output toc.xml is incorrect. I would have expected whatever I set for the anchorref in the <map> element would be adhered to as it transforms to the output.

I'm transforming with transtype=eclipsehelp, and using an anchorref on my <map>.

No matter what I put for my anchorref, the output always adds a leading slash in the link_to attribute of the <toc> element in the Eclipse help output. The leading slash gets included every time.

For example, update hierarchy.ditamap to have <map> element:
<map title="Alpha Component" id="comp.alpha.ed1" anchorref="../com.lak.doc/edition1_1.ditamap#comps" >

And the output hierarchy.xml gets:
<toc label="Alpha Component" link_to="/../com.lak.doc/edition1_1.xml#comps"
 topic="tasks/garagetaskoverview.html">

This only works ok in Eclipse for certain directory structures. In fact, I see no reason for the leading slash, when link_to="../com.lak.doc/edition1_1.xml#comps" works the same.

(Note also that the Language Reference description for anchorref has a misleading example. The anchorref needs a # after the ditamap name to reference the anchor point in that map.)

More critically, this leading slash breaks the ability to use PLUGINS_ROOT in Eclipse to reference the toc files in other doc plug-ins.

For example, change the <map> element in hierarchy.xml to:
<map title="Alpha Component" id="comp.alpha.ed1" anchorref="PLUGINS_ROOT/com.lak.doc/edition1_1.ditamap#comps" >

And transform to eclipsehelp. The output hierarchy.xml file has:
<toc label="Alpha Component" link_to="/PLUGINS_ROOT/com.lak.doc/edition1_1.xml#comps"
 topic="tasks/garagetaskoverview.html">

That output <toc> element does not work in the Eclipse help system. The Eclipse system is expecting PLUGINS_ROOT to be the start of the path, because that tells Eclipse to start at the place where Eclipse knows all of the plug-ins are, and then find plug-in with name="com.lak.doc".

Again, I would have expected whatever I set for the anchorref in the <map> element would be adhered to as it transforms to the output. Adding a leading slash to the link_to attribute was an unexpected result. Any questions or further explanation for why there should be a leading slash, please let me know.

Thanks!
Lee Anne

title: DITA-OT Issue #417: XSL character entity errors for Eclipse output in booktitle
content:

title: DITA-OT Issue #417: XSL character entity errors for Eclipse output in booktitle
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2796993](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2796993), submitted by quinnd

The handling of whitespace for eclipse outputs generated from bookmaps is problematic. If the <booktitle> element has children (such as <mainbooktitle> and <booktitlealt>) and the children are indented in the source (see included source.JPG) the output translates the carriage returns and other non-important whitespace into character entity references. In Firefox this gets rendered in the resulting XML TOC file (mostly) fine, but Internet Explorer deeply indents in attempt to display these entities. The tooltips in the HTML also preserve this incorrect whitespace. The error occurs on line 52 of xsl/map2eclipse.xsl:
<xsl:value-of select="*[contains(@class,' topic/title ')]"/>

If a normalize-space function is inserted it correctly ignores the whitespace between elements in the <booktitle> and its children:
<xsl:value-of select="normalize-space(*[contains(@class,' topic/title ')])"/>

title: DITA-OT Issue #424: Eclipse help MANIFEST.MF filename wrong case, needs CRLF
content:
DITA-OT Issue #424: Eclipse help MANIFEST.MF filename wrong case, needs CRLF
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #424: Eclipse help MANIFEST.MF filename wrong case, needs CRLF
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2813082](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2813082), submitted by bgossett

Eclipse help (starting with Eclipse 3.5?) appears to have these requirements which are not met by DITA OT 1.4.3:

. the meta-inf directory name should be upper case (META-INF)
. the Manifest.mf file name should be upper case (MANIFEST.MF)
. the MANIFEST.MF file's line endings should be CRLF, not just LF

The directory and file names are set in build_dita2eclipsehelp_template.xml. 

The xsl/map2pluginImpl.xsl file defines a newline variable that contains CRLR bytes in a text element:

 <xsl:variable name="newline">
xsl:text
/xsl:text
 /xsl:variable

But apparently during processing only an LR is output in the manifest file. One possible fix is to use explicit carriage return and line feed characters:

 <xsl:variable name="newline">
xsl:text
/xsl:text/xsl:variable

There may be a better fix than this, but this outputs the desired CRLF line ending.

title: DITA-OT Issue #425: Prolog indexterm not processed properly for PDF
content:
DITA-OT Issue #425: Prolog indexterm not processed properly for PDF
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #425: Prolog indexterm not processed properly for PDF
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2815485](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2815485), submitted by craig_sandvik

In PDF output, indexterms in topic prolog are emitted inside fo:inline elements 
between the blocks emitted for shortdesc and body. Problems with this:
- It results in a gob of extra whitespace between the shortdesc and topic body
 blocks (formatted by Antenna House, have not tried other processors).
- The indexterm should be linked to the topic title, not to the gob of 
 whitespace after the shortdesc.

Suggested fix:
1) Change existing prolog template to completely suppress it's contents:
<xsl:template match="*[contains(@class,' topic/prolog ')]"/>

2) Add new template pullPrologIndexTerms:
<xsl:template name="pullPrologIndexTerms">
 <xsl:apply-templates select="ancestor-or-self::*[contains(@class, ' topic/topic ')]/*[contains(@class, ' topic/prolog ')]//opentopic-index:index.entry[not(parent::opentopic-index:index.entry)]"/>
/xsl:template

3) In all the various places where topic title is emitted in a fo:block, call pullPrologIndexTerms inside that block.

title: DITA-OT Issue #426: PDF: keep-with-next on shortdesc
content:
DITA-OT Issue #426: PDF: keep-with-next on shortdesc
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #426: PDF: keep-with-next on shortdesc
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2815492](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2815492), submitted by craig_sandvik
PDF output looks better if "short" (1-3 line) short descriptions have keep-with-next set so they render on the same page as following text. This can't be done universally because shortdesc content can be arbitrarily long.
A workable solution: 1) Define character count value, call it maxCharsInShortDesc. maxCharsInShortDesc is the number of characters in 3 lines of typical text for the output language. This value can be computed by a named template. 2) If the string value of the shortdesc node contains fewer characters than maxCharsInShortDesc, add a low-strength keep to the output fo:block. (A full-strength keep may conflict with the full-strength keeps on title blocks.)
Since the character count for rendered text depends on formatting, the maxCharsInShortDesc will need to be customized based on the font used for each language.
Note this can't be fixed without fixing bug 2815485 (prolog indexterm not processed properly).

title: DITA-OT Issue #432: Move meta module pushes content into non-DITA file
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2832696](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2832696), submitted by [robander](/robander)

I have a map that contains this topicref:
<topicref format="xml" href="mymap.xml" navtitle="Other format"/>

It uses format="xml" because this is not a DITA topic. However, the MoveMeta module still tries to access mymap.xml to push metadata from the map into mymap.xml. This happens even if I set format="randomXml". The MoveMeta module generates this message:
 [pipeline] ERROR FILE DOES NOT EXIST C:\DITA-OT1.5\temp\mymap.xml

If the format attribute is specified, and format!=dita and format!=ditamap, we should not attempt to push any metadata into the target file.

It looks like the first step of the build is also trying to read these files as DITA files, which is incorrect - that step should also recognize the specified format attribute, and not use only the extension. During that step, the build generates this message:

title: DITA-OT Issue #448: Problem of keys attribute in nested topicref elements
