title: DITA-OT Issue #448: Problem of keys attribute in nested topicref elements
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2856742](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2856742), submitted by pvojtechovsky

The "keys" attribute in nested topicref elements are not handled well in case the keys is used in parent and also in children.

For example following XML is not handled correctly:

<topicref keys="k1" href="i18n_tasks.dita" type="task">
<topicref keys="k1_1" href="i18n_generateJavascriptWithMessages_task.dita" type="task"/>
<topicref keys="k1_2" href="i18n_useLocalizedMessageInJavascript_task.dita" type="task"/>
</topicref>

The problem is in org.dita.dost.reader.KeyrefReader. 
1) it is not able to handle nested topicrefs
2) it handles by wrong way even parent topicref, because it assignes key to the last visited child in startMethod.

This problem causes that usage of keyref, which refers to "k1" or "k1_1" will report

> [pipeline] [DOTJ047I][INFO] Unable to find key definition for keyref="k1", href may be used as fallback if it exists. Please make sure the key name is correct.

original bug: 2815485

In my pdf, each child topic was being assigned indexterms from its ancestors. 

The result is that entries in my index have way more included page numbers than they should have.

 <xsl:template name="pullPrologIndexTerms">
 xsl:commentxsl:text[start pulling indexterms]/xsl:text/xsl:comment
 <xsl:apply-templates select="ancestor-or-self::*[contains(@class, ' topic/topic ')]/*[contains(@class, ' topic/prolog ')]

 //opentopic-index:index.entry[not(parent::opentopic-index:index.entry)]"/>
 xsl:commentxsl:text[end pulling indexterms]/xsl:text/xsl:comment
 /xsl:template

if (sharpIndex != -1){ // href value refer to an id in a topic

With these lines:
 if (sharpIndex == 0){ // href value refers to id in same topic file

.append("ohref").append(Constants.EQUAL).append(Constants.QUOTATION)
.append(attValue)
.append(Constants.QUOTATION);

title: DITA-OT Issue #460: keyref within topics ignore @copy-to attributes
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2870935](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2870935), submitted by schwamkrug

Example map:

<map title="Keydef/Keyref Bug Sample">
<topicref href="A.dita" />
<topicref href="B.dita" keys="topicB" copy-to="topicB.dita"/>

<reltable>
 <relrow>
 <relcell>
 <topicgroup collection-type="family">
 <topicref href="A.dita" />
 <topicref keyref="topicB" />
 </topicgroup>
 </relcell>
 </relrow>
 </reltable>

title: DITA-OT Issue #464: Cannot use different TOC titles for same topic in PDF
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2871326](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2871326), submitted by [robander](/robander)

I have the same topic multiple times in my map. I use @locktitle="yes" to try and create different titles for them in different locations. For example:

<topicref href="parent.dita" navtitle="nanananana">
___<topicref href="child.dita" locktitle="yes" navtitle="locked local title"/>
</topicref>
<topicref href="child.dita" locktitle="yes" navtitle="Reuse the child at the top"/>
<topicref href="child.dita" locktitle="no" navtitle="Unlocked title"/>

Currently, if any reference to child.dita uses locktitle="yes", then _all_ TOC entries use the title from the first occurrence in the map (locked local title).

If none of the references to child.dita use locktitle="yes", then all TOC entries use the actual topic title (as expected).

I have a backwards-compatible fix for this that affects bookmarks.xsl and commons.xsl, and will check it in after running it by the PDF code owners.

title: DITA-OT Issue #466: Bad relcolwidth crashes PDF output
content:
DITA-OT Issue #466: Bad relcolwidth crashes PDF output
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #466: Bad relcolwidth crashes PDF output
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2872988](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2872988), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The PDF output currently creates the following marker for each value in a simpletable's relcolwidth attribute:
<fo:table-column column-width="proportional-column-width(1)"/>

If the relcolwidth is "1\* 2\* 3*" then there are three fo:table-column elements. 

If any row in the simpletable has more than three columns, FOP crashes, and no PDF is produced. I have not tested XEP or Antenna House to see if they have the same problem.

We should fix the PDF code to bypass this error, and add a proportional value of 1\* for each column that is missing. I've got a couple of recursive functions that do this by 1) finding the row with the maximum number of cells, 2) counting the number of entries in @relcolwidth, and 3) adding 1\* for each missing item.

I also tested to see whether having more values than entries is a problem, but it is not - the PDF is produced without error.

title: DITA-OT Issue #470: PDF: table @pgwide semantics not implemented
content:
DITA-OT Issue #470: PDF: table @pgwide semantics not implemented
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #470: PDF: table @pgwide semantics not implemented
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2875946](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2875946), submitted by craig_sandvik

According to the DITA-OT language spec, a value of "1" for table attribute pgwide should cause the table to render at page width in PDF output, irrespective of any indentation of the containing block. This behavior is not implemented.

To fix, suggest mofifying the template named "tgroup" in xsl/fo/tables_1.0.xsl. Add the code indicated by comments below, inside the declaration of variable named "table":
 <xsl:variable name="table">
 <fo:table xsl:use-attribute-sets="table.tgroup" id="{@id}">
<xsl:call-template name="displayAtts">
 <xsl:with-param name="element" select=".."/>
 </xsl:call-template>

 <!-- Add code to implement @pgwide semantics. -->
 <xsl:if test="(parent::*/@pgwide) = '1'">
 <xsl:attribute name="start-indent" select="0"/>
 <xsl:attribute name="end-indent" select="0"/>
 <xsl:attribute name="width" select="'auto'"/>
 </xsl:if>
 <!-- End addition -->

 <xsl:apply-templates/>
 </fo:table>
 </xsl:variable>

title: DITA-OT Issue #473: Shortdesc & Abstract formatting is incorrect for PDF
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2879171](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2879171), submitted by [robander](/robander)

This same issue was raised a while back for XHTML, but was not fixed for PDF.

The DITA 1.1 specification says that when shortdesc appears inside `<abstract>`, there are two options for rendering:
1) When the abstract only contains text or other phrase level markup, the shortdesc should be formatted as inline markup.
2) Otherwise, the abstract contains blocks, and the shortdesc should also be formatted as a block.
http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/v1.1/OS/langspec/langref/abstract.html

title: DITA-OT Issue #474: Colon character in <indexterm> causes nesting in output
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2879196](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2879196), submitted by su-laineyeo2

Say you have <indexterm>foo:bar</indexterm> in a DITA topic.

CHM output correctly produces a single index entry that looks like this: 
foo:bar

However, PDF output produces a parent and child pair, like this:
foo
 bar...........................................37

There is a need for people to have colons appear in index entries, so the PDF behavior is not desirable. PDF processing should treat colons as ordinary characters instead of as instructions to create a nested entry.

title: DITA-OT Issue #476: HTMLHelp won't compile properly if outer.transform = "yes"
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2881151](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2881151), submitted by digilante

The generated .hhp, .hhc, and .hhk files contain broken links to content (.dita, .xml) if those content files are not located in the same directory as the .ditamap file. I've discovered the location of content relative to the ditamap directory is the meaning of the inner.transform and outer.transform Ant properties.

Workaround: For dita2htmlhelp transformations, 1) move all your content into the ditamap folder 2)verify that the href attributes for your topicref elements in the .ditamap do not contain "..", and 3) do not set the value of the outer.transform property to "yes" for the dita2htmlhelp target in your build file.

title: DITA-OT Issue #480: indexterm in topicref level are copied into topic/prolog
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2891736](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2891736), submitted by tmakita

Dear Developers,

I found a fatal problem in making middle file in FO output (DITA-OT M22). If I author an indexterm in topicref/topicmeta/keywords, it is copied into topic/prolog/metadata/keywords. Please refer to attached DITA source file and middle file.

According to the DITA 1.1 specification, the indexterm in topiref/topicmeta level and the indexterm in the topic/prolog level must be treated in a diffrent way. followin are extract from specification.

Index range indications may occur in the topicmeta of a topicref at the map level, in the prolog of a topic,
or in the body of a topic, and are interpreted as follows:
- In a map, the start range points to the start of the topic title of the topic being referenced by its
 containing topicref. The end range points to the end of the final child contained by the topic being
 referenced by its containing topicref, or to the end of the final topic referenced by the current map
 (whichever comes first). When a start and end range occur in the same topicmeta, the range applies to
 the containing topicref and its children.
- In a prolog, the start range points to the start of the containing topic’s title. The range ends with a
 matching index range end in the same prolog, or the end of the prolog, whichever comes first. The
 range applies to the containing topic and all its children including child relationships defined in a map.
- In a body, the range starts where the start indexterm occurs and ends at the matching index range end
 indication within the same body, or at the end of the body, whichever comes first. Such an index range
 does not span sub-topics of the topic.

According to this specification, I think that copying indexterm from topicref/topicmeta level to topic/prolog level is not right behavior.

Please reconsider this DITA-OT action.

Regards,

title: DITA-OT Issue #483: This is a bug in the integrator.xml
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2893316](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2893316), submitted by sitwon

I am developing a plug-in for DITA and discovered a bug in the integrator. In my ant targets that are intended to be integrated into build.xml the entities and CDATA sections are being resolved instead of passed through.

For example, if I write:
<replace file="abc.txt" token="<element/>"/>
<replace file="abc.txt">
<replacetoken><![CDATA[<element/>]]></replacetoken>
</replace>
<replace file="abc.txt" token="&lt;element/&lt;"/>

The integrator produces the following in build.xml:
<replace file="abc.txt" token="<element/>"/> <-- This is not valid XML
<replace file="abc.txt">
<replacetoken><element/></replacetoken> <-- This does not match as I wanted it to
</replace> 
<replace file="abc.txt" token="<element/>"/> <-- This works, but was counter intuitive to prodce this correct result.

I have tested in DITA-OT v1.5.

I believe standard package should contains demo/fo/fop/build demo/fo/fop/lib and demo/fo/fop/conf/fop.xconf.

title: DITA-OT Issue #489: map2htmtoc.xsl doesn't allow for extension of root template

title: DITA-OT Issue #489: map2htmtoc.xsl doesn't allow for extension of root template
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2900047](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2900047), submitted by drmacro

Currently the template for "/" in map2htmtoc.xsl does all the top-level processing itself. 

This makes it impossible to extend, but not replace, this processing, in particular, to generate a separate TOC in addition to the default TOC.

Would be best if the business logic was pushed to a named template so the root template could be extended without having to copy the main business logic.

Change would be:
1. Change current <xsl:template match="/"> to <xsl:template name="generate-toc"/> (or whatever name makes the most sense)
2. Create new template:

<xsl:template match="/">
 <xsl:call-template name="generate-toc"/>
/xsl:template

title: DITA-OT Issue #493: String compares with constants may cause NPEs
content:
DITA-OT Issue #493: String compares with constants may cause NPEs
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #493: String compares with constants may cause NPEs
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2914476](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2914476), submitted by drmacro

Whenever a String variable is compared to a constant using equals() the variable should be specified as the parameter to equals() on the constant. This avoids NPEs, e.g., change

myStringVar.equals(Constants.SOME_STRING)

to 

Constants.SOME_STRING.equals(myStringVar)

Likewise, string literals should be compared the same way:

"Foo".equals(myStringVar)

If a given string should never be null, there should be code that checks that precondition somewhere, especially for values that are specified via Ant properties or command-line variables.

title: DITA-OT Issue #494: plus-htmlhelp-alias-map: using same extension point twice
content:
DITA-OT Issue #494: plus-htmlhelp-alias-map: using same extension point twice
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #494: plus-htmlhelp-alias-map: using same extension point twice
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2914574](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2914574), submitted by debbiep-sf

Pasted from dita-users at http://tech.groups.yahoo.com/group/dita-users/message/16550:

plugins/com.moldflow.dita.plus-htmlhelp-alias-map

First, in...

plugins/com.moldflow.dita.plus-htmlhelp-alias-map/plugin.xml

...the calls for the ALIAS and MAP files are both keyed to the same extension, so
the second call overwrites the first and only the MAP file actually gets included in
the final build. To fix this, I changed the code as follows:

ORIGINAL CODE

<feature extension="depend.plus-transtype-htmlhelp.map.basic.hhp.pre"
value="plus-htmlhelp-alias.make-absolute" type="text"/>
<feature extension="depend.plus-transtype-htmlhelp.map.basic.hhp.pre"
value="plus-htmlhelp-map.make-absolute" type="text"/>

NEW CODE

<feature extension="depend.plus-transtype-htmlhelp.map.basic.hhp.pre"
value="plus-htmlhelp-alias-map.make-absolute" type="text" />

One extension, one call. Then, switch over to...

plugins/com.moldflow.dita.plus-htmlhelp-alias-map/build_plus-htmlhelp-alias-map.xml

...and combine the targets to set both properties at once:

ORIGINAL CODE

<target name="plus-htmlhelp-alias.make-absolute"
depends="plus-htmlhelp-alias-map.init" if="plus.htmlhelp.alias">
 <property name="plus.htmlhelp.alias.absolute" location="${plus.htmlhelp.alias}"/>
</target>

<target name="plus-htmlhelp-map.make-absolute"
depends="plus-htmlhelp-alias-map.init" if="plus.htmlhelp.map">
 <property name="plus.htmlhelp.map.absolute" location="${plus.htmlhelp.map}"/>
</target>

NEW CODE

<target name="plus-htmlhelp-alias-map.make-absolute"
depends="plus-htmlhelp-alias-map.init" if="plus.htmlhelp.map">
 <property name="plus.htmlhelp.alias.absolute" location="${plus.htmlhelp.alias}" /> 
 <property name="plus.htmlhelp.map.absolute" location="${plus.htmlhelp.map}" /> 
</target>

I know that not checking for a specified ALIAS file (i.e. if="plus.htmlhelp.alias")
is a bit sloppy, but a) there's no way to do an AND conditional without creating yet
another target and b) you really cannot have an ALIAS file without a MAP file.

Anyhow, with these changes, the ALIAS and MAP files are both appended to the HHP
file as intended. I've been using it in production for a couple months now, but as
always, YMMV.
## 

Michael D. Hayden :: mhayden@silverhammer.org

title: DITA-OT Issue #496: @locktitle not respected by preprocessor
content:
DITA-OT Issue #496: @locktitle not respected by preprocessor
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #496: @locktitle not respected by preprocessor
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2916469](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2916469), submitted by drmacro

Given this topicref in a map:

<topicref locktitle="yes"
 href="topics/topic-02.xml">
 <topicmeta>
 <navtitle>Topic 02 Navtitle Element</navtitle>
 </topicmeta>
 </topicref>

The navtitle on the topicref should be preserved in preference to any title on the target topic. However, with M24 I get this result in the preprocessed map:

<topicref
 class="- map/topicref "
 href="topics/topic-02.xml"
 locktitle="yes"
 type="topic"
 xtrc="topicref:2"
 xtrf="/Users/ekimber/workspace/rsuite-dita-support/test/dita/pdf-generation-test-01/pdf-generation-test-01.ditamap">
 <topicmeta
 class="- map/topicmeta ">
 <navtitle
 class="- topic/navtitle ">Topic 02 In-Topic Navtitle</navtitle>
 <?ditaot gentext?>
 <linktext
 class="- map/linktext ">Topic 02 Title</linktext>
 </topicmeta>
 </topicref>

Note that the <navtitle> reflects the navtitle of the target topic, not the navtitle of topicref. Per the DITA 1.2 spec:

locktitle:

This attribute makes sure the navtitle element or attribute is used if it is present. If locktitle isn't set to "yes", the navtitle is ignored and text is retrieved from the target.
yes
The navtitle in the map is used.
no
The navtitle or title of the topic is used. This is the processing default.

title: DITA-OT Issue #503: commonTopicProcessing template prolog proessing out of order
content:
DITA-OT Issue #503: commonTopicProcessing template prolog proessing out of order
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #503: commonTopicProcessing template prolog proessing out of order
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2928582](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2928582), submitted by drmacro

The current template "_" mode="commonTopicProcessing" has the effect of processing any shortdesc or abstract *before_ the prolog. If you want to, for example, use the author value from prolog, you must override the whole template. 

I rewrote the template as:

<xsl:template match="*" mode="commonTopicProcessing" priority="10">
 <xsl:variable name="topicrefShortdesc">
 <xsl:call-template name="getTopicrefShortdesc"/>
 /xsl:variable
 <xsl:apply-templates select="*[contains(@class, ' topic/title ')]"/>
 <xsl:apply-templates select="*[contains(@class, ' topic/prolog ')]"/>
 <xsl:apply-templates select="$topicrefShortdesc/*"/>
 <xsl:apply-templates select="*[not(contains(@class, ' topic/title '))
 and not(contains(@class, ' topic/prolog '))
 and not(contains(@class, ' topic/shortdesc '))
 and not(contains(@class, ' topic/topic '))]"/>
 <xsl:call-template name="buildRelationships"/>
 <xsl:apply-templates select="*[contains(@class,' topic/topic ')]"/>
/xsl:template

This ensures that prolog is processed before any "body" content (that is, before any shortdesc or abstract). I also eliminated the unnecesary "if topicrefShortdesc" check.

title: DITA-OT Issue #505: Need to parameterize maxmemory and VM args for forked JVMs
content:
DITA-OT Issue #505: Need to parameterize maxmemory and VM args for forked JVMs
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #505: Need to parameterize maxmemory and VM args for forked JVMs
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2930528](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2930528), submitted by drmacro

The PDF2 plugin has three <java> tasks that specify fork="true". One of these (the XEP one, specifies an explicit value for @maxmemory, the others do not specify @maxmemory at all.

In order to process large documents (e.g., the full DITA 1.2 language reference, more memory is required.

In addition, in order to access memory above the 32-bit JVM limit, the <java> target must specify the JVM arg "-d64".

Assuming that the forking of these JVMs is either absolutely required or otherwise advantageous, then the maxmemory and architecture values need to be parameterized.

I would suggest the Ant properties "max.jvm.memory" and "jvm.architecture", declared and used like so:

<property name="max.jvm.memory" value="256M"/>
<property name="jvm.architecture" value="32"/>

Which are then used like so:

<java classname="${fo.saxon.classname}" classpathref="project.class.path" fork="true"
 maxmemory="${max.jvm.memory}"

> <jvmarg value="-d${jvm.architecture}"/>
> ...
> </java>

I have hacked my local copy of fo/build.xml in this way and was able to process the full DITA 1.2 spec in 1000M of JVM memory (about 1200 pages).

An alternative would be to use the JVM_OPTS or ANT_OPTS value in a nested <jvmargs/> element, but I think having explicit properties is clearer.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2950588](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2950588), submitted by drmacro

Given this original attribute specification:

select='replace(normalize-space(string-join($rootTitle, " ")), """", "\""")'

The template processor rewrites it to:

select="replace(normalize-space(string-join($rootTitle, " ")), """", "\""")"

Note the double quotes around the value, where the value requires single quotes.

The workaround is to have as your template XSLT a shell that only includes other XLSTs, but this is still something that should be fixed if at all possible.

DITA-OT Issue #509: Minor improvements to "garage" samples
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #509: Minor improvements to "garage" samples
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2953706](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2953706), submitted by [robander](/robander)

There has been a lot of talk over the last couple of years about improving the Garage samples, but at this point they still have not been updated. I've recently heard complaints about the lack of <shortdesc> elements in these files, which has prompted me to make several minor updates to bring these topics in line with DITA and DITA-OT best practices:
1. Create <shortdesc> elements for each topic. In most cases this means moving the first sentence into a shortdesc. In a couple of cases this means adding a new sentence as the shortdesc.
2. Move the "To do this:" lead-in text from context into the new <stepsection> element in one topic.
3. Update the DTD statements so that they accurately reference the new DITA 1.2 directories.
4. Remove <linktext> elements from links to related files (the link text is automatically retrieved during the build).

Other improvements are likely desirable, but I'm checking these in now just to get them completed.

title: DITA-OT Issue #510: Installing eclipsemap plugin breaks Eclipse output from maps
content:
DITA-OT Issue #510: Installing eclipsemap plugin breaks Eclipse output from maps
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #510: Installing eclipsemap plugin breaks Eclipse output from maps
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2954154](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2954154), submitted by [jelovirt](/jelovirt)

In 1.5.1 M2, if the Eclipse map plugin is installed, an Eclipse help cannot be correctly output using a plain map. The problem is that eclipsemap/xsl/map2plugin.xsl file has

 <xsl:template name="eclipse.manifest.init" mode="eclipse.manifest" match="*">

Which will also be used to process plain maps. Because this template tests for eclipsemap elements e.g. for Bundle-Version, the output version will always be the default 1.0.0.

A fix is to make the template less greedy, ie.

<xsl:template name="eclipse.manifest.init">

And let the template above match only eclipsemap plugin element.

title: DITA-OT Issue #516: /onlytopicinmap does not respect conref
content:
DITA-OT Issue #516: /onlytopicinmap does not respect conref
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #516: /onlytopicinmap does not respect conref
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2961909](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2961909), submitted by [robander](/robander)

I have a map that uses conref to pull a branch from another map:
<map>
 <topicref conref="map2.ditamap#branch1"/>
</map>

In the other map, there are multiple branches:
<map>
 <topicref id="branch1" href="goodtopic1.dita">
 <topicref href="goodtopic2.dita"/>
 </topicref>
 <topicref href="badtopic1.dita">
 <topicref href="badtopic2.dita"/>
 </topicref>
</map>

In this case - my original map only uses the first branch of map2. However, the build is still trying to build files that are not referenced (badtopic1 and badtopic2) - I get File Not Found errors for those or any others outside of the branch. 

We have an option called /onlytopicinmap that is supposed to tell the OT not to build topics which are outside the scope of the originally referenced files. When this option is activated, the build should ignore topics outside of the branch1 in map2, because they are never used by the originally referenced material.

The same thing is true if branch1 in map2 is used with a "mapref" style reference:
<topicref format="ditamap" href="map2.ditamap#branch1"/>

title: DITA-OT Issue #519: XSLFO test for @compact wrong
content:
DITA-OT Issue #519: XSLFO test for @compact wrong
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #519: XSLFO test for @compact wrong
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2970471](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2970471), submitted by nicstoffel

Related to Artifact 1663976.
Line 82-87 of dita2fo-subroutines.xsl:

<!-- If the element has a compact=yes attribute, assert it in contextually correct form. -->

<!-- (assumes that no compaction is default) -->

<xsl:template match="@compact">
 <xsl:if test="@compact = 'yes'">
 <!--xsl:attribute name="compact">compact</xsl:attribute-->
 <!-- NOOP for FO for now; must use padding attributes in block context -->
 /xsl:if
/xsl:template

The test will never match because the compact attribute cannot itself have attributes. Should be:

<!-- If the element has a compact=yes attribute, assert it in contextually correct form. -->

<!-- (assumes that no compaction is default) -->

<xsl:template match="@compact">
 <xsl:if test=". = 'yes'">
 <!--xsl:attribute name="compact">compact</xsl:attribute-->
 <!-- NOOP for FO for now; must use padding attributes in block context -->
 /xsl:if
/xsl:template

title: DITA-OT Issue #524: Integrator adds spaces into XML Catalog entries
content:
DITA-OT Issue #524: Integrator adds spaces into XML Catalog entries
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #524: Integrator adds spaces into XML Catalog entries
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2974667](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2974667), submitted by [robander](/robander)

According to the OASIS XML Catalog specification, the <public>, <system>, and <uri> elements must be empty in order to be valid.

When a DITA-OT plug-in defines these elements with a self-closing tag, the integrator adds them into the catalog-dita.xml file with one or more newlines. For example, the full package ships with the dita132 document types in a demo directory. The catalog in that directory defines:
 <public publicId="-//IBM//DTD DITA Concept//EN"
 uri="dtd/concept.dtd"/>

The integrator adds it to the main catalog-dita.xml file as:
<public publicId="-//IBM//DTD DITA Concept//EN" uri="demo/dita132/dtd/concept.dtd">

</public>

Some tools that read and validate the catalog are reporting errors due to the extra spaces. The integrator should be adding the tags as empty tags, either as self-closing tags or with an end tag and no spaces.

(Opened on behalf of Julio Vazquez, who got errors when Oxygen attempted to validate the catalog file).

title: DITA-OT Issue #526: Output parameters info at INFO level
content:
DITA-OT Issue #526: Output parameters info at INFO level
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #526: Output parameters info at INFO level
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2979328](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2979328), submitted by [jelovirt](/jelovirt)
[echo] *****************************************************************
 [echo] * basedir = …
 [echo] * dita.dir = …
 [echo] * input = …
 [echo] * transtype = xhtml
 [echo] * tempdir = …
 [echo] * outputdir = …
 [echo] * extname = .dita
 [echo] * clean.temp = no
 [echo] * xslt.parser = SAXON
 [echo] *****************************************************************
This is output in the WARNING level, as the default level of <echo> element is warning. If the user runs OT and Ant using the quiet flag (-q), to get only warning and error messages, the parameter info block is still output.

To fix this, the level attribute should be set to "info" on the <echo> elements:

title: DITA-OT Issue #526: Output parameters info at INFO level
content:
<echo level="info">*****************************************************************</echo>
<echo level="info">* basedir = ${basedir}</echo>
<echo level="info">* dita.dir = ${dita.dir}</echo>
<echo level="info">* input = ${args.input}</echo>
<echo level="info">* transtype = ${transtype}</echo>
<echo level="info">* tempdir = ${dita.temp.dir}</echo>
<echo level="info">* outputdir = ${output.dir}</echo>
<echo level="info">* extname = ${dita.ext}</echo>
<echo level="info">* clean.temp = ${clean.temp}</echo>
<echo level="info">* xslt.parser = ${xslt.parser}</echo>
<echo level="info">*****************************************************************</echo>
This will only output the actual warnings and errors in quiet mode, not the parameter info which is basically debug info.

title: DITA-OT Issue #531: Duplicate parameter in XHTML code
content:
DITA-OT Issue #531: Duplicate parameter in XHTML code
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #531: Duplicate parameter in XHTML code
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2986492](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2986492), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The XSLT code for XHTML declares the parameters $filename and $FILENAME. There are some problems with this:
1. We should not declare two parameters that differ only in case. One of these is never used, so we need to consolidate them.
2. In general, the design is to use upper case for parameters, so we should use the $FILENAME parameter instead of $filename
3. The $filename, $filedir, and $CURRENTFILE parameters are declared in the dita2xhtml.xsl shell. This means any user that creates a new shell has to re-declare the parameters. We should move the parameters to dita2htmlImpl.xsl so that no user needs to redeclare them.

So, for the fix, we do this:
1. Move the 3 parameters from dita2xhtml.xsl to dita2htmlImpl.xsl
2. Change $filedir to $FILEDIR
3. Remove $filename and use $FILENAME (currently, the code does not use $FILENAME)

title: DITA-OT Issue #536: pdf2: empty @column-number
content:
DITA-OT Issue #536: pdf2: empty @column-number
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #536: pdf2: empty @column-number
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3000604](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3000604), submitted by sethpark

While building the DITA 1.2 arch spec, several entries were given null values for @column-number, which stops XEP. The cause of the issue is that several entries contained @colname but did not have a @colnum. The first when test is satisfied, but it is unable to return a value to the definition of $colnumval.

I modified the choose statements to first determine whether a colspec with matching @colname has a @colnum; this test prevents the issue. The second "when" statement is unchanged. I modified the third "when" statement just because I didnt understand the original; maybe it was ok.

Here is the modified variable definition (to replace corresponding definition in tbody//entry and thead//entry templates:

<xsl:variable name="colnumval">
 xsl:choose
 <!-- s.park: make sure names match first -->
 <xsl:when test="ancestor::tgroup/colspec[@colname=current()/@colname]/@colnum">
 <xsl:value-of select="ancestor::tgroup/colspec[@colname=current()/@colname]/@colnum"/>
 /xsl:when
 <xsl:when test="@colnum">
 <xsl:value-of select="@colnum"/>
 /xsl:when
 xsl:otherwise
 <!-- s.park: otherwise, trust the relative position, determined by adding the number of preceding sibling entiries, plus "1" -->
 <xsl:value-of select="number(count(preceding-sibling::entry) + 1)"/>
 <!--<xsl:number count="entry"/>-->
 /xsl:otherwise
 /xsl:choose
 /xsl:variable

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3000677](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3000677), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The XHTML output for <msgph> and <systemoutput> currently use <tt>, which creates monospaced font. It should be using <samp> in the output, which is generally rendered in the same monospaced font, but more accurately describes the content. This also gets around some web accessibility checkers that report violations for using <b>, <i>, and <tt> rather than elements with more meaning.

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #547: CSS for prereq links indents prereq element
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3006443](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3006443), submitted by [robander](/robander)

When using the new OT option to put out HTML class values based on all DITA element names, the prereq element is indented. 

This is caused by the following setting in the default CSS files:
.prereq { margin-left : 20px;}

That setting was originally intended for pre-requisite links (any links marked as both required and role="previous" will be displayed at the top with this indentation). That was before we added the ability to include class names based on every DITA element.

The prereq links are placed in a <dt> element, and the <prereq> element is placed in a <div> element. So if we change the CSS file to this, it will fix the indentation:
dt.prereq { margin-left : 20px;}

Converted from [SourceForge issue 3016739](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3016739), submitted by [robander](/robander)

I have an odd situation:
- Map uses chunk="to-content" to create a single XHTML output file
- Toc references a file (P022178main.dita)
- That file has a <link> to a second file (P022178other.dita)
- The second file is not used in the TOC section, but does appear in a reltable

When this happens, the chunk module deletes the temporary file P022178other.dita, but does not change the link inside P022178main.dita. When the topicpull step runs, it tries to pull link text from P022178other.dita, but it generates errors because the file has been deleted.

To fix this, when a local topic only appears in the reltable, the chunk module should not delete it.

title: DITA-OT Issue #556: Chunk output includes index terms in navtitles

title: DITA-OT Issue #556: Chunk output includes index terms in navtitles
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3020314](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3020314), submitted by [robander](/robander)

When using chunk="by-topic", the chunk processor creates new <topicref> elements in the map. It does not give those elements navigation titles. The mappull step has already run, which means that the final navigation step must use fallback processing for navigation titles.

In HTML Help output, the fallback output includes index terms and draft content.

In Eclipse output, there is no fallback, so the topics do not use titles.

I have a fix for the fallback processing, but the best solution is to have the chunk processor create a navtitle and short description when it creates the new topicref.

The sample files should be unzipped to the toolkit install directory. There is an Ant build for HTML Help (chunkchm.xml) and for Eclipse (chunkeclipse.xml).

title: DITA-OT Issue #562: Index file not generated by default for Eclipse Help
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #562: Index file not generated by default for Eclipse Help
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3029074](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3029074), submitted by easirois

When using the Eclipse Map specialization the current default behavior is not to specify the org.help.eclipse.index extension point without specifying <indexExtension/> in the plugin map. This differs from the default behavior when using the base DITA Map using the Eclipse Help transtype.

A workaround is to specify the following element in your Eclipse Collection map after <pluginmeta>:
<indexExtension href="index.xml"/>

This leads to another issue, the current process pipeline has index.xml file hardcoded as the output for the indexes for a plugin. So if someone specified <indexExtension href="myIindex.xml"/>, the plugin.xml file would reference the correct filename, but the build process will always create an index.xml file.

The are two fixes required for this defect:
 1) If nothing is specified the default for both DITA Map and Eclipse Collection map, the processing pipeline will create an index.xml file and have the appropriate index extension point in the plugin.xml file.
 2) Modify the pipeline such that whatever filename is specified in <indexExtension/> is actually created and the appropriate extension created in plugin.xml file.

title: DITA-OT Issue #567: Scale is not correctly computed in XHTML transforms
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3032950](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3032950), submitted by raducoravu

In XHTML transforms if an image has scale set to it, the width and height are computed using ImgUtil.
The ImgUtil has had for a long time the problem of returning the height when getWidth() is called and the width when getHeight is called, but this seems to be fixed in DITA OT 1.5.1.
But the stylesheets which use ImgUtil (dita2htmlImpl.xsl in this case) still use the methods in reverse to compute the width and height for an image. The fix in the XSL has comments like:
AM: currently dost.jar returns the height in function getWidth instead of width 
The fixes were incorporated in bug: 2900417

As a fix, in the XSLT stylesheets which use ImgUtil to get the width and height please make sure that the methods are properly used.

title: DITA-OT Issue #573: Infinite recursivity in replaceString template
content:
DITA-OT Issue #573: Infinite recursivity in replaceString template
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #573: Infinite recursivity in replaceString template
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3036985](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3036985), submitted by raducoravu

The template in the file "DITA-OT/xsl/common/output-message.xsl" called "replaceString" is not correctly implemented.
It may lead to infinite recursivity when the replacement string contains the match.
For example, if the topic reference contains a href like: "DITA_CMMI-ACQ_Concepts/Agreement%20Management.xml" and it has an incorrect "scope='ditamap'" set to it, although it is a topic, the DITA OT tries to complain by showing an error message which tries to replace the '%2' string with the href. As the href contains '%2', the recursivity leads to an Out of Memmory.

The template should get re-implemented like:

 <xsl:template name="replaceString">
 <xsl:param name="string"/>
 <xsl:param name="match"/>
 <xsl:param name="replacement"/>
 xsl:choose
 <xsl:when test="contains($string,$match)">
 <xsl:value-of select="substring-before($string,$match)"/>
 <xsl:value-of select="$replacement"/>
 <xsl:call-template name="replaceString">
 <xsl:with-param name="string"
 select="substring-after($string,$match)"/>
 <xsl:with-param name="replacement" select="$replacement"/>
 <xsl:with-param name="match" select="$match"/>
 /xsl:call-template
 /xsl:when
 xsl:otherwise
 <xsl:value-of select="$string"/>
 /xsl:otherwise
 /xsl:choose
 /xsl:template

It is a template which avoids this problem.

title: DITA-OT Issue #574: xml:lang attribute on ditamaps is not detected
content:
DITA-OT Issue #574: xml:lang attribute on ditamaps is not detected
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #574: xml:lang attribute on ditamaps is not detected
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3038532](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3038532), submitted by su-laineyeo2

The "xml:lang" attribute is supposed to cascade from maps to topics, so you should only have to set it at the root of the primary map file. E.g. if you have a French document in 10 topics held together by a map, you should only have to set <map xml:lang="fr-fr"> at the map root, not in every topic file. However, most output formats, with the exception of PDF, seem to require a language code on every single topic file in order to use the appropriate language settings.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3038933](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3038933), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The troff link handling code is based on the XHTML code - it reuses the XHTML code so that the sorting and grouping does not need to be re-implemented. 

The XHTML code process prereq links at the top of the file, and then excludes them from the main link section. 

Troff never processes them at the start, but excludes them at the bottom. It should process them as XHTML does.

I get these messages:

> gen-list-without-flagging:

> [pipeline] [WARN]: Copy-to task [href="" copy-to="thead-01.xml"] was ignored.

The 1.2 spec clearly requires that the chunk be generated when there is no href:

> to-content: The "to-content" token indicates that the selection should be rendered as a new chunk of content.
> ...

The rendition address of the generated topic is determined as defined for the copy-to attribute. If the copy-to attribute is not specified and the topicref has no id attribute, the address of the generated topic is not required to be predictable or consistent across rendition instances.

This is with 1.5.3M2. I get the same failure under OSX or Windows.

title: DITA-OT Issue #586: Toolkit Allows Unescaped URLs, doesn't handle escaped ones
content:
DITA-OT Issue #586: Toolkit Allows Unescaped URLs, doesn't handle escaped ones
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #586: Toolkit Allows Unescaped URLs, doesn't handle escaped ones
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3058124](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3058124), submitted by drmacro

The 1.2 spec says in clause 3.4.2.1 The href attribute:

"Note that certain characters (including, but not limited to, #, ?, \, and space) are not permitted unescaped within
URIs. Such characters must be percent-encoding (per RFC 3986) if there is a need to represent them within a
string that is a URI. Also note that the “&” (ampersand) and “<” (greater than) characters are not permitted in XML
attribute values, so they must be represented by appropriate character or entity references if there is a need to
represent them within such a string. (Some tools may do the required encoding on the user's behalf while others
may require the user to avoid the special characters or perform the encoding manually.)"

However, in my testing, the Toolkit does not resolve escaped URLs but does resolve the equivalent URL unescaped. The attached data set demonstrates the behavior and the output of the 1.5.2M2 Toolkit.

For backward compatibility the Toolkit should probably continue to resolve unescaped URLs but give a warning but it definitely must resolve escaped URLs.

title: DITA-OT Issue #587: Peer links break with missing format or wrong extension
content:
DITA-OT Issue #587: Peer links break with missing format or wrong extension
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #587: Peer links break with missing format or wrong extension
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3059256](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3059256), submitted by [jelovirt](/jelovirt)

Revision 1.10.4.7 for xsl/xslhtml/rel-links.xsl added @scope="peer" test for non-DITA link handling (row 459). This has the side-effect that if you have a link

 <xref href="foo.dita" scope="peer">Foo</xref>

this will be treated as as non-DITA link. You have to have the format attribute to make it work. However, because format="dita" is the default, I think the default should be respected and the test for peer scope should be removed.

Another problem with peer links is that if dita.extname property is set to the default "xml" and topic files have the the file extension .xml. If you combine content from other content providers and those resources use file extension .dita, the peer links don't work. If your link is

 <xref href="foo.dita" scope="peer">Foo</xref>

this will not pass the test "contains(@href,$DITAEXT)". To allow peer content to not use the same topic extension, this test could be rewritten to

((not(@scope) or @scope='local') and contains(@href,$DITAEXT)) or
(@scope='peer' and (contains(@href,'.xml') or contains(@href,'.dita')))

That is, for local links respect dita.extname extension and for peer links accept both .xml and .dita; the xsl:when content should also be refactored to support both file extensions. It's more complex, but would place less restrictions on file extensions.

title: DITA-OT Issue #588: Problem displaying French content TOC in CHM output
content:
DITA-OT Issue #588: Problem displaying French content TOC in CHM output
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #588: Problem displaying French content TOC in CHM output
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3060269](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3060269), submitted by raducoravu

Issue encountered by one of our Oxygen XML Editor users:

The user has French content in his DITA files (words with French accents like: "développement"). He has "xml:lang='fr-FR'" correctly specified on the DITA Map root.
He also has words with French accents in the topic references (so the TOC will contain titles with French accents).

After transforming to CHM the right hand side of the viewer displays correctly the French characters but the left side of the viewer (the TOC navigator) does not correctly display the accents.

I identified 3 potential problems in the following stylesheets:
1,2) Both the map2hhc.xsl and map2hhp.xsl stylesheets do not specify an output encoding for the transformation (so they use UTF-8 which is the default). 
If I change the "xsl:output"'s and specify the output encoding as " encoding="windows-1252" " then after the transformation the accents will also be visible in the TOC.
3) The map2hhp.xsl which generates the hhp file generates part of it like:

Binary Index=NoLanguage=0x040c French (FRANCE) 

(notice there is no line break between the Index and the Language key/value pairs.
This can be fixed by adding a line break in the map2hhp.xsl, something like:
xsl:text
Language=/xsl:text 

I think number 3 definitely needs to be fixed (minor stylesheet change). 
About number 1and 2: It should probably be investigated what should be the default encoding for writing the hhp and hhc output files. Should it be "windows-1252" by default?

title: DITA-OT Issue #589: Messages extension damages custom message formatting
content:
DITA-OT Issue #589: Messages extension damages custom message formatting
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #589: Messages extension damages custom message formatting
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3062912](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3062912), submitted by paul_cpwr

When you extend the default DITA-OT error messages via the dita.xsl.messages extension point in $DITA_HOME/resource/messages_template.xml, the resulting custom messages in the integrated messages.xml all end up with extra returns at the end of the message elements. 

For example, if your custom message appears as:
<message id="DOTX700E" type="ERROR">
 <reason>This is the reason.</reason>
 <response>This is the response.</response>
</message>

The resulting message in messages.xml after integration is:
<message id="DOTX700E" type="ERROR">
</response>

</message>

The extra white space between elements is not a problem but the extra return at the end of the messages is a problem. This injected return becomes a part of the output content. From a logging perspective, this forces the single message to log as multiple discrete log messages. This is especially problematic if you try to use the XmlLogger.

Also, while does not appear to be fatal, it may be unintentional that all XML comments are stripped out of the messages file (template and extension) during integration, including the XML prolog and the doctype declaration from the template file.

title: DITA-OT Issue #590: Adjacent words get glued together using DITA to RTF
content:
DITA-OT Issue #590: Adjacent words get glued together using DITA to RTF
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #590: Adjacent words get glued together using DITA to RTF
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3063533](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3063533), submitted by raducoravu

When the attached topic gets transformed to RTF the words:
"occurrence" and "simplement" get concatenated together in the output (without the additional space which would be necessary between them).

I suspect that in the XSL: "DITA-OT/xsl/xslrtf/dita2rtfImpl.xsl" in the template:
<xsl:template match="text()">
xsl:choose
<xsl:when test="ancestor::*[contains(@class,' topic/pre ')] or ancestor::*[contains(@class,' topic/lines ')]">
<xsl:call-template name="gen-txt"><xsl:with-param name="txt" select="."/>/xsl:call-template
/xsl:when
xsl:otherwise
 <xsl:if test="starts-with(.,' ') and not(normalize-space(.)='')">xsl:text /xsl:text/xsl:if<xsl:call-template name="get-ascii">
 <xsl:with-param name="txt"><xsl:value-of select="normalize-space(.)"/>/xsl:with-param
 /xsl:call-template<xsl:if test="substring(.,string-length(.))=' ' and not(normalize-space(.)='')">xsl:text /xsl:text/xsl:if
/xsl:otherwise
/xsl:choose
/xsl:template

The tests in the ""starts-with(.,' ') " are incomplete because the first character between the 2 words is a line break and not a space. Because of this the space between the 2 words does not get output anymore. I will also try to post a fix for this.
The XSL should be checked to see if more problems like this are in it.

title: DITA-OT Issue #600: FO: topicmerge drops id on map/topicref without href.
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3085106](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3085106), submitted by jannylun

Problem:
The topicmerge of FO plugin uses generate-id() for map/topicref's without @href in the build-tree mode. In the regular mode, these topicrefs are matched by the wildcard template that doesn't generate an id. This causes the corresponding topicref within opentopic:map to not have an id which leads to the fo conversions determineTopictype fails to identify the topictype.

The example bookmap below shows a scenario where chapter 1 will get formatting as a regular topic while chapter 2 get's chapter formatting.

Solution:
Generate the id for all map/topicref's that don't have a href.

Example:
<bookmap>
 <chapter navtitle="Chapter 1">
 <topicref href="topic1"/>
 </chapter>
 <chapter navtitle="Chapter 2" href="chapter2">
 <topicref href="topic2"/>
 </chapter>
</bookmap>

Br,
Jan

title: DITA-OT Issue #605: Shortdesc metadata missing when using abstract

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #605: Shortdesc metadata missing when using abstract
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3095233](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3095233), submitted by [robander](/robander)

When a topic includes a child <shortdesc> element, it generates metadata tags, such as:
<meta name="abstract" content="Shortdesc content" />
<meta name="description" content="Shortdesc content" />

When the shortdesc is inside an abstract element, there is no equivalent metadata. The shortdesc should create metadata in this case.

As with link previews, if there are multiple shortdesc elements in the <abstract>, they should be separated by spaces.

title: DITA-OT Issue #606: PDF should skip empty columns in property tables
content:
DITA-OT Issue #606: PDF should skip empty columns in property tables
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #606: PDF should skip empty columns in property tables
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3097409](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3097409), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The <properties> element in a reference topic is generally a three column table, containing fields for type, value, and description.

None of these are required. In XHTML, if a properties table does not contain any entries from a given column, that column is skipped. For example, if there is no propdesc or propdeschd element in the table, then the third (empty) column should not be generated.

If only one row skips an entry, then the empty cell should continue to be generated. For example, if the third row is missing <propvalue> but other rows have a value, then the output should continue to insert an empty cell so that the description remains in the third column.

title: DITA-OT Issue #607: Disable Output Escaping Should Not Be Used

title: DITA-OT Issue #607: Disable Output Escaping Should Not Be Used
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3098975](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3098975), submitted by drmacro

The code that handles empty table cells does thi:

<xsl:text disable-output-escaping="yes">&#xA0;/xsl:text

This breaks follow-on transforms that process the HTML because the literal numeric character reference then gets escaped in the final output.

This use of output escaping should be completely unnecessary since   is a valid Unicode character and should work in all HTML contexts.

If this escaping is required for some contexts it must be isolated in a separate mode specific for handling empty table cells so that users of the base transforms can turn it off.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3102827](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3102827), submitted by raducoravu

The class org.dita.dost.util.FileUtils has methods:
isSupportedImageFile()
and 
isValidTarget()

which decide if targets are valid depending on the file extension.

There are problems with this hard-coded approach, for example the ".bmp" image format is not included by default thus not appearing in the output.
Another example: MathML ".mml" and ".mathml" files referenced as images can be recognized by Apache FOP if it uses the additional JEuclid libraries.
Maybe a parameter could be given to the DITA OT specifying an additional list of image extensions. Or at least add the 3 extensions mentioned above to the hard-coded list.

title: DITA-OT Issue #612: Update Saxon command line args for IDIOM PDF build.xml
content:
DITA-OT Issue #612: Update Saxon command line args for IDIOM PDF build.xml
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #612: Update Saxon command line args for IDIOM PDF build.xml
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3103488](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3103488), submitted by raducoravu

The following DITA OT build file:
"DITA-OT\demo\fo\build.xml"

invokes the Saxon 9 processor not as an "<xslt>" ANT task but as a command line Java process.
Some of the arguments which are given to the Saxon processor have been deprecated since Saxon 9.0 and are now removed in Saxon 9.3. This includes the parameters used to specify the output file or the warning level or the catalog resolver. 
See this link for more details:
http://www.saxonica.com/documentation9.1/using-xsl/commandline.html
As the DITA OT is bundled with Saxon 9.1 maybe the command line arguments should be updated like:
<property name="saxon.resolver.command.line" value="-w0 -x org.apache.xml.resolver.tools.ResolvingXMLReader -y org.apache.xml.resolver.tools.ResolvingXMLReader -r org.apache.xml.resolver.tools.CatalogResolver"/>

should be replaced with:

<property name="saxon.resolver.command.line" value="-warnings:silent -x:org.apache.xml.resolver.tools.ResolvingXMLReader
---

<arg line='-o "${buildDir}/stage2.fo"'/>

Should be replaced with:
<arg line='-o "${outputFile}"'/>

Should be replaced with:
In this way people who use a newer version of Saxon will be able to use DITA OT without patches.

title: DITA-OT Issue #617: Java sun.* packages should not be used
content:
DITA-OT Issue #617: Java sun.* packages should not be used
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #617: Java sun.* packages should not be used
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3114353](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3114353), submitted by [jelovirt](/jelovirt)

The Java method org.dita.dost.util.ImgUtils#getBASE64 uses sun.misc.BASE64Encoder method. However, Java documentation[1] recommends that classes in the sun.\* packages should not be used:

"The sun.\* packages are not part of the supported, public interface.
A Java program that directly calls into sun.\* packages is not guaranteed to work on all Java-compatible platforms. In fact, such a program is not guaranteed to work even in future versions on the same platform."

A replacement can be found from Apache Commons Codes[2], in org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64 class.

References:

[1] http://www.oracle.com/technetwork/java/faq-sun-packages-142232.html
[2] http://commons.apache.org/codec/

title: DITA-OT Issue #621: Chunking Issues in DITA 1.5.1
content: Converted from [SourceForge issue 3126578](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3126578), submitted by luhall I am attempting to upgrade from DITA1.4.1 to DITA 1.5.1 toolkit and I'm having problems with chunking. There are some significant differences between the way DITA 1.4.1 and DITA 1.5.1 work in this area. In DITA 1.4.1, this is the code we were using (generated from a java script): We then appended our standard product ditamap (essentially a master map, conrefing in sub-maps, including reltables.) to the custom map we created with these chunked contents. This allowed us to add custom content to any page in our standard product documentation, without having to know in advance which pages required custom content. (We have different writers working on these things.) In DITA1.4.1, when we generated XHTML or Eclipse content, the result was a single output file: . content/mytopic.html containing both our standard product content, plus our custom content. In DITA 1.5.1 it seems the new default behavior is to generate a randomly named output file (e.g. Chunk123456.html) and place this file in the topmost directory. However, our system is context sensitive, so I need to be able to predict the name and location of my output file. I've used the copy-to option to get around this, and I've been tweaking some other attributes, but I'm still experiencing problems. Here's the code I'm using in DITA 1.5.1: I moved this code to the end of the map (ie. after the standard product map info) because when it's placed before the standard product map, none of the related links appear in the chunked content. With these changes, we're getting the combined content, with the correct file name, in the correct directory. However, we are experiencing the following problems: 1. The reference to the css files in the mytopic.html file is incorrect. It points to "commonltr.css" when all our non-chunked files point to "../commonltr.css". Fiddling with args.csspath made no difference. It affects the output, but chunked and non-chunked topics continue to be generated differently. 2. Links to the chunked topics are generated as: in TOC: in Related Links: My Topic Non-chunked topics do not have the "#mytopic" in the link. The good news is that the links work. But the bad news is that our build file is riddled with ERRORS, like the following: [xslt] [DOTX006E][ERROR]: Unknown file extension in href: '../content/ovr_crown_masters_sk.html#ovr_crown_masters_sk'. If this is a link to a non-DITA resource, set the format attribute to match the resource (for example, 'txt', 'pdf', or 'html'). If it's a link to a DITA resource, the file extension must be 'dita' or 'xml'. Set the format attribute and specify the format of the file if href link doesn't point to dita topic file. Otherwise, change the file extension name to 'dita' or 'xml'.The location of this problem was at (File = C:\DocToolkit\doc\RELTABLE.ditamap, Element = topicref:2779) We get this error everytime a chunked topic is encountered in a relationship table. I've tried different settings in the format option, as suggested by the error message, but it doesn't make any difference. No matter what I set it to, I get the same error message. Although the errors don't seem to affect the functionality, the long list of errors in the log file makes it very difficult to distinguish if we have any 'real' problems in the build.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3155375](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3155375), submitted by raducoravu

I do not have privileges to reopen bug ID: 3102827.

The problem is the following:
In the org.dita.dost.util.FileUtils class the configuration file is read from:

File configurationFile = new File("lib"+ File.separator + Constants.CONF_PROPERTIES);

This relative path is made absolute to the location from where the ANT process was started which might be quite different from the DITA Open Toolkit directory.
For example when running DITA OT from inside Oxygen XML Editor the ANT process is started in the Oxygen "lib" folder and thus the fix does not work properly.
You probably need some kind of way to specify to the FileUtils class the directory of the DITA OT installation.

title: DITA-OT Issue #632: Navigation titles in temp maps do not retain original markup
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3157880](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3157880), submitted by drmacro

Given this markup in a topic:

<title>Footnote: <ph><fn>This is a footnote</fn></ph></title>

The effective navigation title of the topicref that includes the topic is "Footnote: (1)".

I cannot think of any circumstance when a footnote callout would be appropriate or wanted (or correct) in a navigation title (that is, in a table of contents).

Thus, footnotes within titles should be suppressed when constructing navigation titles, at least by default. It might be useful to provide a parameter to turn footnote processing on in navigation titles if there was any chance somebody might actually want them.

Note that in Publishing applications, especially in STM publishing (journals), footnotes in titles is a hard requirement (which means that the DITA 1.2 refusal to allow fn directly within <title> is bogus, but that's a separate issue).

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3157890](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3157890), submitted by drmacro
This sample of a generated navigation title in a temporary map:
<subsection
 class="+ map/topicref pubmap-d/subsection "
 collection-type="sequence"
 href="chapters/title-with-footnote.xml"
 type="subsection"
 xtrc="subsection:1"
 xtrf="/Users/ekimber/workspace/dita4publishers/sample_data/epub-test/epub-test.ditamap">
 <topicmeta
 class="- map/topicmeta ">
 <navtitle
 class="- topic/navtitle ">Title With Footnote (1)</navtitle>
Notice that the `<ph>` and `<fn>` within the title are not preserved in the generated navigation title.

Navigation titles must retain their markup just like any other markup in the temporary files. I assume this bug is the result of simply applying the older @navtitle processing for use with the new element-based navtitle but that's not correct behavior.

title: DITA-OT Issue #639: Initializer XMLReader without modifying system variables
content:
DITA-OT Issue #639: Initializer XMLReader without modifying system variables
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #639: Initializer XMLReader without modifying system variables
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3165762](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3165762), submitted by [jelovirt](/jelovirt)

Currently XMLReaders are created by first calling StringUtils.initSaxDriver() to set the prefered parser class to system variable org.xml.sax.driver, then creating the parser instance with XMLReaderFactory.createXMLReader(). To change OT into a direction where it could be run in a JVM that also runs other processes, we should not set system variables as other programs may rely on them.

I propose that we change the parser instantiation process so that we add a new method StringUtils.getSaxDriver() that returns the preferred parser class without modifying system variables. Then parser construction is changed to use XMLReaderFactory.createXMLReader(className) method to get the parser instance. The end result will be the same, a preferred parser is used, but no system variables are changed.

title: DITA-OT Issue #646: MapLinksReader should not be namespace aware
content:
DITA-OT Issue #646: MapLinksReader should not be namespace aware
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #646: MapLinksReader should not be namespace aware
content: Issue #646 is closed with labels none. Retrieval signals: error, exception, map, pdf, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #646: MapLinksReader should not be namespace aware
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3189883](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3189883), submitted by raducoravu

This is kind of hard to explain but here is goes:

One of our customers has a DITA specialization which embeds MathML in DITA <foreign> elements.
If such a MathML equation is used in a <shortdesc> the PDF output will fail with the error:

D:\projects\eXml\frameworks\dita\DITA-OT\build_preprocess.xml:281: net.sf.saxon.trans.XPathException: org.xml.sax.SAXParseException: The prefix "m" for element "m:math" is not bound.

This happens because when the MapLinksReader parses the ".../temp/maplinks.unordered" file which contains the small MathML snippet inside it uses a parser which is namespace aware. This means that namespace declaration attributes will no longer be reported on the "startElement" callback but instead will be reported in the "startPrefixMapping" callback which is ignored.
This means that the MapLinksReader will strip prefix-namespace declarations from XML elements which have them declared and thus the resulting XML fragments will not have properly bound prefixes for the MathML namespace for example.

Suggested fix:
Set this property on the reader:
reader.setFeature("http://xml.org/sax/features/namespaces", false);

The idea is that if you use SAX to process XML and split it into fragments then you should be not namespace aware.
This could maybe come handy in other places as well.

title: DITA-OT Issue #654: Topichead not processed the same as title-only topic
content:
DITA-OT Issue #654: Topichead not processed the same as title-only topic
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #654: Topichead not processed the same as title-only topic
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3260746](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3260746), submitted by None

DITA -OT 1.5.2:

Given the following maps:

bookmap:
<!DOCTYPE bookmap PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA BookMap//EN" "bookmap.dtd">
<bookmap>
<chapter href="map-a.ditamap" format="ditamap"/>
</bookmap>

map-a.ditamap:
<!DOCTYPE map PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Map//EN" "map.dtd">
<map title="Title A">
 <topicref href="title-a.xml">
 <topicref href="topics/topic-2"/>
 <topicref href="topics/topic-3"/>
 </topicref>
</map>

Where title-a.xml is a title-only topic.

The DITA-OT applies chapter numbering and chapter title formatting to the title of title-a.xml. This is correct behavior.

Replace the topic reference to the title-only topic with a topichead.

map-a.ditamap:
<map title="Title A">
 <topichead navtitle="Title A">
 <topicref href="topics/topic-2"/>
 <topicref href="topics/topic-3"/>
 </topichead>
</map>

I would expect the DITA-OT to apply chapter numbering and chapter title formatting to the topichead ("Title A"). Instead, the DITA-OT treats the topichead as though it were a topic title and not a chapter title. The PDF process is not treating a "topichead" <chapter> as equivalent to a "topicref" <chapter>.

title: DITA-OT Issue #657: Bad attribute being applied to fo:bookmark-title element
content:
DITA-OT Issue #657: Bad attribute being applied to fo:bookmark-title element
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #657: Bad attribute being applied to fo:bookmark-title element
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3281074](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3281074), submitted by paul_cpwr

One of the purposes of the i18n-postprocess.xsl file is to add the attribute line-height-shift-adjustment="disregard-shifts" to most text fragments. There is a special template that matches fo:bookmark and fo:bookmark-label that does a straight copy and avoid the addition of the line-height-shift-adjustment attribute, which would be illegal on these elements. 

Sometime in 1.5.x development, bookmark processing changed to use the fo:bookmark-title element instead of fo:bookmark-label. This would not be a problem but the line-height-shift-adjustment is being errantly applied to this element. FO validation in XEP 4.19 is more strict and rendering now fails when XEP 4.19 find a line-height-shift-adjustment attribute on a fo:bookmark-title element.

The fix is to edit the i18n-postprocess.xsl file to extend the template for fo:bookmark and fo:bookmark-label to also include fo:bookmark-title as follows:
<xsl:template match="fo:bookmark | fo:bookmark-label | fo:bookmark-title" priority="+10">

title: DITA-OT Issue #658: Fallback to $locale when xml:lang value is wrong format
content:
DITA-OT Issue #658: Fallback to $locale when xml:lang value is wrong format
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #658: Fallback to $locale when xml:lang value is wrong format
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3281108](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3281108), submitted by robertnthomas

fo expects locale to follow a ll-cc pattern where ll is a 2-character language code and cc is a 2-character country code. When populating attribute xml:lang, authors sometimes unwittingly use the 2-character language code but omit the 2-character country code. For example, the will use 'ja' instead of the 'ja-jp' code that fo expects. The fo style-sheet should fail gracefully when this occurs and substitute the locale variable being used for the job (i.e., $locale).

The ODT output transform ends with a "clean-up-out-dir" target that uses wildcards to delete a lot of files. If other files matching these conditions already exist in the output directory, they will be deleted. The toolkit should only delete files that were generated by the current build.

The delete command currently does the following, which will delete extra log and ODT files that already exist in the output directory (along with the list, temp, and properties files).
 <delete failonerror="yes" includeemptydirs="true" dir="${dita.map.output.dir}"
 excludes="**/*.list, **/*.log, **/*.temp, **/*.properties, **/*.odt">
</delete>

I have a topic in a sub-directory "one/two/", which references an image. The image reference uses a relative path.
In the map, I reference a second (nested) topic, in the sub-directory "one/two/three/", which also references the image.
In the map, I use chunk="to-content" on the parent topic; all nested topics are pulled in for the rendered XHTML file.

title: DITA-OT Issue #661: Conref code improperly generalizes map domain elements

title: DITA-OT Issue #661: Conref code improperly generalizes map domain elements
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3288639](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3288639), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The conrefImpl.xsl file contains code to generalize domain elements, when they are not supported by the new context.

The code iterates over the class attribute, to find the most specialized module that is valid. It is supposed to stop when the module reached is "topic" or "map". 

The code is supposed to check if the $testModule is 'topic' or 'map' -- instead, it does this for 'topic', but uses the wrong variable for 'map'. 
 <xsl:when test="$testModule='topic' or $testElement='map'"><xsl:value-of select="$testElement"/>/xsl:when

This results in the template returning an empty string as the name of the generalized map element. The code (on line 1244) should be
 <xsl:when test="$testModule='topic' or $testModule='map'"><xsl:value-of select="$testElement"/>/xsl:when

title: DITA-OT Issue #671: Conref Push order of validation
content:
DITA-OT Issue #671: Conref Push order of validation
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #671: Conref Push order of validation
content: Issue #671 is closed with labels none. Retrieval signals: conref, map, validation, publishing.

title: DITA-OT Issue #671: Conref Push order of validation
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3344142](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3344142), submitted by htrent

We discovered a potential bug in the DITA OT processing of conref push after or before. What we found is that the validation of topics/maps/etc is done before conref push is compiled into the stage1.xml which means that content that is added via conref pushbefore or pushafter is not validated after the content is placed. This opens the possibility of creating a stage1.xml file that is not valid according to the DTIA standard, but can still be processed by the XSLT. The stage1.xml file is moved through the publishing pipeline using the XSLT, but at this point in the processing no more DITA validation occurs.

What can potentially happen is… 
If topic A (the target topic) contains a step with an id and topic B contains a step that will be pushed into the location of the step in topic A, the validation occurs before the conref push.

The target content in Topic A is... 
<step id=”topicA_ID”><cmd>Step content being replaced</cmd></step> 

The pushed content in Topic B is…
<step id=”topicB_ID” conaction=”pushafter”>Content being pushed</step>

The result is
1.Step content being replaced.
2.Content being pushed.

In this example, since the conref push after is going from like element to like element nothing appears to be incorrect.

HOWEVER…IF

The target content in Topic A is... 
<step id=”topicA_ID”><cmd>Step content being replaced</cmd></step> 

The pushed content in Topic B is…
<step><cmd id=”topicB_ID” conaction=”pushafter”> Content being pushed </cmd> </step>

The result is
1.Step content being replaced.
Content being pushed.

The key point to notice here is that the actual content of the Topic B step/cmd is making it into the final document, but without any style…

This is because the stage1.xml file that is being generated during the push after looks like…

<step id=”topicA_ID”>
 <cmd>Step content being replaced</cmd>
 <step>
 <cmd id=”topicB_ID” conaction=”pushafter”> Content being pushed </cmd>
 </step>
</step> 

Notice that the step is now nested in the step. The style sheet only looks for steps as siblings and not steps as nested elements. The style sheet will process a substep in a step, but since the content is brought in as a step, the proper style is not applied.

SO…

This resolves the issue and inconsistencies we are seeing in the conref pushafter/pushbefore example. The question becomes, did the architecture of conref pushafter and pushbefore anticipate authors to break the basic rules of conrefing like to like elements. 

If the architecture is designed to allow invalid content to be pushed before or after an element, then conref pushafter/pushbefore is behaving correctly. However, if the architecture is designed to ensure valid DITA after a conref pushafter/pushbefore then we have found a bug in the DITA OT processing.

One point to note is this DOES NOT discredit the idea that I might want to conref pushafter an <info> element containing a note after a <cmd>.

This example creates valid DITA in the stage1.xml file

The target content in Topic A is... 
<step><cmd id=”topicA_ID”>Step content being replaced</cmd></step> 

The pushed content in Topic B is…
<info id=”topicB_ID” ><note type=”note” conaction=”pushafter”> Content being pushed </cmd> </step>

The result is
1.Step content being replaced.
NOTE: Content being pushed.

 [xslt] [DOTJ021E][ERROR] Failed to get the image file specified 'D:\projects\eXml\samples\dita\flowers\out\temp\images\Chrysanthemums.jpg' in ODT generation Check whether the image exists and copied to output directory before the final step of ODT generation.
