title: DITA-OT Issue #678: Product name repeated hundreds of times in PDF
content:
DITA-OT Issue #678: Product name repeated hundreds of times in PDF
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #678: Product name repeated hundreds of times in PDF
content: Issue #678 is closed with labels bug. Retrieval signals: error, map, pdf, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #678: Product name repeated hundreds of times in PDF
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3386590](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3386590), submitted by raducoravu
There are differences in processing XSLT stylesheets with version 2.0 or 1.0 even if they are not using any version 2.0 extensions. This is a quote from: http://www.w3.org/TR/2003/WD-xpath20-20031112/#id-backwards-compatibility
When a node-set containing more than one node is supplied as an argument to a function or operator that expects a single node or value, the rule that all nodes after the first are discarded no longer applies. Instead, a type error occurs if there is more than one node. The XPath 1.0 behavior can always be restored by using the predicate [1] to explicitly select the first node in the node-set.

title: DITA-OT Issue #678: Product name repeated hundreds of times in PDF
content:
For example in the DITA-OT/demo/fo/xsl/fo/root-processing.xsl stylesheet there are variables:

<xsl:variable name="mapProdname" select="/*/opentopic:map//*[contains(@class, '
 topic/prodname ')]"/>
<xsl:variable name="bkinfoProdname" select="/*/*[contains(@class, ' bkinfo/bkinfo
 ')]//*[contains(@class, ' topic/prodname ')]"/>

Processed with xslt 1.0 compatibility mode the select returned only one node (even if multiple matched the expression).
While processed with xslt 2.0 such expressions might return more than one node. 

Our usermanual has a <prodname> specified in the bookmap and several chapters. When such XPath expressions are run on the merged DITAMAP from the temporary folder they match hundreds of nodes in the XML document creating a PDF file with lots of product names repeated in the header part.

So the XPath expressions must be rewritten like:

 <xsl:variable name="mapProdname" select="/*/opentopic:map//*[contains(@class, '
 topic/prodname ')][1]"/>
 <xsl:variable name="bkinfoProdname" select="/*/*[contains(@class, ' bkinfo/bkinfo
 ')]//*[contains(@class, ' topic/prodname ')][1]"/>

in order to force the selection of the first match also in XPath 2.0.

This might be the case for other XPath expressions in the DITA stylesheets which would need the extra "[1]" to be appended to them.

The tocjs plug-in comes with a sample Ant build file called buildsample.xml.

title: DITA-OT Issue #683: TocJS needs cleanup for several minor bugs
content:
DITA-OT Issue #683: TocJS needs cleanup for several minor bugs
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #683: TocJS needs cleanup for several minor bugs
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3394000](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3394000), submitted by [robander](/robander)

After playing with TocJS output, I found several items that should be fixed; some are just cleanup, some are fixes. I've got a general fix that covers these items.
In topicref.xsl:
1. Several tests should use class attributes instead of element names (such as topicmeta/navtitle)
2. Edge case: if a topicref / topichead with no href contains both a navtitle attribute and a navtitle element, the resulting TOC duplicates the entire branch (one heading with @navtitle, one heading with <navtitle>)
3. Topicref elements with no @href or title (such as <topicgroup) currently drop all nested topics from the TOC
4. If @toc=no on a topicref, but nested elements use @toc=yes, the output should match other XHTML based outputs

In tocjs.xsl there is a rule for elements with @class containing "map/topicgroup". This will never match anything because the class is wrong, and it is better handled with the fix mentioned above, so I've removed the rule.

The topichead.xsl file is no longer used by the default processing, because topicref.xsl contains rules for any topicref based element with headings and no @href. I've placed a comment in the top of that file to indicate it is no longer used by default.

Last, I've got a few small tweaks for the sample documentation to cover these and related updates.

title: DITA-OT Issue #687: Relcolspec with <title> does not generate link group headers
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3397495](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3397495), submitted by drmacro

Given a reltable like this:

 <reltable
 title="Exam requirements to techniques">
 <relheader>
 <relcolspec
 type="topic">
 <title>Belt Examination Requirements</title>
 </relcolspec>
 <relcolspec
 type="topic">
 <title>Technique Description</title>
 </relcolspec>
 </relheader>
 <relrow>
 <relcell>
 <topicref
 href="topics/rokyu-requirements.dita"/>
 </relcell>
 <relcell>
 <topicref
 href="topics/munetsuki-kotegaeshi.dita"/>
 <topicref
 href="topics/shomenuchi-ikkyo.dita"/>
 <topicref
 href="topics/shomenuchi-iriminage.dita"/>
 </relcell>
 </relrow>
 </reltable>

The related links are generated by the link group heading remains "Related links", not the titles from the relcol spec.

The 1.2 spec is clear that the title should be used as the grouping title if specified:

"Also
 beginning with DITA 1.2, if you add a <title> element to the <relcolspec>
 element, the content of the <title> element is used as the label
 for the related links that are defined and generated by the column."

title: DITA-OT Issue #694: wrong image output dir if using generate.copy.outer=2
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #694: wrong image output dir if using generate.copy.outer=2
content: Issue #694 is closed with labels bug. Retrieval signals: map, html, dita-ot, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #694: wrong image output dir if using generate.copy.outer=2
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3402165](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3402165), submitted by talex24

We use a decentralized DITA setup with main ditamap not in the root directory.
Many DITA files have links to images located in the corresponding 'img'
subdirectories (see a sample simplified setup below).
We have to use the setting generate.copy.outer=2 to generate complete (XHTML) documentation.

PROBLEM: All image links in the resulting HTML files are broken because all image files get 
copied to directories one level below the intended ones. 
(So the links in the HTML files are right, but the image files are misplaced). 
This problem is also reproducible with DITA-OT 1.5.2 and 1.5.3

PROBLEM INVESTIGATION: If using setting generate.copy.outer=2 DITA-OT tries 
to find out the first common root directory to all involved dirs with DITA files 
and sets variable $uplevels accordingly (relatively to main ditamap.) 
All generated file lists (image files also) are addressed relatively
to the common root directory. The target for XSLT transformations is then $output.dir/$uplevels.
But the target directory for 'copy-image' Ant target in build_preprocess_template.xml is simply $output_dir 
and this is why image files get copied to wrong locations.

POSSIBLE SOLUTION: The output dir for Ant target 'copy-image' should be ${output.dir}/${uplevels}
(We've locally modified the corresponding Ant file and this resolved the issue.)
### 

Diff of original and modified build_preprocess_template.xml:
469c469

title: DITA-OT Issue #694: wrong image output dir if using generate.copy.outer=2
content:
< <copy todir="${output.dir}">
> ```
> <copy todir="${output.dir}/${uplevels}">
> ```
> ### 

Sample Setup:
- workspace/doc/
 - doc.ditamap
 - main.html
 - generalA/topicA.dita
 - generalA/img/imageA.png
- workspace/project1/
 - src/dita/topicB.dita
 - src/dita/img/imageB.png

title: DITA-OT Issue #695: Setting of clean_temp is backwards
content:
DITA-OT Issue #695: Setting of clean_temp is backwards
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #695: Setting of clean_temp is backwards
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3404049](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3404049), submitted by drmacro

This code in build_init.xml:

 <condition property="clean_temp">
 <and>
 <isset property="clean.temp" />
 <equals arg1="${clean.temp}" arg2="no" casesensitive="false" />
 </and>
 </condition>

Sets clean_temp to "true" if clean.temp = "no", which is clearly wrong.

The check should either be for a value of "yes" or a not condition on "no", which probably better, e.g.:

 <condition property="clean_temp">
 <and>
 <isset property="clean.temp" />
 <not>
 <equals arg1="${clean.temp}" arg2="no" casesensitive="false" />
 </not>
 </and>
 </condition>

title: DITA-OT Issue #698: Custom profiling issue
content:
DITA-OT Issue #698: Custom profiling issue
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #698: Custom profiling issue
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3406357](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3406357), submitted by awschwartz

PROBLEM: We have encountered a bug when trying to profile using custom attributes in a Map.

In the DebugAndFilterModule class, if a Map is the first file removed from the LinkedList<String> parseList, which is iterated over starting at line 279, custom profiling attributes are not loaded when the DitaWriter writes it out, so the content won't get filtered out. If a topic is first, the custom attributes get loaded and are used. The point of "failure" is in the DitaWriter, when it calls FilterUtils.needExclude(atts, props) around line 1103, props doesn't contain the custom attributes if a Topic hasn't yet been encountered. We see that props is only set to a value on line 1079, which can only be reached if the class attribute is topic/topic.

POSSIBLE SOLUTIONS: Currently, I've implemented a check to see if a ditamap is encountered first in the DebugAndFilterModule's while loop (line 279); if it is, we re-insert it using parseList.addFirst(filename), then continue (there's a safety valve in there as well to make sure the list doesn't just contain maps). This is just a workaround, but it works.

A possibly better solution: I probably don't have a good enough grasp of the DitaWriter's profiling logic, but couldn't the DitaWriter (around line 1050) check for domains and load the props more aggressively, and not just if it encounters a topic/topic class attribute?

REPRODUCING: A quick example may give a better picture of the issue. Given a ditaval file set to exclude everything by default:

<val>
 <prop action="exclude"/>
</val> 

We have to add a custom attribute for profiling, say "hardware-platform", so in our bookmap named radam.ditamap, we'll add a single chapter (though this can happen with multiple chapters) with a hardware-platform prop:

...
 <chapter scope="local" format="dita" href="Generic.xml" navtitle="Generic Topic" hardware-platform="ios-xr-platform">
 <topicref scope="local" format="ditamap" href="map.ditamap" navtitle="DITA Map"></topicref>
 </chapter>
...

We would expect a pretty empty PDF as a result, but run with the out-of-the-box code, profiling does not occur on the bookmap. When we get into the DebugAndFilterModule execution, the output to the log is:

DebugAndFilterModule.execute(): Starting...
DebugAndFilterModule.execute(): Handling file adam.ditamap...
DebugAndFilterModule.execute(): Handling file map.ditamap...
DebugAndFilterModule.execute(): Handling file Concept.xml...
DebugAndFilterModule.execute(): Handling file Generic.xml...

We see that adam.ditamap is the first file processed here, and profiling with our custom attributes doesn’t happen at all. 

Let's say we add in a new topic file and call it c1.xml, and its hashcode value makes it last in the Set that backs these values (the ditaSet variable in GenMapAndTopicListModule, if I'm not mistaken, becomes the value the ListReader will grab on line 231 of DebugAndFilterModule). This will trigger profiling for the bookmap, because the props are loaded into the DitaWriter when it hits c1.xml first:

DebugAndFilterModule.execute(): Starting...
DebugAndFilterModule.execute(): Handling file c1.xml...
DebugAndFilterModule.execute(): Handling file adam.ditamap...
DebugAndFilterModule.execute(): Handling file map.ditamap...
DebugAndFilterModule.execute(): Handling file Concept.xml...
DebugAndFilterModule.execute(): Handling file Generic.xml...

Voila, we'll get a mostly empty PDF.

title: DITA-OT Issue #699: Not so meaningful messages given by ImgUtils
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3411767](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3411767), submitted by raducoravu

When transforming a DITA Map to EPUB I obtained errors like this in the console:

[xslt] [DOTJ023E][ERROR] Failed to get the specified image file '../images/Iris_sanguinea.jpg' for RTF generation. Check whether the image exists and was copied to output directory before the final step of RTF generation.
[xslt] javax.imageio.IIOException: Can't read input file!
[xslt] [DOTJ021E][ERROR] Failed to get the image file specified '../images/Iris_sanguinea.jpg' in ODT generation Check whether the image exists and copied to output directory before the final step of ODT generation.

Actually the error messages are too specific, for example the error code DOTJ023E can be given both on this method (connected with RTF):

org.dita.dost.util.ImgUtils.getBASE64(String, String)

and on this method (which is more generic, without connection to RTF):

org.dita.dost.util.ImgUtils.getHeight(String, String)

The same goes for the other error code (DOTJ021E).
Probably more error codes should be given in such generic cases as when the width and height of images are computed.

title: DITA-OT Issue #705: Scale computation for XHTML uncorrectly looks up images
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3418953](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3418953), submitted by raducoravu

In the stylesheet:

DITA-OT/xsl/xslhtml/dita2htmlImpl.xsl

there is a template called:

<xsl:template match="*[contains(@class,' topic/image ')]/@scale">

The template relies on the fact that the chosen output directory is located exactly inside the folder where the transformed DITA Map is located.

So if you have images referenced in DITA content using the @scale attribute and the "output.dir" is set to a fixed location on the harddrive, the template will complain that it cannot find the images (and thus cannot correctly compute the width and height) like:

 [DOTJ023E][ERROR] Failed to get the specified image file 'C:\Users\radu_coravu\Desktop/out3../images/Chrysanthemums.jpg' for RTF generation. Check whether the image exists and was copied to output directory before the final step of RTF generation.

A while ago I've added another bug that the error message is confusing.

content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #715: Relative CSS paths incorrectly computed for @copy-of
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3431798](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3431798), submitted by raducoravu

If the DITA Map referenced a topic like:

<topicref href="tasks/organizing.xml" copy-to="newFileName.xml"/>

and then we publish to XHTML then in the temp directory the "newFileName.xml" file will contain the following header:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?><?workdir /D:\projects\eXml\samples\dita\garage\temp\tasks?><?path2project ..\?>

We can see that both the "workdir" and the "path2project" PIs have been computed for the original task location which is inside the "tasks" directory.
This leads to problems in the XSLT stylesheets which make use of these PIs to reference custom user CSS stylesheets for example.
In my opinion both PIs should have been computed for the copied reference and not for the original location.

A workaround for the situation is to specify the reference like this:

<topicref href="tasks/organizing.xml" copy-to="tasks/newFileName.xml"/>

title: DITA-OT Issue #716: Task example title processing incorrect for PDF
content:
DITA-OT Issue #716: Task example title processing incorrect for PDF
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #716: Task example title processing incorrect for PDF
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3432267](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3432267), submitted by julio_vazquez

The current example processing has a number of problems with processing titles for this section;
1) Titles are within the bounding box for the example. The titles should be external to the box.
2) If a title is supplied within <example> that title should replace the generated title, not added on a separate line. (This should be true of all titles supplied for any section that currently has generated titles.)
3) The generated example title uses attribute set section.title while a supplied title uses attribute set example.title. Both titles should use the same attribute set so that customization is simplified.

title: DITA-OT Issue #721: Bug in handling of longdescref

title: DITA-OT Issue #721: Bug in handling of longdescref
content: Converted from [SourceForge issue 3447732](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3447732), submitted by tmorales2000 DITA-OT does not correctly resolve either the longdescref[@href] attribute or the @longdescref attribute. Create a topic with a text description in it. Now reference this topic, first with , then with . Make sure your topic has the extension .dita. Building xhtml with DITA-OT causes the resulting HTML (with the images) to have @longdesc attributes pointing to a file with a .dita extension and not the desired .html extension. There is a file in the output directory containing the text description with a .html extension. The file is being correctly copied to the temp directory (preprocess) and is being transformed to xhtml. The problem happens early in the preprocess: while in the temp directory, href references to topics should be fixed to have .xml extensions (to match the copied files). However our longdescref's still try to reference the .dita extension. The code that fixes href's isn't accounting for either longdescref[@href] or @longdescref.

title: DITA-OT Issue #722: Revisions on <plentry> use wrong image for nested <pd>
content:
DITA-OT Issue #722: Revisions on <plentry> use wrong image for nested <pd>
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #722: Revisions on <plentry> use wrong image for nested <pd>
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3451621](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3451621), submitted by [robander](/robander)

Revision flags on <dlentry> or <plentry> result in the XHTML flags appearing for nested terms and for nested definitions. This is done so the image tags remain in context (they cannot be placed on a single wrapper around the dlentry and plentry). 

When processing the <dd> or <pd>, the XSLT calls a template to process flags based on the parent. However, by default, it passes in flag rules for the current element rather than for the parent. This means that if the DITAVAL file overrides start or end graphics on the parent revision, the default images are still used for the <dd> or <pd>.

title: DITA-OT Issue #725: Deprecated property breaks Plus plugins
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3455589](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3455589), submitted by shwordsmiths

Found in 1.5.4.M7, although there's no option for that in the Group menu.

At some point, the code that set the property index.ext.param.encoding (i.e., check for args.dita.locale and then set index.ext.param.encoding to match) was apparently removed from build_init.xml. That broke a couple of the Plus plugins that call index.ext.param.encoding. In both plugins, the fix seems to be to remove index.ext.param.encoding and directly call args.dita.locale instead:

plus-plugins\com.moldflow.dita.plus-transtype-eclipsehelp\build_plus-transtype-eclipsehelp_template.xml
plus-plugins\com.moldflow.dita.plus-transtype-htmlhelp\build_plus-transtype-htmlhelp_template.xml

Replace 

${index.ext.param.encoding}

with

encoding=${args.dita.locale}

I've done it locally and it seems to work okay.

title: DITA-OT Issue #727: v 1.5.4 fails to create PDF with external topic ref
content:
Because the referenced topic is outside the DITA Map Directory, the DITA OT tries to create the PDF file in a folder structure like this:

...\out\map\main.pdf

This is the behavior which the DITA OT has had for many versions.
The problem is that using DITA OT 1.5.4, the directory "out/map" does no longer exist (probably in older versions it was automatically created when the topic.fo was copied there).
So the FOP task fails because the directory where it should place the PDF is not created.

One proposed fix in this build file:
DITA-OT/demo/fo/build_fop.xml 

after this condition is set:

 <condition property="outputFile" value="${dita.map.output.dir}/${outputFile.base}${xsl.formatter.ext}">
 <not><isset property="outputFile"/></not>
 </condition>

to explicitly create the output directory:

<mkdir dir="${dita.map.output.dir}"/>

I am looking for a problem in which the DITA OT failed to delete a certain file at some Java stage and it might be possible that an output stream to that file is not closed in a previous stage.

I looked for all occurrences of FileOutputStream in the dost.jar sources and in most places the output stream seems to be properly closed (on finally statements).
Here are some places where there might arise problems, in case this might help:
1. "org/dita/dost/util/ConvertLang.java" does not close the output streams in a "finally" statement.
2. "dita/dost/module/TopicMergeModule.java" contains some code like:
The file output stream will not get closed by Saxon because the convention is that the instantiator of an output stream is responsible of closing it.
3. "org/dita/dost/platform/FileGenerator.java" has some code like:
fileOutput = new FileOutputStream(outputFile);
 output = new OutputStreamWriter(fileOutput, UTF8);
 ....
 fileOutput.close();
In fact the "output" should be closed as it will also close the fileOutput 4. "org/dita/dost/util/DelayConrefUtils.java" has code like:

title: DITA-OT Issue #754: Check all places where output streams are used in dost.jar
content:
which leads to a similar problem with (2) 5. The files: - org/dita/dost/writer/DitaIndexWriter.java - org/dita/dost/writer/DitaMapMetaWriter.java - org/dita/dost/writer/DitaWriter.java - org/dita/dost/writer/KeyrefPaser.java

title: DITA-OT Issue #773: FO simpletable enhancements and fixed
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #773: FO simpletable enhancements and fixed
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1164321](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1164321), submitted by [jelovirt](/jelovirt)

Fixes:

Using proportional-column-width() required fixed table
lay-out, thus added inline-progression-dimension="100%"
and table-layout="fixed"

Enhancements:

Removed redundant fo:block wrapper to fo:table.

Multiple cases of
 <xsl:param name="...">
 <xsl:value-of select="..."/>
 /xsl:param
turned to 
 <xsl:param name="..." select="..."/>
as passing RTFs instead of a string/number when
string/number values is intended is the Wrong Way and
is a performance hit.

$relcolwidth of find-total-table-width template was
changed from variable to parameter for easier
extendability, e.g. when no @relcolwidth is not set,
overriding template could use the default value of "1*
1\* 1\* ...".

Attribute-sets were added in favor of setting
attributes in LREs. This allowed greater reuse as this
way extending stylesheets to not have to override
templates just to change formatting related attributes.

Changed "@relcolwidth and not(@relcolwidth='')" tests
at various levels to "not($totalwidth = 0)"

Changed "not(@relcolwidth='')" to
"normalize-space(@relcolwidth)" as users make mistakes
with whitespace.

title: DITA-OT Issue #774: FO hyperlinks and FOP-generated PDF bookmarks
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1165068](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1165068), submitted by grahan

Patches to various XSLT stylesheets (see "Details") to:
- Create bookmarks in PDFs generated by Apache FOP
- Convert some xref elements into active hyperlinks

So far, only tested against the demo.langref.pdf target. 
(See PDF in attached zip.)

Details:

Bookmarks:

xsl/topicmerge.xsl
If the root element of the topic does not contain an id 
attribute, then generate one.
Later, we will use these id attributes as anchors for PDF 
bookmarks.

xsl/dita2fo-shell.xsl
Use the id attribute of the bkinfo element as an anchor 
for a PDF bookmark to the cover page.

Added template that uses fop extension "outline" 
element to create PDF bookmarks for topic titles (or 
navtitles).

xsl/xslfo/dita2fo-titles.xsl
xsl/xslfo/topic2foImpl.xsl
Problem: The original topic2foImpl.xsl was inserting 
anchors in a location that was not always on the same 
page as the topic.
(If the topic title started a new page, then the anchor 
was always on the previous page.)

Solution: Move the anchor to the block in 
topic2folmpl.xsl that contains the title text.

Hyperlinks:

xsl/xslfo/dita2fo-links.xsl
Where possible, convert xref elements into active 
hyperlinks. More work to be done here. Related links 
code not touched.

title: DITA-OT Issue #779: Files in temp directory not deleted before build
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1252441](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1252441), submitted by gershonj

Files that have been removed from the source XML 
directory remain in the temp directory. This results in 
old files being included in the DITAMAP and output. 
Could be that the problem is that existing files are not 
overwritten in the temp directory. In any case, adding a 
target that deletes and then recreates the temp folder 
resolved the issue.

As you can see from my modified build.xml, I've added 
a new target named clean.temp, which should be called 
by the book's init target (in my case, it's called by the 
target named composia.ref.init).

To test the current bug (without my fix), simply remove 
a topic from the DITAMAP and remove or rename the 
topic XML file, then republish. The old DITAMAP is used.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1253783](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1253783), submitted by debbiep-sf

The attached patch makes dita2fo-links behave correctly
when there are hyperlinks in topic/xref elements which
refer to topics outside their own directory.

The original code said:
select="document(@href,/)/*/@id", which failed if @href
contained a relative path such as "../otherdir/foo". 
Now these references call a new xslt template,
relative-document-id, which builds the absolute path
from the @xtrf attribute which maplink.xsl had put in.

There may be a cleaner way of doing this by reusing
code that does a similar thing from conref.xsl. I feel
a bit dirty using @xtrf for this purpose.

title: DITA-OT Issue #784: Filtering only supports the 4 Ditabase attributes

title: DITA-OT Issue #784: Filtering only supports the 4 Ditabase attributes
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1325244](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1325244), submitted by mgannon

The code for filtering using the ditaval file, only
filters based on the 4 ditabase attributes (audience,
platform, product, otherprops). It should really filter
based on the attributes that are set in the ditaval
file. This would mean that any specializations would be
able to do filtering based on any attributes in their
dtd and not rely only on the 4 attributes mentioned above.

In the new code, for each element, it checks every
attribute of that element to see if it has been defined
in the ditaval file, and if so, what filtering options
have been set for that attribute. It then
excludes/includes accordingly.

The two methods changed were needExclude() and
checkExclude().

title: DITA-OT Issue #785: Make ${basedir} mine
content:
DITA-OT Issue #785: Make ${basedir} mine
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #785: Make ${basedir} mine
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1326450](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1326450), submitted by debbiep-sf

DITA-OT should not require the ant project base
directory to be the build-system root. I should be
free to specify whatever base directory I need.

When I build a document, the build system tree
(conductor.xml and friends) and my document root
(foo.ditamap and the topics it refers to) are not
necessarily near each other. If DITA-OT requires that
${basedir} be the directory that contains conductor.xml
then I must either anchor my document root at a known
place from this, or use an absolute path for the
document root. I end up having lines like this in
build.xml:
 <param name="args.input"
value="${basedir}/../mpshelp.ditamap"/>
 <param name="output.dir" value="${basedir}/../out"/>

This patch (applied to 1.1.1) allows an ant project
file to specify its own basedir. It need only specify
the build system's location in the <import> line that
brings in conductor.xml.

Here is an example build.xml showing the cleaner look
<project name="mpshelp" default="all" basedir=".">
 <import file="DITA-OT1.1.1/conductor.xml"/>
 <target name="htmlhelp-unix">
 <antcall target="init">
 <param name="transtype" value="htmlhelp"/>
 <param name="args.input" value="mpshelp.ditamap"/>
 <param name="output.dir" value="out"/>
 </antcall>
 </target>
</project>

All relative paths. Much more freedom for me to put my
files where other needs dictate.

Backward compatibility: Existing ant projects which set
their project basedir to the build system root will not
notice anything different after this patch.

I got the idea from these instructions on how to use
<import>:
http://ant.apache.org/manual/CoreTasks/import.html

title: DITA-OT Issue #786: FOP task userconfig file
content:
DITA-OT Issue #786: FOP task userconfig file
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #786: FOP task userconfig file
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1328264](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1328264), submitted by debbiep-sf

The Ant <fop> task has an optional
userconfig="filename" attribute which allows you to
specify a user configuration file to FOP at run-time. 
This is essential if you want to embed fonts in the PDF
output, say, for doing foreign-language text, or if
your company has a corporate font for all documentation.

userconfig can't be specified using <param>; it can
only be specified as an attribute. This means I've had
to split the dita.fo2pdf target into a "userconfig" and
a "nouserconfig" version, differing on whether the
attribute is specified, and put conditions onto each. 
This is what's in the patch (based on DITA-OT 1.1.1).

After patching: user targets that define the
args.fo.userconfig parameter as a filename will pass
the filename on to FOP. Targets which do not define
the parameter will run as before.

title: DITA-OT Issue #787: Wildcard handling for filtering
content:
DITA-OT Issue #787: Wildcard handling for filtering
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #787: Wildcard handling for filtering
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1363426](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1363426), submitted by debbiep-sf

Implements proposal for wildcards in ditaval files as
seen at
http://lists.oasis-open.org/archives/dita-comment/200511/msg00000.html
and submitted to TC for consideration in DITA 1.1.

Short version:
1. It is an error to encounter a filtering property in
 a DITA source file if there is no rule that matches it
 in the ditaval file. (Default in DITA-OT to 1.1.2 is
 to ignore it; Default in DITA-OT 1.2 is to include it.)
2. val="xxx" in ditaval files is a Java regular
 expression. Matched like /^xxx$/ against property values.
3. optional priority="xxx" on each ditaval <prop>
 element, where xxx is a floating-point number. 
 Higher-priority match rules always take precedence. 
 Ambiguous priorities signal an error. If omitted,
 reasonable defaults are used, based on whether the
 action is "include" or "exclude" (include has higher
 priority), and whether the pattern contains wildcards
 (wildcards are lower priority).

title: DITA-OT Issue #788: tweaks to docbook/topic2db.xsl

title: DITA-OT Issue #788: tweaks to docbook/topic2db.xsl
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1385636](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1385636), submitted by efh

When DITA itemgroup contains textual content, the
current output is invalid for DocBook. The following
rule for itemgroup seems to solve the problem.

<xsl:template match="*[contains(@class,'
topic/itemgroup ')]">
 <xsl:variable name="element" select="local-name(.)"/>
 <xsl:variable name="id" select="concat('elem',
generate-id())"/>
 <xsl:call-template name="deflateElementStart">
 <xsl:with-param name="id" select="$id"/>
 <xsl:with-param name="element" select="$element"/>
 <xsl:with-param name="parentID" select="''"/>
 /xsl:call-template
 <xsl:call-template name="makeBlock"/>
 <xsl:call-template name="deflateElementEnd">
 <xsl:with-param name="id" select="$id"/>
 <xsl:with-param name="element" select="$element"/>
 /xsl:call-template
/xsl:template

The current rule for related links creates a bullet
list that, while valid for DocBook, looks like an error
when formatted with DocBook rules. The following rule
adds an identifying title so the related links have a
stated relationship to the rest of the text:

<xsl:template match="*[contains(@class,'
topic/related-links ')]">
 <itemizedlist>
 <title>Related links</title>
 xsl:apply-templates/
 </itemizedlist>
/xsl:template

title: DITA-OT Issue #795: map2hhp [FILES] include
content:
DITA-OT Issue #795: map2hhp [FILES] include
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #795: map2hhp [FILES] include
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1460441](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1460441), submitted by debbiep-sf

Sometimes when compiling Windows HTML Help you need to
explicitly add some files to the [FILES] section in
foo.hhp. For example, there might be a CSS file that
references an image to tile for a background. Such
files aren't automatically included in the CHM by
Windows HTML Help compiler.

This patch adds a HELPFILES parameter to map2hhp.xsl. 
If set to "includelist" then the following line is
added to the output .hhp file in the [FILES] section:
 #include includelist

It is left up to the supporting ant/Java build code to
put the list of files to copy into includelist, and to
put the referenced files there, before invoking the
HTML Help compiler.

Example of use (modified part of dita.map.htmlhelp):
 <xslt processor="trax"
 basedir="${dita.temp.dir}"
 destdir="${output.dir}"
 includes="${user.input.file}"
 extension=".hhp"

style="${dita.script.dir}${file.separator}map2hhp.xsl">
 <param name="DITAEXT" expression="${dita.ext}"
if="dita.ext"/>
 <param name="OUTEXT" expression="${out.ext}"
if="out.ext"/>
 <param name="HHCNAME"
expression="${dita.map.filename.root}.hhc"/>
 <param name="HELPFILES"
expression="includefilelist"/>
 </xslt>
 <copy

file="${build.resource.root}${file.separator}background${file.separator}mfstyle.jpg"
 todir="${output.dir}${file.separator}background"/>
 <echo
file="${output.dir}${file.separator}includefilelist">background${file.separator}mfstyle.jpg
</echo>

title: DITA-OT Issue #796: CSS for ditamap-to-HTML TOC
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1481586](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1481586), submitted by debbiep-sf

map2htmtoc.xsl is not aware of CSS, so sometimes it
looks ugly.

This patch (on DITA-OT 1.2) provides basic stylesheet
support for map2htmtoc:
- Honours user stylesheet variables $args.css and
 $args.csspath, just like topic-to-html transform.
- Puts optional class attribute $args.xhtml.toc.class
 on <body> of resulting HTML, so CSS can detect ToC and
 style it independently of topics.
- Calls empty but overridable templates gen-user-head,
 gen-user-scripts, gen-user-styles so that plugins can
 override default behaviour in a shell.
- Externalizes contenttarget XSLT parameter as
 $args.xhtml.contenttarget, so target="contentwin" can
 be disabled from ant build file if desired.

Missing, requires updates to map DTD:
- generic @outputclass recognition for maps (map.dtd
 does not define outputclass attribute)
- commonltr or commonrtl CSS linking (map does not
 define xml:lang attribute).

title: DITA-OT Issue #807: Refactor of dita2htmlImpl.xsl to improve overrides
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1874104](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1874104), submitted by [robander](/robander)

This patch refactors dita2htmlImpl.xsl (pulled from the 1.4.1 branch). It makes the following changes:
- All messages are now processed with modes so that overrides can easily catch and modify or remove a message.
- The generateCssLinks template is refactored into three distinct calls, to enable specialized topics to add a specific CSS file. 1) Add default CSS, 2) Add specialized CSS, and 3) Add user CSS. A specialized topic can catch #2 and add a CSS file that is specific to that specialization.
- Several named templates were modified to use modes. The old calls to named templates are not yet modified, so that existing overrides of the named templates will continue to work (the named calls could be removed at some point in the future). Using modes makes it possible to override processing for specific specialized elements, rather than having to override processing for every element. The following named templates are now available as moded templates:
 sect-heading
 gen-topic
 dotable
 doentry
 topic.sthead_stentry
 topic.strow_stentry
 place-tbl-lbl
 place-fig-lbl
 chapter-setup
 setTopicLanguage
 chapterHead
 generateDefaultCopyright
 generateDefaultMeta
 generateChapterTitle
 chapterBody
 generateCssLinks

Implements feature request [ 1859421 ] Add plug-in support for string resource-files (https://sourceforge.net/tracker/index.php?func=detail&aid=1859421&group_id=132728&atid=725077)

What this patch does:
- Introduces a new plugin extension point "dita.xsl.strings". Plugins register a strings.xml file with a line in their plugin.xml: <feature extension="dita.xsl.strings" value="path-to/strings.xml" type="file"/>
- When integrated, xsl/common/allstrings.xml is created, containing a list of all strings.xml files, including the standard DITA-OT one in xsl/common.
- Alters the getString template so that it searches all files named in allstrings.xml, and returns any string from any file that matches the requested string name.

By itself, the patch does not affect basic DITA-OT behaviour. No transformation XSLT needs to be changed.

I don't think that this reliably allows a plugin to override a string for an existing DITA-OT string. Doing so would be Hard with XSLT 1.0, but possible in XSLT 2.0.

I've tested this with my own plugin and it works for me. (Note: Saxon 8.x and 9.x before 9.0.0.3 have a bug which breaks this patch. Saxon 6.5.5 has no such problem.)

title: DITA-OT Issue #815: Flagging code duplicates XSL
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #815: Flagging code duplicates XSL
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2778178](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2778178), submitted by [robander](/robander)

Flagging is supported by a series of templates, usually something like this:
set variable $flagrules
set variable $conflictexist
call start-flagit with $flagrules
call start-revflag with $flagrules
<element>
call gen-style with $flagrules and $conflictexist
apply-templates
</element>
call end-revflag with $flagrules
call end-flagit with $flagrules

The $conflictexist variable is only ever used by gen-style, is always set the same way and is always passed when using gen-style.

If we update the gen-style template to set a default value for $conflictexist, we can remove this variable from all of the templates that declare it in dita2htmlImpl.xsl and related code.

It would also be a good idea to have the flagging templates set a default value for $flagrules, because if they are called without the parameter they may break. In most cases, it will still be more efficient to call these templates with the $flagrules parameter.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2914475](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2914475), submitted by drmacro

This patch updates the GenListModuleReader and the DitaWriter to use a Xerces grammar pool. A new object, GrammarPoolManager provides access to a shared grammar pool so the grammar pool can be used across multiple Ant targets. Also included a simple TimeUtils class for capturing timing information.

I have tested both using unit tests (not included because the JUnit framework used by the code under src/ is not consistent with JUnit3/4 as far as I can tell) in isolation and by building dost.jar and using it an otherwise unmodified M24 distribution.

Because this fix eliminates redundant parsing of DTDs, performance improvements are most drammatic with larger input data sets. For example, a map of mine that has about 30 submaps and topics using specializations of the L&T modules went from taking a total of almost 3 minutes to about 20 seconds.

Fix for bug 2879196: colon and other special characters in <indexterm> have side effects and cannot be entered as literal characters. The The current FO plug-in recognizes Frame text-based index markup in <indexterm> text. That's why literal : and ; are not possible and have side effects (also paired <> and sometimes paired [ ]).

title: DITA-OT Issue #832: Clean plugin configuration parser
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3087664](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3087664), submitted by [jelovirt](/jelovirt)
Currently Integrator uses DescParser to parse a plugin configuration file, and DescParser will add the read Features object to Integrator's static variable pluginTable. Multiple Integrators are never run concurrently in the same JVM, so using a static map for features is not a problem. However, the code intent would be more clear if the DescParser would not push the results into Integrator, but rather provided getters to get parsing results.
The patch adds these getters and makes the pluginTable a private, non-static variable. In addition it cleans up DescParser by - calling super on constructor - removing currentElement instance variable because the information is not needed outside the startElement method - removing redundant calls to super's ContentHandler methods, because DefaultHandler's implementation does nothing when called

title: DITA-OT Issue #848: Avoid strings where other types are more appropriate
content:
DITA-OT Issue #848: Avoid strings where other types are more appropriate
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #848: Avoid strings where other types are more appropriate
content: Issue #848 is closed with labels none. Retrieval signals: error, dita-ot, validation.

title: DITA-OT Issue #848: Avoid strings where other types are more appropriate
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3189026](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3189026), submitted by [jelovirt](/jelovirt)

DITA-OT Java code uses Strings in multiple cases when a different data type would be more suitable. The most common case is representing paths or URIs as Strings. The code should be refactored to use either e.g. File or URI classes instead of Strings.

The problems with using a generic String to represent e.g. path include:
- lack of compile-time error catching
- lack of runtime value validation
- reduced developer productivity because developer needs to maintain type information in their head
- need for wider unit tests that also need to handle value validation problems

For more information, see Effective Java 2nd Edition, item 50.

title: DITA-OT Issue #849: Map references with root fragment are not processed
content:
DITA-OT Issue #849: Map references with root fragment are not processed
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #849: Map references with root fragment are not processed
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3470331](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3470331), submitted by thecloudlesssky

Map processing inside of xsl\preprocess\maprefImpl.xsl @ line 149. 

It doesn't account for ditmap references like:

<bookmap id="book">
 <topicref href="map.ditamap#rootElementId" format="ditamap" />
</bookmap>

<map id="rootElementId">
 <topicref id="tr1" ... />
 <topicref id="tr2" ... />
</map>

This statement _passes_ (line 149):
<xsl:when test="not(contains(@href,'://') or $element-id='#none#')">

Then, all elements inheriting from topicrefs are selected with the specified @id:
 select="$file//*[contains(@class,' map/topicref ')][@id=$element-id]"

For the example above, this would select 0 topicrefs because the condition looks _only_ for elements
with the specified @id. The expected behaviour should behave as if there was _no_ fragment identifier in the href.

Therefore the test should be changed to the following (line 149):
 not(contains(@href,'://') or $element-id='#none#') and not(contains($file/_/@class, ' map/map ') and $file/_[@id=$element-id])

This ensures that fragments referencing the root map element are actually processed as if they were just file references.

the system id of dtd entity to look for dtd files and

directory that contains dtd files. It would be helpful
if users don't need to specify the correct system id

dtd files are put in different path.

title: DITA-OT Issue #863: HTML Help should support context sensitivity
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1252447](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1252447), submitted by gershonj

The generated HTML Help file should support context 
sensitivity, allowing the application that opens the CHM 
to open to a specific topic in the CHM.

This can be done in one of the following 2 ways:
1. User provides a resource file that maps the 
 codes/numbers to the topic alias. In this case, DITA-OT 
 should reference the context map file (.h or .hm) in the 
 generated .hhp file.
2. DITA-OT generates the context map in the .hhp file or 
 creates a separate map file (.h or .hm) that is 
 referenced in the .hhp file. The topic's ID (if provided) 
 should be used as the context string; if no ID is present, 
 either don't create a context map for it or revert to some 
 other algorithm for the context string.

I am willing to work on this dev project, since I know 
what needs to be done. In fact, I'll probably have a patch 
ready in a week or two :)

The HTML Help project file (.hhp) should not be written

current implementation puts an XML declaration at the 
beginning of the .hhp file, which generates a warning

title: DITA-OT Issue #869: Filtering at top-level element
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1325346](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1325346), submitted by debbiep-sf

(Copied-and-pasted from
http://groups.yahoo.com/group/dita-users/message/1065)

This works fine with DITA-OT 1.1.1 if I filter to
exclude product "nifty":
**\* begin ***

<!-- file foo.ditamap -->

<!-- ... -->

<topicref href="xmlhelp/blah.xml" product="nifty">

<!-- ... -->

<!-- file xmlhelp/blah.xml -->

<topic>

<!-- ... -->

</topic>
**\* end ***

This doesn't work:
**\* begin ***

<!-- file foo.ditamap -->

<!-- ... -->

<topicref href="xmlhelp/blah.xml">

<!-- ... -->

<!-- file xmlhelp/blah.xml -->

<topic product="nifty">

<!-- ... -->

</topic>
**\* end ***

The error is reported in mappull.xsl, complaining of a
premature end of file, understandable because blah.xml
is now empty, the top-level element (topic) having been
disappeared by the filter.

I expected both to work. My contention is that in many
situations it makes sense for blah.xml to know, all by
itself, which products it applies to, and not hide that
information in an external file (foo.ditamap). If I
suddenly want to extend blah.xml so that it isn't just
in product "nifty", I don't want to have to go trawling
through all the map files on my disk looking for
references to blah.xml and fixing them up.

The DITA spec seems to suggest that what I want to
happen is intended, though how it deals with situations
where filtering is specified at both reference and
referent isn't clear to me.

hierarchy, but DITA-OT 1.1.1 inserts, at the point
corresponding to the <topicgroup> tag, a nameless
enclosing ToC level. I found this in Windows HTML
Help, but the same would apply to any ToC format
generated by DITA-OT 1.1.1. Certainly PDF output type
has trouble with it.

You can see the effect with this map fragment:
 <topicref href="xmlhelp/about/mps_license_admin.xml">
 <topicgroup collection-type="family">
 <topicref
href="xmlhelp/howto/mps_adding_keys.xml" />
 <topicref
href="xmlhelp/howto/mps_delete_keys.xml" />
 </topicgroup>

This patch cosmetically solves the issue for HTML Help,
but it doesn't solve the problem of parents outside of
a <topicgroup> being able to make related links to
topics inside the <topicgroup>, since it looks like a
grandparent/grandchild relationship during processing.
 And then if you have two nested <topicgroups> it
becomes a great-grandparent/great-grandchild link. 
This is what the comment in
xsl/preprocess/maplink.xsl:136 is talking about.

title: DITA-OT Issue #874: View log file in web browser
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1345606](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1345606), submitted by leelix

Based on Steven Anderson's post on Yahoo group,
http://groups.yahoo.com/group/dita-users/message/1077

By default, the logger just
outputs plain text to the screen, but you can change
it quite easily. Here's what I've done, and I think
it will appeal to others.
1. Change your logger to use the XML logger.
2. Output the information to a log file, like
 buildlog.txt.
3. Write up a XSLT stylesheet to display what you
 want.
4. Look at the result in a browser.
5. Skip down the street and throw away your reading
 glasses.

It's easy to do, here's how. When you use ant, run it
like this:

ant -logger org.apache.tools.ant.XmlLogger -logfile
buildlog.xml <target>

where <target> is something like dita2pdf.

You'll get a file called buildlog.xml in that same
directory. You can call it whatever you want to by
changing the name at the command-line.

By default it will use an XSLT stylesheet called
log.xsl. If you have a full ant install, you can get
a sample from your ant\etc directory. Copy that over
to wherever buildlog.xml is at, and if you want to
customize it. If you don't have log.xsl from ant,
create your own. It's a pretty easy XML file to
parse. I've modified it to create a table at the top
of the file that shows me any errors or warnings that
the build has thrown.

Open buildlog.xml in your XML aware browser (Firefox,
Opera, and IE all work).

title: DITA-OT Issue #878: Base directories for hrefs

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #878: Base directories for hrefs
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1357053](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1357053), submitted by debbiep-sf

If my DITA documents are stored in a hierarchy I often
find myself stringing together lots of "../" in hrefs:
 <image href="../../../images/icons/foo.png" />

This makes the file less portable because I need to be
sure that wherever I move it in my directory structure
I have to have the right number of "../" in all the
hrefs. Not good for maintenance.

I would like to be able to say:
 <image href="icons/foo.png">
and have DITA-OT know which directory that is relative
to, specified at build time.

This is like the <base> tag in HTML, FWIW.

Suggested interface (parameters to build):
 href.base: the default directory for all relative
hrefs. If absent, behaviour is the same as current
toolkit (i.e., relative to containing file).

It would be nice for each type of element capable of
holding an href could have its own base: one base
directory for images, one for xrefs, and so on. Perhaps:
 href.base.image
 href.base.xref
 ...

The same goes for specialized elements, so that I could
define a new element <iconimage> and have it base from
images/icons without affecting other elements' bases. 
This may require some tweaking to
org/dita/dost/invoker/CommandLineInvoker.java to deal
with parameters whose names aren't knowable at compile
time.

content: Issue #879 is closed with labels feature. Retrieval signals: map, html, dita-ot, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #879: Be more friendly towards relative directories
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1357054](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1357054), submitted by debbiep-sf

Some parameters can't be relative paths, e.g., the CSS
file for the XHTML transformation. This decreases the
usefulness of these parameters where the built help
might need to be relocated, e.g., to a web server,
since absolute paths will almost certainly be wrong.

I suggest having each XML file that is being
transformed know its path back to the directory
containing the map file. This will exist as a sequence
like "../../../" of some appropriate length.

This can be prepended by the XSLT onto a relative path
for the CSS file so that each HTML file can locate the
CSS that it needs via a relative path.

This could be used for other DITA-OT parameters which
can't presently be relative. It could also be made
available to the XSLT so that <image> tags' href
atttributes could be expressed relative to the document
root rather than the including file. (See RFE 1357053
for more about this.)

title: DITA-OT Issue #880: conref search path
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1357059](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1357059), submitted by debbiep-sf See http://groups.yahoo.com/group/dita-users/message/1221 This message describes a mechanism for including conditional (alternate) text by using conrefs. Essentially:

Do these steps on your operating system:

Where opsys_specific.xml is switched in as part of the build process, depending on the operating system we're writing for. This requires some assistance from the build system. The example assumes that the file opsys_specific.xml is copied over before the build, but that's messy IMHO. I'd rather leave the files where they are and locate them by special means during the build. One way to do this is to have the build system keep a search path list of directories to look in for conref'd content, and to actually conref from the first one found. One extra parameter: conref.base contains a semicolon-delimited list of directories. Any time a conref is encountered, that list is searched, and the first one for which there is a matching filename is chosen to be the source for the content. The earlier example combined with this in the build: conref.base = "${basedir}/specific/unix;." means that ${basedir}/specific/unix/opsys_specific.xml is looked for first, then ./opsys_specific.xml (the default). Anything that is operating-system-specific to Unix will come out of the special conref target; anything else will just be treated as normal. This might be unifiable with the href.base suggestion from RFE 1357053.

title: DITA-OT Issue #882: Xref content generation enforces formatting choices
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1367897](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1367897), submitted by prescod

Imagine that the author has written content like this:
A user might want to write an output stylesheet that formats these like:
The DITA toolkit cannot really produce these outputs, however, because it treats the second output as equivalent to:
In other words it enforces a rule that the "content" of
an external XRef with no content is the URL. In some
cases this is a fine policy, but in others it is
incorrect. People do not always want URLs showing up in
the main body of their text. They might have a policy
that they are always displayed as footnotes or mouseovers.

If the DITA toolkit is going to generate content it
should indicate that it has done so with an attribute
or wrapper element like
`<generated-content>...</generated-content>`. Then it
would be easier to discard in later steps. Alternately,
the target code could go in an attribute to be pulled
out by later steps (if they want to do so).

The same issue is even more important for internal
XREFs. People have a variety of different generated
XREF styles that they use. The toolkit should not
enforce one.

title: DITA-OT Issue #887: Add a new parameter /cssroot:{args.cssroot}
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1400140](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1400140), submitted by wuzhiq

This feature request is submitted base on Deborah's
comments in the SF bug #1328689.
http://sourceforge.net/tracker/index.php?func=detail&aid=1328689&group_id=132728&atid=725074
# 

Date: 2005-12-09 04:54
Sender: debbiep-sf
Logged In: YES 
user_id=1323727

I recommend one addition to this spec:

parameter /cssroot:{args.cssroot}
A local filesystem path (relative or absolute) specifying
where the file named in ${args.css} can be found.

When both /css and /copycss have been specified, the
toolkit
copies the CSS file from ${args.cssroot}/${args.css} to
${args.csspath}/${args.css}.

This enables the CSS source files to be kept in a different
part of the file system than the source DITA (topic or
map),
essential in large distributed development groups.

Example:
- My CSS file is stored at /shared/css/standard.css.
- I am building to /output/\* and want the CSS copied to
 /output/css/standard.css.
- The DITA map is in /doc/dita/thing.ditamap
 I use the build options
 args.css = standard.css
 output.dir = /output
 args.csspath = css
 args.cssroot = /shared/css
 args.copycss = yes
 input.file = /doc/dita/thing.ditamap

title: DITA-OT Issue #891: Improve user-configurable output directory
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1464479](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1464479), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The output directory as currently implemented may be
adjusted to ensure that output files are not generated
outside of that directory. For example, the following
map in plugin A may include topics from plugin B:
c:\projects\pluginA\AAA.ditamap
c:\projects\pluginA\tasks\installAAA.dita
...
c:\projects\pluginA\tasks\removeAAA.dita
c:\projects\pluginB\overviewBBB.dita

If AAA.ditamap is formatted to XHTML, overview.html
will be generated, because it is referenced from the
map. The output directory is adjusted to ensure that
all output files appear within that output directory.
So, with an output directory of c:\projects\out, the
generated files are:
c:\projects\out\pluginA\AAA.xml
c:\projects\out\pluginA\tasks\installAAA.html
...
c:\projects\out\pluginA\tasks\removeAAA.html
c:\projects\out\pluginB\overviewBBB.html

This is not always what users want. We should provide
an option in the ANT scripts that sets other behaviors
(this option may or may not be added to the Java
command line as well).

At a minimum, the following behaviors are required
(described below):
outdirscope="adjust" - the default
outdirscope="limit"
outdirscope="limitwarn"
outdirscope="nolimit"

ADJUST
This is the option that will adjust directories so that
everything fits within the output directory. This is
the current behavior, so it should be the default to
prevent regressions. The generated output is shown above.

LIMIT
The output directory is not adjusted. The generated
output is limited to files that fall within that
directory. So in the sample above,
pluginB/overview.html will not be generated; the
following files are generated:
c:\projects\out\AAA.xml
c:\projects\out\tasks\installAAA.html
...
c:\projects\out\tasks\removeAAA.html

LIMITWARN
Same as LIMIT; however, users are warned that some
files could not be generated. In the sample above, the
user would be warned that pluginB/overviewBBB.html
could not be created.

NOLIMIT
The output directory is not adjusted. All files are
returned. In this case, the following files are generated:
c:\projects\out\AAA.xml
c:\projects\out\tasks\installAAA.html
...
c:\projects\out\tasks\removeAAA.html
c:\projects\pluginB\overviewBBB.html

title: DITA-OT Issue #892: Make conref.xsl plugin-templatable
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1464575](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1464575), submitted by debbiep-sf

If I understand the plugin architecture,
specializations which need to alter the
conductor/*.xsl/catalog files for additional processing
do so by adding to the *_template file during integration.

I propose making xsl/preprocess/conref.xsl templateable
by this mechanism to allow plugins to affect how
conrefs are resolved.

---

Some use cases:

SF #1357059 conref search path:
Runtime control over the directories that conref.xsl
searches for the transcluded component is a way of
inserting variable text (such as product names, version
numbers, ...) into a topic. By creating a plugin which
alters conref.xsl to search in a runtime-specified
directory, the build can be controlled to insert
variable text into the output.

SF #1444900 Add template for getting input file URI:
With a content management system, documents are
referenced by a database ID rather than a file path. 
Overriding the code which resolves a conref into a
location allows CMS users to successfully use conref
for transclusion.

Relax domain check:
Normally it is an error to conref an element which
comes from a topic which allows more domains than the
destination topic declares. In certain rare cases
where the users knows it isn't a problem, this check
can be overridden.

Enforce company conref value policy:
Some companies may insist that all components eligible
for conref be in one paricular directory tree. By
vetting the conref, and failing if it does not refer to 
that directory, authoring policy violations can be
detected early.

---

Since this is a general processing modification which
applies to several transformation types it would be
impractical to do this by wrapping a shell XSL around
conref.xsl; every ant target which references conref
would need to be changed. By making conref.xsl
templatable this can be avoided.

title: DITA-OT Issue #893: Minimal support for fop .92beta and beyond

title: DITA-OT Issue #893: Minimal support for fop .92beta and beyond
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1484928](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1484928), submitted by mstockman

The newest versions of fop won't process the .fo files
built by the DITA-OT toolkit until you manually make
the following changes:
- Replace fox:outline with fo:bookmark
- Replace fox:label with fo:bookmark-title
- Enclose the entire bookmark tree with a
 fo:bookmark-tree /fo:bookmark-tree tag.
- Move the entire fo:layout-master-set to just before
 the bookmark tree, instead of after (where it resides now).

The interesting thing is that after you make those
changes to ensure .92beta compatability, the resulting
.fo file can still be processed successfully by fop
0.20.5, as far as I can tell, so backward-compatability
appears to be maintained.

I realize that trying to keep up with pre-release beta
software is mostly futile, but these changes are
hopefully minor and without consequence, at least until
fop 1.0 is released.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1518264](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1518264), submitted by dafletcha

There are currently two style params, basic-start-
indent and basic-end-indent, defined in dita2fo-
shell_template.xsl. Because these occur after all 
imports take place, it's impossible to override them 
via plugin xsl. Further, unlike DITAEXT, output-
related-links, and others, these params aren't tied 
to ant properties. So to change the default values, 
the only alternative to modfiying the delivered DITA 
xsl is to create a custom ant target to pass these 
parameters in. This seems like a lot of work just to 
tweak FO output.

One solution is to give these two params 
corresponding ant properties. But it seems to me that 
these params don't fit the mold of some of the 
other "global" DITA params like DITAEXT, which 
logically should be set at the build file level.

I think it would be a better idea to move these and 
any other style-only params into a separate imported 
xsl file, so that they can easily be overridden by 
plugin xsl code.

title: DITA-OT Issue #897: HTML Help requires new codepage
content:
DITA-OT Issue #897: HTML Help requires new codepage
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #897: HTML Help requires new codepage
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1520909](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1520909), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The toolkit today expects DITA topics to be in the
UTF-8 codepage. All of the generated text that is added
by default is in this codepage, so the input topics
should be UTF-8 to match.

When the project files are generated for HTML Help
(*.hhk, *.hhc, and *.hhp), they contain text from the
source files, which is still in UTF-8.

My current understanding is that these files must use
the Windows codepage for the source language, and they
must be formatted on a machine that uses this codepage.
As part of the HTML Help transform, we must be able to
convert the project files to the Windows codepage
before those files are compiled. For example, we must
convert:
Japanese files to codepage 943 (Shift_JIS)
Russian files to 1251
Turkish files to 1254
...

I think that the HTML topic files do not need to be
converted, because they display using IE, which can
display most Unicode characters. If we do need to
convert these files, we also need to:
- Update the charset in those files
- When possible, convert Unicode characters to common
 HTML symbols, such as € because those characters
 may not exist in many codepages.

title: DITA-OT Issue #900: Handle optional xrefs more gracefully
content:
DITA-OT Issue #900: Handle optional xrefs more gracefully
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #900: Handle optional xrefs more gracefully
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1553768](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1553768), submitted by su-laineyeo

One thing you very often see in Help systems is inline links like this:

> "If you want to grant certain sites the ability to store cookies, open the Cookies Exceptions Window by clicking Exceptions, enter the site address, and click Allow or Allow for Session."

The hyperlink goes to the topic whose title is "Cookies Exceptions Window."

Here's the rub: What if the toolkit can't find the "Cookies Exceptions Window" topic when it generates the Help file? It would be good if the toolkit were to simply display the xref content as plain text, although the user or the authoring tool would need to populate the xref element so it isn't blank. The sentence in the example above would still be meaningful without an active hyperlink. 

Unfortunately, if the target of an xref can't be found, the output process often either fails entirely, or creates a broken link that appears blue and underlined. 

The processor should recognize an attribute that says whether the link is required. For example, if @importance is "optional", the processor should output the content within the xref as ordinary text. 

This feature would make it possible to give the reader the benefits of rich inline linking, without sacrificing topic reusability.

title: DITA-OT Issue #901: Support Eclipse index output
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1561013](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1561013), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The Eclipse output format could (and should) generate
an index when indexterm elements are present. The index
format is pretty simple, and can be adapted from one of
the current index generators in dost.jar. I started to
adapt one last spring (attached below), but got
sidetracked and never finished it ... so there is no
promise that it works or compiles. It's based on the
Java Help index generator. Of course, the index module
also needs to recognize eclipse as a valid index type.

The format for the Eclipse index is here:
http://help.eclipse.org/help32/index.jsp?topic=/org.eclipse.platform.doc.isv/reference/extension-points/org_eclipse_help_index.html

That page contains this example, for easy reference:
<index>
 <entry keyword="Vehicle">
 <topic href="inventory_of_wheel.html"/>
 <entry keyword="Car">
 <topic href="car.html"/>
 </entry>
 <entry keyword="Ship">
 <topic href="ship.html"/>
 </entry>
 <entry keyword="Airplane">
 <topic href="airplane.html" title="History
of aviation"/>
 <topic href="jet.html" title="Jet engine"/>
 </entry>
 </entry>
...
</index>

title: DITA-OT Issue #905: Push metadata in topicmeta element to topic
content:
DITA-OT Issue #905: Push metadata in topicmeta element to topic
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

content: Issue #905 is closed with labels architecture, feature. Retrieval signals: error, map, dita-ot, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #905: Push metadata in topicmeta element to topic
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1609716](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1609716), submitted by werdenhoff

When building for example web applications that are supposed to handle multiple versions of the same document, a version identifier is needed. DITA specifies the <vrm version=""/> element that can be used for this purpose. I can see several approaches to setting this value.
1. Require the author to include it in topic
2. Have the CMS set it
3. Develop own logic
4. Have DITA-OT push values to topics

I will outline my opinion on each of the mentioned approaches:

1: I consider this solution too cumbersome and error prone. It would take the author too much time to alter each topics version attribute when needed.

2: I suspect this solution is the most commonly used. However there are situations where you don't want to use your CMS
- The CMS might not have support for it
- Using the CMS introduces an additional component that must process the DITAMAPS and therefore an additional error source

3: Wil do the trick, but should be coordinated with DITA-OT people to ensure future support. 

4: I consider this to be the best solution. DITA-OT already has an extensive transformation framework and an approach to specifying metadata that is intuitive.

I think that you should be able to push any metadata from the DITAMAP to one or multiple topics, as long as this is neatly marked up. Search analysis, recall and precision is becoming more vital as content volume grow. Search more than often depends on the amount of metadata we have available. 

Thank you!

Pål Werdenhoff

title: DITA-OT Issue #906: Separate "mapref" processing from mappull
content:
DITA-OT Issue #906: Separate "mapref" processing from mappull
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #906: Separate "mapref" processing from mappull
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1614222](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1614222), submitted by [robander](/robander)

Currently, mapref (a topicref that points to a ditamap) is evaluated as part of the mappull step. There are several problems with this approach:
1. It is difficult to pull in reltables, which cannot be pulled into the middle of a hierarchy. There is a bug report open about this today.
2. Inheritance does not work well. Mappull is supposed to make inherited attributes explicit. If a branch of a map uses importance="required", the current setup makes it difficult to pass that value down to other maps that are retrieved. The same goes for all inherited attributes.
3. I expect future specializations (or even core DITA functions) that will require overrides for mapref behavior. For example, a new specialized element may indicate that the mapref should not be resolved until display time. This is difficult to do with the current setup.

The mapref code should be split from the mappull code. It should run prior to mappull. It would not need to run on any map that does not use mapref.

The new mapref code should meet the following needs:
1. Any titles or topicmeta in a mapref target must be handled appropriately.
2. Resolved Reltables should be placed at the top level of the map (not nested under a topicref, even if that is where the mapref is located).
3. Attributes on the mapref should not be lost. If a mapref uses toc="no", that value should be preserved on the top-level topicrefs that are pulled in.

title: DITA-OT Issue #907: Support RFC4646 language tags in Index modules

DITA-OT Issue #907: Support RFC4646 language tags in Index modules
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #907: Support RFC4646 language tags in Index modules
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1623246](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1623246), submitted by debbiep-sf

RFC 4646 defines additional tags for several languages and (almost) deprecates some others.

xsl/common/strings.xml defines localization packs in terms of the superseded RFC 3066.

Additional languages should be added to xsl/common/strings.xml to support the new naming conventions for languages that DITA-OT already supports:

zh-hant (strings-zh-tw.xml)
zh-hans (strings-zh-cn.xml)
es-419 (strings-es-es.xml)

There are probably many others, but these are most likely to be in use right now.

Obviously we should continue to support the tags zh-tw and zh-cn for the foreseeable future.

title: DITA-OT Issue #908: Integration points for passing params to XSL

title: DITA-OT Issue #908: Integration points for passing params to XSL
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1676947](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1676947), submitted by debbiep-sf

(This example uses XHTML, but the same is true of other transtypes.)

A plugin that adds some new feature to XHTML processing may need to pass run-time information from the build into the XSLT that the plugin supplies.

I want an integration point to pass extra XSLT parameters from the Ant build system to templates in a plugin.

This could be achieved with an extra line in build_general.xml (actually build_general_template.xml):

<target name="dita.topics.xhtml">
 <!--...-->
 <xslt style="${args.xsl}">
 <!-- existing params go here. -->
 <dita:extension id="dita.conductor.xhtml.param"
 behavior="..." xmlns:dita="..."/>
 </xslt>
</target>

With this, a plugin has a way of getting custom Ant parameter values into the XSLT overrides.

title: DITA-OT Issue #909: Make dita.list into an XML file

title: DITA-OT Issue #909: Make dita.list into an XML file
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1686939](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1686939), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The dita.list file used by the processing chain is a text file with several lists of file names. I've several comments about this on various lists: it would be more useful, more extensible, and generally easier to work with if it were in XML. I also wonder if this would allow us to move past some restrictions related to this file, such as the difficulty of using it to include file names that contain spaces.

I expect that we would need to continue to produce the dita.list file as-is for a period of time after introducing an XML version, because there may be several tools making use of it today. New list functions would presumably only be added to the XML version.

A possible related feature is to create a hook that allows users to add their own values to the file. This could also be done simply by adding a new target to the pre-process which augments the file.

title: DITA-OT Issue #911: Allow option to build only topics listed in the map
content:
DITA-OT Issue #911: Allow option to build only topics listed in the map
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #911: Allow option to build only topics listed in the map
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1764905](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1764905), submitted by [robander](/robander)

Currently an XHTML build in the toolkit will generate XHTML for all of the following files:
- Any topic file listed in the map
- Any topic file linked to by those topics, as well as files that those topics link to (etc)
- Any topic file that is the target of a conref

In an information set with many in-line links, this makes it impossible to build only a subset of the topics.

This can also cause problems with output directories. If an in-line link goes to a directory outside the scope of the map, the output directory will be adjusted so that that file will still be generated in a valid location.

Another problem is that a topic may be used as a library for common phrases (used with conref). The build will currently generate an XHTML output file from such a library, even though the file itself is not a good XHTML file.

We should provide a way for the creator of a map to determine which topics are used to generate XHTML. The option should indicate that only those topics referenced within the the scope of the main map are used to generate XHTML. If a map contains references to other maps, those other maps are still considered to be within scope.

title: DITA-OT Issue #912: Allow greater control over the output directory
