title: DITA-OT Issue #912: Allow greater control over the output directory
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1764910](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1764910), submitted by [robander](/robander)

Problem: If I have a file in my map that resides above the map directory, or if I link to a file that resides above the map directory, the output directory changes. This is done to avoid placing files outside of the specified output directory, but the problem is that the output is unreliable: any user may add a link that throws off an entire automated build setup.

Possible resolution: provide an option that determines which output files are returned, and where they are placed. Possibilities include:
- Current behavior: all output files are generated, and the directory is adjusted to accommodate this.
- No change in output directory: generated files may be placed outside of the output directory
- No change in output directory: files outside of the scope of the output directory are simply not returned.

I'm not sure if all of those are needed or not. We can post to the lists to find out which behaviors are most desirable.

title: DITA-OT Issue #914: Let plugins not have to choose to go in "demo" or "plugins"
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1782256](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1782256), submitted by debbiep-sf

Currently plugins can go into either the "demo" or "plugins" directories. A plugin should behave the same whichever one of those directories it is installed to. This almost works, but not quite.

Case in point: the fo plugin adds some targets from its integrator.xml file to the DITA-OT build.xml file. integrator.xml then pulls in some more code, explicitly mentioning the "demo" directory. Meaning that the fo plugin must be installed to the "demo" directory, or those file references will fail.

This example speaks of the dita.conductor.target extension (adding to build.xml) but similar things happen with other extensions (such as the dita.xsl.xhtml extension; look in the javaapiref plugin for an example).

So some plugins work only in "demo". Some work only in "plugins". Some work in either, but those are in the minority.

I don't believe there's a way around this with the current plugin architecture. I'd be happy to be proven wrong.

title: DITA-OT Issue #915: XHTML: Add class to generated <pre>
content:
DITA-OT Issue #915: XHTML: Add class to generated <pre>
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #915: XHTML: Add class to generated <pre>
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1803199](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1803199), submitted by iggraham

It would be really handy if generated XHTML <pre> elements were given a class equal to the source element name, such "pre", "codeblock", or "msgblock". That way a mere CSS could be used to display code-blocks and message-blocks distinctly from generic pre-formatted text without having to resort to a custom stylesheet.

Converted from [SourceForge issue 1813523](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1813523), submitted by easirois

The current eclipsehelp transtype can only produce a plugin. The purpose for this feature is to enhance the capabilities for the eclipsehelp transtype to produce content the is more aware of different national languages - an Eclipse fragment.

The main differences between a plugin and a fragment is that the content in a fragment has a different structure and the main file is a fragment.xml instead of a plugin.xml file.
Unfortunately, one cannot take a peak at the xml:lang value to get an indication of the country and language values. These need to be passed in as a parameter so that the proper directory values can be appended to the $outdir parameter for the XSL output.
This feature should also dump translatable text that usually appears in a plugin.xml file into a plugin.properties file so that Eclipse Help display the apropriate text depending on the users web browser language settings.

A few new files will need to be created for this defect:
- create a fragment.xml file
 - output is an xml file.
- create a plugin.properties file (this one can apply to both a plugin and fragment.
 - output is a text file.

title: DITA-OT Issue #922: Add plug-in support for string resource-files
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #922: Add plug-in support for string resource-files
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1859421](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1859421), submitted by robertnthomas

The plug-in mechanism would be extended to integrate string resource files in a plug-in with the string resource files in the base DOTK (i.e., those strings files found under [dotk]/xsl/common).

One possible implementation would be to require that the plug-in adhere to the same directory/file naming conventions and XML file formats used for strings in base DOTK. In this scenario the string integration would support both extension and override capabilities: a) str elements in the plug-in with new name elements would be added to the base DOTK strings files, and b) str elements in the plug-in with name elements that were redundant with str elements in the base DOTK would be considered overrides taking precedence over the definitions of base DOTK str elements.

Like other plug-in integration tasks, the effects of integrating strings resource files should be reversible when a plug-in is removed.

RATIONALE:

Currently, whenever plug-in developers have need for a string that doesn't occur in the base DOTK string resources the developers must furnish code for string look-up that mirrors code that already exists in the DOTK. The ability to override string definitions in base DOTK would also make the DOTK easier to deploy for customers with rigid wording requirements.

title: DITA-OT Issue #926: Allow spaces in DITA file names
content:
DITA-OT Issue #926: Allow spaces in DITA file names
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #926: Allow spaces in DITA file names
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1982567](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1982567), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The toolkit today does not support spaces in file names. This is due to the Ant design that we are currently using. 

The way we process files now is to create a list of files on a single line in the dita.list temp files, and process that with the includes attribute on the <xslt> task:
 includes="${user.input.file}"

As long as we're using that attribute, we can't support spaces. However, there is another attribute, @includesfile, which takes in the name of a single file instead of a list. That file contains the name of each target on a single line, and spaces within a file name are not a problem. So, I think we can get around the problem by using this new attribute.

We should continue to generate the dita.list information that we generate today, because many builds rely on this. However, we can add a new value for each of our lists, something like this:
fullditatopiclist=a.xml,b.xml,...
fullditatopiclistfile=ditatopics.list

We put exactly the same list into fullditatopiclist (separated by commas) and into ditatopics.list (separated by newlines). We can then update the core toolkit tasks to use @includesfile=ditatopics.list instead of @includes="..."

People with customized builds can switch over to use @includesfile as they are able, and will get support for spaces when they do so.

title: DITA-OT Issue #929: Abstract/parameterize catalog references

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #929: Abstract/parameterize catalog references
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2013764](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2013764), submitted by dave_resch

All catalog references (both file and ID) should be handled as properties in DITA-OT buildfiles.

For example, the catalog import in build_init.xml 

 <import file="catalog-ant.xml"/>

should be

 <import file="${catalog-ant.xml}"/>

The default catalog file reference could be set in any DITA-OT buildfile, for example:

 <property name="catalog-ant.xml"
 location="${basedir}/catalog-ant.xml"/>

Also, references to the Ant catalog by refid, for example

 <xmlcatalog refid="dita.catalog"/>

should be:

 <xmlcatalog refid="${dita.catalog}"/>

Again, the default catalog ID reference could be set in any DITA-OT buildfile, for example:

 <property name="dita.catalog"
 value="dita.catalog"/>

Those changes would allow an alternative Ant-format catalog to be passed in to the DITA-OT build process, by using Java -D command line parameters, or setting properties in a "wrapper" buildfile that imports the DITA-OT buildfiles.

Thanks.

title: DITA-OT Issue #934: Make index output for new transtypes more extensible
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #934: Make index output for new transtypes more extensible
content: Issue #934 is closed with labels architecture, feature. Retrieval signals: map, dita-ot, plugin.

title: DITA-OT Issue #934: Make index output for new transtypes more extensible
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2074933](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2074933), submitted by easirois

This feature is based on a the following discussion that occurred on dita-users:

http://tech.groups.yahoo.com/group/dita-users/message/9505

The purpose of this feature is to allow those who are creating new transtypes the ability to have a hook into the IndexTermExtract Module process without having to update code in the core Toolkit.

The new design leverages the Toolkit's plugin architecture. So you can ship you Java code (via a jar file)as part of your plugin and integrate the Java code into the build process via Ant.

With a great big from help of Deborah Pickett with the ANT code, here is outline for making it easier for the Toolkit to process indexes from new transtypes more extensible.

The reference implementation for this feature will be the Eclipse Map plugin. The feature is backwards compatible. The default behavior is to fallback to the old behavior if the new "indexclass" parameter is not passed to the IndexExtractModule.

Although the Eclipse Map plugin does not make use of all the bits and pieces for this feature they will be described here.

Make a jarfile containing their class and have DITA-OT incorporate it into its classpath. 
<feature extension="dita.conductor.lib.import" value="mycode.jar" type="file"/> 

Add some Ant code to set a property: 

<!-- my_ant.xml --> 

<project> 
<target name="my.eclipsehelp.init"> 
 <property name="dita.eclipsehelp.index.class" value="com.example.EclipseHelp.IndexWriter"/> 
</target> 
</project> 

That Ant code brought into the build: 
<feature extension="dita.conductor.target.relative" value="my_ant.xml" type="file"/> 
And the my.eclipsehelp.init target is called early in the build: 
<feature extension="dita.map.eclipse.index.pre" value="my.eclipsehelp.init" type="text"/> 

So the plugin has three files: mycode.jar with the extension class, a six-line Ant project my_ant.xml, and a plugin.xml with three entries. 

Here is what the Eclipse Map Index integration looks like in build_eclipsehelp.xml.

<target name="dita.map.eclipse.index" unless="noMap" 
 dita:depends="{dita.map.eclipse.index.pre},dita.map.eclipse.init" 
 xmlns:dita="http://dita-ot.sourceforge.net" 
 dita:extension="depends org.dita.dost.platform.InsertDependsAction" 
 description="Build Eclipse Help index file"> 
 <condition property="dita.eclipsehelp.index.class" value="org.dita.dost.writer.EclipseIndexWriter"> 
 <not><isset property="dita.eclipsehelp.index.class"/></not> 
 </condition> 
 <pipeline message="Extract index term." 
 module="IndexTermExtract" 
 basedir="${basedir}" 
 tempdir="${dita.temp.dir}" 
 inputmap="${user.input.file}" 
 extparam="output=${output.dir}${file.separator}${user.input.file};targetext=${out.ext};indextype=eclipsehelp;indexclass=${dita.eclipsehelp.index.class};${index.ext.param.encoding}" /> 
</target> 

I have also defined a new interface - IDitaTranstypeIndexWriter.java as well that will allow the user to control the filename and path is written out to disk. The default value is what is passed via the output parameter in the IndexTermExtract. The one method is getIndexFileName(). What needs to be returned is the absolute URL of the index file that will be written to disk. 

Eric

title: DITA-OT Issue #936: Add PDF to the supported image
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #936: Add PDF to the supported image
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2120219](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2120219), submitted by tmakita

Dear Developers,

I'm using DITA-OT 1.4.2.1 for user system integration. The user is now moving InDesign publishing to DITA.

The important problem is image file. Last day I tested my FO transformation stylesheet to test image elements. Png, gif, tif, eps file is all normally copyed into \out directory. But only PDF file is not copied.

I investigate DITA-OT source files and find that PDF is not assumed supported image file.

Following is the code that I assumed PDF is not supported. (Excerpt form FileUtils.java)

/**
- Return if the file is a supported image file by extension
- @param lcasefn
- @return
 */
 public static boolean isSupportedImageFile(String lcasefn) {
 return lcasefn.endsWith(Constants.FILE_EXTENSION_JPG)
 || lcasefn.endsWith(Constants.FILE_EXTENSION_GIF)
 || lcasefn.endsWith(Constants.FILE_EXTENSION_EPS)
 || lcasefn.endsWith(Constants.FILE_EXTENSION_JPEG)
 || lcasefn.endsWith(Constants.FILE_EXTENSION_PNG)
 || lcasefn.endsWith(Constants.FILE_EXTENSION_SVG)
 || lcasefn.endsWith(Constants.FILE_EXTENSION_TIFF)
 || lcasefn.endsWith(Constants.FILE_EXTENSION_TIF);
 }

Our user usees Adobe Illustrator for make vector graphics. But most FO processor does not support Illustrator .ai file as fo:external-graphic. The alternate way is PDF. We recommend users to convert .ai files to PDF. Then the PDF is acceptable in major FO processor. Now PDF is widely used as vector image file in our user.

It is very unlucky that DITA-OT does not assume PDF as image file. Please consider to add PDF as supported image file. It is urgent request.

Regards,

title: DITA-OT Issue #937: Move CLASSPATH into ant build

DITA-OT Issue #937: Move CLASSPATH into ant build
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #937: Move CLASSPATH into ant build
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2154384](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2154384), submitted by brian_w

In the ant build for the small package, the instructions require four libraries to be placed on the CLASSPATH. These are dost, resolver, xercesImpl, and xalan. In the full package, the same four are again put on the CLASSPATH, along with others that may be needed for specific conversions (such as PDFs). 

We are finding the integration of DITA into a larger build structure is complicated by the requirement that these jars be found on the classpath. Considering that they are always supplied, there seems little risk to building these into the DITA ant builds explicitly. 

It should be sufficient (or at least it is in our build) to add resolver, xercesImpl and xalan to the definition of "dost.jar.path" path variable in build_init.xml, and the same three jars to the "dost.class.path" path variable in build.xml, build_template.xml, and integrator.xml. 

If it turns out that more jars are needed, or these jars are needed in other places that can't be accommodated by using "dost.class.path", then they can still be added to the CLASSPATH. But it would be very helpful to not have to do so, when ant provides a mechanism so that it is not necessary.

title: DITA-OT Issue #941: dita2htmlImpl.xsl should not define doctype
content:
DITA-OT Issue #941: dita2htmlImpl.xsl should not define doctype
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #941: dita2htmlImpl.xsl should not define doctype
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2631145](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2631145), submitted by [jelovirt](/jelovirt)

Currently dita2htmlImp.xsl has xsl:output that declares doctype

 doctype-system="http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml1/DTD/xhtml1-transitional.dtd"
 doctype-public="-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Transitional//EN" 

In normal HTML output this actually makes no difference because dita2xhtml_template also declares the doctype and overrides the the declaration in the imported dita2htmlImp.xsl.

However, for conversions that import dita2htmlImpl.xsl and do _not_ create full HTML documents (i.e. HTML fragments that will be embedded), this is a problem because the doctype-\* attributes cannot be reset. If a new output dita2htmlfragment.xsl tries to use

 doctype-public=""
 doctype-system=""

E.g. Saxon 6 outputs

 <!DOCTYPE div PUBLIC "" "">

Therefore I suggest the doctype-public and doctype-system are removed from dita2htmlImpl.xsl and the shell stylesheets are required to define the doctype if needed. For current HTML conversions this change would not affect the output. Only existing plugins that use dita2htmlImpl.xsl and do not define doctype in the shell would need to be fixed. Without this change conversion that do not want to output doctype have to fork the dita2htmlImpl.xsl.

title: DITA-OT Issue #942: Simplify Install Process (no env variables or shell scripts)
content:
DITA-OT Issue #942: Simplify Install Process (no env variables or shell scripts)
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #942: Simplify Install Process (no env variables or shell scripts)
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2660587](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2660587), submitted by qwcode

I'll admit to some bias as to what's "simple", but here's my idea:

1) 
Implement RFE 2660437, which would allow configuring your classpath via plugins

2) 
Have one distribution, not a full, std, and minimal. 
It would:
- not contain Ant
- contain a lib dir with the required jars; include xalan2.7.1, saxon6.5.5, and saxon9
- contain a default classpath plugin that used whatever processor the dev team wanted as default
 (DebbieP may be referring to this in RFE 2154384)
- contain instructions on how to modify the plugin to point to one of the other processors

The install/setup process then becomes:

1) install Java 
2) install Ant
3) download and extract Dita OT
4) create your build file
5) "ant -f <your build file>"

no fussing with environment variables or shell scripts
(except maybe to add a variable to give Ant more memory, if that becomes necessary)

title: DITA-OT Issue #945: Reduce duplicated code in XHTML <note> processing
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2703335](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2703335), submitted by [jelovirt](/jelovirt) Current 1.5 XSLT for XHTML note processing dublicated quite a lot of code. It was split into multiple templates to make overriding easier, but the code could be rewritten to reduce the duplicate XSLT. If a common named template is added /xsl:call-template /xsl:param /xsl:variable /xsl:call-template /xsl:variable
/xsl:call-template /xsl:call-template /xsl:call-template xsl:text /xsl:text /xsl:call-template /xsl:call-template /xsl:call-template
/xsl:template That takes two parameters, the note type and title, then almost all the note templates can be rewritten to be simply /xsl:template and other type note can also call this common template with /xsl:call-template Only danger note would use the current template, as it generated the title as a block level element. This would retain the exact same possibility to override idividual note types, but in addition overriding stylesheets could override the process.note.common template and change the note processing for all but danger type with one override.

title: DITA-OT Issue #946: startcmd.sh: Run the user's shell, not sh

title: DITA-OT Issue #946: startcmd.sh: Run the user's shell, not sh
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2780998](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2780998), submitted by debbiep-sf

The last line of startcmd.sh says:

sh

which runs the Bourne Shell for users to do their DITA-OT work in.

If we change it to

"$SHELL"

then it will use whatever shell the user has chosen as their default shell. This is probably more polite.

$SHELL is always defined on Unix, so this should never fail. The double quotes are needed in case the user is crazy enough to have a shell located in a path that contains spaces.

title: DITA-OT Issue #947: Process in unique temp directories
content:
DITA-OT Issue #947: Process in unique temp directories
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #947: Process in unique temp directories
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2790755](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2790755), submitted by [robander](/robander)

Currently the DITA-OT scripts take in a single temp dir parameter, which defaults to the temp/ directory under the DITA-OT. All processing takes place in that single directory.

We should be able to update the scripts so that the temp directory value specifies a root temp directory, but the temporary processing takes place in a unique directory within that temp directory. This nested directory could contain a time stamp or random number, such as the following (using the Ant tstamp format):
DITA-OT\temp\temp{yyyyMMddHHmmssSSS}

The advantage to this change is that it should allow multiple builds to take place at the same time.

An implementation needs to be careful about impacts to existing processes:
- Users that specify a temp directory today will still specify the same root directory
- Ant scripts that work in the temp directory may use existing temp.dir parameters to refer to to files in the temp dir

title: DITA-OT Issue #948: For PDF output, xml:lang does not work at the element level
content:

title: DITA-OT Issue #948: For PDF output, xml:lang does not work at the element level
content: Issue #948 is closed with labels feature, plugin/pdf. Retrieval signals: map, pdf.

title: DITA-OT Issue #948: For PDF output, xml:lang does not work at the element level
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2796964](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2796964), submitted by su-laineyeo2

This is a continuation of issue [#2656071](https://sourceforge.net/tracker/?func=detail&atid=725074&aid=2656071&group_id=132728): "xml:lang not used for inserting langauge-specific strings". This was closed with the comment,

> Fixed, but only one language detected per document, i.e. the document.locale can now be set by using xml:lang on the map or first topic. This probably makes sense for PDF, at least until significant additional work is done, since font selection should not be done topic by topic, and the index needs to have a single sort order."

While the fix described above is an improvement, I do not believe that it makes the PDF output processing compliant with the DITA specification or the requirements for multi-lingual documents. For example, one common reason to have multiple languages in a document is to fulfill government requirements for warnings to be given in several languages even though most other text is in English. A mostly-English document may contain a warning in French, and it is is not acceptable for the word "Warning: " rather than the appropriate French string (e.g. "Avertissement: ") to appear in front of the French text. 

Processors should use generated strings and language-appropriate fonts for each element according to its xml:lang value or the xml:lang of its closest ancestor.

Lastday I found the default xref text output for topic, section, table, li and fn in XXX_MERGED.xml. Following is the example. In all cases, I did not supply default text for xref element.

<xref ohref="c_safety_precautions.xml#concept_7FCFF8FD66F44819A8F4F03810EB6840/fn_DA409A2C671E3C40BCDA9876" href="#unique_10/fn_DA409A2C671E3C40BCDA9876" scope="local" class="- topic/xref" xtrf="" xtrc="xref:6" type="fn">2</xref>

title: DITA-OT Issue #951: Disable default xref text output
content:
As you see, DITA-OT adds the default text for empty xref element.

I think DITA to FO stylesheet should do the following:
1. If text of xref is supplied then honor it and use it as title of the xref link.
2. If text of xref is not supplied from author, the stylesheet should automatically generate the title of the xref link.

However above default text output (probably done topicpullImpl.xsl?) prevents this behavor.

And there are more problems.
1. DITA users sometimes wants to add the prefix like 2.1.3 to the topic title. This default text output cannot support it.
2. DITA users sometimes wants to number the table by part (or chapter) like "Table1.2-9". This default text output cannot support it. 
3. The literal "Table" seemes fixed. It is OK in English, but Japanese will use U+8868 instead of "Table".
4. The ol/li prefix format is determined by DITA to FO stylesheet. It cannot determined by preproces. Default prefix format seems 1., 2., 3. then a., b., c. This assumption is very unsuitable for localization. For instance, Japanese use U+4E00, U+4E8C, U+4E09 ... sequence.

As a conclusion, the default text format should be determined by stylesheet. DITA-OT preprocess should not add _ANY_ text to the empty xref. This is a very important problem to implement DITA to FO stylesheet. Please re-consider current xref transforming specification.

Regards,

title: DITA-OT Issue #952: Add Ant parameters for XSLT parameters

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #952: Add Ant parameters for XSLT parameters
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2845278](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2845278), submitted by [robander](/robander)

There are several XSLT parameters that can change processing for the core toolkit:
PRESERVE-DITA-CLASS causes each element to create XHTML class attributes based on the DITA element name, for use by CSS.
NOPARENTLINK prevents generated XHTML files from linking to their parent (based on the map)
BREADCRUMBS allows link processing to add breadcrumb links at the top of the XHTML file
DBG causes processing to output extra debug information
genDefMeta causes the XHTML output to include metadata specifically for web filtering software

These parameters should have equivalent Ant parameters, so that an Ant build can set the values without having to modify or override the XSLT.

title: DITA-OT Issue #957: Better handling of missing entries in PDF
content:
DITA-OT Issue #957: Better handling of missing entries in PDF
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #957: Better handling of missing entries in PDF
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2874200](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2874200), submitted by [robander](/robander)

For various reasons, intended or otherwise, simple tables may end up with more entries in one row than another. Currently, the XHTML output generates empty cells at the end of the short rows, creating one or more implied <stentry/> elements to fill out the row. The PDF output leaves out the extra entries, which results in rows that do not go all the way across, as well as some odd missing borders.

The PDF output should have the same fallback behavior as the XHTML - creating implied <stentry/> elements at the end of rows that are shorter.

This actually comes up more frequently for specialized simple tables, where each entry can be identified independently; at that point a processor knows if entry #3 is missing, and can shift remaining cells to the right. However, the default non-specialized processor cannot know when cells should be shifted, so adding an entry at the end appears to be the best default behavior.

The DITA-OT allows plug-ins to add extension points, so that new plug-ins can add additional processing.

The PDF plug-in, which is now the core PDF code in the toolkit, is not currently extensible. We should add an extension point to the plug-in, and create the following template files to let code hook in to the process:

topic2fo_shell_1.0_template.xsl.

The deprecated XSL-FO based output used the extension point "dita.xsl.fo", so that is already taken. I'm initially suggesting "dita.xsl.xslfo" as the extension point for the current code, but am open to suggestions.

title: DITA-OT Issue #959: Add parameter to control PDF bookmarks (default collapsed)

title: DITA-OT Issue #959: Add parameter to control PDF bookmarks (default collapsed)
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2882072](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2882072), submitted by [robander](/robander)

In output generated from the PDF plug-in, the bookmarks are expanded by default. There should be a parameter to control the style of the bookmarks.

After consulting with Aryeh Sanders, we've determined that the default value should be to collapse the bookmarks (prior versions were expanded by default).

The value can be passed in from Ant by setting the parameter args.bookmark.style to COLLAPSED or EXPANDED. Leaving the parameter or undefined or passing in the empty string will cause the code to use the XSL value, which defaults to COLLAPSED but could be overridden with a plug-in.

title: DITA-OT Issue #960: Provide hook for specializations to add custom headers
content:
DITA-OT Issue #960: Provide hook for specializations to add custom headers
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #960: Provide hook for specializations to add custom headers
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2882103](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2882103), submitted by [robander](/robander)

Specialized sections and simpletables both commonly add regular headings. We should have a hook in the output code so that plug-ins may add headings for these elements without having to modify any other code.

The section title in XHTML is created by processing the current element with mode="dita2html:section-heading". Specialized elements like <prereq> can match that to add a heading without copying any section code. A similar hook should be added for PDF.

For simpletables, when there is no <sthead>, there should be a call such as the following that allows specialized simpletables to create a header row at the proper location:
<xsl:apply-templates select="." mode="default-simpletable-header"/>

By default, this rule will do nothing. Its only purpose is to allow specialization overrides to catch the hook and add generated headers.

title: DITA-OT Issue #961: Convert named PDF templates to mode templates
content:
DITA-OT Issue #961: Convert named PDF templates to mode templates
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #961: Convert named PDF templates to mode templates
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2882109](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2882109), submitted by [robander](/robander)

We should convert some of the named templates in the PDF code to mode templates. Generally, this means - keep the named template, but have it then call itself with a mode. This allows far more flexibility for specialized topics. For example, to add knowledge of a specialized topic type into a named template, you have to override the entire named template. If two specializations try to override the same named template, one gets lost.

For the upcoming 1.5 release, I only want to make minor changes, including the following templates. Based on conversations with Aryeh, I may also consolidate large chunks of repeated code in the processTopic, processConcept, and related named templates.

The change would just convert this:

<xsl:template name="processTopic">
 ...

to this:

<xsl:template name="processTopic">
 <xsl:apply-templates select="." mode="processTopic"/>
/xsl:template
<xsl:template match="*" mode="processTopic">
 ...

Of course, any passed parameters would be passed to the mode template as well. Calls to named templates will be left alone, so that people who override the named template do not lose their function. I see these as immediate candidates for mode templates:

title: DITA-OT Issue #961: Convert named PDF templates to mode templates
content:
* commons.xsl: determineTopicType
* commons.xsl: processTopic
* commons.xsl: processUnknowTopic

title: DITA-OT Issue #965: Add extension point for modifying PDF link text

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #965: Add extension point for modifying PDF link text
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2883406](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2883406), submitted by [robander](/robander)

Currently, there is a named template for determining link text in PDF output (insertReferenceTitle). This template handles references to figures, sections, tables, footnotes, list items, or unspecified elements that contain <title>. The only way to add support for new elements, or to modify support for one (such as a specialized figure), is to override that entire template and copy all of the logic.

If the template is broken up so that processing is sent to the target of the link, it will be possible to add or modify support for individual elements without copying any existing code.

For example, change this:
<template name="insertReferenceTitle">
 if target is fig - get number and title
 else if target is section - get title
 else if target is table - get number and title
</template>

to this:
<template name="insertReferenceTitle">
 process target with mode="insertReferenceTitle"
</template>
<template match="fig" mode="insertReferenceTitle">number + title
<template match="table" mode="insertReferenceTitle">number + title
<template match="section" mode="insertReferenceTitle">title
<template match="new-element" mode="insertReferenceTitle">new-processing

title: DITA-OT Issue #972: Provide finer grained control of links in PDF
content:
DITA-OT Issue #972: Provide finer grained control of links in PDF
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #972: Provide finer grained control of links in PDF
content: Issue #972 is closed with labels architecture, feature, plugin/pdf. Retrieval signals: map, pdf.

title: DITA-OT Issue #972: Provide finer grained control of links in PDF
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2976463](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2976463), submitted by [robander](/robander)

Currently, links in PDF can be turned on (all links appear) or off (no links appear). I've often heard requests for a middle ground - links defined in relationship tables or in the topic itself should appear.

The default today is to turn all links off, and this (for now at least) should remain the default. Today this is controlled by a parameter called disableRelatedLinks, which only allows values of "on/off".

Binary values such as "yes/no" or "on/off" do not work when there are many possible variations. So, to change this, we really need a new parameter, with values that more directly define what is happening. So, I will add a new parameter called includeRelatedLinks, with current values of "all / none / nofamily". The "nofamily" value will hide any family style links: parent / child / next / previous / ancestor / descendant / sibling / cousin. All other links (generated from the map or defined in the topic) will appear. The value "all" will cause all links to appear. The value "none" will remove all links. Other behaviors may be added in the future, with parameter values that describe the actual function (such as something like "intopic" to include only links originally defined in the topic).

The parameter will work as follows:
- If passed in from the java command line (java parameter /foincluderellinks), that value is used.
- Else if it is set in an Ant build file (Ant parameter ${args.fo.include.rellinks}), that value is used.
- Else if it is set in an XSL override or plug-in override of the XSL file (XSL parameter $includeRelatedLinks), that value is used.
- Else take the value from the original disableRelatedLinks parameter (when that is "yes", use "none" here; when that is "no", use "all" here).

As part of this fix, I will also update the way that links are displayed in chapter topics that have the mini-TOC on the left side of the page. If links are turned on, and the chapter topic has any non-child links, those links will be included in a "related-links" section for the chapter topic. Currently those links are discarded no matter what the disableRelatedLinks parameter is set to. Child links for these topics will continue to appear _only_ in the mini-TOC.

The "args.draft" property is documented as a general parameter (for all
transformations).
But for the PDF IDIOM transformation it is not used at all and instead
the IDIOM PDF uses a parameter called "publish.required.cleanup" to
accomplish just that.

Comment by Robert Anderson in a previous email on DITA OT Dev List:

The args.draft parameter was part of the initial toolkit code. When the
Idiom developers created the PDF processing as a plug-in, they used a new
parameter for this rather than using the original one. So, to that extent,

PDF - if you want to open an RFE, we can update it for a future milestone.
The publish.required.cleanup parameter will have to continue to work as
well, so that we do not break any existing builds.

title: DITA-OT Issue #975: Add support for Eclipse Help index redirects
content:
DITA-OT Issue #975: Add support for Eclipse Help index redirects
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #975: Add support for Eclipse Help index redirects
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2987769](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2987769), submitted by easirois

Elcipse 3.6, out June 2010, will add support for index redirects in its help system [1]. A new element will be added to the Keyword Index DTD. 

This feature will add support for <index-see> for the Eclipse Help output parameter. It will also fix some issues with the current implementation as well. 

The current implementation creates an entry for the redirect where the href was defined. Which is fine is the index is in the same file. 
The other issue is that if the redirect is to an index entry that is defined in another plugin, then code will not be able to find the index entry in the plugin
that is current being processed. In this case, a warning will be created stating that the code was not able to find the index entry.

A new build parameter will be created so that we can differentiate between the new and old functionality. The default behavior will be the current implementation, 
which does have a dependency on specific version of Eclipse Help. The build parameter will be something like args.eclipse.index-see (not definite). If someone 
has a better suggestion, please feel free to chime in.

We also need to settle on how the index entries will be coded for the <see></subpath></see>[2]. Part of the issue is that index-see only allows <indexterm>.

Example 1.
<indexterm>PDE
 <index-see>bundle
 <indexterm>
 <index-see>development environment</index-see>
 </indexterm>
 </index-see>
<indexterm>

Though, the empty inner <indexterm> should not cause an issue is this what we need to recommend to writers?

Example 2. - This does not seem quite right. 
<indexterm>PDE
 <index-see>bundle
 <indexterm>development environment</indexterm>
 </index-see>
<indexterm>

Any other ideas?

<index>
 <entry keyword="bundle">
 <topic href="data/help/index/topic1.html" title = "loading"/>
 <topic href="data/help/index/topic2.html" title = "development environment"/>
 </entry>
 <entry keyword="plug-in">
 <see keyword="bundle"/>
 </entry>
 <entry keyword="PDE">
 <see keyword="bundle">
 <subpath keyword = "development environment" />
 </see>
 </entry>
</index>

[1] - https://bugs.eclipse.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=281146
[2] - https://bugs.eclipse.org/bugs/attachment.cgi?id=148061

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3001750](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3001750), submitted by [robander](/robander)

If I have a reltable, and specify a shortdesc for one of my topics, any links generated based on that topic should use the shortdesc from the map (not the shortdesc from the topic). 

For example - if the following reltable is added to the sample hierarchy.ditamap, the first topic (changingtheoil.xml) should link to workbench.xml, and should pull the shortdesc from workbench.xml (because workbench doesn't override the shortdesc). <reltable>
<relrow>
<relcell>
<topicref href="tasks/changingtheoil.xml" type="task">
<topicmeta>
<shortdesc>SHORTDESC IN MAP FOR OIL CHANGING</shortdesc>
</topicmeta>
</topicref>
</relcell>
<relcell>
<topicref href="concepts/workbench.xml" type="concept"></topicref>
</relcell>
</relrow>
</reltable>

title: DITA-OT Issue #983: Create new "textonly" output method
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3019853](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3019853), submitted by [robander](/robander)

We currently have code in several spots that uses mode="text-only", to output text versions of content. For example, it uses alt-text from images and drops index terms. This is often used when content is required in an attribute, such as in an XHTML title attribute.

Currently this code is duplicated in some files, and needed in others. We should instead have a common "text-only" module, that can process any DITA element with mode="ditaot:text-only". Any output transform can import the rules and does not have to duplicate the text-only processing. This module should go in the xsl/common/ directory.

Optionally, we can make this into a template, so that any plug-in that installs a specialization can also provide text-only equivalents of new elements. I've got XSL for the common module but can update it to add a template.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3020309](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3020309), submitted by sfogel2

We need a way to override the "nofamily" setting for the ANT property "args.fo.include.rellinks" at the topic level. Reason: to create proper container topics, or what Microsoft calls orientation topics. We frequently create topics just to be a parent of a bunch of related siblings, where the siblings are a conceptual topic or two plus some task topics. The parent container topic has just a sentence or two introducing the subject matter detailed in the children, and the related links to the children are the bulk (and most important part) of the parent topic, even in PDF. By setting "args.fo.include.rellinks" to "nofamily", we successfully avoid the "noise" of extraneous related links in the PDF, but would want to override this setting for a container topic so we get the chlid related links. Thanks.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3079610](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3079610), submitted by [robander](/robander)

The log from a DITA-OT build currently does not identify which version is running. We should include that information in the log to help track down issues, and help identify what features are or are not available.

Ideally the version should appear at the start of the log in the section that identifies major parameters. For example:

Processing started...
Initialize log directory and file name...
Version : DITA Open Toolkit 1.5.2 Milestone 6
Validate and init input arguments...
 [echo] *****************************************************************

title: DITA-OT Issue #988: Add extension points for TOC output
content:
DITA-OT Issue #988: Add extension points for TOC output
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #988: Add extension points for TOC output
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3086936](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3086936), submitted by [robander](/robander)

For most TOC output, all of the processing is included in a single file. There is no way to extend processing with a plug-in, and there is no way to add support for specializations using the expected modular design.

In particular, the following are commonly used to create output and are not extensible:
map2eclipse.xsl
map2hhc.xsl
map2hhp.xsl
map2htmtoc.xsl

We should modify these to use the normal modular design. While doing that, we need to make sure the existing file names are still usable and do not lose any function. We should also move the actual processing into a sub-directory, so that we do not fill up the main xsl directory with these and any future modules.

To make this change, I will make the following conversion for each of the 4 files listed above.
OLD PROCESSING:
map2eclipse.xsl <= Contains all processing for the TOC

NEW PROCESSING:
map2eclipse.xsl <= Imports all processing for the TOC
map2eclipse_template.xsl <= Template to allow extensions for plug-ins
map2eclipse\map2eclipseImpl.xsl <= Contains the code from the original map2eclipse file

If extensions to the Eclipse TOC are added later - for example, overrides to do special processing for bookmap output - they will go in the map2eclipse directory.

content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #990: Create a basic glossary implementation for PDF
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3125983](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3125983), submitted by aryehsanders

PDF2 glossentries would simply fall back to base processing, instead of having glossary specific formatting; glossterm should be formatted differently than a standard topic title.

glossarylist should not be ignored.

The DITA 1.2 language spec describes the href attribute of the glossarylist element as follows [http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/v1.2/cs01/spec/langref/glossarylist.html](http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/v1.2/cs01/spec/langref/glossarylist.html):

> Points to a manual listing for the current element… If no href is specified, processors may choose to generate an appropriate listing for this element. All of the book listings operate in a similar manner; for example, <toc href="toc.dita"/> points to a topic which contains a manual table of contents, while <toc/> indicates that a processor should generate the table of contents.

In order to adhere to this spec, the glossarylist processing was implemented as follows:
- If the glossarylist element does not contain an href, the main glossary template produces an automatically formatted glossary in the position of the document in which the glossarylist was found, mostly involving the automatic insertion of a new set of pages titled "Glossary", with the text "Glossary" automatically inserted according to the current language using the standard PDF language mechanism.
 - For example, the following source dita will produce a glossary with automatic glossary formatting:

title: DITA-OT Issue #990: Create a basic glossary implementation for PDF
content: - If the glossarylist element does contain an href, the code assumes that the glossary will be formatted manually and does not supply automatic formatting outside of the glossary entries. For example, no auto generated glossary title will appear and no new glossary page sequence will be created. The glossentry elements however, will be formatted based on the new indentation.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3177971](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3177971), submitted by [jelovirt](/jelovirt)
Support multiple feature element for same extension
Currently if a plugin.xml file declares the same feature twice, only the last is used. For example, in

Example 1:

<plugin id="example">
<feature extension="dita.conductor.lib.import" value="gui.jar" type="file"/>
<feature extension="dita.conductor.lib.import" value="backend.jar" type="file"/>

Example 3:

<plugin id="example">

<feature extension="dita.conductor.lib.import" file="backend.jar"/>
</plugin>

Other possible attribute name possibilities would be path or location.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1000: Pluginize DITA-OT base configuration files
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1000: Pluginize DITA-OT base configuration files
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1000: Pluginize DITA-OT base configuration files
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3190356](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3190356), submitted by [jelovirt](/jelovirt)

Currently DITA-OT hardcodes the following information in Ant build files or integration properties:
- built-in transtypes
- import of built-in Ant scripts
- supported image format
- template definitions

OT should "eat our own dogfood" and use the plugin architecture to define this hardcoded information. The benefits of pluginization of built-in configuration include:
- simpler and more consistent code (e.g. all transtypes are defined in plugin files)
- easier to remove unneeded features (e.g. remove troff or rtf support)
- explicit dependency management
- theoretically easier to replace a built-in feature with a custom one

Because backwards compatibility should be mainained until an API breaking release is made, the pluginization process should be made in small steps:
1. Create plugins for built-in features.

Create a plugin for each built-in transtype, i.e. xhtml and docbook as org.dita.xhtml and org.dita.docbook, respectively. The plugin.xml files will only define the plugin id and transtypes. Hardcoded transtypes are removed from build_template.xml. This change will not be observable by end users or plugin developers.
1. Move hardcoded Ant build imports

In the new plugins, add dita.specialization.catalog extension definitions to import corresponding Ant build scripts, e.g. build_dita2docbook.xml. The corresponding Ant import is removed from build_template.xml.The original Ant script is not moved, thus the change does not affect end users or plugin developers.
1. Move template definitions to plugins from integration.properties

Remove templates property from integration.properties and add template defintions to corresponding plugin.xml files. Again, no files are changed and the same templates are processed as before.
1. Move supported image formats to plugins from integration.properties

Remove supported_image_extensions property from integration.properties and add image formats using dita.image.extensions extension point. These can be defined in either in a suitable plugin, possibly as duplicates (e.g. png and svg in xhtml, and svg and tiff in pdf). Other option is to add a base plugin org.dita.base where the image extensions are defined.

These steps should not require any changes by end users or plugin developers, but would make the code more modular and easier to maintain.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1001: Change Java API to be more final and non-public
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1001: Change Java API to be more final and non-public
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1001: Change Java API to be more final and non-public
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3194917](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3194917), submitted by [jelovirt](/jelovirt)

The problem with the current OT Java API is that next to every class is public, even when the class should clearly not be used by other classes outside the package. A good example of this is the platform package, there most of the classes should be package-private as they are useless outside the integration process. The best practice convention in Java for class accessors levels is to be as restrictive as possible, as described e.g. in Effective Java 2nd Edition.

The other problem I see with the API is that classes are non-final. The convention is to design and document for extensibility, or forbid sub-classing by making classes final. Again, a good description of this can be found in Effective Java. The current classes are almost all non-final, but they contain no documentation about how the class should be extended.

These two problems result in a situation where we can't change the classes without the danger of breaking third-party code that extends DITA-OT code. If we changed the classes to be package-private and final where applicable, we could safely modify the classes for performance or refactoring.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1003: Improve log integration
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1003: Improve log integration
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1003: Improve log integration
content: Issue #1003 is closed with labels architecture, feature. Retrieval signals: error, exception.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1003: Improve log integration
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3199755](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3199755), submitted by [jelovirt](/jelovirt)

Current Java code uses DITAOTJavaLogger in most places for logging exception states that occur inside e.g. modules and pipelines. DITAOTJavaLogger outputs log messages to standard out and error, and notifies LogUtils about the number of messages at different levels.

This type of logging approch does not support running multiple conversions at the same time as messages are mixed, and also doesn't allow third-party software access to log messages and their levels. For example, that Ant process that runs OT has only access to stdout and strerr, and cannot forward messages to custom BuildLoggers at the original log levels.

To fix this, modules and pipelines should have the ability to receive a DITAOTLogger instance from the calling classes and then use those loggers instead of creating their own instances of DITAOTJavaLogger. For static utility methods, the method should either get the logger as an argument, or then error cases should be handled by throwning an error (an utility method that is too large to simply throw an exception should be split into smaller methods).

As a side-effect of passing loggers, DITAOTBuildLogger (used by CommandLineInvoker) no longer needs to use LogUtils for counting messages at different levels but rather it can count them itself. This will reduce static state use as per feature 3167087.

Current plug-in framework allows plug-ins only define extensions, no extension points. Integration assumes all extension exist and in effect extension points are defined only in template files or in Java code.
DITA-OT plug-in framework should allow plug-ins to define extension points. This would allow throwing error messages during integration if extension is not supported or ID has a type. This would make extension points definition explicit, instead of the current implicit definition.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1023: Base HTML stylesheets
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3323776](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3323776), submitted by [jelovirt](/jelovirt)

Currently OT supports generating two types of HTML,
- HTML
- XHTML

The implementation is based on XHTML output and the only difference the two is the doctype. However, the XHTML output contains legacy constructs, like using <a> for anchors when the preferred solution is id attributes.

To enable e.g. HTML5 output, a base HTML transformation should be defined and different HTML outputs should extend this base. Doctype definitions and other HTML version specific would then be defined in HTML version specific stylesheets.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1033: Copy the graphic files to the temporary folder
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3392891](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3392891), submitted by tmakita

Dear Developers,
My request is about copying the graphic files to the temporary folder. As far as I know the DITA-OT copies graphic files referenced from DITA topic to the output folder. This is natural in the HTML output because HTML file directly references them. However in the PDF output all of the graphic files copied into the output folder are embedded into the PDF by XSL-FO to PDF converter (e.g. Antenna House Formatter, FOP, XEP).
So the copied graphic files are obstacles for searching real output object (PDF file).
My suggestion is to add option to copy the graphic file to the temporary folder. This folder name is decided by the DITA-OT for each build. If graphic files are copied into temporary folder, the general PDF plug-in converts the middle file into the XSL-FO and PDF converter only converts XSL-FO in temporary file to the PDF in the output folder.
This option makes very clean output. 
Currently not only the referenced graphic files but also the graphic files for <note> elements or the company logo files by every language are copied into output folder. If this request is adopted, I and my user are very happy. Please consider to adopt this suggestion.
Regards,

title: DITA-OT Issue #1034: Make default TocJS output more usable
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1034: Make default TocJS output more usable
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1034: Make default TocJS output more usable
content: Issue #1034 is closed with labels feature, plugin/xhtml. Retrieval signals: map, html, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1034: Make default TocJS output more usable
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3393969](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3393969), submitted by [robander](/robander)

Currently, the TocJS output only works if you:
1. Create your own Ant task to call it, which sets the "output.file" parameter to name the JavaScript TOC, and also runs an XHTML build; or
2. Use another output type that calls TocJS processing on its own

If you just run a default build (with the demo or with the Java command line), and select tocjs as the transform type, you do not get anything usable back. There is no XHTML, no frameset, and the JavaScript TOC is misnamed as "${output.file}".

I plan to redesign the plug-in to produce some good, usable output when running a default build. This change will be based on evaluating the $output.file parameter. If it is set, then we will use the old processing, so as not to break anybody already using it. If it is not set, the build will:
1. Return XHTML output based on the input map
2. Return a frameset based on the name of the input map; for example, MyContent.ditamap will return a frameset named MyContent.html
3. Return the default supporting JavaScript files, plus a JavaScript TOC named toctree.js.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1036: PDF2: runtime switch for localization post-processing
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3401849](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3401849), submitted by donrday

Several users have noted that the current FO transforms are silently draconian in reverting user fonts to the default Helvetica. This can be changed by non-portable customization that users have discovered after much pain. A sensible solution is to provide a runtime switch that would make this behavior optional rather than obsessive--something like "font-localization" with values of OFF (default) and ON. Please discuss whether the design should provide other options and what those behaviors should be, besides just simple on/off.

http://tech.groups.yahoo.com/group/dita-users/message/23827 introduces the problem, and the subsequent thread explains one hard-coded solution. This request is to make the patch the default behavior and to provide a switch to enable either option.

content: Issue #1072 is closed with labels bug, priority/high. Retrieval signals: conref, xref, map.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1072: URLs not decoded by dost.jar
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1541778](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1541778), submitted by debbiep-sf
work correctly in the XSLT parts of the toolkit but don't work when dost.jar manipulates them, because dost.jar's URL-to-filename mapping consists only of replacing slashes with the current operating systems File Separator.

URLs should be treated uniformly across all parts of the toolkit so that filenames can contain any of these escaped characters.

URLs in DITA elements are:
- topicref/@href
- navref/@mapref
- */@conref
- image/@href
- image/@longdescref
- lq/@href
- xref/@href
- link/@href
- object/@classid
- object/@codebase
- object/@data
- object/@archive (space-delmited)

Perhaps there are others.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1073: Some elements are not handled correctly in troff transform

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1073: Some elements are not handled correctly in troff transform
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1575722](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1575722), submitted by sagipolley

There are a number of elements that are not processed
correctly by the troff transform.

These are listed below, along with suggestions for
troff formatting. I will add to the list as and when I
find problems.

My findings are from DITA-OT 1.2.2. I will soon test
with 1.3 and amend this list if necessary.
- `<title>`
 
 Current formatting--some titles (only those inside <refsyn>?) are non-bold, and appended to the previous paragraph (i.e., no line break inserted). See [feature request 1493465](http://sourceforge.net/tracker/index.php?func=detail&aid=1493465&group_id=132728&atid=725077)
- `<simpletable>` and `<properties>`
 
 Current formatting--these are munged together into a continuous flow of text, with no spaces between the sub-elements.
 
 Suggestion--process them in a similar way to `<dl>`. Use the .TP macro to indent each "cell" contents by a different amount. E.g., for a <property>, you could have indents as follows:
 - `<proptype>` - 3
 - `<propvalue>` - 6
 - `<propdesc>` - 9
 
 `<simpletable>` elements are more complicated, because there is no limit on the number of columns...
 
 Other elements that are contained by `<proptype>`, etc., that require indentation (e.g., `<dl>`) would have to have their indentation increased by the appropriate amount depending on their location.
- `<tt>` and `<b>` (and elements such as `<codeph>`, etc.)
 
 Current formatting--none.
 
 Suggestion--make them bold, using the .B or .BR macros.
 
 For example:

title: DITA-OT Issue #1073: Some elements are not handled correctly in troff transform
content:
- `<pre>`, `<codeblock>`, etc.
 
 Current formatting--none.
 
 Suggestion--indent them. Maybe bold them too.
- Special characters
 
 Current formatting--the callout character that I use for `<fn>` (dagger) appears as Ã¢. Something similar happens with em-dashes. 
 
 Suggestion--replace em-dashes with hyphen-hyphen (--).
 Callout characters--maybe replace with double-asterisk?

title: DITA-OT Issue #1074: xhtml output missing XHTML namespace

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1074: xhtml output missing XHTML namespace
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1615310](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1615310), submitted by debbiep-sf

XHTML documents must place elements in the namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" (see http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml1/#normative).

The dita2xhtml transform puts HTML elements in the null namespace. This precludes mixing document types such as XHTML + SVG or HTML + MathML.

xsl/xslhtml/\* needs to be modified so that it puts elements into the XHTML namespace for dita2xhtml, and into no namespace for dita2html.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1080: Index page range issues
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1856031](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1856031), submitted by craig_sandvik

If an indexterm start and end range occur in the same map//topicref/topicmeta instance, the rendered page range should include at least the span of the topic linked directly to the topicref. In testing with a linked topic that spans more than one rendered page, the rendered index has only the starting page number and not the page range.

The map markup is:
<topicref navtitle="Uninstallation" href="uninstallation.xml" id="x">
<topicmeta><keywords>
<indexterm start="page range test">page range test</indexterm>
<indexterm end="page range test"/>
</keywords></topicmeta>
...
</topicref>

title: DITA-OT Issue #1080: Index page range issues
content:
It's also not clear in the 1.1 language spec whether the range should span topics linked by child topicrefs when the start and end indexterm are in the same map//topicref/topicmeta instance. Relevant spec para: 

> In a map, the start range points to the start of the topic title of the topic being referenced by its containing topicref. The end range points to the end of the final child contained by the topic being referenced by its containing topicref, or to the end of the final topic referenced by the current map (whichever comes first). When a start and end range occur in the same topicmeta, the range applies to the containing topicref and its children.

Above copied from 1.1 language spec for [indexterm](http://www.ditainfocenter.com/eclipsehelp/index.jsp?topic=/org.ditausers.infomanager.LangSpec1.1/langref/indexterm.html)

title: DITA-OT Issue #1081: chunking to-content reprocesses maps and duplicates content
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1081: chunking to-content reprocesses maps and duplicates content
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1081: chunking to-content reprocesses maps and duplicates content
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1897497](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1897497), submitted by debbiep-sf

The "chunk" pipeline stage is run after the "mapref" stage, so when chunking runs, there is already one complete map at ${user.input.file}.

It therefore makes no sense that ChunkModule.java calls mapReader.read() for every map in fullditamaplist. At best it is redundant. At worst it processes topicrefs having chunk="to-content" multiple times, resulting in duplicated subtopics being included in a chunked topic.

Example:

main.ditamap contains a mapref to sub.ditamap. sub.ditamap contains a topicref to top.dita and sets chunk="to-content".

When the chunk code runs, it operates once on main.ditamap, which now (post-mapref-stage) contains a reference to top.dita. Chunking is performed. The code then operates on sub.ditamap, which contains a reference to top.dita. Chunking is performed again. The result is that the children of top.dita in the map are added to top.dita twice.

The attached patch calls mapReader.read() only on the input map, preventing this duplication.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1086: metadata in ancestor map not inherited by topics in childmap
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2043490](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2043490), submitted by julia_m

We are using DITA OT 1.4.1. This issue has to do with the "metadata pushing section" of the OT.

In this link: http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/v1.1/CS01/archspec/topicmetainheritance.html

It is stated that prodinfo metadata is inherited from maps to topics. My testing confirms that metadata at the map level does not show up in html versions of topics in the map, if the topics belong to a nested map. 

For example, topics A-D belong to a content_unit map that is reused in multiple larger maps. The larger maps are used for different products. According to the spec, topics A-D should inherit prodinfo metadata from larger maps.

That is, in this map:
<map>
 ... product info here ...
 <topicref> this topic inherits the metadata info from the map</topicref>
 <topicref href="other-map"> ... topics in this other_map do not inherit metadata from the larger map
</topicref>
</map>

title: DITA-OT Issue #1086: metadata in ancestor map not inherited by topics in childmap
content:
- The "other-map" is the content_unit map that is referenced in several larger product maps.
- If topics in the "other-map" do not contain any prodinfo metadata (prodname, version and component), and the "other-map" does not contain any prodinfo metadata, when this map is referenced in the larger map, the topics from the other_map do not inherit prodinfo from the larger map.
- However, those topics that belong to the larger map directly, inherit metadata from the map (if they don't have their own metadata specified), which is according to the spec.

To summarize, smaller maps and their topics should be made metadata-agnostic and inherit metadata from parent maps. 

Thank you,

Julia

title: DITA-OT Issue #1095: Empty tags result in invalid HTML
content: Converted from [SourceForge issue 2915751](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2915751), submitted by craig_sandvik If empty filepath, apiname, uicontrol etc appear in source, XHTML transform creates an empty singleton span tag, as in `` rather than ``. The singleton empty tag is invalid according to HTML 4.0 spec. IE and FireFox interpret the singleton as an open tag. This can be fixed by changing the xsl:output method to "xhtml". That does imply a commitment to Saxon (since it is new in XSLT 2.0). When I tested, it works to set xsl:output @method to "xhtml" and leave the stylesheet version at "1.0". That enables the new output type, but does not inflict XSLT 2.0 semantics on the existing template code.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1096: Topic type determination and dispatch not flexible enough
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1096: Topic type determination and dispatch not flexible enough
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1096: Topic type determination and dispatch not flexible enough
content: Issue #1096 is closed with labels bug, obsolete, plugin/pdf. Retrieval signals: map, plugin.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1096: Topic type determination and dispatch not flexible enough
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2928562](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2928562), submitted by @drmacro

The current processing model for the base topic/topic template uses the determineTopicType mode applied to the topicref for a given topic to determine the topic type and then dispatches processing specific to that topic type.

This is too limited in two ways:
1. It doesn't allow topics, in particular nested topics that are not referenced by topicref, to contribute to the topic type determination
2. The dispatch of templates for known topic types is hard code and there is no way to extend the list of type-to-processing mappings.

I think the right solution involves:
1. Having determine topic type use the topic element if the topicref-based determination returns "simpleTopic". 
2. Rather than using named templates for different mode types (e.g. processTask, processConcept), use a separate mode for non-top-level topics (that is, topics that don't start page sequenes) and use normal match templates, passing the topic type as a tunnel parameter. This would then allow overriding of base type-specific processing by letting plugins catch topic/topic, examine the topic type, and either call next-match if it's not a type they care about, or do the appropriate processing.

transformers. For example Xalan-C uses less memory than the Java
implementation and on bigger projects is mutch faster. The patch is here:

http://static.zapletalovi.com/temp/dita-xslt-liaisons-patch.zip

The zip file contains patch for current CVS version that slightly
modify most of Ant scripts (changes <xslt processor="trax"...> to
<xslt processor="${xslt.processor}"...>) and several source files that
must be added to package src/org/dita/dost/ant that implements the
Liaisons.

The patch does not changes the default behaviour -- using the standard
trax processor (Saxon or Xalan-J) but it adds several configuration
values:

<!-- You can use commandline XSLT processors instead of TraX, examples:
<property name="xlst.processor"
value="org.dita.dost.ant.XalanCLiaison" />
<property name="xlst.processor"
value="org.dita.dost.ant.SablotronLiaison" />
<property name="xslt.processor.binary"
value="c:/tools/xalan-1.11/xalan.exe" />
<property name="xslt.processor.verbose" value="false" />
-->

<property name="xlst.processor" value="trax" />

There are several implementations for Sablotron, Xsltproc, OracleXDK
and others. The most compatible processor is Xalan-C. Please note you
have to use patched Xalan-C if you have version 1.10. The patch should
be in the 1.11. Its here (for both CVS and 1.10):

https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/XALANC-653

Lukas

title: DITA-OT Issue #1111: Add tool support for SVG files

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1111: Add tool support for SVG files
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1352386](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1352386), submitted by pat_willekens

Despite the many advantages of the SVG image format, there is no general support yet for this format in the DITA toolkit. 

SVG files are a perfect match for organisations using complex diagrams in their documentation (technical drawings, electrical diagrams etc). SVG can solve many problems for these organigrams:
- the diagrams can be zoomed and panned without having to deal with the limited image resolution that other image formats (such as JPG) have. The image resolution makes it virtually impossible to work with complex and large diagrams (such as full electrical diagrams of a machine) unless huge image files are generated which are impractical to work with.
- SVG is XML and thus should work well within the overall infrastructure for nice features such as including links within graphics, immediately guiding the user to the right location on the graphic as a reference.
- SVG files are in an open-standard text format so we can potentially do things like full-text searches that will scan graphic as well as topic content.
- being an XML text document (with binary includes for bitmaps), translation memory software can be configured to find and translate labels and callouts.

I think everyone in the community who is writing technical documentation would benefit from tool support and best practice documentation for the use of SVG files. The solution should be architected to be interoperable for all DITA users and should integrate well with XML and SVG editors and other content management and processing tools.

The args.eclipsehelp.toc property is not used to set the name of the toc.xml file generated by map2eclipse.xsl. However, it is passed as a param (TOCROOT) to the map2plugin.xsl, so the resulting plugin.xml file refers to the toc.xml file as ${args.eclipsehelp.toc}.xml.

Thus, if you set args.eclipsehelp.toc to a non-default value, you get a plug-in that points to a non-extant toc.xml file.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 1800852](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1800852), submitted by debbiep-sf

The DITA-to-XHTML XSLT for figures is monolithic and hard to override only pieces of.

The sequence for figures is always: title, desc, content. This results in the content appearing below the figure, which may not match the style that users want. Overriding this requires the entire template to be rewritten, duplicating much code.

This code should be refactored so that it generates document fragments for title, desc, content, and then passes those fragments to a (moded) template which assembles them into a whole. This provides more override points for users to develop their own style, and for specializations to tweak the general layout of a figure.

Much of this goes for tables too.

Currently, the parameters recognized by CommandLineInvoker.java are hard-coded into the class. Consequently, CommandLineInvoker cannot accept additional parameters from plug-ins, such as the custom.dir parameter from the fo plug-in.

One potential solution would be to:

1) Populate the paramMap field with parameter definitions from a properties file (e.g., CLParameters.properties) instead of with parameter definitions from within the class.

1) plug-ins would be able to share the convenience of the CommandLineInvoker

2) Code maintenance for CommandLineInvoker.java could be simplified.

Converted from [SourceForge issue 1931451](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=1931451), submitted by dvint

I have a situation where the writer wants to reuse the same topic in 2 different locations in a given ditamap. With the current OT v1.4.1 we get an HTML file that has two sets of parent links. If these happened to be sequenced topics then we get 2 sets of next and previous links as well.

By processing the files as single standalone file you create this problem. I first questioned this model when I first started implementing DITA. I was told at the time this was done to speed up the processing, as a very large book might take too much time to process. The time needed is the time needed when you want it done correctly. I think the processing model should be more like the PDF2 effort where a merged file is processed to PDF. This same file could be used to process to HTML.

At the very least the storage and management model needs to be separated from the processing. Having one file in the editing area is fine and what is needed, but when published I need a unique page so it can be properly parented and chaned ina next/previous structure.

thanks
..dan

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2538093](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2538093), submitted by @robertnthomas
Lower-case Latin characters and lower-case Roman numerals appear in second- and third-level list numbering for non-Western locales. This presentation only makes sense when the locale uses the Latin alphabet as the basis for its character set (i.e., Western locales).
The Arabic numerals used for the first level of list numbering are universally understood regardless of locale. One way to remedy this localization bug would be to use compound numbering with Arabic numerals for non-Western locales. For example, a list item whose context is 2. > d. > v. would be receive a list label of '2.4.5' instead of 'v.'
