content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2803935](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2803935), submitted by tmakita
Current DITA-OT implementation does not allow plugins to accept parameters from Java command-line. It is because command-line parameter is hard-coded in CommandLineInvoker.java. I think it is fatal defect for plugin. Usually the plugin needs dynamic parameter inputted from user. But if plugin need parameter, the only way for it is to rewrite the CommandLineInvoker.java and rebuild the dost.jar.
[Solution] Categolize commad-line parameter into two. One is the core parameter to the DITA-OT, the other is for plugin. Core parameter is the same as coded in CommandLineInvoker.java. The other parameter can be any string as long as it is specified as /xxx:yyy. In this situation, xxx is parameter name and yyy is its value. This solution will make more flexibility to the plugin.
However this solution allows any parameter strings written in command-line. If the DITA-OT developer prefer to limit the parameters, there is a way to place property file for the parameter to the plugin directory and reflect it to the command-line parameter checking. In this way, I think it is possible to point out the wrong command-line parameters. - As I am not familiar with dost.jar, please ignore wrong description if exists.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1143: Pass output directory and original source dirs as XSL params
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1143: Pass output directory and original source dirs as XSL params
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1143: Pass output directory and original source dirs as XSL params
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2909270](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2909270), submitted by drmacro

As of M23 the standard transformation types there is no way, from within the XSLT, to know what the output directory is nor what the original input directory was. Both of these values are needed in order for extensions to find files that are needed in order to do custom processing that either gets things from locations relative to the original input or puts additional things in the target output (e.g., using xsl:result-document in XSLT 2 transforms).

Because the Toolkit creates a temporary copy of the input documents you cannot use document-uri() on the initial context document to get the original input directory.

Thus, all the standard transformation types should pass as XSLT parameters the original input directory and/or the original filename of the input document and the output directory. That is, the following parameters should be added to all transforms:
<param name="OUTPUTDIR" expression="${output.dir}"/>
<param name="INPUTFILE" expression="${args.input}"/>
Note that plugin transforms can locate files relative to the location of the transform itself without additional parameters since document() is by default relative to the XSLT style sheet, not the input document.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1149: Consistent Ant property names
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1149: Consistent Ant property names
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1149: Consistent Ant property names
content: Issue #1149 is closed with labels ant, feature. Retrieval signals: map, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1149: Consistent Ant property names
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3023241](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3023241), submitted by [jelovirt](/jelovirt)

The Ant scripts in DITA-OT have basically three types of properties:
- arguments properties
- internal properties that may be overridden
- internal properties that should never be overridden

The current naming scheme does not reflect the difference between properties. For example:
- ${output.dir} should be ${args.output.dir} or ${dita.output.dir}, as "args." and "dita." prefixes are used elsewhere to reflect property type
- ${base.temp.dir} should be ${dita.base.temp.dir} for consistency with ${dita.temp.dir}
- ${clean.temp} should be either ${args.clean.temp} or ${dita.clean.temp}
- ${dita.ext} is the internal value property for ${dita.extname}, the current naming doesn't make this obvious

The property naming scheme could improve readability if we had e.g.
1. for argument properties:
 - "args." prefix for all argument properties: e.g. ${output.dir} and ${transtype} would become ${args.transtype} and {args.output.dir}, respectively, or
 - argument properties use no prefix: e.g. ${args.input} would become ${input}
2. "dita." prefix for internal properties that may be set outside by advanced users: e.g. ${dita.temp.dir} as currenly
3. "_dita" prefix for internal properties that should never be set outside the Ant scripts: e.g. ${dita.ext} would become ${_dita.extname} and ${noMap} would become ${_dita.noMap}

In cases such as ${args.transtype} or ${input} there should be a backwards compatibility support, but in most cases renaming the extension could be silent.

If the change were be implemented in phases, the easiest would be to 
1. prefix all internal properties and flags with "_" to improve readability
2. rename internal properties to match argument properties so that only difference is the prefix
3. introduce support for prefixed/unprefixed argument properties and start supporting them internally
4. rename remaining properties that do not follow the convention.

content: Issue #1164 is closed with labels feature. Retrieval signals: error, dita-ot, validation.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1164: Avoid strings where other types are more appropriate
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3487222](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3487222), submitted by @jelovirt

DITA-OT Java code uses Strings in multiple cases when a different data type would be more suitable. The most common case is representing paths or URIs as Strings. The code should be refactored to use either e.g. File or URI classes instead of Strings.

The problems with using a generic String to represent e.g. path include:
- lack of compile-time error catching
- lack of runtime value validation
- reduced developer productivity because developer needs to maintain type information in their head
- need for wider unit tests that also need to handle value validation problems

For more information, see Effective Java 2nd Edition, item 50.

This tracker continues from tracker #848.

Currently PDF2 tables are output by default with a border around the whole table and a border around the header row. This behavior is hard coded and there should be a way to control the default.
However, the default does not comply to exchange table model way of controlling borders with frame/rowsep/colsep. The current default is frame=all, but for rowsep the default is different between header and body rows. To simplify the processing, same rowser should be used on all rows.

Add configuration options to optimize processing. Like [CAP theorem](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CAP_theorem), not all performance dimensions can be optimized at the same time:

When specifying chunk="to-content" for a topicref where there are two or more subordinate topics with the same topic ID, the topic IDs are correctly rewritten in the chunked result.

However, the corresponding topicrefs in the resolve map are _not_ rewritten to reflect the IDs of the topics as chunked.

The merged XML does not retain topic groups from the orignal map. It must do so as topic groups may determine the semantics of nested topicrefs. In the D4P pubmap design, the topic group <frontmatter> implies frontmatter semantics on nested topicrefs and that indicator is necessary in order to distinguish frontmatter topics from body topics (likewise, the D4P pubmap design has a <pubbody> topic group that distinguishes body topics from non-body topics.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3495571](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3495571), submitted by @jannylund

processTopicNotices currently calls insertBodyStaticContents to generate statics. This should preferable be changed as it makes it impossible to avoid page-numbers in Notices.

Suggestion:
Replace `<xsl:call-template name="insertBodyStaticContents"/>` with `<xsl:call-template name="insertPrefaceStaticContents"/>`. Both use the same names for the statics but I would say preface has more in common with notices than body, and it makes it possible to avoid page-numbers up to the place where body content starts.

Same thing of course happens with topicref's put inside `<frontmatter>`:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1187: Index generation should be independent of transtype.
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3516642](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3516642), submitted by @jannylund

DITA-OT contains several different features for generating indexes. (One within PDF2, one used for Eclipsehelp, etc). As index generation and sorting is a rather complex thing, it should be splitted out to not be depending on transtype. The index generation could happen as early as possible and generate an XML file (similar to Eclipsehelp's index.xml?) that can later be processed to match the wanted output.

This would allow users that publish the same content to several platforms to have synchronized indexes in all output formats as well as reduce the code overlap of having several tools to solve the same problem.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3516644](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3516644), submitted by @jannylund

Localization should be configured in one place. Currently PDF2 uses an "insertVariable" functionality and XHTML uses the "getString" functionality. This would require splitting out the variable functionality so it would not be part of an output type.

A first step against a better solution would be to make the variable files in an generic format and generate the transtype specific localizations using integrator.xml (or maybe on the fly?).

Looking in the "topicmergeImpl.xsl" it seems to me that all attributes of <glossarylist> are ignored:
<xsl:template match="*[contains(@class,' bookmap/glossarylist ')]" priority="2" mode="build-tree">

Please see this forum thread http://www.oxygenxml.com/forum/viewtopic.php?f=20&t=6670&p=20738#p20738

Basically a PDF document can have metadata stating the author name, document version, etc. In the Adobe PDF Reader for example you can right click the PDF and show the "Properties" dialog to see these details.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1207: Table colwidth attribute always treated as proportional

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1207: Table colwidth attribute always treated as proportional
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 2374525](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=2374525), submitted by su-laineyeo2
According to the Exchange Table model, the colwidth attribute used in the colspec element (http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/v1.0/langspec/colspec.html) can be used to specify either absolute or proportional column widths. See http://dtd.nlm.nih.gov/options/OASIS/tag-library/19990315/n-6i00.html .
The Open Toolkit does not seem to process absolute widths appropriately. For example, if you have one column with a colwidth of "1cm" and another column with a colwidth of "3cm", in PDF output the second column will be three times the width of the first column, but it won't be 3cm wide. In HTML output both columns appear with the same width.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1209: border-after-width.conditionality mismatches border-bottom
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1209: border-after-width.conditionality mismatches border-bottom
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3157541](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3157541), submitted by dkelly10

In demo\fo\cfg\fo\attrs\tables-attr.xsl, attribute-set name="__tableframe__bottom" contains `<xsl:attribute name="border-after-width.conditionality">retain</xsl:attribute>`. The corresponding border width is set with border-bottom-width; however, border-after-width.conditionality only applies to border-after-width. The observed behavior is that even though the border-after-width.conditionality is set to retain, the bottom border is not retained at page breaks. To achieve the expected behavior (border is retained at page breaks), the corresponding border controls should use border-after rather than border-bottom, since border-bottom does not support .conditionality.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1211: PDF fails to resolve keyrefs to topics in non-href elements
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3239041](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3239041), submitted by su-laineyeo2

The DITA 1.2 spec says:

"When a key definition is bound to a resource addressed by @href or @keyref and does not specify "none" for the @linking attribute, all references to that key definition become navigation links to the bound resource... For key reference elements that become navigation links, if there is no matching element in the key definition, normal link text determination rules apply as for `<xref>`."

For PDF output, this is not working. For example, say you have:
<map>
 <keydef keys="mytopic" href="mytopic.dita"/>
<map>
<topic>
...
<term keyref="mytopic"></term>
...
</topic>
Actual result: Nothing is appearing in PDF output in the location of the `<term>` element.
Expected result: The topic title from the "mytopic.dita" file should appear in the location of the `<term>` element.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3393398](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3393398), submitted by None

First off my apologies, I don't know much about the DITA-OT or the ant builds in general.

We have 3 large builds that each generate around 20 Docs in 2 languages. Each large build fails around 10% of the time.

The failure can occur during many phases but commonly occurs during "Move metadata entries..." and "Process chunks...". The xml file it fails on doesn't appear to have any rhyme or reason but it always fails with the same error message:

> [pipeline] [DOTJ009E][ERROR] Cannot overwrite file 'C:\IDD_Builds\DITA-OT1.5.1\temp\temp20110816145418752\ttst_adding_swimlane.xml' with file 'C:\IDD_Builds\DITA-OT1.5.1\temp\temp20110816145418752\ttst_adding_swimlane.xml.temp'. The modified result may not be consumed by the following steps. Check to see whether the file is locked by other application during the transformation process.

The only thing that ever changes about the error message is the file and the timestamp.
After this message there are invariably a number of warnings and file not found exceptions and an eventual failure when it attempts to read the file in the output dir but it doesn't exist.

The builds always run on Microsoft Windows Server 2003 x86. The docs are generated in English and Japanese and fail equally on both. No event log is generated during the error.

The temp directories were getting deleted so in an attempt to gain more info I disabled temp cleanup and I can tell you that when cleanup is disabled the *.xml.temp file is left behind but not the *.xml file itself

I've recreated it twice, the first time the xml.temp file looked like a proper formed xml file the second time it contained nothing.

On the second recreation I also had Process Monitor running. The complete log is far to large to upload and even the subset during the 20 seconds surround when this file was being manipulated is quite large. So I filtered to only display entries that begin with "C:\IDD_Builds\DITA-OT1.5.1\temp\temp20110816145418752\ttst_adding_swimlane.xml". This includes both the xml and xml.temp file process operations Hopefully that will be enough information. I'm attaching the log to this bug

title: DITA-OT Issue #1219: XHTML file paths case-sensitive but errors not reported
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1219: XHTML file paths case-sensitive but errors not reported
content: Issue #1219 is closed with labels bug, invalid, platform-dependent, plugin/xhtml, priority/medium. Retrieval signals: error, conref, xref, map, pdf, html, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1219: XHTML file paths case-sensitive but errors not reported
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3458346](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3458346), submitted by expertinfo

For XHTML transformations, file paths (for topicrefs, and possibly xrefs and conrefs) are not case-sensitive during the first stages of the transformation, which means topics are copied into the temp directory. But in a subsequent step they are case-sensitive, which means that a file path with wrong casing will not be processed into the output directory.

However, even if non-case-sensitive paths may be correct for cross-platform compatibility, the erroneous paths are not reported in the error log, which makes these errors very hard to spot, and may lead to missing topics in the output.

File paths with wrong casing should be reported as missing topics in the error log.

(BTW: in other transformations, like PDF, file paths are not case sensitive, which means that even when the casing is wrong in a ditamap, the transformation will work. This is inconsistent, and all transformations should probably be case-sensitive, but with clear error reporting regarding missing files).

title: DITA-OT Issue #1226: @chunk="to-content select-branch" breaks PLUGINS_ROOT links
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3496281](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3496281), submitted by @emth

Let us assume we have a DITA map called M.ditamap and in a sub-folder called "concepts", we have a topic called T.xml which belongs to M.ditamap.

If in concepts/T.xml you want to link to another document called "N" in an Eclipse Help System, you might do this:

 <xref href="PLUGINS_ROOT/N/section_name.html" format="html" scope="peer">

However, when you transform M.ditamap into HTML format, the link in T.xml will be transformed into this:

 <a href="concepts/PLUGINS_ROOT/N/section_name.html">

That seems to be because ChunkTopicParser.java doesn't consider PLUGINS_ROOT links a special case. If you set the @scope attribute to "external", the problem disappears, but that in turn adds the @target="_blank" attribute into the HTML file, which is not desirable when you're linking to another document in the document set.

The two patches in the attached ZIP fix the issue, but I'm quite honestly no good at all with Java so you might be able to come up with a more elegant solution.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1230: Dubious uses of attribute-set "base-font"
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1230: Dubious uses of attribute-set "base-font"
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3501184](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3501184), submitted by cnahr

The style sheet demo/fo/cfg/fo/attrs/commons-attr.xsl declares an attribute-set "base-font" that resets font-size to its default value.

This attribute is used in quite a few other style sheets in the same directory. Many of these uses make sense: they refer to elements that should in fact reset the font size, e.g. tables and new paragraphs.

However, this attribute is also pervasively applied to all text that uses font-family monospace. This includes "tt" in hi-domain-attr.xsl; all uses in pr-domain-attr.xsl; and all uses in sw-domain-attr.xsl.

I can see no reason why attributes with font-family monospace should always reset font-size. Similar attributes with other fonts never do this. Unless there is actually a reason that I'm ignorant of, all such occurrences of use-attribute-sets="base-font" should be removed.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1232: Metadata not correctly inherited by topics in child ditamaps
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3512088](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3512088), submitted by saanvik
According to the spec, metadata in a parent ditamap should cascade to topics referenced in a child ditamap (see http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/v1.2/os/spec/archSpec/cascading-in-a-ditamap.html)
<map>
 <topicmeta>
 <category>Guide</category>
 </topicmeta>
 <topicref href="a.xml"/>
 <topicref href="child_ditamap.ditamap" format="ditamap"/>
</map>
<map>
 <topicref href="child_a.xml"/>
</map>
the metadata in parent.ditamap should cascade into child_a.xml.
It does not. Tested in 1.5.4 and in 1.6.M1.
I've attached files from the 1.5.4 samples directory to illustrate the issue. I modified hierarchy.ditamap to add a category element. I also created a child ditamap, hierarcy_concepts.ditamap and moved all the concept references to that. I then added it as a child of hierarchy.ditamap.
The output is build using ant -f build_demo.xml and accepting all the defaults.
The output of task files (the ones referenced from hierarchy.ditamap) contain the category metadata. The output of concept files (the ones referenced in the child ditamap) do not.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1236: <span> tags added around step when DRAFT on
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1236: <span> tags added around step when DRAFT on
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3517050](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3517050), submitted by @robander

When a step or substep has @rev, AND that revision is set to "flag", AND the "draft" parameter is turned on, `<span>` tags are generated around the `<li>` tags for each revised step or substep. This is invalid XHTML, and causes problems for some browsing tools that expect all list items to be children of the `<ol>` or `<ul>`.

The `<span>` tag is created to allow special draft formatting based on the revision, but for block elements it is supposed to be `<div>`. I'll update the XSL to place `<div>` directly inside of the list item instead of placing `<span>` around the list item.

At the same time, there are several sections of code in this module that can be cleaned up (calls to flag templates can be condensed, and repeated code for `@importance` can be moved to a common template).

title: DITA-OT Issue #1238: Doesn't work with SAXON 9 HE (9.4.0.3)
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3519820](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3519820), submitted by @mkarg

I tried to run DITA-OT with saxon9he.jar contained in SAXON 9 HE (9.4.0.3) original zip archive, but DITA-OT does not work. Using the sxaon9.jar + saxon9-dom.jar contained in the "DITA-OT Full Bundle", DITA-OT is working correctly. It seems DITA-OT is dependend of exactly this revision of saxon 9!

Here is the error message:

> [maplink] ...\maplinkImpl.xsl:130: Fatal Error! Cannot find a matching 1-argument function named {http://exslt.org/common}node-set(). There is no Saxon extension function with the local name node-set

In fact SAXON is right, as SAXON is a XSLT 2.0 processor, so node-set() is not needed. This is not pure XSLT, so it is incorrect to say that SAXON can drive DITA-OT. In fact, only the SAXON contained in DITA-OT can drive DITA-OT.

A simple solution would be to upgrade your XSLT level to 2.0, so this non-standard function can be removed.

Cloning the Git repo for the OT should yield the same fileset as is included in the _Full Easy Install_ distribution, plus the additional files required for toolkit development.
_(Currently, the Git repo does not include Ant and various other .xml/.xsl files included in release packages.)_
This self-contained approach provides several advantages: 1. Each clone could serve as a functional toolkit in production environments. 2. Client-specific customizations in local clones could be easily merged with new toolkit releases. 3. Official SourceForge repo could be referenced as a Git submodule in existing Git-based projects. 4. Currently, it is not possible to provide separate font mappings for the same character based on its language. This is most relevant to CJK. The issue is that the charset for a character is determined by looking in the relevant i18n file. However, "relevant" is determined by the language of the entire document, not the current element.

I recommend we change the Java processing to look up in the appropriate i18n file of the most recent xml:lang attribute.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1256: coderef does not support any file location
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1256: coderef does not support any file location
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

content: Issue #1256 is closed with labels architecture, feature, preprocess, won't fix. Retrieval signals: keyref, map.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1256: coderef does not support any file location
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3517515](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3517515), submitted by julio_vazquez

According to the 1.2 specification, coderef should be able to retrieve the contents of any text-based file using either href or keyref. However, if a file that is not in the current map folder or a child of that folder is specified, coderef cannot retrieve the contents unless you specify the processing option generate.copy.outer="3". This limitation should not exist as code, which is not DITA source, may be anywhere in the file system and relative paths that are parallel to the current map or file should be supported by the processor. In fact, it's quite possible that a network drive or some other repository might be involved which could be problematic. We might want to note in the specification that a copy of the code should be available in the local file system or external and peer scopes must be fully supported.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1257: Simplify common XHTML code for flag/revision
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3518865](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3518865), submitted by @robander

The XSLT code used for XHTML has many areas that could be condensed in order to simplify the code, making it easier to understand and easier to override. My initial focus with this update is to simplify processing for flags and revisions. This code is highly repetitive, and for many templates, over 50% of the code is devoted to it.

Goals:
1. PENDING PERFORMANCE TEST: if performance is not affected by this, I would like to condense most current templates so that they do not need to set the "flagrules" variable and pass it. Doing so in most cases would reduce this code (set variable, call multiple templates with the variable) from 15+ lines to 3 or 4.
2. Regardless of #1, there are common templates today that can be used to condense some flagging code. For example, several instances today call "start-flagit" followed by "start-rev", both passing the flagrules parameter. These can be condensed to "start-flags-and-rev"; similar changes can condense the 2 end templates.
3. There are roughly 31 templates that set the "revtest" variable, all using the same 5 lines of internal logic. These should be condensed.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1261: Separate tool from content

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

content: Issue #1261 is closed with labels architecture, feature. Retrieval signals: map, pdf, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1261: Separate tool from content
content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3519843](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3519843), submitted by @mkarg

Currently the DITA-OT expects to find all [i. e. content (.dita, .ditaval), customization (.xsl) and tool (DITA-IT itself)] inside of the DITA-OT's file structure. This does not match professional production needs. Typically on modern desktops, tools and content are separated. For example, DITA-OT (the tool and the default stylesheets) are installed on %ProgramFiles% where only administrators have write access since Windows Vista, while content (topics, maps, etc.) are found on %AppData%, which ist the current user's profile where he stores all his private work.

While it is just a pity but not a real problem that the documentation does not tell how simply it is to set up a private content directory (one will find out soon), it is a problem that customization has to be put into DITA-OT (i. e. %ProgramFiles%) so (a) an administrator is needed and (b) it is shared by all projects of all users on this PC. Certainly I do not want to find conflicting extensions making me trouble in my project just because some other user needed to install an extension. Also, the extension mostly is dependend of the project but not of the PC, so it has to be installed on all PCs editing this project (which not necessarily is all PCs in a company).

To sum up, it would be great if the manual would tell how to put customization in %AppData% so it could stay with the content instead of asking the administrator to modify the local DITA-OT installation. A tool is a tool. Material is material. The need to have different colours in a PDF is a material change, not a tool change.

content:
Converted from [SourceForge issue 3521009](http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=3521009), submitted by @infotexture

A custom CSS file specified via `args.css` may contain references to background images and other assets that are required for branded HTML output.

Currently, these referenced assets are not copied to the output folder unless dedicated copy rules are set up in a custom Ant target.

OT processing could be extended with an additional parameter switch to parse the custom CSS file for image references (such as background: url("../images/bg_header.gif")) and copy those to output automatically.

A similar approach could be used to handle assets referenced in a custom frameset file, such as favicons referenced in the head element, etc.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1267: PDF support for figurelink/tablelink.style
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1267: PDF support for figurelink/tablelink.style
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1267: PDF support for figurelink/tablelink.style
content:
Cross-references to figures & tables are currently handled differently in HTML & PDF output.

In HTML output, the link text includes only the figure/table number (_Figure 1_), whereas the same Xref in PDF also includes the title and page number (_Figure 1: The figure title text_ on page 10).

For XHMTL output, two parameters govern this behavior: `args.figurelink.style` & `args.tablelink.style`, but these settings currently have no effect on PDF output.

PDF processing should be extended to support these parameters so that figure and table references can be generated in the same style as used in HTML output.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1269: East European languages have corrupted characters in chm TOC
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1269: East European languages have corrupted characters in chm TOC
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1269: East European languages have corrupted characters in chm TOC
content:
Some characters in East European languages show wrongly in TOC when building chm. The problem is that chm requires data to be in windows-1250 codepage, while it actually is build as iso-8859-2. By changing codepages in 'codepages.xml' to windows-1250 for East European languages I got all characters shown correctly.

Here are some problematic characters I could find and how they are currently shown in TOC (you can find a fuller list by checking differences of these codepages at http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows-1250 ):

cs:
ť => »
ž => ł

pl:
ś => ¶
ą => ±

sl:
ž => ł

title: DITA-OT Issue #1270: Chinese (Taiwan) shows garbled TOC in chm
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1270: Chinese (Taiwan) shows garbled TOC in chm
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1270: Chinese (Taiwan) shows garbled TOC in chm
content:
Chinese (Taiwan) shows TOC in chm in wrong codepage. I'm using language code 'zh-tw'.

Problem seems to be the following: File map2hhpImpl.xsl adds '-' to the language code before analysing it (zh-tw-), but later on when ConvertLang.java checks languages.properties, the language code seems to be 'zh-tw' while languages.properties supposes it should be 'zh-tw-'.

By adding
zh-tw=0x0404 Chinese (TAIWAN, PROVINCE OF CHINA)
to languages.properties I got the Taiwanese TOC to show correctly. Without this change the .hhp file will assume that the encoding is 0x0804 Chinese (CHINA), which is incorrect for Taiwanese.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1271: Chm TOC shows wrong characters for many languages
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1271: Chm TOC shows wrong characters for many languages
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1271: Chm TOC shows wrong characters for many languages
content:
As one example, the letter Ά shows incorrectly in TOC for chm for Greek. By changing html output to 'windows-1253' instead of 'iso-8859-7' in codepages.xml I got it to show correctly.

The compiler of HTML Help Workshop uses different encodings from what are used by DITA-OT currently. The ones that work correctly are:
- windows-1250 for East European languages (instead of iso-8859-2)
- windows-1252 for Western languages (instead of iso-8859-1)
- windows-1253 for Greek (instead of iso-8859-7)
- windows-1254 for Turkish (instead of iso-8859-9)
- windows-1257 for Estonian (instead of iso-8859-1)

In some of these cases the differences are only about some special characters. And windows-1252 is a superset of iso-8859-1 (except for control characters in the range 80-9F). But in some there are more relevant differences, and it would be nice if the correct codepage would be used.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1283: xref with desc and no href not handled in XHTML

title: DITA-OT Issue #1283: xref with desc and no href not handled in XHTML
content:
Code for processing xref in XHTML explicitly handles `<desc>` to convert it to hover-help. It does this by processing the desc with a mode, and then processing all contents except for desc.

When an xref comes through with no href value, the code just processes all contents. There is no template match for xref/desc so that element generates ugly yellow output with the "unrecognized element" fallback process. Sample markup:
I'll update this so that when there is no href, we:
1. generate `<span>` with the common attributes (ID, xml:lang, class, etc)
2. attach desc to that span as hover help
3. process all contents except desc, as we do for "normal" xref

title: DITA-OT Issue #1287: Eliminating startcmd
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1287: Eliminating startcmd
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1287: Eliminating startcmd
content:
Following my difficulties with the build of DITA-OT (see #1285) I have considered changes to the build files to make the process less arcane and obscure.

I propose modifying build.properties to include default values for the required elements of the class path, xercesImpl.jar, resolver.jar, etc. The defaults would be defined relative to `${lib.dir}`, i.e. src/main/lib. In over for this to work best, buildxml would be altered to define `src.dir` and `lib.dir` BEFORE reading build.properties, so that the build.xml definitions would take precedence.

The required `CLASSPATH` for processes invoked by ant could then be set within the various build file components. Users of standard and minimal distributions would modify the build.properties file to indicate their preferred locations.

The other part of startcmd is the setting of `ANT_OPTS` to the required memory for the java process. This is only required for the full-easy-install, which should be a hands-free install and run.

There are two alternatives.
1. As the full-easy includes an ant distribution which it expects full-easy users to take advantage of, simply modify the ant script to set `ANT_OPTS` to the appropriate values.
2. provide an ant.conf file to install in `$HOME/.ant/`. The build can check for the presence of this file. If present, keep going. If not, copy ant.conf to `$HOME/.ant`, issue a message explaining what has happened, and get the user to start again.

The great disadvantage of 2 is that the ant.conf file will be referenced for all ant builds. However, as this is part of full-easy, such users are unlikely to be using ant for other purposes.

Option 1 seems to me to be the cleanest. The ant distribution in tools will only be referenced by users of DITA-OT, so the `ANT_OPTS` can be specific to the OT.

I will prepare diffs for the relevant files and post them to this issue.

content: Issue #1289 is closed with labels feature. Retrieval signals: error, dita-ot, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1289: Improve error messages
content:
Individual messages can be improved at any point, but I'm opening this general tracker to track the more significant changes coming in the final iteration of DITA-OT 1.6.

The recent DITA-OT usage survey listed error messages as one of the biggest trouble spots in DITA-OT processing. Earlier test builds of this release added all messages to the DITA-OT documentation, including a rough first pass at cleanup.

For the final release we'll be doing further cleanup in a few areas:
- Removing unnecessary / duplicated information from messages to make them more direct. For example, some messages indicate an invalid parameter value, then tell you what parameter to specify - effectively giving the information twice. Those also tend to list only the Ant parameter name, which is unhelpful to people using other methods to run the build.
- Add more information to the messages where possible to make them more useful; for example, in the message about an invalid transformation type, include the specified (invalid) value
- Move some potential responses into the documentation, rather than having many potential resolutions as part of the text

content: Issue #1295 is closed with labels bug, plugin/xhtml. Retrieval signals: error, keyref, html.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1295: Various errors when using term with keyref in XHTML
content:
(Found while validating / updating error messages for term/@keyref)

XHTML contains some complex processing for term elements with keyref attributes, which will pull terms or abbreviations from associated glossary topics. I've found several issues with term processing:
1. When the term is empty and the glossentry does not have a surfaceForm element, no text is pulled (it does not properly retrieve text from glossterm); it should pull from the term
2. The retrieval from glossary elements uses xsl:value-of, which will pull in draft information / index terms and lose formatting such as the > in a menu cascade; it should use apply-templates with the common "text-only" mode
3. The hover text is a copy of the term or surface form; it should be the definition (more useful / common to pop up the definition when hovering over a new term, rather than simply a copy of the term). I'll create a template based on the getSurfaceForm mode that gets the definition.

The templates for working with this use exsl:node-set, which I know we're trying to get away from, but I'm not cleaning those up as part of this issue (unless @jelovirt or somebody else wants to do that additional work after my updates).

title: DITA-OT Issue #1298: Not all attributes defined on a DITA Composite are copied in the preprocessing stage
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1298: Not all attributes defined on a DITA Composite are copied in the preprocessing stage
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1298: Not all attributes defined on a DITA Composite are copied in the preprocessing stage
content:
The callback `org.dita.dost.reader.MergeTopicParser.startElement(String, String, String, Attributes)` by default copies all attributes defined on the element in the string buffer. But for a `<dita>` element it makes a fast return and does not copy the attributes defined on the <dita> element to the string buffer.

Why is this a problem?
1. The attributes xtrf and xtrc are not passed further.
2. The `<dita>` element (at least the one which is XML Schema based) could have extra proxy-namespace declarations which are not copied and the XML would become namespace not-wellformed.

By the way, maybe in the entire dost.jar StringBuffer could be replaced with StringBuilder which is faster.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1300: Add a hook to set @summary on table in XHTML
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1300: Add a hook to set @summary on table in XHTML
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1300: Add a hook to set @summary on table in XHTML
content:
DITA does not (yet) provide a standard way to provide a table summary, which is often used to enhance accessibility (providing a long text description of the table which is not visible in browsers but can be read by a screen reader). This is close in meaning to the existing <desc> element on tables, except that this content has been used by many to include descriptive text for all users (not just screen readers). Moving it to the summary would hide that text from the browser, and duplicating it actually reduces usability because screen readers will read it twice.

Some users have a requirement to provide this attribute, and currently must do so following some local convention - for example (only an example), using something like this:
To enable local conventions, we should add a hook for table and simpletable processing that extensions can catch in order to add summaries. Note that this could also be useful for specialized tables that always have a standard description - for example, the hook could be used to add a standard summary to all <choicetable> elements. I'll update the code so that tables and choicetables include the following line, which (by default) will leave the current empty summary attribute:
<xsl:apply-templates select="." mode="generate-table-summary-attribute"/>

title: DITA-OT Issue #1302: Add a way for cross-references to pick up generated text for sections
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1302: Add a way for cross-references to pick up generated text for sections
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1302: Add a way for cross-references to pick up generated text for sections
content:
We have several specialized sections that generate XHTML and PDF output with standard generated text (localized as needed). For example, we have a specialized message topic with a section specialized as msgExplanation, which appears with the generated text "Explanation". Within those topics, cross references from one message section to another should pick up that same generated text. Currently the only way to do this is to override the entire pre-process section that handles cross references to sections; ideally, there should be a hook so that specializations can directly provide generated text for cross references without overriding the way that all xref elements are handled.

Currently the processing for general block references will set the title in this priority:
1. If in same document and title is specified on target
2. Else if in another document and title is specified
3. Else if same document and specittle attribute on target
4. Else if other document and spectitle attribute on target
5. Otherwise use href value

In between 4 and 5, I'm adding a hook where we process the target with mode="topicpull:get_generated_text". By default no title will be specified. Specialized elements like the msgExplanation example can now match msgExplanation with this mode, and return the generated text for that section.

Currently implementing this only for the section element, where we've got many instances, but this could be extended to handle generated text for tables, figures, or other explicitly supported elements.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1306: Typo in XSLT mode results in extra fallthrough text for step
content:
When steps are processed, each one is processed with mode="add-step-importance-flag" which is used to add the Optional / Required generated text.

Single step tasks use a different path which displays the step as a paragraph rather than an ordered list. For that path, there is a typo in the mode, it is calling with mode="add-add-step-importance-flag". This mode does not exist, so as a result, all of the text content of the step comes out at the start with no formatting, then again with normal formatting.

Correcting the mode name fixes the problem.

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1313: Separate flagging logic from XHTML code
content:
The primary XSLT logic that supports DITAVAL flagging is tightly connected to XHTML output processing. This leads to a lot of extra overhead in the XHTML code, because it checks for styles, start/end flags, and start/end revisions on virtually every element.

We should pull this logic out into its own module. This will provide several benefits:
- Major simplification to XHTML code (easier to understand, maintain, and override)
- Makes the logic reusable by any transform
- For documents with no flagging, may improve performance by bypassing the flag code entirely
- Even for documents with flagging, this will limit flag evaluation to elements that need it, rather than every element

Details of how to pass the flag information from this first-scan into the rendering step are still to be worked out.

content: Issue #1318 is closed with labels architecture, feature, priority/low. Retrieval signals: map, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1318: Support content input via URI
content:
DITA-OT process should be able to accept input content via a URI, not only file system path. A new argument property should be used for URI input, e.g. `args.input.uri`. By default, DITA-OT should support URL schemes which are supported by Java `URLConnection`.
Plug-ins should be able to configure a `URIResolver` or an `EntityResolver` instance to process URIs. This will allow mapping e.g. `cms:GUID-1234` to `https://cms.example.com/resources/GUID-1234.ditamap` and the source file can then be retrieved during preprocessing.
Implementation phases could be as follows: 1. Support file URI scheme for `args.input.uri`.
Initially support only file URI scheme. 2. Catalog processing is used during resolving the resources.
This allows using non-file URI schemes in documents as long as they resolve to file URIs. 3. Support any URI scheme which can be processed with vanilla Java or with e.g. Apache Commons Net.
Mainly targeting RESTful data sources. 4. Support `URIResolver` or `EntityResolver` to return content source (e.g. directly from a database)
Optionally also allow setting `URLStreamHandlerFactory`.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1324: Avoid strings where other types are more appropriate

content: Issue #1324 is closed with labels feature, priority/low. Retrieval signals: error, dita-ot, validation.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1324: Avoid strings where other types are more appropriate
content:
DITA-OT Java code uses Strings in multiple cases when a different data type would be more suitable. The most common case is representing paths or URIs as Strings. The code should be refactored to use either e.g. File or URI classes instead of Strings.

The problems with using a generic String to represent e.g. path include:
- lack of compile-time error catching
- lack of runtime value validation
- reduced developer productivity because developer needs to maintain type information in their head
- need for wider unit tests that also need to handle value validation problems

For more information, see Effective Java 2nd Edition, item 50.

This issue continues from issue #1164.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1328: Mark dead links in preprocessing
content:
Preprocessing should mark dead links with either a processing instruction or an attribute in a namespace.
This will allow further processing skip those links without trying to read the target and error message for the missing resource can be issued only once.
Because using attribute will allow SAX processing act early before reading the element content, attribute approach is probably preferable.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1334: Command line tool for running DITA-OT
content:
There should be a command line tool to run DITA-OT without needing to set-up anything. The tool should: - handle all environment issues, like system variables - abstract Java and Ant away
The arguments given to the tool may be directly passed to Ant, or can be processed before passing the information to Ant. For example, the usage could be
Thus `INPUT` would be processed to be `-Dargs.input=INPUT` and `TRANSTYPE` to `-Dtranstype=TRANSTYPE`. 

DITA-OT already has the legacy `CommandLineInvoker` and this command line tool could also support the legacy argument format of `/t:TRANSTYPE`etc.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1340: The "DitaWriter" class does not properly resolve entities when catalogs are referenced with <nextCatalog> in the catalog-dita.xml
content:
If a DITA DTD specialization is integrated as a plugin and a reference to its catalog is made in the "catalog-dita.xml" the PDF output fails.

Problem:

The DitaWriter class has now become an XMLReader and in the overwritten method:

resolveEntity.....

instead of using the Xerces catalog support it uses some custom way of parsing XML catalogs.
This custom code does not properly go into `<nextCatalog>` entries.

Proposed fix:
1. Comment out the method "resolveEntity" from DitaWriter, remove unnecessary "catalogMap" .
2. When entity resolver is set to parent reader:

`reader.setEntityResolver(CatalogUtils.getCatalogResolver());`

also set the same catalog resolver to the current class:

`DitaWriter.this.setEntityResolver(CatalogUtils.getCatalogResolver());`

title: DITA-OT Issue #1344: <related-links> element breaks child links
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1344: <related-links> element breaks child links
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1344: <related-links> element breaks child links
content:
1. Open `$DITA_HOME/samples/concepts/garageconceptsoverview.xml`.
2. Add this `<related-links>` element after the `<conbody></conbody>` element:
3. Go to `$DITA_HOME` and run `ant -f build_demo.xml` and generate Eclipse Help output. 4. Open `$DITA_HOME/out/concepts/garageconceptsoverview.html`in a web browser.
I suspect the root cause of the problem is somewhere else, but I haven't had the time to delve any deeper into the jungle of XSL files that is DITA-OT yet, so I'm not exactly sure where. Problem 2 is clearly related, though, so I suspect it might have something to do with attribute inheritance.
<related-links format="html" scope="external">
 <link href="http://www.example.org">
 <linktext>Example 1</linktext>
 </link>
 <link href="http://www.example.com">
 <linktext>Example 2</linktext>
 </link>
 </related-links>

title: DITA-OT Issue #1344: <related-links> element breaks child links
content:
If you generate output again after that, it seems to me like the child links in that chapter wrongly inherit the `@scope` attribute value from the `<related-links>` element above, which results in the handling of the `@href` attributes to be thrown to the `xsl:otherwise` condition in the `determine-final-href` template, which applies templates with the `ditamsg:unknown-extension` mode and leaves the `@href` attribute untouched.

Because there's no template with the `ditamsg:unknown-extension` mode in `xsl/xslhtml/rel-links.xsl`, the title of the topicref being linked to is prepended to the `@href` attribute value in the output file, which obviously results in an invalid link.

That problem is easily fixed by copying `ditamsg:unknown-extension` from `xsl/troff/rel-links.xsl`, for example, but that still leaves the `@href` attribute values unmodified in the final output file, which means that they'll have `$DITAEXT` as their extension rather than `.html`.

One workaround is to assign the `@scope` attributes to the individual `<link>` elements rather than the `<related-links>` element like so:
<related-links format="html">
 <link href="http://www.example.org" scope="external">
 <linktext>Example 1</linktext>
 </link>
 <link href="http://www.example.com" scope="external">
 <linktext>Example 2</linktext>
 </link>
 </related-links>

title: DITA-OT Issue #1344: <related-links> element breaks child links
content: The [spec](http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/v1.2/os/spec/langref/related-links.html#related-links) says the `@scope` attribute value is allowed in `<related-links>` elements, though, so I think that should be possible without breaking the child links, too.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1361: An easier way to send customization parameters to stylesheets
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1361: An easier way to send customization parameters to stylesheets
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1361: An easier way to send customization parameters to stylesheets
content:
See this [thread](http://tech.groups.yahoo.com/group/dita-users/message/26982) for an use-case.

When making customizations to the DITA OT XSLT stylesheets some developers feel the need to take in the stylesheets different choices (or do use different values) depending on custom parameters which they set to the ANT process.

Unfortunately setting a new system property to the ANT process is not enough, they also need to modify the build files and pass that new parameter to the XSLT stylesheets. Then the XSLT stylesheets need to be modified in order to add a new `xsl:param` which will receive the value from the build process.

I think this approach could be simplified. For example in XSLT the method `system-property(string)` can be used to obtain the value of a system property. Unfortunately the `<xslt>` task does not seem to pass by default system properties from the ANT process to the stylesheets.

But the ANT `<xslt>` task seem to be able to receive a [`<syspropertyset>`](http://ant.apache.org/manual/Types/propertyset.html) which could specify that all command line parameters could be passed as system properties to the transformer.

I have not tried this but the end result would mean that the user would pass an additional param to ANT and the param would be read in the stylesheets using `system-property(string)`.

Maybe this would also mean that future parameters which are used for XSLT customization would not need to be specified in the ANT build files and defined as xsl:param in the stylesheets.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1391: Add new job status file format
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1391: Add new job status file format
content: Issue #1391 is closed with labels architecture, feature, priority/medium. Retrieval signals: map, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1391: Add new job status file format
content:
DITA-OT has two job status files, `dita.list` and `dita.xml.properties`, that are both Java properties files. The properties file only supports String to String mapping, thus file lists are represented comma separated lists. As a result, DITA-OT doesn't support commas in file names.

A new job status storage format should be added to enable file lists which retain each file path as a separate entity. The format should also support map values, to support e.g. key mapping and should be extendable to be able to also include various preprocessing cache files.

The file format could be YAML or JSON, but this would require new library dependencies. Thus the format should be XML.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1398: Allow defining source input base directory
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1398: Allow defining source input base directory
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1398: Allow defining source input base directory
content:
Currently input is defined with `args.input` and the processing assumes the the source base directory is the input file parent directory. When files are referenced which are outside the base directory, uplevels are automatically adjusted based on `outer.control`. There is no way to define which is the directory which is used as the base directory. On hosted DITA-OT installations, this may present a security hole if `outer.control=warn` is used, or content may be left unprocessed if `outer.control=fail` is used.
Add `args.input.dir` to allow explicitly specifying input base directory.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1402: Foreign and Unknown elements not ignored in PDF
content:
Unknown elements should be ignored by default, when special coding is not provided for a specific set of unknown content. 

Foreign is similar, though the spec says that content should be passed through; I think this is generally only true for HTML, and even there it is probably not the best default.

We should add a rule to PDF processing to skip processing these elements by default.

Tested by adding this to one of the sample topics:
Other default transform types in the DITA-OT already hide this content by default (tested with XHTML variants, ODT, RTF, DocBook, TROFF).

title: DITA-OT Issue #1412: abbreviated-form element poorly supported
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1412: abbreviated-form element poorly supported
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1412: abbreviated-form element poorly supported
content: Issue #1412 is closed with labels feature, priority/medium, stale. Retrieval signals: map, pdf, html.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1412: abbreviated-form element poorly supported
content:
This is a more general case of bug #1193.

The abbreviated-form element is not well-handled by the OT for either PDF or XHTML output. In the case of PDF, nothing is output at all. In XHTML, the glossterm is always output, regardless of whether this is first use or not. The glossSurfaceForm or glossAcronym are never output.

I believe that the DITA 1.2 spec defines the abbreviated-form element to solve the tricky problem in topic-based authoring of first-use and subsequent use for terms that get abbreviations. At Oracle, we take this problem seriously, and it is a major concern that the OT, which is supposed to be a reference implementation, does not support the behavior intended by the spec.

Please escalate this! 

Here are my suggestions for how the DITA OT could process abbreviated-form. Please refer to this paper as a reference: https://www.oasis-open.org/committees/download.php/38692/DITA1.2FeatureDescriptionAcronym.pdf

**\* For Maps and submaps (excluding bookmap and submaps of bookmap):
- First occurrence in a topic uses long (glossSurfaceForm) form and all subsequent occurrences in the same topic use the abbreviation. No other behavior and no assumptions made across topics.

**\* For Bookmap:
- Provide an ANT parameter to set the "what constitutes a first occurrence" preference. Possible values: part, chapter, indent1, indent2, topic.
- First occurrence, as defined in the parameter, gets glossSurfaceForm and subsequent occurrences get abbreviation. 
- I actually believe that a value of part is extreme, but someone might want it.

**\* Examples for bookmap:

If parameter=chapter, then only the first occurrence in the chapter gets the glossSurfaceForm, and all other occurrences in the chapter get the abbreviation. The next chapter starts all over.

If parameter=level1, then each time the first indent level under a chapter (in the TOC) changes, then there is a new first occurrence. level1 could be viewed as equivalent to a Sect1 in DocBook. And so on.

If parameter=topic, then each new topic can have a first occurrence and behavior is the same as I suggested for maps and submaps.

Notice I don't distinguish between XHTML and PDF for bookmaps. In my opinion, the two transtypes behave the same. No doubt I've missed something. Thanks.

The @class attribute from the <mapref> element ("+ map/topicref mapgroup-d/mapref ") does not cascade to the referenced map.

Mapref implementation incorrectly cascades the mapref class to referenced elements.

content:

title: DITA-OT Issue #1414: The ANT build should fail by default if the XSL-FO processor cannot create the PDF file
content:
By default the ANT process finishes with success even if the creation of the PDF by the XSL-FO process failed. This is bad, the user might have the impression that the PDF was updated and in fact it was not.

There are three cases:

1) Apache FOP is used. Unfortunately the Apache FOP ANT task never fails, it just reports errors in the console, see https://issues.apache.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=54219, so this should either be patched in the DITA OT or wait for a fix on the Apache FOP side.

2) RenderX XEP is used. The build file has a parameter "xep.failOnError" but by default it is set to "false". In my opinion the default should be changed to "true".

3) Antenna House is called by using `<exec>`. In my opinion it should also set a failonerror="true" on the task or at least have a parameter for this like the XEP task.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1418: PDF2 transtype breaks when bookmap has parts
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1418: PDF2 transtype breaks when bookmap has parts
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1418: PDF2 transtype breaks when bookmap has parts
content: Issue #1418 is closed with labels bug, plugin/pdf, priority/medium. Retrieval signals: map, pdf, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1418: PDF2 transtype breaks when bookmap has parts
content:
The PDF2 transtype in DITA-OT 1.6.3 breaks in several places when a bookmap has book parts (the part element) as parent of chapter elements. In several places the code assumes that the highest level (last) ancestor of an element containing class=topic/topic is a topic that represents a chapter, whereas in a bookmap with parts, this is not true. Because of this, key markers fail to be set.

One of the areas that breaks is here, in commons.xsl:
In this template, the $level variable is expected to be 1 for a chapter and 2 for a topic that is at the first TOC level under a chapter (the equivalent of a Sect1 in DocBook). When a part is present, a chapter topic gets level 2 and the Sect1 topic gets level 3, and so the markers are not set when they should be. A fix for this would be to fix the following template to take parts into account if they are there:
<xsl:template match="*" mode="get-topic-level" as="xs:integer">
<xsl:if test="not(ancestor::*[contains(@class, ' topic/topic ')])">
prevents the current-header marker from being set, because there actually is a topic/topic ancestor for the chapter, which is the part.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1426: PDF creation fails with "com.suite.sol.ditaot.DetectLang cannot be found"
content:
**Issue only affects DITA-OT 1.7.**

If you follow the instructions in the [Building](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot#building) section and after that try to run `ant -f build_demo.xml` and choose the `pdf` output type, the build fails with an error like this:
$DITA_HOME/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/build.xml:178: taskdef class com.suite.sol.ditaot.DetectLang cannot be found
The bug was introduced in c1ca4064451da6e06d3581a3d18cb8b43416956d: the problem is that `fo.jar` isn't built when you run the `jar` target. Something like https://github.com/emth/dita-ot/commit/e4c00cd2531ed85f24fb282edfb07283119a3879 is one option, but you could also just modify the [instructions](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot#building) to mention that you also need to run `ant jar.plug-ins` after running `ant jar`.

Moreover, as opposed to what the instructions say, it seems to me that having just `src/main/lib` in `CLASSPATH` is not enough. Setting your `CLASSPATH` to include nothing but `src/main/lib/icu4j.jar` and `src/main/lib/resolver.jar` is sufficient, though.

(You _could_ also do something like `ant -lib $DITA_HOME/lib jar`, I suppose.)

content:
Applies to (at least) OT 1.5.4, 1.6.1, 1.7, PDF output with FOP, XEP. Not tested with Antenna House.

Scenario: I have a reltable that specifies that TopicA should have a related link to TopicB and TopicC. I use this reltable with a map that does not reference TopicC. In the resulting PDF output, TopicA contains a working related link to TopicB and a non-working related link to TopicC. Neither the map nor the reltable use @collection-type. This is not the expected behavior. Descriptions of reltable functionality specify that reltables do not generate related links to topics that are not referenced by the input map. This is the behavior observed in XHTML and HTML Help builds.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1438: Problem with whitespace in CHM index generation

title: DITA-OT Issue #1438: Problem with whitespace in CHM index generation
content:
A CHM index may contain multiple index entries where there should be only one. This occurs, for example, if the indexterm contains a trailing space in one location, but no trailing space in a second location (but the outcome also changes if source code formatting is applied). In the PDF output with XEP, these entries are grouped correctly as I would expect it.
In addition, in CHM output, empty indexterms cause warnings during the conversion and **\* entries in the output. When transforming to PDF with XEP, these entries are just ignored. While I would like to have an option to detect empty indexterms, I think this should be done in an optional validation.
Data to reproduce can be found here: https://gist.github.com/4569515

- h2d
- legacypdf
- net.sourceforge.dita4publishers
- net.sourceforge.dita4publishers/common.html
- net.sourceforge.dita4publishers/common.mapdriven
- net.sourceforge.dita4publishers/common.xslt
- net.sourceforge.dita4publishers/xmldomain.html
- (...)
- org.dita/
- org.dita/base
- org.dita/docbook
- (...)
- org.uottawa/
- (...)
If I have 10 plugins for org.mycompany, I could have 10 repositories in git and one repository linking to all the submodules. I would be abbe to clone directly into org.mycompany. And If I use repositories from others people, like dita4publishers, there will be no conflict.

content:

title: DITA-OT Issue #1463: Image as child of "dt" may result in duplicate text
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1463: Image as child of "dt" may result in duplicate text
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1463: Image as child of "dt" may result in duplicate text
content:
When a definition term contains an image but no text, and the image uses the alt attribute, that alt text appears as the contents of the term (in addition to the image).

This is caused by the mode "pull-in-title", which runs after the contents of `<dt>` are processed.

The "pull-in-title" does some fancy key work, but in this case no keys are used. The last condition checks to see if the contents of the element are empty using normalize-space; if they are, it processes with "text-only". In this case normalize-space returns an empty string because there is no text content; text-only returns the alt text of the already-processed image.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1464: Flagging a simpletable row throws off @keycol counting
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1464: Flagging a simpletable row throws off @keycol counting
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1464: Flagging a simpletable row throws off @keycol counting
content:
The check to see if an entry is part of the "keycol" column counts entries by assuming that only entries can be in the row:
<xsl:variable name="thiscolnum">
 <xsl:value-of select="number(count(preceding-sibling::*)+1)"/>
</xsl:variable>
When flagging is active on a row, there are extra elements added to the row, which throws off the count. Fix to dita2htmlImpl.xsl (and similar fixes in taskdisplay.xsl and refdisplay.xsl) should only count entries:
<xsl:variable name="thiscolnum">
 <xsl:value-of select="number(count(preceding-sibling::*[contains(@class,' topic/stentry ')])+1)"/>
</xsl:variable>

title: DITA-OT Issue #1465: New doc topic listing non-standard tweaks to preprocessed files

DITA-OT Issue #1465: New doc topic listing non-standard tweaks to preprocessed files

content: Issue #1465 is closed with labels feature. Retrieval signals: map, dita-ot, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1465: New doc topic listing non-standard tweaks to preprocessed files
content:
In a few cases, output from the DITA-OT preprocess may add elements to the temporary topics that would not otherwise conform to the DITA standard or original DITA document type. For example, to simplify processing for a variety of output formats, the preprocess may detect image information and add @dita-ot:image-width or @dita-ot:image-height to the image element.

We should add a topic to the developer section of the doc that clearly lists all such modifications, so that 1) other extensions can take advantage of them, and 2) new transform types written based on strictly conforming documents can be aware of them.

I currently envision 3 sections in a single topic:
1. Modifications that would not comply with the original doctype (like those above)
2. Modifications that are valid according to the OASIS document types, but _may_ not comply with more restrictive specializations. For example, adding map-based links to a topic type that excludes `<related-links>`
3. Modifications that are generally not intended to comply with the original doctype. For example, chunking may pull many topic types into one document, even if no existing doctype explicitly allows that combination of nesting.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1468: Reference to remote image does not appear in PDF

title: DITA-OT Issue #1468: Reference to remote image does not appear in PDF
content:
The PDF output does not contain the image.

This happens because the generated XSL-FO prepends to the image @href the base input directory instead of leaving it unchanged (being an absolute URL).

In the XSL:

DITA-OT/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/xsl/fo/commons.xsl

the template:
<xsl:template match="*[contains(@class,' topic/image ')]">
should declare a variable like:
<xsl:variable name="finalHref">
 <xsl:choose>
 <xsl:when test="contains(@href, ':/')">
 <!-- Absolute reference. -->
 <xsl:value-of select="@href"/>
 </xsl:when>
 <xsl:otherwise>
 <xsl:value-of select="concat($input.dir.url, @href)"/>
 </xsl:otherwise>
 </xsl:choose>
 </xsl:variable>

I'm facing a serious problem found in DITA-OT 1.7.3. The problem is that DITA-OT TopicMerge sets unexpected `@xml:lang` attribute to topic. Here is a example.

[bookmap: sample_ja.bookmap]
<bookmap xml:lang="ja" id="GUID-BC13DC41-C380-4E24-9047-B0E6018F4D86">

 xml:lang="en" oid="concept_D941EF43C15A40D0BF155B7C5B8003F0" id="unique_1">

content:

title: DITA-OT Issue #1482: Incorrect processing of subject scheme maps
content: Issue #1482 is closed with labels bug, preprocess, preprocess/filtering, preprocess/keyref, priority/medium, stale. Retrieval signals: keyref, map, html, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1482: Incorrect processing of subject scheme maps
content:
DITA-OT 1.7 does not handle subject scheme maps properly in regard to validating the attribute values against the specified subject schemes. While the simplest test yields the expected warning messages when the content contains attribute values not specified in the subject scheme, it requires that the subjectScheme map be referenced with type="subjectScheme" specified. (The DITA 1.2 spec does not suggest this behavior; if it is a DITA-OT requirement, we need to document it.) 

More realistic test cases using schemeref elements simply fail, however, regardless of whether type="subjectScheme" is specified.

The DITA maps and topic are located at https://gist.github.com/keberlein/5237276 .
<subjectdef keys="operating-systems">
 <subjectdef keys="linux">
 <subjectdef keys="redhat"/>
 <subjectdef keys="suse"/>
 </subjectdef>
 <subjectdef keys="unix"/>
 <subjectdef keys="windows">
 <subjectdef keys="windows7"/>
 <subjectdef keys="windows8"/>
 </subjectdef>
</subjectdef>
One DITA topic with following values for the platform attribute: ubuntu, mandriva, solaris
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE map PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Map//EN" "map.dtd">
<map>
 <title>Example of a map referencing a subject scheme</title>
 <mapref href="baseScheme-with-enumeration.ditamap" type="subjectScheme"/>
 <topicref href="t-creating-controlled-values.dita"/>

title: DITA-OT Issue #1482: Incorrect processing of subject scheme maps
content:
</map>

**The expected results are generated -- warning messages**
[filter] [DOTJ049W][WARN] The attribute value platform="mandriva" on element "step" does not comply with the specified subject scheme. According to the subject scheme map, the following values are valid for the platform attribute: redhat,windows8,windows7,windows,suse,linux,unix,operating-systems
 …
 [filter] [DOTJ049W][WARN] The attribute value platform="solaris" on element "step" does not comply with the specified subject scheme. According to the subject scheme map, the following values are valid for the platform attribute: redhat,windows8,windows7,windows,suse,linux,unix,operating-systems
Unfortunately, the DITA-OT is incorrectly building the list of valid labels; it should NOT include operating-systems, according to the examples and guidance provided in the DITA 1.2 spec. See the examples in http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/v1.2/os/spec/langref/subjectScheme.html#subjectScheme , as well as http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/v1.2/os/spec/langref/enumerationdef.html#enumerationdef
I removed type=’’subjectScheme” from the <mapref> element Test-2.ditamap. **As a result, no warning messages are generated.**

title: DITA-OT Issue #1482: Incorrect processing of subject scheme maps
content:
Here the master map references a subjectScheme map which in turn references another subjectScheme map. This is standard use case that is outlined in the DITA 1.2 spec.

**Test-3.ditamap** contains the following content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE map PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Map//EN" "map.dtd">
<map>
 <title>Example of a map referencing a subject scheme</title>
 <mapref href="extensionScheme.ditamap" type="subjectScheme"/>
 <topicref href="t-creating-controlled-values.dita"/>
</map>

**extensionScheme.ditamap** contains the following content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE subjectScheme PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Subject Scheme Map//EN" "subjectScheme.dtd">
<subjectScheme>
 <schemeref href="baseScheme.ditamap"/>
 <enumerationdef>
 <attributedef name="platform"/>
 <subjectdef keyref="operating-systems"/>
 </enumerationdef>
</subjectScheme>
**Results:** No warning messages.
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE subjectScheme PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Subject Scheme Map//EN" "subjectScheme.dtd">
<subjectScheme>
 <schemeref href="baseScheme.ditamap" type="subjectScheme"/>
 <enumerationdef>
 <attributedef name="platform"/>
 <subjectdef keyref="operating-systems"/>
 </enumerationdef>
</subjectScheme>

title: DITA-OT Issue #1484: Enable default revision markers using active xml:lang value
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1484: Enable default revision markers using active xml:lang value
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1484: Enable default revision markers using active xml:lang value
content:
**Note - originally submitted this issue as a minor bug against new code, but that new code wasn't actually checked in. Now adding in the complete working new code. Original comments remain here, see first comment for follow-up.**

The flagging pre-process includes the ability to set up default revision markers, using the canned text "Start of change" and "End of change". 

This default is commented out by default, but we enable it in an override. The text is generated in the context of the `<revprop>` element in the DITAVAL, so the active xml:lang value is unavailable. For that reason we pass in the active xml:lang as a parameter.

When two `<revprop>` elements apply in one element, the first one takes in the xml:lang parameter, but does not pass it to processing for the second `<revprop>`, so the language is lost. The code should be updated to pass the language for additional default revisions:
<xsl:apply-templates select="following-sibling::revprop[1]" mode="start-revflagit">
 <xsl:with-param name="lang" select="$lang"/>
 <xsl:with-param name="biditest" select="$biditest"/>
 </xsl:apply-templates>

title: DITA-OT Issue #1489: External keys are lost if using onlytopic.in.map
content:
The "onlytopic.in.map" argument is supposed to cause XHTML build to generate HTML topics for only those documents referenced from the map (not targets of `<xref>`). 

I have a map with external and peer `<keydef>` elements. When I run a normal build, the keys are added to the keydef.xml file in our temp directory, allowing key processing to work with them later. When I activate the "onlytopic.in.map" the code in GenListModuleReader kicks out of element processing for external/peer topicref elements, before it actually processes @keys, so they are never added to keydef.xml.

Processing for each element starts with startElement:
https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/develop/src/main/java/org/dita/dost/reader/GenListModuleReader.java#L634

Inside startElement, we check to see if onlyTopicInMap is true:
if (outputUtils.getOnlyTopicInMap() && this.canResolved()) {

If so, a few lines later, we return from startElement if the target is external/peer:
if (ATTR_SCOPE_VALUE_EXTERNAL.equalsIgnoreCase(attrScope) ...

Down at the end of startElement, we process @keys:
parseAttribute(atts, ATTRIBUTE_NAME_KEYS);

To reproduce, I just edited our hierarchy.ditamap sample to begin with:

title: DITA-OT Issue #1489: External keys are lost if using onlytopic.in.map
content:
<topicref href="tasks/garagetaskoverview.xml" type="concept">
 <keydef href="http://www.ibm.com" scope="external" navtitle="ibm" keys="ibm"/>
 <keydef href="tasks/organizing.xml" navtitle="local key" keys="organize"/>
 <topicref keys="oil" href="tasks/changingtheoil.xml" type="task"/>
 <topicref href="tasks/organizing.xml" type="task"/>
And run with this command: ant -f build.xml -Dargs.input=samples/hierarchy.ditamap -Dtranstype=xhtml -Dclean.temp=no -Donlytopic.in.map=true
In the temp dir, the key "ibm" is dropped from keydef.xml when onlytopic.in.map is true.
