title: DITA-OT Issue #1517: start-indent in attribute-sets body__toplevel and body__secondLevel being ignored in conbody and refbody
content:
The order of the attribute-sets is backwards (it should be xsl:use-attribute-sets="conbody body__toplevel"). As it is, the default value for start-indent--obtained from attribute-set conbody--overwrites the value specified in attribute-set body__toplevel. This means that attribute-set body__toplevel becomes useless for conbody because it only contains attribute start-indent. A parallel problem also occurs with attribute sets body__secondLevel and conbody (it should be xsl:use-attribute-sets="conbody body__secondLevel").

A similar precedence error also occurs with refbody in reference-elements.xsl.

Fall through code for body is working correctly.

content: Issue #1527 is closed with labels feature, plugin/xhtml, priority/low, stale. Retrieval signals: map, html, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1527: Create dynamic filters that use subject scheme maps in XHTML output
content:
XHTML output produces static web pages. To produce web pages for different audiences (in the broadest sense), it's possible to filter content using DITAVAL files.

For example, it's possible to specialize a new profiling attribute, populate a list of its possible values from a subject scheme map, and filter on chosen values using DITAVAL files.

We can make these filters as complex as we want but ultimately we need to create static XHTML pages for each desired combination.

As a feature request, can I suggest adding a (Javascript-enabled?) transform that adds a drop down menu to a web page, and allows the content to be filtered dynamically using values obtained from subject scheme maps.

This would allow a single output to be created that would satisfy all possible readers.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1535: Specialized class cannot be handled during XML parsing
content:
I have created a class inherited the topic/entry class by specialization. While parsing the Dita file, I found that some of the attributes such as namest, nameend are missing. 
The reason is the DitaWriter class override the method startElement() and it filter those attributes in method processAttributes(). And those specialization classes are not included in method copyElementName(). 
I would suggest to use TOPIC_ENTRY.matcher to check with the class attribute of the element instead of comparing to qName. 
Thanks. 

Ben

title: DITA-OT Issue #1537: Whitespace issue when @conref is preceded by a linefeed in map <title>
content:
I'm seeing what I believe is a bug in the conref processing in OT 1.8. I have a ph with @conref in a map title. When the ph containing the @conref is preceded by a linefeed, no whitespace appears in the resolved title. When the ph containing the @conref is preceded by a space, all is well. Additionally, when a similar @conref appears in a topic and is preceded by a linefeed, whitespace appears before the conref'ed ph as expected. The error only appears to occur when the @conref occurs inside a map title. This error occurs in both XHTML and PDF output generated from a default OT 1.8 instance.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1543: Topics referred to in both a <reltable> and a regular DITA map are wrongly interpreted as resource-only in HTML transtypes
content:
In the DITA-OT user guide, these topics are referred to in both `reltable.ditamap` and other DITA maps:
- `readme/distribution_packages.dita`
- `readme/DITA-globalization-xhtml.dita`
- `dev_ref/plugin-addgeneratedtext.dita`

`<topicref>` elements that are descendants of `<reltable>` elements get interpreted as resource-only topics. I'm not quite sure how this happens because it doesn't seem like those `<topicref>` elements inherit the attribute value from the DTD and my Java-fu isn't strong enough to figure it out by just looking at the code, but [I do think it's supposed to be like that (see #13021)](https://wiki.oasis-open.org/dita/DITA_1.3_Proposals).

In any case, since the topicrefs I listed above are referred to in both `reltable.ditamap` _and_ other DITA maps (with an implied processing role of "normal"), they should appear in the HTML output as usual, but at the moment, they don't. You can check for yourself by trying to open the "[Supported languages: HTML-based transformations](http://dita-ot.github.io/1.8/readme/DITA-globalization-xhtml.html)" section in the user guide.

The really interesting thing about this issue is that which topics are interpreted as resource-only in this situation seems to be dependent on the operating system. I tried running `ant site` on a clean dita-ot/dita-ot GitHub checkout (the `develop` branch) on Windows, OS X, and Linux, and it was _only_ on Windows that `dev_ref/plugin-addgeneratedtext.dita` was interpreted as resource-only — on OS X and Linux, only the other two topicrefs were affected. Again, you can see this for yourself by trying to open "[Modifying or adding generated text](http://dita-ot.github.io/1.8/dev_ref/plugin-addgeneratedtext.html)" (I suspect the current version was produced on a Mac).

This patch seems to fix the issue:

title: DITA-OT Issue #1545: Inconsistencies between plugins when flagging the root element of a topic
content:
Flagging the root element of a topic does work in for example the html plugin. But it doesn't work in pdf2. 

There's a comment in the code (plugins/org.dita.pdf2/xsl/fo/flagging-preprocess.xsl) which suggests that flagging shouldn't work:

 <!-- Don't flag topics, just like in the HTML output -->
 <xsl:template match="*[contains(@class, ' topic/topic ')]" 

But I suspect this comment predates the 1.7 flagging updates.

I would like to make flagging work on the topic root element for pdf2 and have worked out how to fix the code.

Also discussed here: http://tech.groups.yahoo.com/group/dita-users/message/31152

Nigel

title: DITA-OT Issue #1546: changes to domain attr set files require inclusion of XSLT stylesheet
content: OT 1.8 (and previous versions). When creating a PDF plugin, it's necessary to include the corresponding XSLT stylesheet when including a domain attribute set file in the plugin. For example, if I include ui-domain-attr.xsl in my plugin and make customizations to the uicontrol attribute set, I have to also include ui-domain.xsl in my plugin in order to see the customizations. This is unlike other attribute set files, where it is not necessary to include the corresponding XSLT stylesheet just to see the changes. Is this by design?

title: DITA-OT Issue #1557: enable <tm> to accommodate copyright symbol
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1557: enable <tm> to accommodate copyright symbol
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1557: enable <tm> to accommodate copyright symbol
content: Currently, the <tm> element can output trademark, registered trademark, and service mark symbols, depending on the value of @tmtype. A gap in this paradigm is the copyright symbol, which must be manually included via the literal or numeric character or by using, for example, @otherprops to mimic the processing for the other three symbols. Another consequence of the lack of copyright symbol processing is that the formatting for the copyright symbol must be done in font-mappings.xml and/or an i18n file rather than via an attribute set, as is the case with the other three symbols. A fourth valid value for <tm> would make life a little easier. (It seems unlikely that no one has ever requested this, but a search of this repository did not turn up any issues. My apologies if it is a duplicate.)

title: DITA-OT Issue #1565: FILTERFILEDOC variable is broken when no filter file is used
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1565: FILTERFILEDOC variable is broken when no filter file is used
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1565: FILTERFILEDOC variable is broken when no filter file is used
content:
<xsl:variable name="FILTERDOC" select="document($FILTERFILEURL,/)"/>
When there is no filter file, the $FILTERFILEURL variable is empty, and the document() function ends up creating a copy of the entire input file.

For the default OT install, this is no longer much of an issue, because the code was refactored in version 1.7 to move flag processing into a pre-processing step. However the dita4publishers code makes use of $FILTERDOC to test for images in the filter file, and copy those images to the output directory. We should fix the $FILTERDOC variable so that if there is no filter file, the variable does not copy the main input file.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1571: pdf2 plugin: top level topic titles styled as normal text
content:
<bookmap>
 <booktitle>
 <mainbooktitle>...
 </booktitle>

 <bookmeta>...
 </bookmeta>

 <frontmatter toc="no">
 <topicref href="colophon.dita" format="dita">
 </topicref>
 <booklists>
 <toc/>
 </booklists>
 </frontmatter>

 <part><topicref href="reference.ditamap" format="ditamap" /></part>
</bookmap>
Individual documentation projects use this master unmodified, and provide a custom copy of reference.ditamap which is a normal map file.

We are producing booklet size documents, a few pages up to around 50 pages long.

We do it this way so that we have the bookmap control over frontmatter. We do not have sections or chapters.
However the top level topics have a calculated topic level of 0 and are formatted as normal sans text.

This occurs because the bookmap/part occurence is subtracted from the topic level when it shouldn't be. It should be substracted if and only if the part has a href refering to a local dita topic. However the topic level calculation does not take that into account.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1571: pdf2 plugin: top level topic titles styled as normal text
content:
<xsl:template match="*" mode="get-topic-level" as="xs:integer">
 <xsl:variable name="topicref" select="key('map-id', ancestor-or-self::*[contains(@class,' topic/topic ')][1]/@id)"/>
 <xsl:sequence select="count(ancestor-or-self::*[contains(@class,' topic/topic ')]) -
 count($topicref/ancestor-or-self::*[contains(@class,' bookmap/part ') or
 (contains(@class,' bookmap/appendices ') and
 exists(@href) and
 (empty(@format) or @format eq 'dita') and
 (empty(@scope) or @scope eq 'local'))])"/>
 </xsl:template>
should have some bracketing changed so that the check for for a href to a local scoped dita topic applies to both the bookmap/part case as well as the existing bookmap/appendices part.

thus
<xsl:template match="*" mode="get-topic-level" as="xs:integer">
 <xsl:variable name="topicref" select="key('map-id', ancestor-or-self::*[contains(@class,' topic/topic ')][1]/@id)"/>
 <xsl:sequence select="count(ancestor-or-self::*[contains(@class,' topic/topic ')]) -
 count($topicref/ancestor-or-self::*[(contains(@class,' bookmap/part ') or contains(@class,' bookmap/appendices ')) and
 exists(@href) and
 (empty(@format) or @format eq 'dita') and
 (empty(@scope) or @scope eq 'local')])"/>
 </xsl:template>

title: DITA-OT Issue #1577: Remove default finger image for notes in PDF
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1577: Remove default finger image for notes in PDF
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1577: Remove default finger image for notes in PDF
content:
Breaking this item out from the bug reported in issue #1234 . 

I've had several people report that the finger image used in PDF to highlight <note> elements is offensive for some cultures, and generally just not a good default for the PDF code. The image has been used since the original code was developed by Idiom, and I'm not aware of any actual request to remove it. Both @keberlein and @mkaatman have recently mentioned the cultural problems, so I'm opening this issue for any discussion / removal.

In a default build, the image is set to appear for note elements with @type set to note, notice, fastpath, important, remeber, restriction, tip, or other. Right now I'm inclined to leave the variables in each locale file, but set them to empty for these types. As a result, we'll continue to check for images -- so users who override the image with their own will see no change. The default processing would find no image, so the note would have less indentation (spanning the space currently covered by image and text).

title: DITA-OT Issue #1581: Change bars from DITAVAL crash FOP
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1581: Change bars from DITAVAL crash FOP
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1581: Change bars from DITAVAL crash FOP
content:
Breaking this off from issue #1175 

When using changebar in a DITAVAL for revisions, the PDF code creates `<fo:change-bar-begin>` and `<fo:change-bar-end>` in the current context of the document. This means that for nearly every case, those elements become children of `<fo:block>` or `<fo:inline>`. This doesn't meet the letter of the XSL-FO spec, which only allows change bars as a child of `<fo:flow>`. When FOP encounters the change bars in these locations, it crashes.

We should update the build so that when using FOP, we skip generating those change bar elements, allowing the build to finish. AH currently ignores the elements, so we may as well leave them in, in case support comes along later. I'm not sure about XEP, but I think the original testing with this code used XEP so I'm guessing it either supports or ignores the markup.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1600: Indirect reference to keys erases one file, causes failures
content:
Encountered an issue similar to this with a much larger sample, encountered this specific issue while trying to debug the original with a clean set of samples. 

In my original case, the product defines a large set of plugins. Each set defines content in one set of maps, and creates a related map to define keys for topics in that plug-in.

All plug-ins pull in a common map from a peer directory, which in turn pulls in every key map. The result: every plug-in pulls in the common key map with a single topicref, which in turn pulls in key definitions from every plug-in; everybody can then use the common keys. No files are generated from outside the plug-in, but keys are retrieved.

When I construct a similar sample with the hierarchy samples, using 1.8.2, I get a java crash during the dit2xhtml stage. In this case all of my content and all of my keys are inside of samples/ but I go out and back in to define the keys. Checking the temp directory shows that tasks/washingthecar.xml is empty (zero length file), even though it is defined the same as other files. The only way this runs is if I set generate.copy.outer=3, which adjusts the output directory, even though no files are generated outside of that directory.

To reproduce, add this line to samples/hierarchy.ditamap:
Create this file peer/allkeys.ditamap:

title: DITA-OT Issue #1600: Indirect reference to keys erases one file, causes failures
content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE map PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Map//EN"
 "../dtd/technicalContent/dtd/map.dtd">
<map>
 <topicref href="../samples/samplekeys.ditamap" format="ditamap"/>
</map>
And create samples/samplekeys.ditamap:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE map PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Map//EN"
 "../dtd/technicalContent/dtd/map.dtd">
<map title="keys">
 <topicref href="tasks/garagetaskoverview.xml" type="concept" keys="overview"
 processing-role="resource-only"/>
 <topicref href="concepts/lawnmower.xml" type="concept" keys="lawnmower"
 processing-role="resource-only"/>
</map>
I get the failure with this command:
C:\DITA-OT1.8.M2>ant -f build.xml -Dargs.input=samples/hierarchy.ditamap -Dtranstype=xhtml -Dclean.temp=no 

I get a "clean" build with this:
C:\DITA-OT1.8.M2>ant -f build.xml -Dargs.input=samples/hierarchy.ditamap -Dtranstype=xhtml -Dclean.temp=no -Douter.control=quiet -Dgenerate.copy.outer=3

The clean build adjusts the output directory, which isn't actually needed, but is more of a minor annoyance than anything (I am not surprised by that when using -Dgenerate.copy.outer=3).

title: DITA-OT Issue #1604: Failed to read job file: XML document structures must start and end within the same entity.
content:
One of our clients obtained this error quite frequently in her transformations. How I think this happens:
1) You run a transformation which fails for some reason (out of memory for example). Probably the temporary files folder remains without being deleted. 2) You run a second transformation after giving the application more memory (or after removing the error from the first one). This second transformation fails with errors like:
[gen-list] [Fatal Error] :1:150693: XML document structures must start and end within the same entity.
 [gen-list] GenMapAndTopicListModule.execute(): Execution time: 1.991 seconds

 BUILD FAILED
 C:\PFW\Oxygen XML Editor 15.1\frameworks\dita\DITA-OT\build.xml:56: The following error occurred while executing this line:
 C:\PFW\Oxygen XML Editor 15.1\frameworks\dita\DITA-OT\plugins\org.dita.base\build_preprocess.xml:32: Failed to run pipeline: Failed to create empty job: Failed to read job file: XML document structures must start and end within the same entity.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1604: Failed to read job file: XML document structures must start and end within the same entity.
content:
Removing the temporary files folder manually and retrying solves the issue.

In my opinion this jobs.xml file should be forcefully deleted sometime very early at the beginning of a transformation.
Or if the user has opted to clean the temporary files directory (by default it is cleaned) to also try to remove this folder before the transformation as well as trying to remove it after it because incomplete data might be inside it.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1610: Filtered content leads to total fail of PDF rendering
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1610: Filtered content leads to total fail of PDF rendering
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1610: Filtered content leads to total fail of PDF rendering
content:
DITA-OT can filter content before rendering it thanks to the processing of .ditaval files.

This worked reliably until DITA-OT moved to FOP 1.x. Since then, it will fail rendering of PDF completely due to the fact that FOP 1.x is more strict about empty tables. The problem is caused by the fact that in case the .ditaval filters so much content (intentionally!) that a table will effectively is empty, instead of skipping the table, it still produces an empty fo:table-body element. Actually this is invalid FO markup, as fo:table-body must never be empty. While FOP 0.x silently ignored this situation, FOP 1.x correctly stops rendering -- with the effect that no PDF file is produced at all!

The solution is rather simple: In case a table will be empty (due to .ditaval filtering or any other condition), no fo:table-body must be produced at all. As a result, the table will be skipped completely, which is correct, since it makes no sense to have a completely empty table in a PDF document (note that 'empty' means 'having really no content', which certainly is something different than 'having a single zero-size cell as its sole content').

As this is a showstopper for me (cannot migrate from DITA-OT 1.5.4 to 1.8 due to that bug) I really beg for a soon fix! :-)

title: DITA-OT Issue #1634: XML Catalog which has a DOCTYPE declaration is not properly parsed by Integrator task
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1634: XML Catalog which has a DOCTYPE declaration is not properly parsed by Integrator task
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1634: XML Catalog which has a DOCTYPE declaration is not properly parsed by Integrator task
content:
<!DOCTYPE catalog PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD XML Catalogs V1.1//EN" "http://www.oasis-open.org/committees/entity/release/1.1/catalog.dtd">
 <catalog xmlns="urn:oasis:names:tc:entity:xmlns:xml:catalog">
 <group prefer="public">
 <public publicId="-//OASIS//DTD DITA MyOilTask//EN" uri="dtd/my_oil_plugin_task.dtd"/>
 </group>
 </catalog>
The org.dita.dost.platform.IntegratorTask will fail to parse the XML because the "org.dita.dost.platform.InsertAction" does not set a catalog resolver to the XML Reader created via the "org.dita.dost.util.StringUtils.getXMLReader()" utility method and thus the DOCTYPE public ID fails to be resolved to a DTD.

When the Catalog Manager from Xerces parses XML Catalogs it uses the org.apache.xml.resolver.helpers.BootstrapResolver to resolve references the XML Catalogs themselves might have to DTDs.

System.err.println("Encoded :" + new File("/home/test/projets en développement/eXml/test/dita/transform6/map.ditamap").toURI().toURL());
 new URI(new File("/home/test/projets en développement/eXml/test/dita/transform6/map.ditamap").toURI().toURL().toString());

title: DITA-OT Issue #1646: Inconsistent link text in keyref links to elements with <title>
content:
The link text for `<xref>` is determined like this:

| topicref | link text |
| --- | --- |
| `@navtitle` | `@navtitle` value |
| `<navtitle>`, no `@navtitle` | `<section>` title |
| no `<navtitle>`, no `@navtitle` | `<section>` title |

Furthermore, it seems that DITA-OT never uses the value of `<navtitle>` as the link text -- only `@navtitle` (see the fourth link in `topic4.dita` in the Gist).

Should the navtitle really ever be used as the link text if the keyref points to an element with a `<title>` child? It seems counterintuitive to me.

DITA-OT Issue #1655: DITA-OT does not rewrite xrefs to topic elements correctly during preprocessing when chunk = "to-content" is specified
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1655: DITA-OT does not rewrite xrefs to topic elements correctly during preprocessing when chunk = "to-content" is specified
content: Issue #1655 is closed with labels bug, preprocess, preprocess/chunking, priority/medium, stale. Retrieval signals: xref, map, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1655: DITA-OT does not rewrite xrefs to topic elements correctly during preprocessing when chunk = "to-content" is specified
content:
When chunk = "to-content" is specified, DITA-OT creates a ditabase document during preprocessing that contains all of the topics that are being chunked. If the topics' IDs contain any duplicates, then unique IDs are generated to make all of the topic IDs unique in the ditabase document. However, xrefs to topic elements don't properly get rewritten. I am enclosing a sample .ditamap containing three topics that demonstrates the problem.

In the sample, the topics intro.dita, topic1.dita, and topic2.dita all contain id = "topicid" on the topic. This is valid since the ID is unique within each topic.

The chunk.ditamap contains chunk = "to-content" on intro.dita telling the DITA-OT that we want intro.dita, topic1.dita, and topic2.dita output as a single file. During preprocessing, the DITA-OT will create intro.dita as a single ditabase document containing the contents of the three topics. Since taken together there would be duplicate IDs, the DITA-OT writes unique IDs for the contents of topic1.dita and topic2.dita in the ditabase document.

The problem is the xrefs in topic1.dita and topic2.dita are not rewritten to contain the new, unique IDs.

Reproducible using DITA-OT1.7.5 and DITA-OT1.8.4.

https://drive.google.com/file/d/0ByZs7YV5C0j0QWV3TVppSGRZXzQ/edit?usp=sharing

title: DITA-OT Issue #1661: Xref handling assumes success in resolving href
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1661: Xref handling assumes success in resolving href
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1661: Xref handling assumes success in resolving href
content: Issue #1661 is closed with labels bug, invalid, plugin/pdf, priority/medium. Retrieval signals: error, xref, pdf, dita-ot, plugin.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1661: Xref handling assumes success in resolving href
content:
<xsl:variable name="destination" select="opentopic-func:getDestinationId(@href)"/>
<xsl:variable name="element" select="key('key_anchor',$destination)[1]"/>
will fail if the destination is resolved to something that is not a node in a document, which will be the case if the @href can't be resolved (e.g., a bogus URL like: `<xref href="urn:error:Unresolvable reference to /w:document/w:body[1]/w:p[70]">`)

The failure message is:

> /Applications/oxygen/frameworks/dita/DITA-OT/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/xsl/fo/links.xsl:218: Fatal Error! In the key() function, the node supplied in the third argument (or the context node if absent) must be in a tree whose root is a document node

The fix is to check the value of $destination and bail if it's not a usable input to the `key()` function.

content: Issue #1664 is closed with labels bug, preprocess, priority/medium. Retrieval signals: map.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1664: Preprocessing results in unexpected output with Java 8
content: Integration tests fail with Java 8 because map metadata does not match expected output. I think this is because ConcurrentHashMap returns items in a different order in Java 8 than in Java 7. This could be fixed by just adjusting expected results, but it's actually a bug in the processing logic and preprocessing should be checked instead. A possible cause is to process map files in so that you serialize the results before all maps are processed, but the output starts to depend on the processing order; instead, the resulting map files should be serialized only after all maps are processed.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1676: When <navtitle> is used in a map, move-meta copies that navtitle to following entries
content:
Noticed this with 1.7.4 but verified in 2.0M3

I have a map that has a few navtitle elements and a few navtitle attributes, using @locktitle in a few instances to lock a local title. After the move-meta step, the first navtitle in my map is copied into all following topicref elements. PARA TEXT The EGM96 geoid is used as a reference. TEXT AFTER

 Then I have another topic "main.dita" which has an inner topic which references to the first one: ABC MAIN

</topic> </topic> and does not work. has a variable "conref-source-topic" which is computed like: <xsl:value-of select="ancestor-or-self::*[contains(@class, ' topic/topic ')][last()]/@id"/> and it actually should be computed like: <xsl:value-of select="ancestor-or-self::*[contains(@class, ' topic/topic ')][1]/@id"/> because the "ancestor-or-self" returns the closest ancestor (in this case the context node which is a topic with a conref) on the "1" index and returns the highest level ancestor on the "last()" index.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1685: New page-sequence generation approach for PDF
content: Issue #1685 is closed with labels feature, plugin/pdf, priority/medium. Retrieval signals: map, pdf.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1685: New page-sequence generation approach for PDF
content:
Current PDF page-sequence generation works so that top-level topics are traversed, the topicType for each topic is determined and based on that a page-sequence is generated. An alternative approach could be added, where the map is traversed instead, page-sequences are generated, and topics are pulled in. These two approaches can be called push and pull, or topic and map driven, respectively.

Both approaches work, but with map driven it's easier to
- generate page-sequence so that map structures at multiple levels are used to determine the output, and
- group topicref structures into single/multiple page-sequences.

The map driven generation could be made the default, but for legacy support the old topic driven generation should be retained. A parameter can be used to determine which implementation to use.

in generate-page-sequence-master there is this conditional page sequence template:

I see the cause of the problem: the post-conref topic has the IDs on the `<entry>` elements rewritten.

Here is the warehouse entry as authored:

title: DITA-OT Issue #1690: External links are broken inside conreffed content
content:
I suspect that the OT does this in order to ensure that there are no ID conflicts in the post-resolution topics--Jarno can confirm.

I know the OT dev team has discussed this in the past and I may have in fact have insisted on this behavior (it's the sort of thing I might have insisted on).

But the doing of it definitely precludes linking into conreffed content as you're trying to do and also precludes the "this topic" addressing I discussed earlier.

This will probably require some discussion among the OT dev team to decide what the best approach is. But my thinking at the moment is that implementors have no choice but to maintain the original IDs in the conreffed content.

This problem could be avoided by adding another form of address indirection, the equivalent of keys but for elements within topics. I proposed such a feature early in the 1.3 work but the TC correctly, I
think, decided it was too much complexity for the value provided.

But the downside is that addressing in the face of conrefs gets a little sticky because you have to rely on things working in a particular way and it leaves open the possibility that of duplicate IDs post conref
resolution. 

But I think the analysis to date has been that these risks are worth the reduced complexity.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1691: Preprocessing conref step does not fix up external links
content:
https://dita-ot.github.io/1.8/dev_ref/preprocess-conref.html describes how links internal to the conreffed content are randomised to make them unique within the topic they get included in, and how internal links within the conreffed content are updated to match the new targets.

That works fine, but this breaks when content external to the conreffed content links inside the conreffed content. The external links are not fixed up by the process and they are thus broken.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1700: VERSION_PATTERN typo
content:

title: DITA-OT Issue #1700: VERSION_PATTERN typo
content:
According to https://dita-ot.github.io/1.8/dev_ref/plugin-support.html, it is possible for the package.version value to be of the form major.minor.micro.qualifier, where qualifier is ( [0..9] | [a..zA..Z] | ’_’ | '-' )+. This construct, however, does not align with the VERSION_PATTERN regular expression defined in dita-ot/src/main/java/org/dita/dost/platform/Integrator.java.
I think this is a typo, and VERSION_PATTERN should be defined as private static final Pattern VERSION_PATTERN = Pattern.compile("\d+(?:\.\d+(?:\.\d+(?:\.[0-9a-zA-Z_\-]+)?)?)?");

title: DITA-OT Issue #1711: The "path2project-uri" is not output in chunked topics [DITA OT 1.8]
content:
Let's say my DITA Map references a topic like:
<chapter chunk="to-content" href="path/topic.dita" type="concept" collection-type="sequence"/>
In the temporary files folder the "topic.dita" will contain only this PI:
when it should also contain:
This is because the "org.dita.dost.writer.ChunkTopicParser" class only outputs the older path2project PI.

As side effect, paths to common CSSs for the XHTML outputs will be invalidly computed.

content:
Error message:
[java] [pipeline] Error at xsl:import on line 43 column 74 of topicmergeImpl.xsl:
 [java] [pipeline] XTSE0165: java.net.MalformedURLException: unknown protocol: plugin
This happens because after ba7e5b1a1b0c4658c9c36b2c5431295621a83435, `topicmergeImpl.xsl` [imports](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/commit/ba7e5b1a1b0c4658c9c36b2c5431295621a83435#diff-5c4822bd3acfb034af5a3d23aea04aa5R43) `dita-utilities.xsl` using the `plugin` protocol, but as far as I can tell, `TopicMergeModule.java` doesn't use the DITA-OT XML catalog, which means the stylesheet can't resolve that URI correctly.

**EDIT**: `output-message.xsl` also needs to be imported and `<xsl:variable name="msgprefix">DOTX</xsl:variable>` added.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1721: Using glossref in the DITA Map does not produce by default content for abbreviated-form
content:
Let's say in the DITA Map I have a glossref:
to a glossentry and then in another topic I have an abbreviated form referencing to it:
When producing PDF by default the abbreviated form will not be shown at all in the PDF.
In order to make this work, you would need to set "print="yes"" on the glossref but this would mean that the glossentry will also be added as content in the PDF (although not in the TOC), thing which may not be desired by users.

So I think the behavior should be:

If the glossref is with print="no" (the default value) the abbreviated form should be expanded properly and the PDF content should not contain the glossentry inside.

If the glossref is with print="yes", the abbreviated form should also be expanded properly and have a link on it pointing to the glossary content in the PDF.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1724: Active revision on table row throws off headers attribute
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1724: Active revision on table row throws off headers attribute
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1724: Active revision on table row throws off headers attribute
content:
The headers attribute is used on table entries to associate content cells with header cells, for use by screen readers. The code to line up entries with their column and row headers is complex, to account for spanned cells. 

The code that counts positioning assumes that <tbody> only contains <row>, and that <row> only contains <entry>. This is still true in the source but can be thrown off by the code added a while back to pre-process revision flags, which can add start- and end-prop info as subelements in these locations. Some code needs to be updated so that it does not count nodes with *, instead it should explicitly count rows, entries, colspecs, etc.

The current result: if using revision (or other) flags that supply alt text, the code accidentally picks up some or all of that alt text, and places it in the headers attribute.

Sample topic with revised table elements:

content:
DITA-OT Issue #1727: Obey @scalefit attribute on an image
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1727: Obey @scalefit attribute on an image
content:
Right now setting scalefit="yes" on an image does nothing in the XSL-FO and XHTML-based outputs.
It should probably work for the XSL-FO output.

The scalefit attribute:

http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/v1.2/os/spec/langref/image.html#image

> Allow an image to be scaled to fit within available space. If, for a given image, any one of height, width, or scale is specified, those attributes determine the graphic size, and any setting of scalefit is ignored. If none of those attributes are specified and scalefit="yes", then the image is scaled (the same factor in both dimensions) so that the graphic will just fit within the available height or width (whichever is more constraining).
> 
> The available width would be the prevailing column (or table cell) width--that is, the width a paragraph of text would have if the graphic were a paragraph instead. The available height is implementation dependent, but if feasible, it is suggested to be the page (or table cell) height or some other reasonable value.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1737: Support DITA 1.3 base element topic/div
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1737: Support DITA 1.3 base element topic/div
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1737: Support DITA 1.3 base element topic/div
content:
topic/div is the only new base element type in DITA 1.3. To support it we simply need the trivial fallback handling in each output type, e.g., div -> div in HTML, div -> fo:wrapper in FO (or produces no direct output, just applying templates to its children).

This support cannot be implemented as a standalone plugin because this template must be imported before any non-base XSLT modules so that it doesn't inadvertently override templates for specializations of div (e.g., all the learning2 interactions).

I'm happy to take on the task. 

I'd like to do this in 1.7 and 1.8 as well so that plugin implementors don't have to worry about getting a fallback for topic/div.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1752: Internationalizing eclipse help not working
content:
According to https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/916, it should be possible to specify two properties and have the eclipsehelp transformation build the correct directory structure 
META-INF
| - MANIFEST.MF 
nl
| - language
 | - country
 | - content
Currently the build produces the META-INF and MANIFEST.MF, but does not build the correct directory structure for the output. - the allowed values for the language parameter are documented, but the ones for the country parameter are not. I tried a bunch of things, assuming that it was a two character code intended to build the correct directory structure, using locales supported by the browser. - the values for the supported languages appear to use hyphens, instead of the standard underscore (i.e. zh-cn instead of zh_CN, as required by eclipse. (for more info on eclipse standards, see http://help.eclipse.org/luna/index.jsp?topic=%2Forg.eclipse.platform.doc.isv%2Fguide%2Fproduct_def_nl.htm)

title: DITA-OT Issue #1757: Provide way in plugin.xml to specify the list of public parameters added for each transtype
content:
Let's say you develop a plugin for the DITA OT which contributes a new transtype.
In addition to the common parameters your plugin also accepts a set of custom parameters which can be set by the end user to customize the output generation.
Right now the user needs to look in the plugin's documentation in order to see which parameters are accepted by the plugin, what description, values and default values they have.

If there would be some kind of metadata in the plugin.xml which would advertize for each transtype a list of parameters (with name, type, possible values and description) then an automated script or a GUI interface could automatically discover and show to the end user the set of parameters which could be configured for that particular transtype.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1768: 1.3: Support key-based, cross-deliverable referencing

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

content: Issue #1768 is open with labels DITA 1.3, feature. Retrieval signals: map, html, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1768: 1.3: Support key-based, cross-deliverable referencing
content:
This requires enabling a multi-pass process by which the first pass for a given root map generates an intermediate data set (which could be a DITA map) that binds keys to locations in the deliverable being generated.

Maps that reference this deliverable can then use the intermediate data set to generate deliverable-specific links to the other deliverable. If the intermediate data set is itself a map, this can be implemented by simply including the intermediate map in the root map so that it has the highest key precedence.

There are some practical challenges. Eliot has defined a general abstract implementation approach and provide that as input to the design.

The main implementation challenge for the OT appears to be modifying the existing HTML and FO transforms to capture the mapping of source keys to deliverable-specific addresses, since this is something those processes were never architected to do.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1774: 1.3: Support MathML and Equation domains
content:
Proposal 13111

I have basic support for both domains that I can contribute. For MathML I generate inline markup for HTML and FO. For HTML can also generate references to the MathJax Javascript library.

Note that FOP (with jEuclid) and Antenna House support MathML rendering natively. XEP does not.

This means that a full FO implementation would require the ability to separately generate SVG or raster images from MathML source. This could be done using jEuclid. However, I'm not particularly motivated to do it in the OT since FOP supports MathML directly. RenderX can provide the necessary MathML rendering support themselves as they see fit.

However, having said that, in the context of EPUB generation I may need to implement the option to generate rasters and SVGs from the MathML in any case (to support EPUB readers that don't support MathML sufficiently [which currently is all of them]), so I may end up doing this anyway.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1788: Generalized @props and @otherprops format appears to not be supported
content:
According to the 1.2 spec (and extended in 1.3), the generalized syntax "attname(value)" should be recognized in `@props`, `@otherprops`, and any defined conditional attribute.
<val>
 <prop action="include" att="deliveryTarget" val="html" />
 <prop action="include" att="deliveryTarget" val="HTML" />
 <prop action="exclude" att="deliveryTarget" val="PDF" />
 <prop action="exclude" att="deliveryTarget" val="pdf" />
</val>
Looking at the 2.0 FilterUtil code, it looks like it's not set up to handle this syntax. We need to correct that if at all possible. Or else there's something wrong with my test, but I think it's correct.

Test data set and 1.8.5 results: https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/20078596/dita-ot-keyref-filter-test-pub-01.zip

Update: DITA-OT 2.0.M3 and 2.0.M4 have this problem, too. In M1 and M2, I ran into other problems and couldn't continue.

When I add one of the missing topic files to the related-links element of an other topic file, the DITA-OT doesn't treat it any more as resource-only. The DITA-OT seems to assume that "isolated" topic files (only mentioned in a ditamap but not in other topic files) are resource-only.

content: Issue #1801 is closed with labels bug, preprocess/keyref. Retrieval signals: keyref, map, html, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1801: Space in URL leads to duplicate entry for key-based file reference
content:
See https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/20078596/dita-ot-bugs/escaped-url-mismatch.zip for sample data, including generated output and job.xml file.
Given these two topicrefs in a map:
<keydef keys="topic-01" href="../topics/DITAComm%20Topic-dtd.xml"/>
 <topicref keyref="topic-01" keys="chapter-01"/>
Where "DITAComm Topic-dtd.xml" is the only topic referenced by the map, the job.xml file has two entries, one with the escaped space in the URL, flagged as resource-only, and one without, flagged as not resource only.

The resulting HTML output has no topic.

So either the URI is not being escaped during the resource-only processing or it's being inappropriately unescaped during key resolution to determine normal-mode topics, resulting in a mismatch that leads to the topic being incorrectly handled as resource-only.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1802: Navigation topicref to keydef-defined key leaves topic as resource-only when it should not
content:
See https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/20078596/dita-ot-bugs/resource-only-topic-bug.zip for sample content and output.
Given only these two topicrefs in a map:
<keydef keys="topic-01" href="../topics/DITAComm_Topic-dtd.xml"/>
<topicref keyref="topic-01" keys="chapter-01"/>
The resulting .job.xml file lists the topic file as resource only and the topic is not reflected in the HTML
In this case the normal-mode topicref must result in a normal-mode use of the topic even though the key definition is resource-only. So the .job.xml file should reflect resource-only="false" for the topic.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1818: Too many HTML files in output in spite of "onlytopic.in.map=true"
content:
In DITA-OT 2.0, the XHTML transform under special circumstances creates too many HTML files in the output directory, in spite of the parameter `onlytopic.in.map` set to `true`.

Test files: https://gist.github.com/maer2712/d0247e9d121562a2f992

Command line: 

`[dita.dir]\bin\dita.bat -f xhtml -i src\test.ditamap -o out\xhtml\test -filter src\test.ditaval -temp t:\tmp -v -l log\antlog.log -Donlytopic.in.map=true`

The transform creates a file `index.html` without any links. This is correct because all content is filtered away. The transform also creates a file `test_inner\Inner.html`, which is not correct.

This problem exists also in DITA-OT 1.8 (XHTML transform and HTMLHelp transform).

title: DITA-OT Issue #1837: Remove keydef processing from XHTML rendering code
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1837: Remove keydef processing from XHTML rendering code
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1837: Remove keydef processing from XHTML rendering code
content:
Currently keys are (for the most part) resolved in one preprocessing step. For linking elements, all is good. For phrase elements, it pulls in text when needed.

The XHTML step then does extra processing that probably belongs inside the keyref process. Specifically, for non-linking elements that can't take `@href`, the XHTML code returns to the keydef.xml file to look up targets. This means we resolve the key twice - once when figuring out link text and setting up keydef.xml, then again when publishing XHTML (and any other format that wants to make a link). This is done for `<ph>`, `<keyword>`, `<cite>`, `<dt>`, `<term>`, and `<indexterm>` (when `$INDEXSHOW is active).

Suggestion: when we evaluate these elements during the keyref preprocess, we have easy access to linking information. We should set something like `@dita-ot:href` that can be easily interpreted by any final rendering step. When I suggested this to @jelovirt he pointed out we would also want `@dita-ot:format` and `@dita-ot:scope`

The one element I'm iffy about is the specialized `<abbreviated-form>` element. The source element is EMPTY so if we populate it in the preprocess, later stages that expect normal DITA may be thrown off. Also, we can't know in preprocess whether to use an abbreviation or a long form (that depends on the final rendering context). Potentially, we could put both the long and abbreviated form inside of `<dita-ot:info>` or similar, which is not so risky and more easily ignored by later steps?

title: DITA-OT Issue #1840: Keyref processing doesn't use only first keyword or term
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1840: Keyref processing doesn't use only first keyword or term
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1840: Keyref processing doesn't use only first keyword or term
content:
The DITA 1.2 spec says 

> For elements on which no `@href` attribute is available..., matching content is taken from the `<keyword>` or `<term>` elements within `<keywords>` within `<topicmeta>`. If more than one `<keyword>` or `<term>` is present, the matching content is taken from the first of them.

DITA-OT 2.0 and earlier incorrectly will use all `<keyword>` or `<term>` elements in key defining element. Only the first should be used.

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1850: Pass xml:lang to second step of troff (text) output
content:
Troff uses a two-step process. Step1 converts all DITA elements to simple block/inline elements, and resolves all generated text. Step2 formats that to troff.

I'm working on an override to Step2 that controls wrapping based on language (allowing DBCS text to split between characters). This wrapping code only operates when the language allows. Currently, the input to Step2 has no language info, because all generated text is set in step 1.

I need to pass `@xml:lang` from step 1 to step 2. Currently the only attributes passed for every element are `@xtrf` and `@xtrc` - making it simple to add `@xml:lang` to this section:
<xsl:template name="debug"><xsl:apply-templates select="@xtrf|@xtrc|@xml:lang"/></xsl:template>
<xsl:template match="@xtrf|@xtrc|@xml:lang">
 <xsl:attribute name="{name()}"><xsl:value-of select="."/></xsl:attribute>
</xsl:template>
The wrapping code based on it is still in progress and will definitely be a 2.1 thing, though this item on its own could probably go into 2.0.2. For the moment I only plan to put this in 2.1, because I doubt anybody else will need it.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1865: DITA 1.1 DTDs should point to each other using 1.1 specific Public IDs
content:
Let's say my DITA topic has a DOCTYPE like:
which is OK. But if you open that, it refers to all modules like:
<!ENTITY % topic-type PUBLIC
"-//OASIS//ELEMENTS DITA Topic//EN"
 "topic.mod" >
 %topic-type;
Notice that the public IDs are not 1.1 specific. Because of this, they
will be mapped through the XML catalog support to the default 1.2 public
IDs.
All these inner-reference PUBLIC IDs between the DTDs (including 1.2
DTDs) should have been modified to refer directly using the proper version.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1870: PDF2 output plugin fails rendering tables
content:
I've been building my DITA sources with pre-2.0 version successfully for a while now. Trying a build on DITA-OT 2.0.1 on a 64 bit Windows 7 system, I get the following problem in a lot of places:

> [xslt] C:\DITA-OT2.0.1\plugins\org.dita.pdf2\xsl\fo\tables.xsl:507: Fatal Error! An empty sequence is not allowed as the value of variable $entryNumber
> [xslt] Failed to process C:\DITA-OT2.0.1\temp\temp20150313171311548\stage1a.xml
> 
> BUILD FAILED
> C:\DITA-OT2.0.1\build.xml:41: The following error occurred while executing this line:
> C:\DITA-OT2.0.1\plugins\org.dita.pdf2\build.xml:155: The following error occurred while executing this line:
> C:\DITA-OT2.0.1\plugins\org.dita.pdf2\build.xml:335: Fatal error during transformation using C:\DITA-OT2.0.1\plugins\org.dita.pdf2\xsl\fo\topic2fo_shell_fop.xsl: An empty sequence is not allowed as the value of variable $entryNumber; SystemID: file:/C:/DITA-OT2.0.1/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/xsl/fo/tables.xsl; Line#: 507; Column#: -1

The offending code seems to be in org.dita.pdf2/xsl/fo/tables.xsl:

title: DITA-OT Issue #1870: PDF2 output plugin fails rendering tables
content:
<xsl:template name="countEntryNumber">
 <xsl:choose>
 <xsl:when test="@colname">
 <xsl:variable name="colname" select="@colname"/>
 <xsl:if test="ancestor::*[contains(@class, ' topic/tgroup ')][1]/*[contains(@class, ' topic/colspec ')][@colname = $colname]">
 <xsl:number select="ancestor::*[contains(@class, ' topic/tgroup ')][1]/*[contains(@class, ' topic/colspec ')][@colname = $colname]"/>
Where apparently a colname in an entry element is matched up with a colname in the colspec.

My source contains neither a colname attribute in the failing table entry, nor a colspec. Adding an appropriate number of empty colspecs with colname="col[1-9]" solves the problem.

I assume that the pdf2 plugin is not the actual culprit, but some other code fails with appropriately populating colspecs in tables that don't have them.

If this helps at all, the problem seems to appear in files that have more than one table.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1877: Searchtitle Incorrectly Used for HTML Title
content:
In OT 2.0, if you specify a `<searchtitle>` in a topic, that value is used for the `<title>` element in HTML transformations.

If anything, the `<searchtitle>` should be copied to the generated topic's metadata (in my plugin, I create `<meta name="searchtitle">`), but not used for `<title>` unless there is a specific use case that demands it.

I saw this in OT 1.8 with `<navtitle>` (but never tested `<searchtitle>`).

title: DITA-OT Issue #1884: Element conref does not properly support specialization
content:
For example I cannot make a conref from an OL to a STEPS or from a PH to a B element.

Let's say for simplicity sake that I have a bold element defined in a topic:
According to the [specification](http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/v1.2/os/spec/archSpec/conref.html#conref) I can make a conref from a base element to a more specialized element (and not the other way around).
So I can do this in another topic:
But although this is a valid construct the publishing does not expand the conref + it reports as an error that it cannot find the target ID.

The XSLT stylesheet which is used for resolving conrefs is `DITA-OT\xsl\preprocess\conrefImpl.xsl` and it has a template which resolves conrefs:
<xsl:variable name="target" select="key('id', $elemid)[local-name()=$element][ancestor::*[contains(@class, ' topic/topic ')][1][@id=$topicid]]"/>
thus forcing the name of the source element to be equal to the name of the target element.
In my opinion it should look at the `@class` attributes set on source and target elements and allow the conref if the source is a generalization of the target or disallow it with a meaningful message if it is not.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1886: Error running DITA-OT 2.0.1 with XEP
content:
Faced this when trying to upgrade to DITA-OT 2.0.1:
May be more a doc bug, you'll be judge.

If you follow the install instructions that are available at http://www.dita-ot.org/2.0/readme/installing-minimal-package-on-linux.html you end up stuck for the PDF renderer section:

It says:
Optional: For PDF output, set up the XSL-FO processor:

Processor Action
RenderX Add the RenderX installation directory to the local.properties file as the xep.dir property, for example:
xep.dir=/usr/share/java/xep

Unfortunately, this does not seem to be enough to have xep run properly on a DITA-OT 2.0 install.

It's eventually missing the "pdf.formatter=xep" instruction at least, but also fails when run:

[xep] Error: Could not find or load main class com.idiominc.ws.opentopic.fo.xep.Runner
[xep] Java Result: 1

If it requires additional steps, they should be described in the install guide.

I'd be happy to contribute on the doc update... if I get the list of required steps to follow to have xep run properly.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1891: [OT-2.0] @copy-to does not generate output topic if no other topicref to original topic exists
content:
When I use @copy-to="newtopicname.dita" on a topicref, the expected topic ("newtopicname.html") is not generated, but references to it point to the nonexistent newtopicname.html.

This seems to happen only when the topicref with the @copy-to is the only instance of the original topic. When I add a second topicref to the original topic, then both the original and renamed topics are generated.

However, the spec as I read it does not require more than one instance of the topic to exist for renaming to occur. And, there are use cases for renaming a topic even though it is the only instance being generated for a particular output. My use case is that I have a number of deliverables generated from the same set of source files, and the landing page for each set of HTML files should be index.html. It would be very inconvenient to have one index.dita file with all versions of the landing page content in it.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1893: [OT-2.0] Can't Use Extension Point dita.xsl.html.cover
content:
Trying to add overrides to this extension point fails because the extension point is specified after templates in map2html-coverImpl_template.xsl.

This code:
`<dita:extension id="dita.xsl.html.cover" behavior="org.dita.dost.platform.ImportXSLAction" xmlns:dita="http://dita-ot.sourceforge.net"/>`
is at the end of map2html-coverImpl_template.xsl, after templates, so on build you get an error that all import statements must occur at the start.

To fix:
- Move the templates from map2html-coverImpl_template.xsl to another XSL file.
- Specify an xsl:import to the new XSL file before the extension point.

As you can see, the othermeta has been inherited by the topic. But, as stated in the [dita 1.2 spec](https://dita.fluidtopics.com/book#!book;uri=urn%253Adita%253ADITA1%255C0dita-1.2-specification.ditamap%253Fv%255C2DITA1.2-spec-XHTML;breadcrumb=urn%253Adita%253ADITA1%255C0architectural_specification.dita%253Fv%255C2DITA1.2%255C3-spec%255C3-XHTML-urn%253Adita%253ADITA1%255C0archSpec%255C3-base.dita%253Fv%255C2DITA1.2%255C3-spec%255C3-XHTML-urn%253Adita%253ADITA1%255C0archSpec%255C0ditamarkup.dita%253Fv%255C2DITA1.2%255C3-spec%255C3-XHTML-urn%253Adita%253ADITA1%255C0archSpec%255C0dita%255C3-metadata.dita%253Fv%255C2DITA1.2%255C3-spec%255C3-XHTML-urn%253Adita%253ADITA1%255C0archSpec%255C0reconciling%255C3-topic%255C3-and%255C3-map%255C3-metadata.dita%253Fv%255C2DITA1.2%255C3-spec%255C3-XHTML), othermeta and source metadata (among others) should not cascade to children.

This bug has been introduced has part of the fix for #1086.

The fix may be to revert the incriminated commit (the one that I am unable to find).

title: DITA-OT Issue #1905: Sort plugin folders before integration
content:
The "org.dita.dost.platform.Integrator.execute()" has a set with all plugin directories "org.dita.dost.platform.Integrator.descSet".
Ideally it would be a TreeSet. In this way if I run the integrator on mac, linux, or windows, with no matter what Java VM I obtain the same result. This is useful when you have the DITA OT committed to a SVN or GIT project and you run the integrator and try to commit with the least amount of changes.

Also it's useful if you have two plugins with the same ID and no matter on what platform/Java VM you run the integrator the plugin from the folder which comes lexicographically first will be loaded and used.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1910: Refactor troff code to be usable for other text-like transform types
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1910: Refactor troff code to be usable for other text-like transform types
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1910: Refactor troff code to be usable for other text-like transform types
content: We already ship the troff code as a plug-in, which has two steps. First, convert to an intermediate syntax, mostly blocks and phrases. Then, convert to troff. This should be split up to make that intermediate format more usable by other transform types. Currently, I'm intending to refactor the troff code into two plugins; first converts to the div/span syntax, second takes that and creates troff output. Long term goal is to reuse that intermediate format for a plain text transform, but that will not be part of this issue. I'm not sure if the plain text transform will be bundled with a DITA-OT package or not - guessing @jelovirt would suggest it be a separate download? - but given that we already ship troff, I think we should split the two steps into distinct plugins that continue to ship with DITA-OT.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1914: Consolidate packages to one version
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1914: Consolidate packages to one version
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1914: Consolidate packages to one version
content: We've had more than one DITA-OT distribution for many years now, to try and meet the needs of different audiences. That has been useful for the few who really only want the small packages, but I think the benefit is outweighed by the confusion from people who need the Everything package and end up with standard or minimal. I've tried to keep the package distinction for quite a while, but I think I'm finally convinced it's not worth the effort - we should just have the one package (corresponding to the DITA-OT 2.0 Client distribution). Those who do not need extra libraries can remove them, or build the minimal packages directly from Git.

content: Issue #1919 is closed with labels feature, plugin/troff, priority/medium, won't fix. Retrieval signals: general issue behavior.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1919: Improve line wrapping in troff
content:
Troff code implements line wrapping (default is to wrap at 65 characters). Not the most elegant code but works for the general case.

Currently the code is based on spaces; it has no special support for Asian languages where lines can wrap between most valid characters. I've worked out a fix that supports wrapping by testing such characters (comparing characters to common line wrapping rules). May not be 100% for some punctuation, but works for the common case.

While working on this I also added support for a line length of "NONE" which will remove line wrapping from text content, leaving the wrapping up to display systems.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1922: Index continued markers don't work if both primary and its secondary entries continue
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1922: Index continued markers don't work if both primary and its secondary entries continue
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1922: Index continued markers don't work if both primary and its secondary entries continue
content:
In the 1.7, 1.8 and 2.x versions, when a primary entry also has secondary entries which in turn have tertiary entries, the code generates a table around the primary and around each secondary so that it can then use table markers to generate "continued" messages in the case where a given entry breaks across a column or page boundary.

Unfortunately, the code uses the same marker name for the primary and secondary markers. At least with Antenna House this results in garbled marker text in the result as both markers are fetched and end up overlapping each other.

The solution is to use distinct marker names for each index level. This should be a relatively easy fix but I haven't tried to implement a fix yet (but I will as this fix is required for a client).

This particular configuration of index entries is something of an edge case (which is probably why it's not been reported to date) but it can occur, especially in documents where primary entry has secondary entries that then have long lists of tertiary entries. A picture showing a real sample is attached (it reflects my manual fix to the marker names)

The fix should be as easy as just reflecting the index level (primary or secondary) in the marker name.

![index-sample-fixed_page_1](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1004229/7848429/4e14bd5e-0491-11e5-97d4-a3603c92a73b.png)

title: DITA-OT Issue #1936: Version 2.0.1: Fatal Error! xsl:import elements must come first
content:
After installing a XHTML extension plugin to the stock DITA-OT 2.0.1, I got the following error:

/opt/DITA-OT2.0.1/plugins/org.dita.xhtml/xsl/map2html-coverImpl.xsl:82:103: Fatal Error! xsl:import elements must come first

After looking around and bisecting the map2html-coverImpl(_template).xsl, it turns out that
the extension id for " dita.xsl.html.cover" is at the end of the template.
Thus, when installing a plugin that creates an extension to dita.xsl.html.cover, it adds a <xsl:import /> line after the named templates.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1941: Add `noparent` option to `args.rellinks`
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1941: Add `noparent` option to `args.rellinks`
content:
The deprecated `args.hide.parent.link` parameter specifies whether to hide links to parent topics in the HTML or XHTML output, while still generating child, next, and previous links.

The `args.rellinks` parameter that is recommended as a replacement does not currently include an option that would replicate this behavior. _(Available options are `all`, `none` & `nofamily`.)_

In order to serve as a full replacement for `args.hide.parent.link`, `args.rellinks` should be extended with a `noparent` option.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1945: copy-to attribute not processed correctly in javahelp transform
content:
In the javahelp transform, when a copy of a DITA topic is created with the copy-to attribute of topicref, the navigation links (the links to parent topic, next topic, previous topic) remain the same as for the topicref without the copy-to attribute. This is incorrect, the navigation links should reflect the position in the DITA map of the topicref element with the copy-to attribute.

The generated map.jhm and toc.xml files that go into the final help jar file include only the location that is set in the href attribute of the initial topicref (the one that does not have a copy-to attribute).

Example of map:
<map title="Growing Flowers">
 <topicref href="topics/care.dita">
 <topicref href="tasks/pruning.dita"/>
 <topicref href="topics/flowers/iris.dita" copy-to="topics/flowers/iris2.dita" navtitle="IRIS COPY" locktitle="yes"/>
 <topicref href="tasks/gardenPreparation.dita"/>
 </topicref>
 <topicref href="topics/index.dita" collection-type="sequence">
 <topicref href="concepts/springFlowers.dita" collection-type="sequence">
 <topicref href="topics/flowers/iris.dita"/>
 <topicref href="tasks/pruning.dita" copy-to="tasks/pruning2.dita" navtitle="PRUNING COPY" locktitle="yes"/>

title: DITA-OT Issue #1948: Extend `dita` command with an option to run build scripts
content:
As the `dita` command is essentially a wrapper around Ant, add an option that would allow users to run Ant build scripts by passing the script as an argument to the `dita` command (perhaps `-s` or `-script`):
This would simplify migration to OT v2.1 for those who use Ant build scripts to define parameters in advance, copy and rename files and generate output for multiple targets with a single command.
Users who previously relied on `ant -f` would benefit from the advantages of the new `dita` command as the preferred method of transforming DITA content without having to install and configure a separate copy of Ant as suggested in dita-ot/docs#24.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1956: Chunk to-content produces invalid doc when nested topic not same type as parent topic
content:
Given a topic like:
<concept>
 ...
 <topic>
 ...
 </topic>
</concept>
And a topicref that chunks the root topic like so:
<topicref keyref="ch01"
 copy-to="chunk-01.dita"
 chunk="to-content select-topic by-topic"
 >
The resulting topic is not well formed in that the closing tag is `</topic>` not `</concept>`

This result is produced by the ChunkModule Java code.

I get the same result with 1.8.5 and 2.1 official release.

I have not yet determined the code issue.

Will provide a gist with test case docs.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1959: Install should overwrite existing plugin or at least provide option to force overwrite
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1959: Install should overwrite existing plugin or at least provide option to force overwrite
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1959: Install should overwrite existing plugin or at least provide option to force overwrite
content:
If I use "dita -install {zip URI}" to install a plugin and then repeat the command, I get the message that the plugin is already installed.

If the plugin installation fails because there is an unmet dependency reinstallation still fails.

Since there is little or no chance of data loss when reinstalling a plugin the install action should either always overwrite or should provide the option of forcing the overwrite. e.g., something like "dita -f -install {zip URI}"

For the "force" case, the existing plugin should be uninstalled automatically and then the plugin installed.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1960: Need dita action to list IDs of installed plugins
content:
The dita -uninstall action requires knowledge of the plugin ID but there is no way to get the plugin IDs of the installed plugins from the dita command--you have to look in the plugin.xml files for each plugin.

Would like an action that lists the plugin IDs and plugin versions

This would also allow for scripts that can check dependencies and current installation status in support of coordinated installation of multiple plugins.

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1964: Update copy-html to work like copy-image, with parameter for destination directory
content: Issue #1964 is closed with labels feature, preprocess, priority/low. Retrieval signals: map, html, plugin.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1964: Update copy-html to work like copy-image, with parameter for destination directory
content:
In preprocess we have the `copy-image` task, which copies images from the source directory. For X/HTML this goes straight to the output directory. The task sets a property to figure out the destination directory. I've taken advantage of this by initializing the `copy-image.todir` property in a plugin: for one output type the images are placed in a generated directory in the temp dir, which is later zipped together with the rendered content.

I'd like to be able to do the same with HTML topics referenced from the map - I should be able to set the copy destination in the same way as the images, so that they become part of my zip.

Any objection to updating the `copy-html` task so that it works the same way as `copy-image`? I suspect the main reason for the property in `copy-image` is to handle the uplevels variable. I suspect the same uplevels support is probably missing today in `copy-html`, so that may be another reason to make this update.

Current `copy-html` task:
<target name="copy-html"
 dita:depends="{depend.preprocess.copy-html.pre},copy-html-check"
 dita:extension="depends org.dita.dost.platform.InsertDependsAction"
 unless="preprocess.copy-html.skip"
 description="Copy html files">
 <copy todir="${output.dir}">
 <fileset dir="${user.input.dir}" includesfile="${dita.temp.dir}/${htmlfile}"/>
 </copy>
 </target>
Suggested revision, based on `copy-image`:

title: DITA-OT Issue #1964: Update copy-html to work like copy-image, with parameter for destination directory
content:
<target name="copy-html"
 dita:depends="{depend.preprocess.copy-html.pre},copy-html-check"
 dita:extension="depends org.dita.dost.platform.InsertDependsAction"
 unless="preprocess.copy-html.skip"
 description="Copy html files">
 <condition property="copy-html.todir" value="${output.dir}/${uplevels}" else="${output.dir}">
 <equals arg1="${generate.copy.outer}" arg2="1"/> 
 </condition>
 <copy todir="${copy-html.todir}">
 <fileset dir="${user.input.dir}" includesfile="${dita.temp.dir}/${htmlfile}" />
 </copy>
 </target>

content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1970: colspec added by default to tables in OT2.1 causes non optimal presentation
content:
In preprocessing (NormalizeFilter.java ?) colspecs are added for columns in tables that have no colspec specified by the user.
For users of XEP and AntennaHouse the best results are achieved by letting the FO processor decide on the width of the columns based on the content of those columns.
Where an author does require a specific column width ratio they will specify colspecs in the usual way.

Now, after preprocessing I cannot tell if the specified colowidths are deliberately added by the user (and set to be all the same width) or added by the preprocessor.
Please can we have an Ant param that controls if the colwidth is added automatically or not by the pre processor (or at least some additional indication that the colwidths that exist were not specified by the author)

example below
<table frame="all" id="table_3vm_b3f_lf" outputclass="tablewidthcolumn dochistory" class="- topic/table ">
 <tgroup cols="4" class="- topic/tgroup ">
 <colspec class="- topic/colspec " colnum="1" colname="col1" colwidth="1*"/>
 <colspec class="- topic/colspec " colnum="2" colname="col2" colwidth="1*"/>
 <colspec class="- topic/colspec " colnum="3" colname="col3" colwidth="1*"/>
 <colspec class="- topic/colspec " colnum="4" colname="col4" colwidth="1*"/>

title: DITA-OT Issue #1971: Discussion: managing plugins dependencies (id, list and versions)
content:
I really like the new install feature of the DITA-OT 2.x, and I am wondering if this feature could be pushed deeper. Maybe this is already planned for the future. 
For a single project, managing all the plugins dependencies and versions can become a challenging issue with the number of plugins involved. 
This problem might be fixed using a dependency manager, but those are complex to set-up.
Another way to fix the issue is to have a repo with a copy of the entire installations but it is not always easy to update all the dependencies in this scenario too.

While working with Javascript, I use to work with npm to manage javascript dependencies and I am wondering if some ideas could be implemented in the DITA-OT. npm uses a package.json file to manage dependencies, an xml alternative would be great too.

Below is a theorical example
<package>
 <name>Project one</name>
 <version>1.3.1</version>
 <otversion>2.0.1</otversion>
 <description>My company project</description>
 <author></author>
 <keywords>
 <keyword>html5</keyword>
 </keywords>
 <dependencies>

title: DITA-OT Issue #1971: Discussion: managing plugins dependencies (id, list and versions)
content:
Check the dependencies repo url: `git@github.com:dita-community/org.dita-community.adjust-copy-to.git#develop`. Usually the '#' specify the branch or the tag. A convention is needed here.

It would be great to have the following features built-in in the OT:
1. a standardized way to document plugins version 
2. adding the version information when declaring plugin dependencies
3. an install option to install a plugin using a repository, in the correct branch or tag, documented in the a package.xml file, specially since most of the plugins available are in git repos.
4. a way to list all plugins installed with their versions (ref https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/1960)
5. a way to update dependencies
6. a way to remove plugins from the package.

One interesting thing, is that the generated package.xml could exchange between people, so it makes things easier for everyone to get all the same set-up for a project.

I know this is a huge work and I am wondering if it could be useful for the community.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1984: PDF2: Make generation of page masters and page sequence masters easier to extend
content:
The current code in layout-masters.xsl doesn't provide any way to extend or override the set of page masters and page sequence masters except by completely copying the createDefaultLayoutMasters template.

A better solution would be to have a template that produces the fo:layout-master-set that then calls both the default set creation and then applies templates two modes, one for creating page masters and another for creating page sequence masters.

This change would then set the stage for making page sequence generation also more flexible.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1988: Defer reading images list to end of preprocessing
content:
DITA-OT Issue #1988: Defer reading images list to end of preprocessing
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #1988: Defer reading images list to end of preprocessing
content: In the current preprocessing design, list of images is generated during gen-list target. However, this relies on listing image formats in a configuration file and not relying on `<image>` element references, since key defined images are not processes at that point. An alternative design would be to create a list of images during image-metadata target where image dimensions are read. This would allow getting an accurate list of images that doesn't rely on `@format` or file extensions.

content:
We are building an online-help system using DITA including troubleshooting topics. These topics are nested inside other topics to create a decision tree in a map.
So the map looks like this:
topic problems
 topic unread emails
 topic decision
 troubleshooting topic 1
 troubleshooting topic 2
The map contains a relationship table in which all those to topics are linked. These links work properly when we put the map and the topics in the same folder. title: DITA-OT Issue #2014: Keyref text resolution not using link text unless on link element
content:
Based on clarifications to the keyref processing rules in DITA 1.3 (content was there in 1.2 but difficult to interpret):
http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3/errata01/os/complete/part1-base/archSpec/base/processing-keyref-for-text.html#processing_key_references

For _any element_, text can be pulled from `<linktext>`, which makes that a good default way to specify text with a key (number five in the list of rules). Otherwise (rule 6), normal rules apply as they would for xref, such as pulling from `<navtitle>`.

I've tested this with traditionally non-linking elements `<cite>` and `<keyword>`, then with `<xref>` and `<link>`. I tried keys that place text in `<keyword>`, `<linktext>`>, `@navtitle`, and `<navtitle>`. Results:
- For non-linking elements, text is only pulled from `<keyword>`. If a link target is added, references to the other three will use the URI as link text.
- For `<xref>`, text is pulled from the first three but not from `<navtitle>`. If a link target is added, the URI is used for that case.
- For `<link>`, cases without a link target are removed. With a link target, results match `<xref>`.

Including `test.ditamap` and `cit-test.dita`:

 <keydef keys="citkeyword"><topicmeta><keywords><keyword>text in keyword</keyword></keywords></topicmeta></keydef>
 <keydef keys="citlinktext"><topicmeta><linktext>text in linktext</linktext></topicmeta></keydef>
 <keydef keys="citnavatt" navtitle="navtitle attribute"/>
 <keydef keys="citnavel"><topicmeta><navtitle>navtitle element</navtitle></topicmeta></keydef>
 <keydef keys="xrefkeyword" href="http://www.dita-ot.org" format="html" scope="external">

content:
Pre-processing of map `` elements different in DITA-OT >=2.0 After a couple of hours deep-dive I'm pretty sure that the pre-processing behaviour of populating the `` elements inside the pre-processed DITA maps during mappull has changed. I'm almost sure that this is not intentional behaviour and hope it can be fixed or worked around easily. Given the following minimalistic input. map.ditamap: Topic navtitle topic.dita: Concept title

My concept

 This will generate the following pre-processed version of map.ditamap in the temp folder (stripped debug attributes etc....): Topic navtitle Concept title Concept title

title: DITA-OT Issue #2016: Pre-processing of map <navtitle> elements different in DITA-OT >=2.0
content:
The result of this changes is that all navigational items in output like an index.html TOC file or a CHM HHC file show the `<navtitle>` of the map and not the `<title>` of the topic while the `<navtitle>` of the map should only be used if the `@locktitle` attribute was set to 'yes'. 

To rule out some possible causes I tried the following: 
- Remove the `<navtitle>` element from the map: then it works as expected 
- Set a `@locktitle` attribute to 'no': no change 
- Add an empty `<navtitle>` element: no change, the empty navtitle is preserved still 

Most prominent questions: 
1. Is this a known issue? 
2. Can you please confirm it is not intentionally so should be changed? 
3. Are there any (known) workarounds 

Please, note that I've tested on different DITA-OT versions and on different systems. All with the same result. Doing a deep-dive in mappullImpl.xsl proofs that the behaviour is not as expected.
