content: Issue #2017 is closed with labels bug, preprocess, priority/medium, stale. Retrieval signals: keyref, map, pdf.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2017: Reltables do not work if using any keys outside map directory
content:
When key definitions are includes from outside the current map directory, links that should be generated by `<reltable>` elements do not appear in PDF2 output. This happens even if the `<reltable>` doesn't use any keys from the external map. 

Consider the following map:
<map>
 <mapref href="../common/keydefs.ditamap"/>
 <keydef keys="foo" href="foo.dita"/>
 <keydef keys="bar" href="bar.dita"/>

 <topicref keyref="foo"/>
 <topicref keyref="bar"/>

 <reltable>
 <relcell>
 <topicref keyref="foo"/>
 </relcell>
 <relcell>
 <topicref keyref="bar"/>
 </relcell>
 </reltable>
</map>
In this example, the keys foo and bar are defined locally, but the map also has keys from another map a level above the current maps's directory.

The links that should be appearing with topics foo and bar do not appear in PDF2 output. If the reference to the external map is removed, the `<reltable>` links are generated as expected.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2020: CHM encoding of HTML content inside topics should always be UTF-8
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2020: CHM encoding of HTML content inside topics should always be UTF-8
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2020: CHM encoding of HTML content inside topics should always be UTF-8
content:
One of our users had the following problem:

Let's say I have a DITA topic, I have no language specified to it's considered to be en-us.
At a certain point in the topic I use a certain non-ASCII character `<ph>✓</ph>`.

After publishing to CHM, the character is replaced with an invalid character in the HTML output.
This happens because the "org.dita.dost.util.ConvertLang" Java task has looked into the `/org/dita/dost/util/codepages.xml` and considered that for en-us it should use "iso-8859-1" which cannot encode that specific character. Looking in the same codepages.xml file the encoding is UTF-8 for certain languages.

In my opinion the encoding used for the HTML content obtained from the DITA topics (not for the HHP and HHC files which are created separately) should always pe UTF-8 and the codepages.xml should be eliminated.

What I could find on the web about this:

> If the HTML is encoded as Unicode (UTF-8 or UTF-16 aka UNICODE) non-English chars won't be handed correctly in the HH navigation (TOC, Index, Search). The embedded browser (content area on right of the help viewer) will however display the topic text fine since this is a UNICODE enabled control.

Or at least for en-us we could use utf-8 because it is a perfect superset of ASCII which can encode all English chars.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2047: PDF flagging should use common preprocess code
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2047: PDF flagging should use common preprocess code
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2047: PDF flagging should use common preprocess code
content:
A couple years ago we introduced a preprocess step to add flagging information from DITAVAL documents into DITA content. This makes it easy for any output format to support flagging without having to re-implement the logic for flagging. XHTML code was converted to use the preprocess step at that time.

The PDF2 plugin runs the common preprocess step but ignores the result. It runs an extra processing step to set up flagging, so the logic is duplicated. We should remove the extra step and make use of the common preprocess logic.

I've got the basics working now but need additional updates for elements where fall-through processing of flags would result in out of context images (such as flagged `<tbody>` or `<ol>`).

title: DITA-OT Issue #2048: Flagging preprocess grabs too much with check for defaults
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2048: Flagging preprocess grabs too much with check for defaults
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2048: Flagging preprocess grabs too much with check for defaults
content:
The flagging preprocess code copies active revisions into topics so that later steps do not need to evaluate any flagging logic. Active flags are gathered in the `getrules` template. The template ends with the following code that is intended to copy default flag rules (for example, any default rules properties / rev in general, or default rules for `@audience` when an element uses `@audience`). Current code is grabbing too many rules:
<!-- default flags -->
 <xsl:if test="$current/@audience | $current/@platform | $current/@product | $current/@otherprops">
 <xsl:copy-of select="$FILTERDOC/val/prop[empty(@att) and @action = 'flag']"/>
 </xsl:if>
 <xsl:if test="$current/@rev">
 <xsl:copy-of select="$FILTERDOC/val/revprop[empty(@att) and @action = 'flag']"/>
 </xsl:if>
Problems:
- It copies any default flag rule (no attribute specified) but not defaults for a given attribute (if `@audience` is specified we should get the default rule for `@audience`)
- It would copy a (IMHO invalid) flag rule that specifies no attribute but still has a value, even if that value doesn't match anything on the current element
- For revisions, it copies _all_ revision elements, because none specify `@att` (that check should be for `@val`) - I originally noticed this issue because every revision setting in my DITAVAL conditions ended up added to elements that specified `@rev`

title: DITA-OT Issue #2052: Different behaviour when using locktitle attribute for PDF and XHTML transformations
content:
The difference comes from the fact that the HTML transformation treat the _locktitle_ attribute as **inheritable** and PDF not when the TOC is computed.

In the HTML transformation the TOC title for _tasks/changingtheoil.dita_ topic is taken from DITA map because the _locktitle_ attribute is set on the parent topic group.

The specification is a bit confusing for me:
http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/v1.2/os/spec/langref/navtitle.html#navtitle

> When navtitle is used in a map, it functions in the same way as the navtitle attribute; both are used to specify a navigation title for the target of the <topicref> element. That is, the title itself will only be used as an actual navigation title when the title is locked; the title is locked when the closest ancestor topicref element sets or inherits the attribute locktitle="yes".

It says that the locktitle attribute can be inherited.

But in the section _Metadata in maps and topics_, you can find the next phrase.

http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/v1.2/os/spec/archSpec/metadata-in-maps-and-topics.html#metadata-in-maps-and-topics

> The content of the <navtitle> element is used as a navigation title only if the @locktitle attribute of the parent <topicref> element is set to "yes".

that tells nothing about inheritance.

Is it the _locktitle_ inheritable? Which output is correct?

title: DITA-OT Issue #2057: Table processing different for first child of conbody and subsequent children
content:
Two structurally identical tables that are both children of conbody are processed differently. Both tables have colspec=2 and no colwidth specified. The toolkit injects an automatic colwidth of 50% in the first table and nothing in the second table. Reversing the order of the tables shows that it's always the first table that has the colwidth injected and not subsequent tables.
The behavior of the second table is preferable, because autofit is a better option when localizing the doc into multiple languages.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2062: Support "artlbl" option in PDF
content: We have the argument `args.artlbl` in HTML based transforms - useful for review, it shows the name of an image alongside that image. Any objections if I add support for that same parameter to PDF2? I know that @keberlein has clients that would like it, and I've got some users who expect it as well.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2065: HTML output discards trademark symbols
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2065: HTML output discards trademark symbols
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2065: HTML output discards trademark symbols
content:
HTML processing currently discards trademark symbols in certain languages, whereas PDF processing includes the ™ and <sup>®</sup> symbols as expected regardless of the XML language setting.

With DITA source such as:
the HTML output includes the ™ trademark symbol in the first _(English)_ paragraph, but discards it in the second where the `@xml:lang` attribute marks the content as German:
In PDF output, the trademark symbol appears in both cases as MyProduct™.

According to comments in `org.dita.xhtml/xsl/xslhtml/dita2htmlImpl.xsl` [Line 1142](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/develop/src/main/plugins/org.dita.xhtml/xsl/xslhtml/dita2htmlImpl.xsl#L1142), this behavior appears to be intentional, though no such rule seems to be applied in other transformation types:

> Use the TM for US English and the AP languages (Japanese, Korean, and both Chinese).
> Ignore the TM for all other languages.

Though the appropriate usage of trademark symbols in non-English languages is certainly debatable, I would expect OT to handle them consistently across transformation types and render them in HTML output as authored.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2071: PDF index should not drop terms based on first character
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2071: PDF index should not drop terms based on first character
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2071: PDF index should not drop terms based on first character
content: Issue #2071 is closed with labels feature, plugin/pdf. Retrieval signals: error, pdf, plugin.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2071: PDF index should not drop terms based on first character
content:
Index sorting in PDF2 is based on groups with specified characters. If a primary index begins with a character from a group, it goes in that group. If the starting character is not part of a group, the term is dropped with an error message. For example, all of the following are dropped from English indexes:
Rather than dropping terms, we should move unexpected terms to the "Special characters" section of the index. We should keep a message but maybe lower to Info level (sometimes useful to know, as in the second two samples, but often the correct behavior, as in the first).

I've got this working when the index grouping file consistently uses the key "Specials" for the group that includes special characters. This is inconsistent today; some use it, some have no key for the group, some translate the key. The key itself is just an ID, and never appears in rendered output; as part of this, I plan to add that specific key to the special character group in all languages. 

If the sort can't find that key, I think the only option is to continue the current behavior (drop the term, with an error). We could create another group with the key, but that would give bad results if the group already exists using a different key (presumably, part of a plugin or customization dir that already modifies the sort).

title: DITA-OT Issue #2074: PDF index headers should be consistent across languages
content:
Index headers in PDF2 are currently inconsistent across languages:
- Some have headers for every section (special characters, numbers, letters) - for example, Chinese and Japanese
- Some have headers for letters, but not for the other groups - for example, English, German
- Some have no headers, even for letters - for example, Swedish, Finnish

I'd like to make them consistent, with headers for every section in all languages. I can add translations for special characters and numbers for all of the languages that are currently missing translations. (Ideally these might come from the string file, but that's a larger design change to the index code that I don't really want to mess with right now.)

title: DITA-OT Issue #2077: Topics with processing-role="resource-only" generate XHTML
content:
Reported to me by a user (not sure which OT version), but I replicated with 2.1.1. If a map has nothing but key definitions (that is, nothing but references with `processing-role="resource-only"`), XHTML output still generates result files for each of the topics. Resource-only topics should be available to the transform for whatever reason, but should not be generating output.

To reproduce: in `hierarchy.ditamap`, add `processing-role="resource-only"` to every `<topicref>`. Build to XHTML; all topics are still generated. PDF output fails, I assume because no real content goes in the PDF. I tested this test both with the original `<topicref>` (add `@processing-role` manually) and with `<keydef>` (pick up default `@processing-role` and add `@keys`).

If I set the first topic in the map to `@processing-role="normal"`, but leave the others as `resource-only`, XHTML still generates all topics. PDF correctly includes only the one normal topic.

Sample set: 
[2077.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/1005790/2077.zip)

title: DITA-OT Issue #2104: DITA-OT dita2htmlImpl.xsl less tolerant with not matching colname attributes
content:
The following scenario could be processed by DITA-OT < 2.0 and raises an error in DITA-OT 2.1.0:
- A topic contains a table
- One of the table entries has a specified colname that is not declared as colspec

Although this is also an error at source it will be more backward compatible to make the processing tolerant and generate a warning only.

Source material to reproduce:
- table-colspec.ditamap
- topic-colspec.dita

Error fragment from DITA-OT log:

> [xslt] Transforming into C:\DITA\dita-ot-2.1.0\out
> [xslt] Processing C:\DITA\dita-ot-2.1.0\temp\1\topic-colspec.dita to C:\DITA\dita-ot-2.1.0\out\topic-colspec.html
> [xslt] Loading stylesheet C:\DITA\dita-ot-2.1.0\plugins\org.dita.xhtml\xsl\dita2html.xsl
> [xslt] C:\DITA\dita-ot-2.1.0\plugins\org.dita.xhtml\xsl\xslhtml\dita2htmlImpl.xsl:2085: Fatal Error! An empty sequence is not allowed as the value of variable $colspec
> [xslt] Failed to process null

Possible work-around:
Add a '?' to line 2085 of plugins\org.dita.xhtml\xsl\xslhtml\dita2htmlImpl.xsl:
<xsl:variable name="colspec" select="../../../*[contains(@class, ' topic/colspec ')][@colname and @colname = $this-colname]" as="element()?"/>

content: Issue #2105 is closed with labels bug, preprocess, priority/medium. Retrieval signals: map, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2105: Behavior of the force-unique flag
content:
Since DITA-OT version 2.0 there is a new option to automatically generate `copy-to` attributes to duplicate `<topicref>` elements.

This is an interesting feature and I gave it a try. However this feature has undesired side-effects for DITA maps that contain a relationship table. Topics part of relational links will also get a `copy-to` attribute with the final effect of getting too many redundant topics and none of the relational links is effectively added because the files do not match anymore.

Although this requires some thinking I can imagine the following improvements:
- Just ignore the content of the relationship table to detect duplicate `<topicref>` elements.
- Optionally if a duplicated `<topicref>` is part of a relational link, then wrap it inside a `<topicgroup>` like indicated below.
 original:
<relcell> ...
<topicgroup collection-type="choice">
<topicref href="A.dita" />
<!-- the following href equals to each generated copy-to attribute: -->
<topicref href="A-2.dita" linking="sourceonly"/>
</topicgroup>
</relcell>
I fear it gets complicated if the `<topicref>` does already inherit other collection-type or linking attribute values or if it contains children.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2112: PDF: Missing attribute sets for Glossary, Index & ToC
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2112: PDF: Missing attribute sets for Glossary, Index & ToC
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2112: PDF: Missing attribute sets for Glossary, Index & ToC
content:
The `static-content-attr.xsl` file includes _(empty)_ attribute sets that can be used to apply attributes to the headings that appear in the headers and/or footers of body pages:
- `<xsl:attribute-set name="__body__even__footer__heading">`
- `<xsl:attribute-set name="__body__even__header__heading">`
- `<xsl:attribute-set name="__body__first__footer__heading">`
- `<xsl:attribute-set name="__body__first__header__heading">`
- `<xsl:attribute-set name="__body__odd__footer__heading">`
- `<xsl:attribute-set name="__body__odd__header__heading">`

There are no such attribute sets for Glossary, Index, or ToC, so there's currently no way to align them with their body counterparts.

The Glossary, Index, and ToC attribute sets are currently limited to 8 odd/even header/footer & pagenum variants, whereas the `__body__` variants include additional `__first__`, `__last__` and `__heading` attribute sets that should be added for Glossary, Index, and ToC to support consistent headers and footers across the entire publication.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2113: Using of 'dita.specialization.catalog.relative' extension point does not override native DITA-OT XML catalogs.
content:
Using of 'dita.specialization.catalog.relative' extension point does not override native DITA-OT catalogs. It adds references to new catalogs below references to native DITA-OT catalogs. For example:
<nextCatalog catalog="plugins/org.dita.specialization.dita11/catalog.xml"/>
<nextCatalog catalog="plugins/org.oasis-open.dita.v1_2/catalog.xml"/>
<nextCatalog catalog="plugins/com.custom.plugin/catalog.xml"/>
<nextCatalog catalog="plugins/org.dita.specialization.eclipsemap/catalog.xml"/>
In this situation DITA-OT ignores customization in custom catalog (such as adding new attributes or custom elements). If references to the native DITA-OT catalogs are removed all work as expected and customized DITA files could be correctly resolved.

Was reproduced using DITA-OT 2.1; extending xhtml/html5 plugin; OS Windows 10.

Proposed solution: Add references to 'org.dita.specialization.dita11' and 'org.oasis-open.dita.v1_2' catalogs after custom catalogs.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2140: Run dita command using java headless mode
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2140: Run dita command using java headless mode
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2140: Run dita command using java headless mode
content:
On OS X (also Windows?), running DITA builds annoyingly steals the focus when the java process is started. However, java can be run in headless mode and not do this. Headless mode also consumes fewer system resources, and as far as I can tell there's no reason not to build in headless mode.
We could improve the dita command by running java in headless mode by default. If there's a reason why headless mode might be problematic for some users, we could add a build flag "--not-headless" to override this behavior.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2141: Resolve coderef before conref
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2141: Resolve coderef before conref
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2141: Resolve coderef before conref
content:
Currently, the preprocessing order of operations resolves coderefs late — after conref resolution is complete. This can result in coderefs not being resolved. For example: - Topic A contains an example with a coderef in it. - Topic B conrefs the example from topic A.
At the time the file lists are generated, Topic B doesn't have a coderef in it, so the coderef never gets resolved in topic B, only in topic A.
This can easily be fixed by moving coderef resolution before conref resolution. A coderef will never require conref resolution of its contents, so changing the order won't result in conrefs not being resolved.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2144: Add configuration for SAX pipes

title: DITA-OT Issue #2144: Add configuration for SAX pipes
content:
Add support for configuring SAX pipes in Ant `<pipeline>` task. The configuration syntax could look something like:
<pipeline message="Resolve topic fragment." taskname="topic-fragment">
 <sax>
 <filter class="com.example.filter.FooFilter"/>
 <filter class="com.example.filter.BarFilter">
 <param name="bar" expression="true"/>
 <param name="baz" expression="true" if="baz.skip"/>
 </filter>
 <filter class="com.example.filter.BazFilter" singleton="false" unless="baz.skip"/>
 </sax>
</pipeline>
- All filters must implement [`AbstractXMLFilter`](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/develop/src/main/java/org/dita/dost/writer/AbstractXMLFilter.java) - Filters are singleton by default

title: DITA-OT Issue #2153: Make it easier to set watermark for PDF output
content:
For Docbook for example you have a parameter which controls this:

http://docbook.sourceforge.net/release/xsl/1.75.2/doc/fo/draft.watermark.image.html

For DITA you would need to overwrite in your custom.xsl a lot of templates, starting with the one which generates the frontmatter + many templates from the "org.dita.pdf2/xsl/fo/static-content.xsl" like "static-content.xsl".
At least we would have a single XSLT template which we could overwrite for this in a customization.

Looking also at Docbook, they have lots of parameters for PDF customization. This happens because in Docbook it's very easy to define a parameter, you just define it as an XSLT parameter.
For DITA you always need to also define an ANT parameter which tunnels its value to the XSLT parameter.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2154: PDF title metadata is not generated correctly when a DITA map document has xml:lang attribute set
content:
Let's consider a sample DITA Map:
<map title="цветы" xml:lang="ru-ru">
 <topicref href="topics/introduction.dita"/>
</map>
I've transformed the map to PDF using **pdf2** transformation. After that, I've loaded the PDF in the **Adobe Reader** and I've displayed the **Document Properties** dialog. 
In the **Document Properties** dialog the document title is not displayed correctly. It is displayed the label **XMP structure: 1** instead of the map title.

I've analyzed a bit the PDF transformation and I've noticed that the **x:xmpmeta//dc:title** element from the **topic.fo** document contains **fo:inline** elements.
<x:xmpmeta>
 <rdf:RDF>
 <rdf:Description rdf:about="">
 <dc:title line-height-shift-adjustment="disregard-shifts">
 <fo:inline line-height="100%" font-family="Times New Roman, Times">цветы</fo:inline>
 </dc:title>
 <xmp:CreatorTool>DITA Open Toolkit</xmp:CreatorTool>
 </rdf:Description>
 </rdf:RDF>
 </x:xmpmeta>
I think this could be the reason of the problem because the **Apache FOP** processor is not expected to encounter these elements inside the XMP metadata language.
A solution would be to skip these elements from the **i18n-postprocess.xsl** stylesheet which processed the **stage3.fo** and produces the **topic.fo**

content: Issue #2170 is closed with labels enhancement, plugin/pdf, priority/low. Retrieval signals: error, pdf.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2170: Flagging on kwd in PDF will not work
content:
The template in pr-domain.xsl that handles pr-d/kwd uses value-of, rather than apply-templates to output the kwd element contents. As a result, the `suitesol:flagging-inside` element (stage1a.xml) will never be handled.

I've tested a fix replacing both `<xsl:value-of select="."/>` directives with `<xsl:apply-templates />` and it works correctly.

This error exists as early as DITA OT 1.6 and is still present in OT 2.2.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2188: chunk="to-content" combined with copy-to="xxx" gives rise to java NullPointerException
content:
Using the following example map file, a null pointer exception is generated by OpenToolkit v2.2 during metadata processing. The exception didn't occur in v2.1.
<map>
 <title>MyDoc</title>
 <topicmeta>
 <publisher>Acme Inc.</publisher>
 </topicmeta>
 <topichead navtitle="Manual">
 <topicref navtitle="Toolbars" href="toolbars.dita#t_toolbars"
 copy-to="ToolbarsChunk.dita" chunk="to-content">
 <topicref href="toolbars.dita#t_save"/>
 </topicref>
 </topichead>
</map>
Notes: (i) if either the chunk="to-content" or copy-to attribute is missing, the map is processed ok. (ii) Also the map must have metadata present for the null pointer exception to appear (though output appears incorrect). Little bit of investigation makes me suspect the fault is actually earlier than the metadata stage - the file named by the copy-to attribute is missing in any of the lists generated earlier.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2200: Related-links de-duplication key should not look at profiling attributes
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

content: Issue #2200 is open with labels enhancement, good first issue, priority/medium. Retrieval signals: map, html, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2200: Related-links de-duplication key should not look at profiling attributes
content:
There is a situation in which a topic with a single child topic gets included in two parts of a DITA Map, with different profiling attributes specified on the ancestors, something like this:
<!DOCTYPE map PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Map//EN" "map.dtd">
 <map>
 <title>DITA Topic Map</title>
 <topicref href="parent.dita" audience="expert">
 <topicref href="child.dita"/>
 </topicref>
 <topicref href="parent.dita">
 <topicref href="child.dita"/>
 </topicref>
 </map>
Then the DITA Map is published to XHTML without any DITAVAL filtering (or with particular filtering which allows all topicrefs to be included). When you look inside the generated "parent.html" instead of one you will find two references to the ""child.html".
at the two functions called "related-links:hideduplicates" and "related-links:link", they create the uniqueness key by also appending existing profiling attributes like platform, product, audience to it.
In my opinion, this should not be done. The filtering is probably done before this stage anyway.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2221: Improve error message for keyref that includes topic ID
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

content: Issue #2221 is closed with labels enhancement, preprocess/keyref, priority/medium, stale. Retrieval signals: error, keyref, xref.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2221: Improve error message for keyref that includes topic ID
content:
Where "concept_qd2_gt4_t5" is the ID of a topic (not an element within a topic), the OT fails to resolve the reference and does not produce a working link.

The keyref is incorrect as authored: you are only supposed to include non-topic element IDs, so this case is author error.

However, the OT could detect this error and report it as "You specified a topic ID as part of a key ref, that won't work."

In addition, it could also go ahead and treat the keyref as a keyref to the topic since that's what the author thought they were requesting.

The current behavior is to simply report the reference as unresolvable. But using oXygen, for example, the link is resolved (because oXygen is clearly not distinguishing between keyrefs to topics by ID an other keyrefs--they should also report this issue or simply not allow it to occur). So it's confusing to a typical user as to why the link didn't work when clearly the reference is correct.

It took me a while to figure out what I had done wrong, and that was only in the context of making this issue report. And I helped design the keyref mechanism.

content: Issue #2225 is closed with labels ant, enhancement, priority/low. Retrieval signals: error.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2225: Build parameters should accept consistent true-ish and false-ish values
content:
Currently, different build parameters accept true / false or yes / no values, and might be case-sensitive. This increases the likelihood of user errors when building content.

My recommendation is twofold:
- For consistency in usage and documentation, we standardize the default build parameters to use either true / false or yes / no (not a mishmash).
- For backward compatibility and to help users avoid errors, the build should parse, case-insensitively, "true-ish" values equivalently and likewise with "false-ish" values. That is to say, YES = yes = true = True.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2226: gen-variable should lower-case the content of xml:lang in strings file
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2226: gen-variable should lower-case the content of xml:lang in strings file
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2226: gen-variable should lower-case the content of xml:lang in strings file
content:
A variables file in `customization.dir` with an upper case locale (such as `de_DE.xml`, as suggested in the `vars/README.txt` file) will never be matched in `dita-utilities.xsl` (findString). This is because the xml:lang attribute set in the strings.`*.xml` contains the literal filename portion, with no lower-casing, but the predicate in the `findString` template does an exact compare (`[@xml:lang = $l]`). 

To make this bullet-proof, `org.dita.dost.pdf2.VariableFileTask` should lower-case the filename string when it generates the `xml:lang` attribute. 

We've been able to work around this issue by making sure we use lowercase for the filename, but with the `README.txt` suggesting that the locale could be uppercase, it may trap others.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2244: Bug in ...\org.dita.pdf2\xsl\common\topicmergeImpl.xsl - Reference to glossary entry does not work
content:
The xref in oxygen of course resolves correct.
However, the final PDF contains
"As **#unique_5/unique_5_Connect_42_gls_oxygen** stores much"
which apparently is a proof that the link was not solved.
I found the solution in `\org.dita.pdf2\xsl\common\topicmergIimpl.xsl` which has to be applied in the official distribution ...

Version 2.2.2 line 159
<xsl:template match="*[contains(@class,' topic/topic ')] | dita-merge/dita">
<!--HSX I had to exclude glossentry from the match in order to 
 propagate the correct id prefix. Other templates do this correctly.
 The situation occurred when trying to refer xref a glossterm -->
 <xsl:template match="*[contains(@class, ' topic/topic ')]
 [not(contains(@class, ' glossentry/glossentry '))] |
 dita-merge/dita">
The fix works since more than 6 months will all versions since. See the example PDF files on page 4 [topicmergeFix_Scherzer.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/153061/topicmergeFix_Scherzer.zip)

title: DITA-OT Issue #2259: DITA-OT assumes strong constraints rather than weak constraints
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2259: DITA-OT assumes strong constraints rather than weak constraints
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2259: DITA-OT assumes strong constraints rather than weak constraints
content:
[Section 2.5.5.4 of the DITA 1.3 Specification](http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3/os/part1-base/archSpec/base/constraints-strong-and-weak.html) states

> By default, constraints are weak unless they are explicitly designated as strong

Technically, the DITA-OT is in compliance with the spec because 2.5.5.4 also states

> Processors also can be configured to treat all constraints as strong

Strong constraints can be overly restrictive in many use cases. This is why the specification defaults to weak. For instance, strong constraint processing prevents a step in a task topic from having a conref to a step in a general task topic, despite the fact that step in both cases have identical content models and are unaffected by the strictTaskbody constraint that is preventing the conref from being resolved.

This issue is important to me because I use constraints extensively in the technical content DTDs. Having the DITA-OT default to strong constraints prevents easy interoperation between out-of-the-box technical content instances and the constrained technical content instances.

I understand that there may be use cases where strong constraint enforcement is essential. Perhaps the DITA-OT could be modified to accept an ant parameter that makes strong and weak constraint processing selectable.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2261: Eclipse Help - automatically build the contexts.xml + JAR
content:
Looking through some DITA OT patches we have for Eclipse Help, the transformation can be configured to automatically build the contexts.xml (useful if you want to point to certain topics from dialogs for example) and to create the JAR containig the entire help.
What it would take:

1) Additional targets to generate the contexts and build the JAR:
<target name="generate.contexts">
 <echo>Generate contexts.xml file from topic output files.</echo>
 <xslt in="${output.dir}/${dita.map.filename.root}.xml" out="${output.dir}/contexts.xml" style="${dita.plugin.org.dita.eclipsehelp.dir}/xsl/contexts.xsl">
 <xmlcatalog>
 <catalogpath>
 <pathelement location="${dita.dir}/catalog-dita.xml"/>
 </catalogpath>
 </xmlcatalog>
 </xslt>
 </target>

 <target name="build.eclipsehelp.jar" depends="generate.contexts"> 
 <property name="help.jar" value="${dita.map.filename.root}.jar" />
 <echo>Building Eclipse help jar file: ${help.jar}</echo>
 <jar destfile="${dita.map.output.dir}/${help.jar}" basedir="${dita.map.output.dir}">
 <include name="**/*"/>
 <exclude name="${help.jar}"/>
 <exclude name="plugin.*"/>
 </jar>
 </target>

title: DITA-OT Issue #2261: Eclipse Help - automatically build the contexts.xml + JAR
content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
 <!--OXYGEN PATCH FOR EXM-18224-->
 <xsl:stylesheet xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform" 
 xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" 
 exclude-result-prefixes="xhtml" 
 version="2.0">

 <xsl:output method="xml" indent="yes" encoding="UTF-8"/>

 <!-- The path of the dir where the Table of Contents file is located (relative to the base dir of
 the Eclipse plugin). -->
 <xsl:param name="prefixHelpInstallPath" select="''"/>

 <xsl:template match="/">
 <xsl:element name="contexts">
 <xsl:apply-templates/>
 </xsl:element>
 </xsl:template>

 <xsl:template match="topic[@href]
 [ends-with(@href, '.html') or ends-with(@href, '.xhtml')]">
 <xsl:apply-templates select="document(@href)" mode="addContext">
 <xsl:with-param name="href" select="@href"/>
 </xsl:apply-templates>
 <xsl:apply-templates/>
 </xsl:template>

 <xsl:template match="text()"/>
 <xsl:template match="text()" mode="addContext"/>

 <xsl:template match="*[@id]" mode="addContext">
 <xsl:param name="href"/>
 <xsl:element name="context">
 <xsl:attribute name="id">
 <xsl:value-of select="@id"/>
 </xsl:attribute>
 <xsl:variable name="title" select="normalize-space(/xhtml:html/xhtml:head/xhtml:title)"/>
 <xsl:if test="string-length($title) > 0">
 <description><xsl:value-of select="$title"/></description>
 <topic label="{$title}" href="{concat($prefixHelpInstallPath, $href, '#', @id)}"/>
 </xsl:if>
 </xsl:element>
 <xsl:for-each select="descendant::*[@id]">
 <xsl:apply-templates select="." mode="addContext">
 <xsl:with-param name="href" select="@href"/>
 </xsl:apply-templates>
 </xsl:for-each>
 </xsl:template>
 </xsl:stylesheet>

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2275: Sample content misleading
content:
It would appear that the content in the samples folder is misleading.

Take the case that someone has no prior knowledge of DITA. They do a search, and find the toolkit.

They download it, and see what's there.

They find a DITA processor, some instructions and some sample content. They build the sample content.

It works! Brilliant! Isn't DITA easy! All you need is Notepad to hack some DITA files.

They use the content in the samples folder as their guide. Surely this is what DITA content looks like?

Is this far-fetched? It sounds bonkers, but I'm pretty sure it happens.

The toolkit now includes source documents for the user guide.

With a bit of imagination, would it be possible to replace the samples folder with the user guide content?

Instead of a newbie building the samples content, they build the user guide instead, in various different forms.

I'm sure it would be more representative of 'real' DITA content.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2282: Toolkit Log Should List Referenced But Undefined Keys
content:
Although there might be situations where it is expected that some keyrefs point to keys that are not defined, it is probably far more frequent that content creators need to know about undefined key references. They can't rely on authoring tools to provide this information because the authoring scope could easily differ from that of publication.

Some closed issues suggest that in the past, the toolkit logged such instances, but recent versions (1.8, 2.0) do not.

It might be desirable to have the option to suppress such logging by a build parameter or to log these as information-only rather than warnings.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2286: Implement release management domain processing for org.dita.html5
content:
I implemented the processing of the `relmgmt-d` elements for `org.dita.pdf2` (https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/pull/2248). Here I used a custom `<booklist>` element to hook the creation of a change-history, compareable to `<figurelist>` or `<toc>`.
Now I think about how to implement the processing for `org.dita.html5`. Personally I'd like to hook the creation of the change-history by element, as I did for `org.dita.pdf2`. Unfortunately there is no pendant for `bookmap` (no `webmap`). The `bookmap` is not intended for webhelp publishing (but it works fine), so hooking on `<booklist type="change-historylist"/>` may not be the best decision. And there is no pendant for the `<booklist>` element in the standard DITA Map.

> **Info** The `<booklist>` element is a specialization of `<topicref>`.

@jelovirt suggested to discuss this in a public manner (in a Github issue), because this is a design decision.

I'd personally prefer if processing is toggled technically equal, independent of the transtype. Why should I set an Ant property for HTML but use an XML element for PDF to hook the same processing? This feels weird to me. But the `pdf2` is more focussed on element hooks and the `xhtml` types are more focussed on Ant property hooks.

What do you think? How would you like to have this implemented?

title: DITA-OT Issue #2288: build_dita2htmlhelp.xml should use environment variable
content:
<target name="use-init.hhcdir" unless="env.HHCDIR">
<condition property="hhc.dir"
 value="C:\Program Files (x86)\HTML Help Workshop"
 else="C:\Program Files\HTML Help Workshop">
 <available file="C:\Program Files (x86)\HTML Help Workshop" type="dir"/>
</condition>
<available file="${hhc.dir}/hhc.exe"
 property="HTMLHelpCompiler"
 value="${hhc.dir}${file.separator}hhc.exe"/>
</target>

which should actually use
<target name="use-init.hhcdir" unless="env.HHCDIR">
 <!--HSX Flaw in Dita-OT ... do not use C: but use ${env ...} -->
 <condition property="hhc.dir"
 value="${env.ProgramFiles(x86)}\HTML Help Workshop"
 else="${env.ProgramFiles)}\HTML Help Workshop">
 <available file="${env.ProgramFiles(x86)}\HTML Help Workshop" type="dir"/>
 </condition>
 <available file="${hhc.dir}/hhc.exe"

 value="${hhc.dir}${file.separator}hhc.exe"/>

The hard assignment to C:\ ... might work for 99% of Windows installations and is probably there for some reason in the past. However, my OS is on D:\ (for good reasons) and nevertheless it seems appropriate to me that the environment variables are used.

The severity of this issue is of course moderate, but I think it's a good time for the small change.
Cheers ... Helmut

title: DITA-OT Issue #2300: HTML: Topicsetref with key scope breaks output by munging result filenames
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2300: HTML: Topicsetref with key scope breaks output by munging result filenames
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2300: HTML: Topicsetref with key scope breaks output by munging result filenames
content: Issue #2300 is closed with labels needs reproduction, stale. Retrieval signals: map, html.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2300: HTML: Topicsetref with key scope breaks output by munging result filenames
content:
Using the test case here: https://github.com/dita-community/dita-test-cases/tree/master/topicsets and using OT 2.2.4 on OS X

The map includes the following combinations of topicsetref and topicset:
- No keyscope on either
- Keyscope on topicsetref, none on topicset
- Keyscope on topicset, none on topicsetref
- Keywcope on both topicset and topicsetref

The key resolution behavior is not completely defined in these cases.

However, regardless of whether or not the keys should be resolved, the key scopes on the topicsetrefs appear to be causing the OT to generate references to munged filenames for the topics in Map B. 

I think this behavior is incorrect. 

The nature of topicsets is that they are treated as "independent units" in the context of HTML-type outputs. The implication is that the topicset's output will be produced at some other time and integrated with the referencing map's output at delivery time or at read time.

The OT's current behavior seems to anticipate this as it's constructing references to the supposed HTML generated from Map B but not actually processing Map B to produce that output. 

If Map B is processed separately then there's no way for Map B to know how it is used from any Maps and therefore no way for it to produced the variously-munged result filenames the OT is generating for the different uses.

It think this is really symptomatic of a deeper design issue with topicsetrefs, namely that they can't really work as specified in the face of key scopes and branch filtering.

But if the OT simply does not munge the filenames of result files generated for topicsets then the current behavior will work when there are key scopes just as it does when there are not key scopes (assuming that the generation of the output for the map containing the topicsets is coordinated with the generation of the output of the referencing maps).

title: DITA-OT Issue #2301: PDF: Key references to scoped keys in topicsets are not resolved
content:
Using the test case here: https://github.com/dita-community/dita-test-cases/tree/master/topicsets and using OT 2.2.4 on OS X

This may actually be a more general issue with resolution of scoped keys in PDF but there is a topicsetref-specific wrinkle here that is separate from any general key scope resolution issues.

The current behavior is that _none_ of the key references are resolved in the PDF. 

In the test case there are combinations of topicsetref and topicset where both specify key scope names.

In this case the DITA 1.3 specification does not say what the correct behavior is. However, it does say that topicsetref should be treated like other map-to-map references which strongly implies that the "merge the scopes" behavior defined for map references that refer to the map element.

That is, there should be one effective scope with two scope names, not a parent scope (defined by the topicsetref and a child scope (defined by the topicset).

However, either behavior can be supported based on the current 1.3 specification since it doesn't explicitly say what happens for topicsetref. But behaving the same as a map-to-map ref would certainly be the least surprising behavior.

For this test, if you generate PDF from Map A then all but one of the xrefs should resolve. The unresolved xref will reflect the scope combination option not implemented.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2302: XHTML transtype problem (and solution): Content from RTL tables is aligned to the left
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2302: XHTML transtype problem (and solution): Content from RTL tables is aligned to the left
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2302: XHTML transtype problem (and solution): Content from RTL tables is aligned to the left
content:
Insert a table with arabic content into a topic. Put xml:lang="ar" and dir="rtl" on the root of the topic, then transform it to XHTML. You can use this fragment below, but the problem can be seen on english content in a RTL table also. النبات الحبي النباتات الحبية المختلفة و منتجاتها
The text from table cells are aligned to the left inside each of the cells. This is wrong, it should be aligned to the right. For LTR tables it should be to the left. The problem is in the file: `DITA-OT2.x/plugins/org.dita.xhtml/xsl/xslhtml/dita2htmlImpl.xsl` in template: `` Here is computed the style attribute for each of the table entries. There are some default values for text-align and vertical-align set to "left" and "top". The default values should not be specified, so the browser can infer them from the parent elements/styles. **The solution is:** Remove the xsl:otherwise blocks.

content:
<xsl:variable name="align" as="xs:string?">
 <xsl:choose>
 <xsl:when test="@align">
 <xsl:value-of select="@align"/>
 </xsl:when>
 <xsl:when test="$group/@align">
 <xsl:value-of select="$group/@align"/>
 </xsl:when>
 <xsl:when test="$colspec/@align">
 <xsl:value-of select="$colspec/@align"/>
 </xsl:when>
 <!-- PATCH START --> 
 <!--
 <xsl:otherwise>
 <xsl:value-of select="$table.align-default"/>
 </xsl:otherwise>
 -->
 </xsl:choose>
 </xsl:variable>
 <xsl:if test="exists($align)">
 <xsl:text>text-align:</xsl:text>
 <xsl:value-of select="$align"/>
 <xsl:text>;</xsl:text>
 </xsl:if>
 <xsl:variable name="valign" as="xs:string?">
 <xsl:choose>
 <xsl:when test="@valign">
 <xsl:value-of select="@valign"/>
 </xsl:when>
 <xsl:when test="$row/@valign">
 <xsl:value-of select="$row/@valign"/>
 </xsl:when>
 <xsl:when test="$body/@valign">
 <xsl:value-of select="$body/@valign"/>
 </xsl:when>
 <!-- PATCH START --> 
 <!--
 <xsl:otherwise>top</xsl:otherwise>
 -->
 </xsl:choose>

> /Users/staylor/Dev/dita_source_files/build/deps/DITA-OT2.2.4/build.xml:41: The following error occurred while executing this line:
/Users/staylor/Dev/dita_source_files/build/deps/DITA-OT2.2.4/plugins/org.dita.xhtml/build_general.xml:162: Fatal error during transformation using /Users/staylor/Dev/dita_source_files/build/deps/DITA-OT2.2.4/plugins/org.dita.html5/xsl/dita2html5.xsl: In the key() function, the node supplied in the third argument (or the context node if absent) must be in a tree whose root is a document node; SystemID: file:/Users/staylor/Dev/dita_source_files/build/deps/DITA-OT2.2.4/plugins/org.dita.xhtml/xsl/xslhtml/dita2htmlImpl.xsl; Line#: 1128; Column#: -1

After much experimenting, I discovered this was breaking when a `<tm>` tag was present in the link text of a related link, as in this example.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2310: Use DITA to manage string content and vars?
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2310: Use DITA to manage string content and vars?
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2310: Use DITA to manage string content and vars?
content: Issue #2310 is closed with labels feature, plugin/pdf. Retrieval signals: keyref, map, pdf, html, dita-ot, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2310: Use DITA to manage string content and vars?
content:
OK, maybe this is just a wild and crazy idea? I don't know enough about XSLT to evaluate the idea fully, nor do I know enough about the processing architecture behind the DITA-OT.

My primary interaction with the DITA-OT is through PDF and the PDF2 plug-in. The following is written with this in mind, but should be suitable for all transforms.

Well, here goes ...

DITA is about documentation and managing content, so why not put the DITA-OT strings and graphics into DITA? Move them from XSLT to DITA.

This would encompass the language dependent strings, language dependent graphics, language agnostic graphics and language agnostic 'string constructs' used in headers and footers. There are no doubt other similar strings for other transforms.

It would require a DITA specialisation. Let's call it 'dotvars'. I'm sure someone can improve on this. 'dotvarstopic' & 'dotvarsmap'.

The content model would be necessarily sparse. Firstly to encourage a good match to XSLT variables and constructs, and secondly because the semantic model is at the text, string, image level. In other words, no rich content model, and minimise confusion.

I would suggest that the content model is primarily based upon a specialisation of `<dl/>`, say:

title: DITA-OT Issue #2310: Use DITA to manage string content and vars?
content:
`<dotvarsdt/>` would provide the XSLT variable name.

Multiple `<dotvarsdd/>` would provide alternative definitions for the XSLT variable.

`<dotvarsdd/>` would have a child element of `<ditaelement/>` to indicate the DITA element that the XSLT transform should choose. In turn, this would have a `<ditaattribute/>` element to indicate the attribute of the DITA element that the XSLT transform should choose. `<ditaelement/>` could also contain itself as a child, to correspond to the DITA element tree.

So, an example for the map title might look like this:
<dotvarsdl>
 <dotvarsdlhead>
 <dotvarsdthd>Map title</dotvarsdthd>
 <dotvarsddhd>Alternative definitions</dotvarsddhd>
 </dotvarsdlhead>
 <dotvarsdlentry>
 <dotvarsdt>maptitle</dotvarsdt>
 <dotvarsdd><text conkeyref="document/title"/></dotvarsdd>
 <dotvarsdd>
 <ditaelement>map<ditaelement>title</ditaelement></ditaelement>
 </dotvarsdd>
 <dotvarsdd>
 <ditaelement>map<ditaattribute>title</ditaattribute></ditaelement>
 </dotvarsdd>
 </dotvarsdlentry>
</dotvarsdl>

title: DITA-OT Issue #2310: Use DITA to manage string content and vars?
content:
xml:lang would provide i18n support. The process would match the xml:lang defined by the DITA content with equivalent xml:lang variables.

It would be possible to group variables of the same language into a dotvarstopic with xml:lang at the topic level. Alternatively, it would be possible to group variables of the same type into a topic with xml:lang at the `<dotvarsdl/>` or `<dotvarsdd/>` level.

The aim would be to first attempt a match for the specific language, en-GB, or the generic language, en, or with a language agnostic variable.

As an example, there is an international symbol for X-rays that would be language agnostic. However, the Canadians have their own symbol. So if the language of the DITA content were en-CA or fr-CA, then it would pick up the Canadian symbol. Otherwise, it would pick up the international symbol.

How about the string constructs for headers and footers?

Firstly, it is necessary to link variables defined by `<dotvarsdl/>` to their use in a string construct. Maybe `<dotvarsstringvar/>`? The XSLT transform would match `<dotvarsstringvar>maptitle</dotvarsstringvar>` to its definition by `<dotvarsdt>maptitle</dotvarsdt>`, and then pick up the first <dotvarsdd/> that is not empty, and matches xml:lang.

A string construct could have multiple lines. This would be represented not by multiple `<dotvarsdd/>`, but by a series of child 
`<dotvarsblock/>`. The use of 'block' might be too close to XSL:FO language. It would be a specialisation of `<p/>`, but should use naming applicable to a XSLT transform that can produces XSL:FO or XHTML. Therefore, not simply `<dotvarsp/>`. Hmmm? XHTML does use `<p/>`! It would, however, be useful to use an element name that signifies it is part of the transform.

It would be necessary to have a mechanism to pick up XSLT generated standard variables. For example: date and time, page number, current top topic title. These would not really have a content model as they would just be place holders. Element names such as: `<dotvarsdate/>`, `<dotvarspagenum/>`, `<dotvarstoptopic/>`? The assumption is that it would be possible to format these with attribute sets, so the elements would be empty.

An example might be:

title: DITA-OT Issue #2310: Use DITA to manage string content and vars?
content:
<dotvarsdl>
 <dotvarsdlhead>
 <dotvarsdthd>Odd page header</dotvarsdthd>
 <dotvarsddhd>Document name and page number on one line, current top topic on second line</dotvarsddhd>
 </dotvarsdlhead>
 <dotvarsdlentry>
 <dotvarsdt>oddpageheader</dotvarsdt>
 <dotvarsdd>
 <dotvarsblock><dotvarsstringvar>maptitle</dotvarsstringvar> | <dotvarspagenum/></dotvarsblock>
 <dotvarsblock><dotvarstoptopic/></dotvarsblock>
 </dotvarsdlentry>
</dotvarsdl>
One new attribute would be very useful, to pick up and connect with XSLT attribute sets: @attribute-set. It would need some careful thought about which elements should have this.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2312: Remove unimplemented parameter extension points from HTML5 plug-in
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2312: Remove unimplemented parameter extension points from HTML5 plug-in
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2312: Remove unimplemented parameter extension points from HTML5 plug-in
content:
However, these can't be used because they aren't implemented in an Ant build template `<xslt>` step. That wasn't done (rightly, I think) because the HTML5 plug-in uses the base HTML Ant templates.
- Implementing the missing extension-points would require duplicating the templates from the base HTML plug-in, which would be a maintenance problem and just bad generally.
- Implementers who want to add parameters to the HTML5 transformation can instead:
 - require the base HTML plug-in as well as the HTML5 plug-in
 - extend the base HTML plug-in's parameter extension points
- Keeping the un-implemented HTML5 extension points obscures that fact and creates confusion because implementers should rightly expect these extension points to work.

I'll submit a PR to remove these.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2316: Build takes forever performing image-metadata check on external images
content:

title: DITA-OT Issue #2316: Build takes forever performing image-metadata check on external images
content: Issue #2316 is closed with labels plugin/html5, preprocess, stale. Retrieval signals: error, exception, html, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2316: Build takes forever performing image-metadata check on external images
content:
OT version: 2.2.4
Transformation type: extension of the HTML5 transformation
Platforms: Mac OS X (local) and UNIX (Jenkins)

Part of our docset references some 1200 images directly by URL rather than maintaining duplicate copies that are likely to become out of date. When I build locally, the image-metadata check generates many errors like the following:

> Failed to read image https://www.webassign.net/images/Ihat.gif metadata: sun.security.validator.ValidatorException: PKIX path building failed: sun.security.provider.certpath.SunCertPathBuilderException: unable to find valid certification path to requested target

This happens even though I can access the images in question using the same URL in my browser.

When I build on our Jenkins server, the build keeps running (stuck at this step) for over 12 hours until we abort it.

I can work around the problem (tested locally only) in either of two ways:
- set the noImagelist property to skip the image-metadata check altogether
- change all the "https" protocols to "http" in the DITA source

These workarounds should not be needed. The image-metadata step should handle this situation more gracefully. Some ideas that occur to me:
- omit checking external images altogether
- omit checking external images after a certain number of such checks have failed or timed out
- omit checking external images based on a build parameter
- check external images using http if https fails (and notify in the log)
- always check external images using http (and notify in the log if the DITA source uses https)

title: DITA-OT Issue #2317: PDF: Values set for @expanse attribute are not used
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2317: PDF: Values set for @expanse attribute are not used
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2317: PDF: Values set for @expanse attribute are not used
content:
For the PDF2 transformation and the codeblock, fig, and pre elements, there is no difference when expanse="page" versus expanse="column". 

I would have expected expanse="page" to force the element to be rendered aligned with the page margin (where H1 begins) as opposed to being rendered aligned with the indentation that is specified for the content.

Per the DITA 1.3 spec at http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3/os/part1-base/langRef/attributes/displayAttributes.html#display-atts:

> **@expanse**
> Determines the horizontal placement of the element. Allowable values are:
> 
> **page**
> Places the element on the left page margin for left-to-right presentation, or right page margin for right-to-left presentation. 
> **column**
> Aligns the element with the current column margin 
> **textline**
> Aligns the element with the left (for left to right presentation) or right (for right to left presentation) margin of the current text line and takes indention into account. 
> **spread**
> Indicates that, if possible, the object should be rendered across a multi-page spread. If the rendition target does not have anything corresponding to spreads then spread has the same meaning as "page". 
> **-dita-use-conref-target**
> See Using the -dita-use-conref-target value for more information. 
> 
> In DITA tables, in place of the @expanse attribute used by other DITA elements, the @pgwide attribute is used in order to conform to the OASIS Exchange Table Model. The @pgwide attribute has a similar semantic (1=page width; 0=resize to galley or column).
> 
> Some DITA processors or output formats might not be able to support all values.

---

Does the DITA-OT transformation NOT support the @expanse attribute?

I have a ZIP that contains a test set of files, but I cannot attach it here.

content: Issue #2319 is closed with labels plugin/pdf, question, support. Retrieval signals: pdf.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2319: PDF2: Is there a 'best practice' method to creating custom stylesheets?
content:
There are a number of options to creating custom stylesheets.

One method would be to put all the customisations into one of the two custom.xsl files.

For a simple customisation, that is probably a good idea.

The alternative is to use the two custom.xsl files to import customised stylesheets and retain the original file names. For a more complex customisation, it can help to retain the original file name.

However, if you start with a full copy of the original stylesheet, then there will be a lot of templates, variables, etc., etc. that are left untouched.

So, the question is whether to leave these untouched templates, etc., in the customised stylesheet, or to delete them?

Apologies if this is an obvious question!

title: DITA-OT Issue #2321: Topicset @type attribute warning in move-meta-entries
content:
Version: DITA-OT 2.2.4
Transformation: HTML5 customization
Platform: OS X

Since upgrading my plugin to 2.2.4, I see warnings in my build log for topicsets:

> file:/Users/staylor/Dev/dita_source_files/m_a_common_topicsets.ditamap:12:69: [DOTX019W][WARN]: The type attribute on a topicref was set to 'topicset', but the topicref references a 'concept' topic. This may cause your links to sort incorrectly in the output. Note that the type attribute cascades in maps, so the value 'topicset' may come from an ancestor topicref.

My map doesn't specify `@type="topicset"` anywhere. I'm reasonably sure this is an error in xsl/preprocess/mappullImpl.xsl:

title: DITA-OT Issue #2321: Topicset @type attribute warning in move-meta-entries
content:
<xsl:template match="*" mode="mappull:verify-type-value">
 <xsl:param name="type" as="xs:string"/> <!-- Specified type on the topicref -->
 <xsl:param name="actual-class" as="xs:string"/> <!-- Class value on the target element -->
 <xsl:param name="actual-name" as="xs:string"/> <!-- Name of the target element -->
 <xsl:param name="WORKDIR" as="xs:string">
 <xsl:apply-templates select="/processing-instruction('workdir-uri')[1]" mode="get-work-dir"/>
 </xsl:param>
 <xsl:choose>
 <!-- The type is correct; concept typed as concept, newtype defined as newtype -->
 <xsl:when test="$type=$actual-name"/>
 <!-- If the actual class contains the specified type; reference can be called topic,
 specializedReference can be called reference -->
 <xsl:when test="contains($actual-class,concat(' ',$type,'/',$type,' '))">
 <!-- commented out for bug:1771123 start -->
 <!--xsl:apply-templates select="." mode="ditamsg:type-mismatch-info">
 <xsl:with-param name="type" select="$type"/>
 <xsl:with-param name="actual-name" select="$actual-name"/>
 </xsl:apply-templates-->
 <!-- commented out for bug:1771123 end -->
 </xsl:when>
 <!-- Otherwise: incorrect type is specified -->
 <xsl:otherwise>
 <xsl:apply-templates select="." mode="ditamsg:type-mismatch-warning">
 <xsl:with-param name="type" select="$type"/>
 <xsl:with-param name="actual-name" select="$actual-name"/>
 </xsl:apply-templates>
 </xsl:otherwise>
 </xsl:choose>

title: DITA-OT Issue #2335: PDF2: Page sequence logic
content:
I'd like to take a step back and describe some of the issues with PDFs and book publishing. Hopefully, by having a debate at this level, it will inform some of the decisions and requirements for PDF2.

`TLDR:` See summary at end. [Cats Reading Books](http://theverybesttop10.com/cats-reading-books/).

Equipment manufacturers have a large number of regulations and safety requirements to consider. These increase in severity from domestic equipment, to industrial to medical equipment. This often leads the manufacturer to print a booklet and include it with the equipment. The rationale is that the customer is more likely to read a printed booklet than they are to look at embedded documentation or an online resource.

Apple is a good example. Whilst they are known for minimalist documentation, they usually include a densely printed booklet with all the regulatory and safety requirements that the product meets, for multiple territories. Does anyone read this? The regulators certainly do, and so the primary aim is to avoid litigation.

The issue with printed technical documentation is that the print run is limited to the demand for the product. Apple doesn't have an issue with this, of course, but many equipment manufacturers produce equipment in much smaller quantities. This leads to low print runs, and often short run digital print. It also affects the binding, and printed documentation is often in plastic spiral binding, or wire, calendar style binding, or even hole punched and put in ring binders. Medical equipment might include a book shelf worth of ring bound documentation.

So, what are the requirements for PDF and print?

Firstly, both ditamap and bookmap are equally valid and useful. Ditamap is great for a small safety or how to booklet. Bookmap handles the requirements for larger tomes.

Usually, the start of a new section is on a fresh page. By section this would be a chapter, ToC, appendix, etc. in a bookmap, or a top level topic in a ditamap. Top level implies the top level in a ToC, which would be the root of a ditamap, and a first level heading. Section in this context is not a DITA `< section/>`.

If the book is printed, then the start of each section would be on an odd page, and it would have facing pages, `$mirror-page-margins = true()`. This is pretty much ubiquitous, and applies equally to ditamap and to bookmap. By contrast, a PDF as an online or embedded resource might not require facing pages. A bookmap is almost certain to use facing pages because of its formality, whether it is actually printed or not.

The start of a section would typically include the section title, and perhaps the chapter number for a bookmap. As this information might also be in the page heading, the page heading is often removed from the first page of a section. This leads to a possible requirement for a different first page design. However, this is not always the case.

The requirement for a last page is quite different to that for a first page. There is no requirement for first page, last page design symmetry. The requirement for a last page is to do with pagination. If the book uses facing pages, then a situation can often arise where one section ends on an odd page, and the next has to start on an odd page. So the requirement, in this situation, is for the addition of a blank even page between the two sections.

Usually, a last blank page will use the even page design. However, with loose binding, a customer might enquire whether the page should be blank, or whether some information is missing. In this situation, a company might include a statement such as this in the heading: "This page is intentionally blank". This is typically the only requirement for a last blank page design. If there is such a requirement, then this design could typically be used for every section type: chapter, appendix, ToC, index, etc.

`TLDR:`
So a lot rests on the choice of facing pages or not, `$mirror-page-margins`.

Without facing pages:

Only a single page design, not odd and even page designs.
If there is a first page requirement, this could be an odd or even page.
The last blank page pagination situation never arises, by definition. Therefore, no last page requirement.

With facing pages:

Typically both odd and even page designs, although they could, perhaps, use the same design.
If there is a first page requirement, it will be an odd page.
The last blank page pagination situation does arise.
A last blank page might require an 'intentionally blank' statement.

For DITA, and the DOT, a summary of the differences between map types:

Ditamap:
Equally likely to use facing pages, or not. Cannot safely assume no facing pages.
Less likely to have a first page design, but cannot safely assume no first page design.
A simple ditamap booklet might well use the same page designs for ToC and body.
A simple ditamap PDF might not use facing pages, and might only need a single page design for ToC and body.

Bookmap:
More likely to use facing pages.
More likely to use a first page design.
The formality of a bookmap might lead to a last blank page with an 'intentionally blank' statement.

No map:
PDF2 should also be able to create a PDF for a single topic, without either a ditamap or bookmap.
PDF2 would need to assume a default design, either ditamap or bookmap. Probably ditamap.
Does a PDF of a single topic require a front page and a ToC? Probably not.

The hope and expectation is that this should cover the majority of the requirements for PDF and printed documentation, say 90% plus. Of course, technical documentation can always throw up peculiar situations and requirements.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2339: @keyscope on the root <map> element causes builds to fail
content:
It seems that using `@keyscope` on the root `<map>` element causes builds to fail. (Put aside for the moment the fact that a keyspace on `<map>` is a bad practice. The spec allows it, so it should work: "Map authors define the boundaries for key scopes by specifying the `@keyscope` attribute on `<map>` elements, `<topicref>` elements, or elements that are specializations of `<map>` or `<topicref>`. ")

Sample map:
<map keyscope="widget">
 <title>Keyscope test 4</title>
 <keydef keys="module">
 <topicmeta>
 <keywords>
 <keyword>Widget</keyword>
 </keywords>
 </topicmeta>
 </keydef>
 <topicgroup keyscope="gadget">
 <keydef keys="module">
 <topicmeta>
 <keywords>
 <keyword>Gadget</keyword>
 </keywords>
 </topicmeta>
 </keydef>
 <topicref href="topic1.xml" keyscope="doodad">
 <keydef keys="module">
 <topicmeta>
 <keywords>
 <keyword>Doodad</keyword>
 </keywords>
 </topicmeta>
 </keydef>
 </topicref>
 </topicgroup>
</map>
With a simple keyref such as `<ph keyref="module"/>` in topic1.xml, the build fails. With a pathed keyref such as `<ph keyref="widget.gadget.doodad.module/>` in topic7.xml, the build still fails.

Removing the keyspace definition from the `<map>` and using `<ph keyref="module"/>` in topic1.xml, the key resolves to "Widget," as expected. Using `<ph keyref="gadget.doodad.module"/>`, the key resolves to "Doodad," as expected.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2345: Logic bug in findString
content:
<xsl:when test="exists($l)">
 <xsl:variable name="stringfile" select="$stringFiles[@xml:lang = $l]/@filename" as="xs:string*"/>
 <xsl:variable name="str" as="element()*">
 <xsl:for-each select="$stringfile">
 <xsl:sequence select="document(., $stringFiles[1])/*/*[@name = $id or @id = $id]"/><!-- strings/str/@name opentopic-vars:vars/opentopic-vars:variable/@id -->
 </xsl:for-each>
 </xsl:variable>
I've highlighted `$stringFiles[1]`. I think this must be wrong because the `$stringfile` variable is a list of filenames that is then iterated by the for-each but the for-each will only ever use the first value in `$stringFiles`. I think the correct behavior (or intended behavior) is to use the current item in the for-each loop.

The result of this bug should be that overrides are never found or are found if and only if the override happens to be the first one found.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2348: Implement link specializations in relationship tables
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2348: Implement link specializations in relationship tables
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2348: Implement link specializations in relationship tables
content:
Since #2199, related links can be specialized to model special types of links. So now you can model something like that in a topic:
...
<related-terms class="- topic/related-links termentry/related-terms ">
 <relatedTerms class="- topic/linklist termentry/relatedTerms ">
 <relatedTerm keyref="TERM_Anmelder" class="- topic/link termentry/termRelation termentry/relatedTerm "/>
 </relatedTerms>
 <hypernyms class="- topic/linklist termentry/hypernyms ">
 <hypernym keyref="TERM_Benutzer" class="- topic/link termentry/termRelation termentry/hypernym "/>
 </hypernyms>
</related-terms>
...
This works pretty well. Unfortunately these special relationships currently cannot be modelled with relationship tables, because they are designed differently.

It would be nice, if the type of relation also could be defined here, e.g. in the `<relheader>`.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2349: Support additional definition list rendering options
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2349: Support additional definition list rendering options
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2349: Support additional definition list rendering options
content:
The default definition list output differs significantly between HTML & PDF output, which often confuses new users. 
- In HTML output for `<dl>` & `<parml>`, terms are rendered on one line, with definitions on a line below. 
- In PDF output, definition list entries are converted to table rows, with term and definition in columns.
- Parameter list entries render in PDF with an style reminiscent of HTML, with indented definitions.

We should consider adding a parameter that would toggle definition list rendering between the default (table) and an indented style as used for `<parml>` or [alternative presentation styles](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2198#issuecomment-171953011) such as those provided by the [dita-generator](http://dita-generator.elovirta.com/#p4).

This would permit users to configure the rendering style that best matches their needs and allow them to sync presentation between HTML & PDF, or render `<dl>` & `<parml>` consistently.

While some users [prefer](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2198#issuecomment-171953766) the default tabular output to conserve vertical space in simple scenarios where term and definition are both short, this format actually requires **more** space in lists where definitions are significantly longer than their terms.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2358: args.hdf should not have a root element
content:

title: DITA-OT Issue #2358: args.hdf should not have a root element
content: Issue #2358 is closed with labels plugin/html5, plugin/xhtml. Retrieval signals: error, exception, html, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2358: args.hdf should not have a root element
content:
The parameter `args.hdf` specifies an XML file that contains content to be placed in the document head, see [dita-ot docs: HTML-based output parameters](http://www.dita-ot.org/2.2/parameters/parameters-base-html.html).

`args.hdf` is parsed and needs to have a root element. Because of that, you cannot inject a bunch of `<link>` and `<script>` elements at once to, for example, include multiple JS and CSS files. You only can inject a single element.

If you put multiple elements in the XML file, SAX complains about that:
Error reported by XML parser Cause: org.xml.sax.SAXParseException; systemId: file:/../hdf.xml; lineNumber: 4; columnNumber: 2; The markup in the document following the root element must be well-formed.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2365: Improve documentation of args.hdf
content:
It is possible to inject code into the HTML header using a hdf file, that can be passed using the `args.hdf` parameter. A hdf file must be a valid XML file. Therefore it needs to have a root element. So it is not possible to inject multiple elements.

**Valid**:
<!-- For header file processing, pull out the wrapping DIV if one is there -->
<xsl:template match="/div" mode="add-HDF">
 <xsl:apply-templates select="*|comment()|processing-instruction()|text()" mode="add-HDF"/>
</xsl:template>
Currently this is not explained in the docs, see [HTML-based output parameters](http://www.dita-ot.org/2.2/parameters/parameters-base-html.html) -> `args.hdf`.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2371: Putting chunked topicrefs to topics in composite in topicgroup results in unchunked result
content:
Using 2.3 develop branch:

Given a `<dita>` document with two topics, if I create a map that references the two topics in the composite using only chunk="select-branch to-content" topicrefs and and the topicrefs are **not** in a topicgroup, then only the requested chunks are created and nothing is generated for the composite as a whole.

However, if I change the map _only_ by moving the topicrefs to the composite topics into a topicgroup element, then, in addition to the requested chunked topics, the processor creates two unchunked files for the composite (temporary .dita files and then corresponding HTML files using the XHTML transform).

In this case the unchunked files should not be created since they were not requested and are not wanted (and even if it was appropriate to generate the unchunked result there should not be two of them).

This suggests a logic bug in the chunk processing.

Note that having the chunked topicrefs be children of regular topicrefs does not appear to be a factor, only being in or not in a topicgroup.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2372: PDF2 pagination: force-page-count
content:
#2335, `commons-attr.xsl`

This uses a test for bookmap, it should use a test for `$mirror-page-margins` instead.

It makes a wrong assumption for both bookmap and ditamap. There is no reason that a bookmap will always use facing pages, and similarly there is no reason a ditamap will always use plain pages.

Current:
<xsl:attribute-set name="__force__page__count">
 <xsl:attribute name="force-page-count">
 <xsl:choose>
 <xsl:when test="/*[contains(@class, ' bookmap/bookmap ')]">
 <xsl:value-of select="'even'"/>
 </xsl:when>
 <xsl:otherwise>
 <xsl:value-of select="'auto'"/>
 </xsl:otherwise>
 </xsl:choose>
 </xsl:attribute>
 </xsl:attribute-set>
Should become:
<xsl:attribute-set name="__force__page__count">
 <xsl:attribute name="force-page-count">
 <xsl:choose>
 <xsl:when test="$mirror-page-margins">
 <xsl:value-of select="'even'"/>
 </xsl:when>
 <xsl:otherwise>
 <xsl:value-of select="'auto'"/>
 </xsl:otherwise>
 </xsl:choose>
 </xsl:attribute>
 </xsl:attribute-set>

title: DITA-OT Issue #2373: PDF2 pagination: Last page logic
content:
#2318, #2335, `layout-masters.xsl`

I think the logic here is just wrong! First, it is the source of the bug in #2318. By default, it adds a last page to all sequences except for `ditamap-body-sequence`, and it is an even page. If `$mirror-page-margins` is false, there shouldn't be an even page at all, but the last page logic can insert one as a last page.

By commenting out `blank-or-not-blank="blank"` it misses out on a crucial aspect of paginataion with facing pages. That is that it is necessary to add a blank page if one section ends on an odd page, and the next section starts on an odd page.

I assume it was commented out for the sake of the back cover?

Current:

title: DITA-OT Issue #2373: PDF2 pagination: Last page logic
content:

 <xsl:template name="generate-page-sequence-master">
 <xsl:param name="master-name"/>
 <xsl:param name="master-reference"/>
 <xsl:param name="first" select="true()"/>
 <xsl:param name="last" select="true()"/>
 <fo:page-sequence-master master-name="{$master-name}">
 <fo:repeatable-page-master-alternatives>
 <xsl:if test="$first">
 <fo:conditional-page-master-reference master-reference="{$master-reference}-first"
 odd-or-even="odd"
 page-position="first"/>
 </xsl:if>
 <xsl:if test="$last">
 <fo:conditional-page-master-reference master-reference="{$master-reference}-last"
 odd-or-even="even"
 page-position="last"/>
 <!--blank-or-not-blank="blank"-->
 </xsl:if>
 <xsl:choose>
 <xsl:when test="$mirror-page-margins">
 <fo:conditional-page-master-reference master-reference="{$master-reference}-odd"
 odd-or-even="odd"/>
 <fo:conditional-page-master-reference master-reference="{$master-reference}-even"
 odd-or-even="even"/>
 </xsl:when>
 <xsl:otherwise>
 <fo:conditional-page-master-reference master-reference="{$master-reference}-odd"/>
 </xsl:otherwise>
 </xsl:choose>
 </fo:repeatable-page-master-alternatives>
 </fo:page-sequence-master>

 </xsl:template>

title: DITA-OT Issue #2373: PDF2 pagination: Last page logic
content:
Boolean algebra is less than ideal, because the new default of `$last` is false does not mean no last page, it means there might be a blank last page, if pagination requires. More fuzzy logic than boolean. The second test for `$mirror-page-margins` might not be necessary because if it is false, there will not be a need for a blank last page.

The back cover now overrides the default with a `true()`.

All the simple master sequences would change so that `"***-last"` is also wrapped in the test `<xsl:if test="$mirror-page-margins">`, except for the back cover.
