content: Issue #2376 is closed with labels enhancement, plugin/pdf, stale. Retrieval signals: map, pdf.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2376: PDF2 pagination: Default page designs
content:
I suggest the defaults for `$mirror-page-margins`, `$add-first-page` and `$toc-use-body-pages` would be map based:
<xsl:choose>
 <xsl:when test="$mapType = 'bookmap'">
 <xsl:variable name="mirror-page-margins" select="true()"/>
 <xsl:variable name="add-first-page" select="true()"/>
 <xsl:variable name="toc-use-body-pages" select="false()"/>
 <xsl:otherwise>
 <xsl:variable name="mirror-page-margins" select="false()"/>
 <xsl:variable name="add-first-page" select="false()"/>
 <xsl:variable name="toc-use-body-pages" select="true()"/>
 </xsl:otherwise>
 </xsl:choose>
This would put the basic pagination settings in `basic-settings.xsl`, so they are easy to find, and should be easy to understand.
This could also do away with the need for `ditamap-body-sequence`. Certainly its use in `layout-masters.xsl` is just to set defaults, and would not be necessary. However, it is also used in `root-processing.xsl`, so I'm not entirely sure.
`ditamap-body-sequence` only does half a job for ditamap as it leaves the ditamap using the standard ToC. The two new proposed variables, `$add-first-page` and `$toc-use-body-pages`, in conjunction with $mirror-page-margins` would be a much better solution.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2378: PDF2 pagination: "This page is intentionally blank"
content:
#2335, `layout-masters.xsl`, `vars`

The last proposed change to pagination. When the pagination requires a blank page between sections, the header would carry the message, "This page is intentionally blank".

So, this would be a new page design, but it would be generic, and would be used for chapters, appendices, ToC, index, glossary, etc. as required.

The drawback is that it introduces a new string, that would need translation.

The page design would not, necessarily, need a footer.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2379: Invalid ODT after conversion
content:
Hello,

If you convert the DITA 1.3 specification source at http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3/os/part3-all-inclusive/dita-v1.3-os-part3-all-inclusive-dita.zip to ODT you get an invalid document, which can't be opened with LibreOffice. In fact the content.xml entity in it is not well formed XML.

These are the steps to reproduce it:

1) Unzip the downloaded file
2) Go to dita-v1/dita-1.3-specification-learningTraining
3) Run "dita -i dita-1.3-specification-learningTraining.ditamap -f odt -o <directory>"
4) Open the result in LibreOffice 5.

Best regards,

Werner.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2391: @keyref attribute no longer processed to @href on <mathmlref>
content:
So my small DITA topic uses the new DITA 1.3 mathmlref element:
and in the temporary files folder the topic should contain an extra @href on the "mathmlref", @href added by the "KeyrefPaser".
This does not happen because the method:

org.dita.dost.reader.GenListModuleReader.startElement(String, String, String, Attributes)

has an if clause which skips the "mathmlref" from processing because it considers it to be inside a foreign element (because the parent "mathml" element is an extension of foreign):
So the "GenListModuleReader" reports my topic has no keyref and it will no longer be processed to add an @href to it.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2396: The collection-type on DITA Map should affects all topics from the map
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2396: The collection-type on DITA Map should affects all topics from the map
content:
Reading the DITA 1.3 documentation, it is not very clear if the collection-type attribute on a DITA map should cascade to all topicrefs from the DITA map or other referenced DITA map. https://www.oxygenxml.com/dita/1.3/specs/archSpec/base/ditamap-attributes.html
So, for the next DITA map:
<map collection-type="sequence">
 <title>Sample DITA map</title>

 <topicref href="topic-A.dita">
 <topicref href="topic-A1.dita"/>
 <topicref href="topic-A2.dita"/>
 </topicref>

 <topicref href="topicB.dita"/>
</map>
I expected to find in the XHTML ouput the next links between topics: topic-A --next--> topic-A1 --next--> topic-A2 --next--> topic-B topic-B --prev--> topic-A2 --prev--> topic-A1 --prev--> topic-A
For the moment, only the topics from the first level of the DITA map are affected by this property:
topic-A --next--> topic-A1 topic-B --prev--> topic-A2
Should the collection-type value cascade to all topicrefs when it is set on a DITA map?

title: DITA-OT Issue #2403: Remove the text-align="justify" property for the PDF TOC entries
content:
If the TOC entries are long enough to be rendered on multiple lines, the first lines are displayed justified. We have users that dislike this presentation mode and ask how to disable it.

Searching in the GitHub history, I see that this property was set to fix an issue regarding an uneven right edge on PDF TOC, see #735. 

I've tested with Apache FOP 2.1 and DITA-OT 2.5 and the numbers from the right side seems to be aligned correctly. 

So, could we discard the changes from the issue #735?

title: DITA-OT Issue #2427: DTD-defined entities disappear from document
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2427: DTD-defined entities disappear from document
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2427: DTD-defined entities disappear from document
content:
I recognize that many feel entities are evil, wrong, and should not exist, but please leave that aside for the moment.

The DITA DTD from OASIS defines one entity in `topic.mod`:
We've got this in a lot of documents, because for a long time, our editor-of-choice was set to save characters as entities when possible. Because it's in `topic.mod`, it's a legal entity in any DITA topic or topic specialization (because all topic shells should include that module). When that entity exists, it is dropped during parsing - the entity is removed, and no character is inserted in its place. 

It appears that any entity defined in a DTD has this problem; entities defined in the document as part of the `!DOCTYPE` do not. To test, I've added an entity into a topic, and I've added one new entity in the DTD. 

For ease of testing, I added this into `topic.mod` next to the current definition of `nbsp`, but keep in mind that (however silly) this would be valid as part of any doctype shell or specialization module:
My topic uses this entity, and one defined within the file:

title: DITA-OT Issue #2427: DTD-defined entities disappear from document
content:
]> Garage Concepts

Test an entity that's defined in this topic: [&phrasey;]

Now an entity from the DTD: [&testy;]

 When built to HTML or PDF, the output looks like this - both `nbsp` and `testy` from the DTD are dropped, but `phrasey` from the topic is preserved: Test an entity that's defined in this topic: [This is a bit of text]

title: DITA-OT Issue #2430: Use of keyword keyref in a DITA Map
content:
Let's say my DITA Map has inside it something like:
<keydef keys="original">
 <topicmeta><keywords><keyword>Original Content</keyword></keywords></topicmeta>
 </keydef>
 <keydef keys="product_name">
 <topicmeta>
 <keywords><keyword keyref="original"/></keywords>
 </topicmeta>
 </keydef>
and in a DITA topic I have:
Should the "product_name" key be resolved to the "Original Content" text in the published output for the HTML topic? Right now it is not, with either DITA OT 1.8 or 2.x.
A workaround would have been to use a conref instead of a keyref in the DITA Map:
<keydef keys="original">
 <topicmeta><keywords><keyword id="originalID">Original Content</keyword></keywords></topicmeta>
 </keydef>
 <keydef keys="product_name">
 <topicmeta>
 <keywords><keyword conref="#originalID"/></keywords>
 </topicmeta>
 </keydef>

title: DITA-OT Issue #2431: topicpullImpl.xsl: topicpull:get-stuff_topicpos fails to detect same file when there is a resource part of the href URI
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2431: topicpullImpl.xsl: topicpull:get-stuff_topicpos fails to detect same file when there is a resource part of the href URI
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2431: topicpullImpl.xsl: topicpull:get-stuff_topicpos fails to detect same file when there is a resource part of the href URI
content:
<xsl:template match="*" mode="topicpull:get-stuff_topicpos">
 <xsl:choose>
 <xsl:when test="starts-with(@href,'#')">samefile</xsl:when>
 <xsl:when test="contains(@href,'#')">otherfile</xsl:when>
 <xsl:otherwise>firstinfile</xsl:otherwise>
 </xsl:choose>
 </xsl:template>
Assumes that all same-file hrefs will have only a fragment identifier but that is not the case.

As least in the case of select-branch chunks, the target URIs are like:
Where Chunk1344404415.dita is the chunk file that contains the reference and target.

In this case, topicpos is incorrectly set to "otherfile" and then the link text resolution fails because the code that handles the otherfile resolution gets the wrong working directory and builds an unresolvable target URI when the chunk and the pre-chunking target topic are not in the same directory.

In this case the working directory is determined from the closest preceding workdir-uri PI, which will reflect the original location of the original topic, not the location of the chunk.

Thus there are two bugs here:
1. The failure to determine that the target is in the same file
2. A bug in the chunk processing that does not either omit or rewrite the workdir URIs so that they correctly reflect the location of the chunk.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2436: PDF2 attribute tweaks for context table/@orient=land
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2436: PDF2 attribute tweaks for context table/@orient=land
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2436: PDF2 attribute tweaks for context table/@orient=land
content:
There are three sub-issues here:
1. `section/title` followed by `table/title` produces two titles with no extra vertical space between them.
2. Table rotation that is preceded by other body content on the same page causes bizarre column width behavior that can violate the page bottom boundary. Rotated tables should always be preceded by a page break.
3. `start-indent` inheritance causes unwanted `table` indentation. The table's `fo:container` applies inherited `start-indent` and then the `fo:block` wrapping the `table` `title` and the `tgroup` applies the inherited `start-indent` an unwanted second time.

Here are the overrides I created in one of my customizations to deal with these issues:
<xsl:attribute-set name="table__container">
 <!-- Tagsmiths: Ensure that the table has spacing below section titles -->
 <xsl:attribute name="space-before">0.6em</xsl:attribute>
 <!-- Tagsmiths: Force rotated tables to start on a new page -->
 <xsl:attribute name="page-break-before" select="if (@orient eq 'land') then 'always' else 'auto'"/>
 </xsl:attribute-set>

 <xsl:attribute-set name="table">
 <!-- Tagsmiths: Break start-indent inheritance to prevent it from being applied
 a second time. The first application of start-indent occurs on this block's
 parent fo:block-container. -->
 <xsl:attribute name="start-indent">0pt</xsl:attribute>
 </xsl:attribute-set>

title: DITA-OT Issue #2446: Menu cascade accessibility
content:
Common practice is to use a right angle bracket as part of a menu cascade: `File > New`. In this case, the angle bracket is considered ASCII art, and per Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.0, should be avoided.
As a workaround for HTML, it is acceptable to wrap an abbreviate tag around the the angle bracket so screen readers will detect and read the content of the abbreviation tag:

title: DITA-OT Issue #2447: Relationship table accessibility
content: When relationship tables are published to HTML, the links are formatted as a set of `div` elements. While this was acceptable under Web Content Accessibility Guidelines(WCAG) 1.0, WCAG 2.0 calls for lists of links to be formatted using list markup. HTML processing should be updated to conform to the recommendations of WCAG 2.0.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2450: Transformation errors when computing topic's short description which has keyrefs to a merged/chunked topic
content:
The problem seems to be related to the fact that there is a related link(see snowdrop.dita) to a topic (iris.dita). The 'iris.dita' topic has a short description with keyrefs to a topic that was merged/chunked.

I've tested with DITA-OT 2.3.1.

[flowers.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/424493/flowers.zip)

title: DITA-OT Issue #2452: [DOTX031E][ERROR] The file 'topic.dita' is not available to resolve link information in XHTML transformation when using chunk='to-content' feature
content:
The XHTML transformation fails when a DITA map uses the `chunk='to-content'` feature and there are related-links to the merged topics. The error that I get is:
[topicpull] Recoverable error on line 576 of topicpullImpl.xsl:
[topicpull] FODC0002: java.io.FileNotFoundException:
[topicpull] C:\Users\radu_pisoi\Desktop\temp\dita-issue\issue2\flowers\temp\xhtml\topics\flowers\concepts\springFlowers.dita (The system cannot find the path specified)
[topicpull] file:/C:/Users/radu_pisoi/Desktop/temp/dita-issue/issue2/flowers/topics/flowers/snowdrop.dita:9:33: [DOTX031E][ERROR]: The file file:/C:/Users/radu_pisoi/Desktop/temp/dita-issue/issue2/flowers/temp/xhtml/topics/flowers/concepts/springFlowers.dita is not available to resolve link information.
I noticed that if I remove the related-link to the topic merged in the parent topic, then the issue disappears.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2455: Use fo:block instead of fo:wrapper for ID containers
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2455: Use fo:block instead of fo:wrapper for ID containers
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2455: Use fo:block instead of fo:wrapper for ID containers
content:
I wrote this already as comment to the pull request #2229. But I noticed that one was already closed/merged. So here a new issue:

Using FOP I have additional space before a title and I could identify the empty fo:wrapper elements to cause this.

My sample fo code looks like this (the spaces for indention were added by hand to make it easier to read and are not present in the actual code):
<fo:block border="solid blue">
 <fo:marker marker-class-name="current-h2">Title</fo:marker>
 <fo:wrapper id="unique_3"/>
 <fo:wrapper id="_OPENTOPIC_TOC_PROCESSING_d89e342"/>
 <fo:block border="solid red">Title</fo:block>
</fo:block>

title: DITA-OT Issue #2455: Use fo:block instead of fo:wrapper for ID containers
content:
producing this output:
![dita-ot-title-wrapper](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/12510240/17726447/4d4d938c-6453-11e6-9216-6d10ad1750d2.PNG)
So the fo:wrapper elements generate a blank line.

When I change the fo:wrapper to fo:inline the result doesn't change.

When I change the fo:wrapper to fo:block the additional space disappears:
![dita-ot-title-block](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/12510240/17726492/abbb6732-6453-11e6-8058-6b3e9c82c2cd.PNG)

So I think at least for FOP fo:block should be used. I can't test it with XEP or AH, though.

Maybe there could be a named template "idContainer" with different overriding for different engines?

However, when using fo:block the @keep-with-next behavior of two consecutive titles will no more work since the first title will only be kept together with the (empty) id container block. So an additional keep-together.within-column="always" for the while title element is required - which should have no negative side effects...

title: DITA-OT Issue #2463: Feature request: Test if PDF file is open before publishing it
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2463: Feature request: Test if PDF file is open before publishing it
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2463: Feature request: Test if PDF file is open before publishing it
content: The Adobe Reader locks a file, that means you cannot overwrite it, when it is opened in the Adobe Reader. Sometimes, when publishing locally, authors forget to close the PDF file before publishing it. Then, the FOP publishing runs (what can be time consuming) and then tries to overwrite the file. If it is open, it fails, and authors need to close the PDF and rerun the process. It would be nice, if the process would try to delete the output file before publishing. If it cannot be deleted, because the file is open, the author would save duplicate publishing time.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2475: Wrong error message in: Error: Failed to run pipeline: [DOTA069F][FATAL] Input file
content:
In the event that the referenced DTD file is incorrect the error message reports the source file as non existent. 

In:

![1](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/7548378/18418662/7848b73a-7842-11e6-9a04-77dc49e4edf2.png)

I was able to convert a file successfully. 

In:

![2](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/7548378/18418663/784c645c-7842-11e6-9042-32183333c278.png)

I changed the DTD file name from /home to /HOME to make it invalid, but the message that comes back is:

Error: Failed to run pipeline: [DOTA069F][FATAL] **Input file 'file:/home/phil/dita/dita-ot/src/main/docsrc/samples/test.xml'** cannot be located or read.

despite:

title: DITA-OT Issue #2475: Wrong error message in: Error: Failed to run pipeline: [DOTA069F][FATAL] Input file
content:
This is highly misleading and confusing!

The erroneous message arises because in the Java source, a single try statement wraps far too many statements and then attempts to decode errors via an enormous set of catch blocks. A better solution would be to use a number of try statements each more local to the statements to be executed to obtain a more granular result.

This error is extremely damaging to the credibility of the DITA OT because new users attempting to use it for the first time become highly frustrated with the time they must waste tracking down this error. Indeed, it will beyond the capability of most new users to resolve this error expeditiously because the error message is so misleading.

A better error message such as: "DTD file ... not found" would allow even a novice to resolve this error quickly and in doing so gain confidence in their ability to use this toolkit successfully.

I therefore implore you to fix this error promptly in order to preserve the honor and respect that the Open Source Software process so rightly deserves.

This was discovered on OT 2.3.1 and exists still in 2.3.2.

If a bookmap contains a <data> element that contains an <image> element with a relative path in the @href attribute, all keyref file resolutions prepend the file resolutions with the relative path. That is, if the image @href contains something like ../../, that is prepended to all resolved file references for conkeyrefs.

content: Issue #2485 is closed with labels enhancement, plugin/pdf, preprocess, priority/medium, stale. Retrieval signals: map, pdf.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2485: New common merge process
content:
We currently have a single merge process code in OT, the one originally developed for PDF. However, it’s not really optimal for general use and IMO is not particularly good. We should develop a new merging code based on this code and merge PDF to use it.
The current output from merge is
<map>
 <opentopic:map>
 <!-- map contents -->
 </opentopic:map>
 <!-- topics -->
</map>
I suggest the new output is like compound topic, but can also contain a map. Also, the map should be output the the end of the document, because it's more efficient from processing point of view.
<dita>
 <!-- topics -->
 <map>
 <!-- map contents -->
 <map>
</dita>

So stylesheet should set @width="100%" to expand table to page size. The "%" value refers its closest ancestor area's width. So in most cases it woks well.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2493: related-links should not generate links to unreferenced topics
content:
I could not find an issue for this and I'm unsure, whether this a desired behavior. So I do not know, whether this is a bug report or an enhancement request.
**tl;dr:** We use keymaps to define keys once and then refer to those maps to propagate the keys to use them in publication maps. Unfortunately, the related-links mechanism, as it is implemented, does not care for, if a topic is referenced in a map, it looks for, whether the key is defined and then processes it. This creates link stubs, see screenshot.
This is the publication map **map.ditamap**. It has a link to the key map and refers to **chapter1** and **chapter2** but not to **chapter3**.
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE map PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Map//EN" "map.dtd">
<map>
 <title>DITA Topic Map</title>
 <topicref>
 <mapref href="keymap.ditamap" toc="no" format="ditamap"/>
 </topicref>
 <topicref keyref="chapter1"/>
 <topicref keyref="chapter2"/>
</map>
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE map PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Map//EN" "map.dtd">
<map>
 <title>Keymap</title>
 <topicgroup>
 <keydef keys="chapter1" href="chapter1.dita" processing-role="resource-only"/>
 <keydef keys="chapter2" href="chapter2.dita" processing-role="resource-only"/>
 <keydef keys="chapter3" href="chapter3.dita" processing-role="resource-only"/>
 </topicgroup>
</map>

title: DITA-OT Issue #2493: related-links should not generate links to unreferenced topics
content:
The **chapter1** topic has related links to **chapter2** and **chapter3**, but, because **chapter3** is not referenced in the map, the related link should not be generated.
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE topic PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Topic//EN" "topic.dtd">
<topic id="topic_kky_2y5_kx">
 <title>chapter1</title>
 <shortdesc>chapter1 is defined on keymap and referenced in map.</shortdesc>
 <related-links>
 <link keyref="chapter2"/>
 <link keyref="chapter3"/>
 </related-links>
</topic>

title: DITA-OT Issue #2500: Table layout="auto" when no colwidths specified
content:
Let's say my DITA topic has inside it a table which has no column widths specified: ZUZU aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa a bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb b ccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc c ddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd d
and I publish it to XHTML. The layout of the HTML table is automatically computed based on the cell preferred sizes, so the first column will take a larger amount of space. If I publish to PDF I get a warning: and the resulting table has both columns equal in width. In my opinion when there is no column width specified on the colspecs, the table layout should be auto. FOP does not take the "auto" into account but at least the warning is gone + it works with XEP and probably also Antenna House.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2504: Adjust table row span after filtering
content: DITA source has tables with row spans and profiling attributes on rows. When publishing, the filter strips out some rows and the original `@morerows` is no longer valid. Right now this will fail in error because XSLT cannot deal with invalid tables like these. One solution to fix this would be to write the custom table coordinate attributes during initial parse _and_ replace the `@morerows` with `@dita:rowspan-end`. This is similar to what CALS does with column span, specifying span end column name instead of span length. After filtering this could be converted back to `@morerows` by calculating the length with the current coordinates. This would also work when conref push is used to push new rows into a rows span. title: DITA-OT Issue #2505: Generated IDs and hrefs do not match when chunk = "to-content" with DITA-OT 2.3.3
content:
With DITA-OT 2.3.3, when using chunk = "to-content", the generated IDs and hrefs do not match. Attaching chunktest.zip which clearly demonstrates the problem. The output was generated with the DITA-OT html5 plugin.

The zip file contains two directories: nochunk and chunk

The nochunk directory contains a simple .ditamap with three topics. Examining the DITA sources and the output we see:

chunktest.ditamap references the three topics intro.dita, overview.dita, and creating.dita. The output index.html file references intro.html, overview.html, and creating.html.

intro.dita contains an id="intro" on the topic <concept> element and an id="animals" on the <table> element. intro.html contains an id="intro" on the <body> element and an id="intro__animals" on the <table> element; the html5 plugin concatenates the topic's ID, a '__' instead of a '/', and the element's ID.

The chunk directory contains the same .ditamap except now chunk="to-content" is on the intro.dita topicref, which means that intro.dita, overview.dita, and creating.dita will be chunked into a single output file.

Examining chunk/out/index.html now shows hrefs to intro.html#intro, overview.html#overview, and creating.html#sqlj which attempt to point to the IDs for the individual topics which are now part of the single ditabase output file. The fragment identifiers are the original, unmodified IDs.

Examining chunk/out/intro.html now shows IDs "intro" (at the start of the original intro topic), intro__overview, and intro__sqlj. The IDs seem to be formed by concatenating the topmost topic ID, a '__' and the original subtopic ID.

The IDs and hrefs don't match.
[chunktest.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/529892/chunktest.zip)

title: DITA-OT Issue #2518: Chinese punctuation looks lower than Chinese characters in published PDF
content:
We use DITA-OT with FOP to publish DITA files into PDF file and find the following problem. (But when we test it using AH to do the publish, it is correct.)

The content in DITA files are most in Chinese. The requirement is Chinese characters should use SimSun or SimHei while number and Alphabat characters should use Times New Roman. We find some Chinese punctuations like ‘%，。’ will be shown lower than other Chinese characters, which looks not good.

But if we changed font-mappings file like following, the Chinese punctuations shown as the same baseline as Chinese Character.
<logical-font name="Normal">
 <physical-font char-set="default">
 <font-face> SimSun, Times New Roman, Times</font-face>
 </physical-font>
 <physical-font char-set="Simplified Chinese">
 <font-face>SimSun</font-face>
 </physical-font>
 <physical-font char-set="Symbols">
 <font-face>ZapfDingbats</font-face>
 </physical-font>
 <physical-font char-set="SubmenuSymbol">
 <font-face>ZapfDingbats</font-face>
 </physical-font>
</logical-font>

title: DITA-OT Issue #2518: Chinese punctuation looks lower than Chinese characters in published PDF
content:
The only thing we do is changed `<font-face> Times New Roman, Times, SimSun</font-face>`
to `<font-face> SimSun, Times New Roman, Times</font-face>`

But it make another problem: all characters in files are in SimSun or SimHei, including number and alphabat which we want them in Times New Roman. Furthermore, some entity like ` ` defined in `zh-CN.xml` file will be shown in "#", which looks like it doesn't find the correct character set.

content: Issue #2520 is closed with labels bug, preprocess, priority/high. Retrieval signals: map, html, dita-ot, plugin.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2520: force-unique=true does not work
content:
1. Create two files:
 - _topic.dita_: an arbitrary valid topic
 - _map.ditamap_ containing: `<map><topicref href="topic.dita"/><topicref href="topic.dita"/></map>`
2. Run _dita-ot_: `dita -f html5 -i map.ditamap -Dforce-unique=true`
- **Actual**: in _out/_ **no _topic_2.html_** (only _topic.html_) has been created - **Expected**: in _out/_ the files **_topic.html_ and _topic_2.html_** should be created
It seems commit [983be7e](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/commit/983be7e95566ffc81b4c477bc0a57630d3729dee) caused this issue. Following fix/workaround works for me:
1. In [_build_preprocess_template.xml_](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/develop/src/main/plugins/org.dita.base/build_preprocess_template.xml) replace
 - `<module class="org.dita.dost.module.CopyToModule"/>` with
 - `<module class="org.dita.dost.module.CopyToModule"><param name="force-unique" value="${force-unique}" if="force-unique"/></module>`
2. Via an Ant target that is execute after all preprocess steps append all _//topicref/@copy-to_ files of _${user.input.file.listfile}_ to _${fullditamapandtopicfile}_ and _${fullditatopicfile}_
3. Integrate changes above: `dita -install`
4. Ignore warnings like `[copy-to] [DOTX064W][WARN] The copy-to attribute [copy-to="topic_2.dita"] uses the name of a file that already exists, so this attribute is ignored.`

content:
<stepsection id="stepsection_01" class="- topic/li task/stepsection ">
To configure the settings of the color measurement instrument, go to step 
<xref keyref="REFERENCE-TOPIC/step-color" format="dita" type="step" class="- topic/xref " 
href="../topics/tWhenConnectingMultiplePrinters.dita#task_ops_1q4_wx/step-color">
<?ditaot usertext?>Connecting a single printer</xref>.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2528: List of DITA Open Toolkit issues which in my opinion would need to be addressed
content:
At some point I told @jelovirt I had a list of DITA Open Toolkit issues which I considered that need to be addressed so I'm opening this issue as a way to split enumerate those issues in categories and enumerate them. 

- DITA 1.3 support:
 - Support for MathML:
 https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/1774
 https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2391
 - Support for SVG:
 https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/1123
 - Support for Troubleshooting: 
 https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/1771
 
 - Key scope related bugs:
 https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2410
 https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2393
 https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2525
 ~https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2523~
 
 - Branch filtering related bugs:
 ~https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/1998~
 https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2147
 https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/1999
 
Now various other issues:

- Recent problem related to the changing of the processing stages, conref can no longer be used in keyword metadata:
https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2420

- Issues related to the map reference expansion which possible could be fixed by the mapref processing @jelovirt in working on:
~https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2494~
~https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2476~ (obsolete)

- ~Navigation title without locktitle in topicref overrides topic title: 
https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2187~ (resolved)

- PDF TOC issue which can probably be fixed now after the upgrade to Apache FOP 2.1:
~https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2403~

- ~Flagging no longer works with specialized @props attributes:~
~https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2392~ (obsolete)

- Distinct HTML files are created for multiple references to the same topic, even if they are in the same key scope (or there is no key scope defined):
https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2363

- ~NullPointerException in Eclipse Help output:~ https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/1885 (closed)

- Issues related to chunking. Such issues usually result in broken links between topics, broken references to the CSS files...: 
https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2298
~https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2452~ (resolved)
https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2385
https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2450
https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2040
https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2188
https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2064

- Problem with abbreviated-form handling:
https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2067

- Problem with related links and profiling attributes:
 https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2200 

- Ambiguous error messages:
~https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2079~

- PDF Bookmark part with no title generates empty entry in TOC:
https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/1930

As a conclusion, I think chunking has the most problems right now in the DITA OT. The DITA 1.3 support is also half baked, support for some major features is missing and there are problems with the implemented features.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2533: Error for xsd-based topic without title
content:
When trying to process an xsd-based topic without title element (it will be added by a custom preprocess step) I get an error (OT v2.4):

> [...]\DITA-OT\plugins\org.dita.base\build_preprocess.xml:47: Failed to run pipeline: [DOTJ022F][FATAL] Failed to parse the input file '[...]\no-title.dita' because all of its content has been filtered out. This will happen if the input file has filter conditions on the root element, and a ditaval excludes all content based on those conditions.

A similar sample using RNG works fine - so there seems to be no general requirement for topics to have a title element.

To ensure this is no issue of xs:redefine I created a primitive sample without any redefine that should still fulfill the basic (technical) requirements of a DITA schema:
[no-title.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/618481/no-title.zip)

title: DITA-OT Issue #2536: Full-width colon and semicolon are not recognized as Asian characters
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2536: Full-width colon and semicolon are not recognized as Asian characters
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2536: Full-width colon and semicolon are not recognized as Asian characters
content:
Unicode characters `0xff1a` (full-width colon) and `0xff1b` (full-width semicolon) and other full-width characters are not recognized as Chinese characters. As a result, they are not included in the `fo:inline` element that contains surrounding Asian (Chinese) text, and are outputted to the PDF with incorrect line height. These characters are often used in Chinese content.

Root cause: `cfg/fo/i18n/zh_CN.xml` specifies Chinese characters only up to `0xff00`.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2538: Link to keyscoped topic not properly resolved.
content:
So, the DITA Map looks like this:
<topicgroup keyscope="product1_scope">
 ...........
 <topicref keys="archiving" href="product1/c_archiving_mod.dita"/>
</topicgroup>
<topicgroup keyscope="product2_scope">
 ...............
 <topicref keys="archiving" href="product1/c_archiving_mod.dita"/>
</topicgroup>
<topicref href="linking.dita"/>
Because "c_archiving_mod.dita" is referenced in two key scopes, we will have in the output file two HTMLs for it: "c_archiving_mod.html" and "c_archiving_mod-1.html". And that's good. The "linking.dita" should generate links to both those HTML files using fully qualified key scoped:
But in the generated "linking.html" you will have both links point to the same HTML file (the one generated from the first context).

I looked a little bit in the code, the method `org.dita.dost.writer.KeyrefPaser.processElement(Attributes)` resolves key references based on the current "KeyScope" map. Unfortunately the map contains these mappings:
although in my opinion the "product2_scope.archiving" should have been re-written (possibly in the org.dita.dost.module.KeyrefModule.execute) to point to "product1/c_archiving_mod-1.dita" because the DITA Map has already been re-written to do so.

Might also be related with #2523

title: DITA-OT Issue #2541: Support duplicate key scopes
content:

content: Issue #2541 is closed with labels bug, preprocess/keyref, priority/medium. Retrieval signals: map, html.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2541: Support duplicate key scopes
content:
Per [DITA 1.3 spec][1] key scope tree can contain duplicate key scope names and they should not be merged:

> Within a root map, two distinct key scopes with the same name have no relationship with each other aside from that implied by their relative locations in the key scope hierarchy.

Current `KeyScope` stores the child scopes as a map, using name of the scope as the key. This doesn't allow duplicates the exist as sibling scopes in the tree. The implementation should be changed to store the child scopes as a list instead.

[1]: http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3/os/part1-base/langRef/attributes/the-key-scope-attribute.html

title: DITA-OT Issue #2550: generate.copy.outer=1 not working properly, copies images outside of output dir
content:
This sample demonstrates a few issues with `generate.copy.outer=1` but the most significant is that I've found a way to generate files outside of the designated output directory. I ran into this with a user document in 2.3.1, but have reproduced in 2.4 now.

My map structure looks odd and is presented here as a simple test case - but variants of this exist in our real documentation. I have a map nested down in `sub1/sub2/`. It references a topic and an HTML file in the same directory; the topic references an image in the same directory. Trouble comes with the uplevels reference to `wayup.dita`:
I've run two builds to `html5`; the builds match except for `generate.copy.outer`, which I've tried as both "1" and "3".
"3" seems to work. `index.html` is generated in the output equivalent of the main directory. Image and HTML file are properly copied to the same directory, and the image appears in `maindir.html`. Links between topics work.
"1" demonstrates several problems. Most significant: the image is copied outside of the output directory. The `uplevels` variable here (on Windows) is set to `..\..\` because there is a topic 2 levels up from the map. The image's output directory is constructed as:
<condition property="copy-image.todir" value="${output.dir}/${uplevels}" else="${output.dir}">
 <equals arg1="${generate.copy.outer}" arg2="1"/> 
 </condition>

title: DITA-OT Issue #2550: generate.copy.outer=1 not working properly, copies images outside of output dir
content:
I think what's actually wanted, but I'm not sure how to get it, would be output dir + path to image + uplevels + file name.
Other issues: - `index.html` and CSS are placed directly in the output directory as expected. Index file links to other files as if they are there - Generated topic from the main dir is placed within `sub1/sub2/` in the output directory - HTML is copied to `sub1/sub2/` inside the output directory - related to #1964, but I think the fix I suggested there would end up causing the issue seen with images (copy outside)

title: DITA-OT Issue #2561: Support for mathmlref element
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2561: Support for mathmlref element
content: Issue #2561 is open with labels DITA 1.3, feature, priority/high. Retrieval signals: exception, html, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2561: Support for mathmlref element
content:
Right now I'm working on support for `<mathmlref>`. This is a subset of #1774, but I don't expect to implement all of it in DITA-OT at this point so I've opened an issue specific to that element. (Once complete, whatever is done to make it work should be easily redone to make `<svgref>` work, a small subset of #1123)

The DITA specification says:
> Processors _SHOULD_ process the MathML as though the `<m:math>` element had occurred directly in the content of the containing `<mathml>` element.

http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3/os/part2-tech-content/langRef/technicalContent/mathmlref.html

I've got this part of the way done but have encountered a few issues:
1. `<mathmlref>` appears inside of a specialization of `<foreign>`, so the preprocess ignores it - the reference never registers. At this point I've set `MATHML_D_MATHMLREF` to the class value, as with other known class values, and added exceptions in `DebugFilter.java` so that it's processed. This feels like a hack. I wouldn't think this is appropriate for my own specializations. But this is an OASIS one, with an OASIS defined processing behavior, so it seems like we really should extend things to support it. For example: `if (foreignLevel <= 1 || MATHML_D_MATHMLREF.matches(atts.getValue(ATTRIBUTE_NAME_CLASS))){`
1. This feels very much like the `<coderef>` element. So I've used that debug filter to get the math targets added into `.job.xml`, because I expected a later step to pull in the math, much like with code references. But, I'm not sure this is the correct approach.
1. Again like coderef, I tried to add a SAX filter, in the same `topic-fragment` step -- but it doesn't use the XML catalog, so couldn't parse the Math files (they have a DTD reference). I later heard from @jelovirt that the step which processes image metadata might be a good (catalog-aware) spot to add the filter, but I haven't tried this yet.
1. I'm more comfortable in XSL anyway so I tried to do that instead - but the `.job.xml` file isn't set up to retrieve only topics that use math, and throwing every DITA topic into a new XSL step is wasteful. Plus, so far, the files are processed in the source directory like code targets, and don't exist in the temp directory.

At this point I decided to seek advice. What would the ideal approach be here?

title: DITA-OT Issue #2567: HTML5 plugin defines args.html5.classattr but still references args.xhtml.classattr
content:
DITA-OT 2.4.2's org.dita.html5 plugin.xml defines the following parameter:

 <param name="args.html5.classattr" desc="Specifies whether to include the DITA class ancestry inside the HTML5 elements." type="enum">
 <val default="true">yes</val>
 <val>no</val>
 </param>

In DITA-OT 2.3.3 and earlier, this parameter was args.xhtml.classattr and was shared by all HTML-based transforms.

However, DITA-OT 2.4.2's org.dita.html5 build_dita2html5_template.xml passes the following Ant parameter to the HTML5 XSLTs:

 <param name="PRESERVE-DITA-CLASS" expression="${args.xhtml.classattr}" if="args.xhtml.classattr"/>

title: DITA-OT Issue #2572: PDF processing of links from the same topic to the same topic has changed between 2.3.3 and 2.4.2
content:
This is really difficult to explain...

The link processing has changed somewhere between `DITA-OT 2.3.3` and `DITA-OT 2.4.2`. With the `DITA-OT 2.3.3`, multiple links to the same target in the same topic are always processed. It does not matter, whether it is a `@href` or `@keyref`.

With `DITA-OT 2.4.2` only the first link from the same topic to the same topic is generated correctly. Maybe this is not a bug, but a feature. It may make sense, because you probably do not need multiple references to the same topic in the same topic. 

| **Output with DITA-OT 2.3.3** | **Output with DITA-OT 2.4.2** |
|--------------|-------------|
| ![xref1](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/3266567/22019158/9bd0aa26-dcb2-11e6-8839-e87be88e88e4.png) | ![xref2](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/3266567/22019214/db2923ce-dcb2-11e6-9011-de019135d73e.png) |
| [bookmap-2.3.3.pdf](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/710909/bookmap-2.3.3.pdf) | [bookmap-2.4.2.pdf](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/710910/bookmap-2.4.2.pdf) |

**But**: Unfortunately this also affects conkeyrefed modules, e.g. conkeyrefed `<xref>` elements or conkeyrefed modules that contain a `<xref>` element. So, if you, for example, conkeyref a `<note>` element with a `<xref>` element in two separate topics, the `<xref>` is only processed in the first topic. It does not matter, whether there are 0...n chapters in between.

[test-files.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/710907/test-files.zip)

title: DITA-OT Issue #2579: args.logdir has no effect
content:
To generate a log file with the toolkit, the log file name must be specified on the DITA command line. Its path, if not specified, if always relative to the input directory. Setting args.logdir has no effect.

If we are not going to implement this parameter, we should deprecate it and indicate that it does nothing.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2583: Plugin installation looks for Ant code in base directory
content:
Reported in the google group, and I've reproduced on both 2.4.1 and 2.4.3: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/dita-ot-users/4lnue2bt8Is
C:\DITA-OT\dita-ot-2.4.3>bin\dita --install
[integrate] [Fatal Error] :-1:-1: Premature end of file.
[integrate] Premature end of file.
I tried changing `plugin.xml` to use a name other than `build.xml`:
`<feature extension="dita.conductor.target.relative" value="testbuild.xml"/>`

With that, it's clear that the integrator is looking for my build file in the DITA-OT base directory:
C:\DITA-OT\dita-ot-2.4.3>bin\dita --install
[integrate] C:\DITA-OT\dita-ot-2.4.3\testbuild.xml (The system cannot find the file specified.)
In my 2.4.1 install, I tried changing the actual file name (and `plugin.xml` entry) to `mybuild.xml`, with that failure. I then tried `happybuild.xml`, and ... it worked. Changing back to `build.xml` works. I have no idea and think I may have entered some non-deterministic test universe. But I can reliably reproduce this issue in 2.4.3.

I also built my own (similar) transform types before ever seeing this report, in 2.4.1, and did not encounter this issue. So again, I'm confused.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2612: DITA OT integrator should not look directly for resources in the basedir
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2612: DITA OT integrator should not look directly for resources in the basedir
content:
Let's say I have a separate build file located in some other folder which runs the DITA OT integrator:

 <project basedir="." name="bla" default="dist">
 <import file="d:/path/to/DITA-OT2.x/integrator.xml"></import>
 <target name="dist">
 <antcall target="strict"/>
 </target>
 </project>

it will fail with a message like:

 d:\projects\eXml\frameworks\dita\DITA-OT2.x\integrator.xml:46: C:\path/to/custom/buildDir/resources does not exist.

If we look inside the "integrator.xml" it should use in all places the "dita.dir" parameter but instead, in certain places like here:

 <fileset dir="${basedir}/resources">

 it uses the basedir parameter which usually points to the place where the ANT Java process has started.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2617: Page number in link text settings
content:
Let's say that I create a link to a topic. If I set the custom link text, the label "on page X" is no longer pre-pended to the link when generating the PDF output.
This decision was taken in #274.

Some people may want the "page X" to be generated even if there is custom link text inside the xref:

https://www.oxygenxml.com/forum/post41740.html#p41740

So maybe we should add some setting to control the "on page" behavior. For example there may be people who do not want it at all in the PDF as they intend the PDF for web consumption.

content:
I've got document type plugins that each ended up requiring a module in the other. 

One plugin already had a `<require>` element in `plugin.xml` to reference the other. When the second ended up using a module from the first, I added in a `<require>` element to that plugin, which resulted in:
C:\DITA-OT\dita-ot-2.4.3>bin\dita --install -v
Searching for integrator.xml ...

integrate:
Error: java.lang.StackOverflowError

C:\DITA-OT\dita-ot-2.4.3>
As an easy test to reproduce this is to add the following line to `org.dita.xhtml/plugin.xml`. The htmlhelp plugin already requires XHTML, so adding the reverse dependency sets up the stack overflow.
`<require plugin="org.dita.htmlhelp"/>`

Quite low priority, but I'd made several changes before running `-install` so it wasn't immediately obvious what was causing it.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2642: Simplify creation of prerequisite links
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2642: Simplify creation of prerequisite links
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2642: Simplify creation of prerequisite links
content:
* A is a previous sibling of B AND * A has `@importance=required` set AND * the parent topic sets `@collection-type=sequence`
There are quite a number of cases where in order to add prerequisite links it's necessary to replicate this structure in a `<relcell>` (or as a resource-only hierarchy) because the navigation hierarchy doesn't — and shouldn't — cast A as a previous sibling of B within a sequence of topics. In addition, it's often desirable to set `@linking=targetonly` on the prerequisite topicref to avoid a Next link from A to B. So you have something like:
<reltable>
 <relheader>
 <relcolspec/>
 <relcolspec/>
 </relheader>
 <relrow>
 <relcell>
 <topicgroup collection-type="sequence">
 <topicref href="A.dita" importance="required" linking="targetonly"/>
 <topicref href="B.dita"/>
 </topicgroup>
 </relcell>
 <relcell/>
 </relrow>
</reltable>

title: DITA-OT Issue #2642: Simplify creation of prerequisite links
content:
This doesn't let authors visualize the topic relationships (as a tabular rendering of a relationship table should), it's tedious, and I don't find anything in the DITA spec that requires this particular implementation.

I'm suggesting that in addition to the current implementation (which is useful in cases where the navigation _does_ happen to match the current rules), we add a simpler way to define prerequisite links in a relationship table. I propose that a prerequisite link to A be created from B if:

- A and B are in the same relationship table row AND
- A has `@importance=required` specified directly or by inheritance from the `<relcell>` or `<relcolspec>` elements

With this implementation, it would be possible to define topic prerequisite links in a simple reltable structure.
<reltable>
 <relheader>
 <relcolspec importance="required" linking="targetonly"/>
 <relcolspec/>
 </relheader>
 <relrow>
 <relcell><topicref href="A.dita"/></relcell>
 <relcell><topicref href="B.dita"/></relcell>
 </relrow>
</reltable>
Forgot to say, this also _vastly_ simplifies things if a topic has multiple prerequisites.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2643: Branch filtering prohibits key scopes to properly work
content:
I'm attaching a sample project, I'm testing with DITA OT 2.4.4.

[keyscopesAndBF.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/885046/keyscopesAndBF.zip)

So I have a DITA Topic which looks like this:

 <!DOCTYPE concept PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Concept//EN" "concept.dtd">
 <concept id="concept_qlr_spc_dt">

 <topichead navtitle="Product1Scope" keyscope="ks1">

The title seems to be properly computed if I remove the <ditavalref> from the second keyscope.

content: Issue #2645 is closed with labels bug, preprocess, stale. Retrieval signals: map, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2645: Map-based shortdesc implemented only for "first-use"
content:
It's possible to specify a shortdesc in the map to be used for link descriptions, but this works only for the first instance of the topic.
<topicref href="t_i_create_course_parent.xml" collection-type="family">
 <topicmeta>
 <shortdesc>MAP BASED SHORTDESC</shortdesc>
 </topicmeta>
The impact of this behavior is that the same shortdesc (and linktext) is used for every reference to the topic, even when it's desired to override based on context — which is the main point of being able to specify map-based overrides to the shortdesc and linktext.

Tested in DITA-OT 2.3.1.

content: Issue #2648 is closed with labels bug, plugin/pdf. Retrieval signals: map, pdf, dita-ot, plugin.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2648: Incorrect topicset/topicref processing in FO template
content:
First level topicrefs within topiset container are excluded from FO/PDF processing.

As far as I understand [this selector](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/develop/src/main/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/xsl/fo/root-processing.xsl#L225) should be more accurate. Something like this
`<xsl:for-each
select="opentopic:map/*[contains(@class, ' map/topicref ') and not(contains(@class, ' mapgroup-d/topicset '))] |
opentopic:map/*[contains(@class, ' mapgroup-d/topicset ')]/*[contains(@class, ' map/topicref ')]">`

Otherwise 
`<map>
<topicset id="xxx">
 <topicref href="..."/>
</topiset>
</map>` 
will lead to incorrect FO tree and broken PDF.

Let's say that in the topic I have a keyref to an image:

and in the DITA Map I have this:

title: DITA-OT Issue #2658: Extra temp folder created in output folder when a key points to an image, PDF transformation, OT 2.4.5
content:
During some PDF transformations with OT 2.4.5 (and several previous versions), temporary folders containing images are created in the output folder as well as the temp folder.

This appears to happen when a key refers to an image.

In my testing, I found that the PDF builds fine without these extra folders if I change plugins\org.dita.base\build_preprocess.xml, Line 472, so that "todir" points to the temp directory ${dita.temp.dir} instead of the output directory ${output.dir}. 

[EDIT: not recommended for production; see comment below]
<target name="copy-html" depends="" unless="preprocess.copy-html.skip" description="Copy html files">
 <copy todir="${dita.temp.dir}" failonerror="false"> <!-- Line 472 -->
 <dita-fileset format="html"/>
 </copy>
</target>

content: Issue #2666 is closed with labels enhancement, plugin/pdf, priority/low, stale. Retrieval signals: map, pdf, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2666: Blank page after TOC in PDF in single page layout (with solution)
content:
When using a single-page layout (`<xsl:variable name="mirror-page-margins" select="false()"/>`), there is always a blank page created after the TOC, at least when the TOC is on a single page. I haven't tested this with a 2 page TOC.

| DITA-OT | 2.4.6 and earlier |
|--|--|
| Formatter | FOP |

To fix this, the following template in **toc.xsl** need to be modified:

title: DITA-OT Issue #2666: Blank page after TOC in PDF in single page layout (with solution)
content:
<xsl:template name="createToc">
 <xsl:if test="$generate-toc">
 <xsl:variable name="toc">
 <xsl:choose>
 <xsl:when test="$map//*[contains(@class,' bookmap/toc ')][@href]"/>
 <xsl:when test="$map//*[contains(@class,' bookmap/toc ')]">
 <xsl:apply-templates select="/" mode="toc"/>
 </xsl:when>
 <xsl:when test="/*[contains(@class,' map/map ')][not(contains(@class,' bookmap/bookmap '))]">
 <xsl:apply-templates select="/" mode="toc"/>
 <xsl:call-template name="toc.index"/>
 </xsl:when>
 </xsl:choose>
 </xsl:variable>
 <xsl:if test="count($toc/*) > 0">
 <fo:page-sequence master-reference="toc-sequence" xsl:use-attribute-sets="page-sequence.toc">
 <xsl:call-template name="insertTocStaticContents"/>
 <fo:flow flow-name="xsl-region-body">
 <xsl:call-template name="createTocHeader"/>
 <fo:block>
 <fo:marker marker-class-name="current-header">
 <xsl:call-template name="getVariable">
 <xsl:with-param name="id" select="'Table of Contents'"/>
 </xsl:call-template>
 </fo:marker>
 <xsl:copy-of select="$toc"/>
 </fo:block>
 </fo:flow>
 </fo:page-sequence>
 </xsl:if>
 </xsl:if>
</xsl:template>

title: DITA-OT Issue #2671: Property to control if PDF is built for Web or for print
content:
Ideally for producing the PDF we should have a parameter deciding if end user wants PDF for print or PDF for web.
Because with PDF for print when you have image maps you want those links to appear under the image, ideally the image would also present the hotspot borders and show some figures on each of them. With PDF for web you do not want the links under the image and you do not want the [on page] page number on each link. When printing to PDF for web people might want by default to have related links appear.
Let's say you have a web link in the DITA topic like:
If you publish PDF for web, you show the *Some link text* and it's clickable. Put if you publish PDF for print, after the link text you should probably have a [http://www.oxygenxml.com] appended so that people know where to browse when reading the printed book.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2675: Something about Ant
content:

content: Issue #2675 is closed with labels none. Retrieval signals: keyref, map, html, dita-ot, plugin, validation.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2675: Something about Ant
content:
1. Perhaps it makes sense to add Ant [if/unless namespaces](https://ant.apache.org/manual/ifunless.html) to the [build project root](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/develop/src/main/plugins/org.dita.base/build_preprocess_template.xml#L9).
Since DITA-OT Ant version is 1.9.7, these namespaces automacally open the possibility to use if and unless attributes on tasks and inner elements.
Also Ant itself can be upgraded (http://ant.apache.org/antnews.html) (release notes https://archive.apache.org/dist/ant/).

1. Despite the fact that there is [preprocess.mapref.skip property](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/develop/src/main/plugins/org.dita.base/build_preprocess_template.xml#L336), we have no chance to skip mapref resolution. Because the keyref task contains its own mapref resolution pipeline (do we really need to resolve them twice?), and that one does not respond to `preprocess.mapref.skip`.
It doesn't affect the result of full preprocessing, but mapref resolution is likely to break ditamap validation in some cases. So for partial preprocessing it may be useful to have a possibilty to switch it off.
With (1) it is quite simple:

title: DITA-OT Issue #2675: Something about Ant
content:
3. The BranchFilterModule gives birth to a new (filtered) topics, which are [added to the .job.xml](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/develop/src/main/java/org/dita/dost/module/BranchFilterModule.java#L223). But the [branch-filter task](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/develop/src/main/plugins/org.dita.base/build_preprocess_template.xml#L219) doesn't rewrite file lists, they are [rewritten later - in the chunk task](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/develop/src/main/plugins/org.dita.base/build_preprocess_template.xml#L409). The chunk task execution depends on `preprocess.chunk.skip` property and can be skipped, then these new topics will never be exploded and processed.
I think it would be useful to add the following lines to the end of the branch-filter task.
(2) и (3) will reduce the number of dependencies between tasks, so they can be easily switched off without breaking the output. It's concered with [this discussion](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/pull/2672#issuecomment-298951918).

content: Issue #2680 is closed with labels bug, plugin/pdf, stale. Retrieval signals: error, map, pdf, dita-ot, plugin.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2680: Image paths for PDF not calculated correctly when map in sub-directory
content:
In the attached file structure there are two map files. Map1 is at the root point of the tree; Map2 is in a sub-directory, "_Subdir_version", under the project root.

I built** a pdf using release 2.4.6, using these, then that for Map1 builds correctly. That for Map2 gives the following errors:

> [fop] SEVERE: Image not found. URI: file:/D:/_Dita_ImagePathBug_Document/en_GB/../images/Placeholder.png. (See position 2:-1) 
[fop] SEVERE: Image not found. URI: file:/D:/_Dita_ImagePathBug_Document/en_GB/../images/Placeholder.png. (See position 3:-1) 

The path should have been `D:/_Dita_ImagePathBug_Document/en_GB/_Subdir_version/../images/Placeholder.png`

The problem appears to lie in the file `plugins\org.dita.pdf2\xsl\fo\commons.xsl`, in the template:
<xsl:template match="*[contains(@class,' topic/image ')]">
<xsl:with-param name="href" select="if (@scope = 'external' or opentopic-func:isAbsolute(@href)) then @href else concat($input.dir.url, @href)"/>

title: DITA-OT Issue #2680: Image paths for PDF not calculated correctly when map in sub-directory
content:
In the `concat` the code implies the first term, `$input.dir.url` is the user-specified input dir (that is, in the example: `D:/_Dita_ImagePathBug_Document/en_GB/_Subdir_version`). But it's not. It actually seems to be the `root/base` dir needed to include all files for the project. In the example it is `D:/_Dita_ImagePathBug_Document/en_GB/`.

So, for the relative links to work correctly, the concat also needs to include the relative path from the root dir to the directory holding the map being built:
`concat($root.dir.url, $reldir.to.input.dir.url, @href)`.

I did a temporary work-around for myself, calculating the relative path part in the ant build file and passing it as a further parameter to the xslt; this has cured the problem. I'm not going to suggest it because I'm sure there's a neater way of doing it just within commons.xsl. The variable "$input.dir.url" should probably be renamed too, to match what it actually represents.

**The build I used for the failed build had the paramaters:

> -f pdf2 -Dargs.chapter.layout=BASIC -Dargs.figurelink.style=NUMBER -Dgenerate.copy.outer=3 -Dargs.draft=yes -Dclean.temp=no -temp D:\build\temp -v -i D:\_Dita_ImagePathBug_Document\en_GB\_Subdir_version\Map2.ditamap -o D:\build\out-pdf\_Dita_ImagePathBug_Document\en_GB\_Subdir_version

[_Dita_ImagePathBug_Document.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/985799/_Dita_ImagePathBug_Document.zip)

title: DITA-OT Issue #2696: Problem with abbreviated-form and language
content:
[abbrev-form-lang-pb.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/1010367/abbrev-form-lang-pb.zip) I attached a sample map. When published it yields this warning: > [DOTX058W]: No glossary entry was found associated with key ' KEY ' on abbreviated-form element. The build will try to determine the best display text and hover text for terms and abbreviations. Looking at the sample content, there is a glossentry: Test topic

TEST

 As the topic which references the glossentry does not have the xml:lang set on it, it's considered to be with "en-US". But the glossentry has xml:lang='en' so in the XSLT stylesheet `org.dita.xhtml\xsl\xslhtml\dita2htmlImpl.xsl`. The XSLT template called "getMatchingTarget" decides that it should not return the glossentry because of the xml:lang impedance mismatch. A couple of problems: 1. The warning is not helpful at all to identify the problem. 2. Ideally if the language of the source cannot be fully matched with the language of the target we could have some kind of fallback and use the glossentry anyway, maybe give a warning about this. But why should the "getMatchingTarget" try to match the languages anyway?

title: DITA-OT Issue #2702: generated links to topics under a chunked to-content topic point to wrong id

title: DITA-OT Issue #2702: generated links to topics under a chunked to-content topic point to wrong id
content:
This issue is related to the HTML5 transform.

When linking to a child of a chunked="to-content" topic the resulting href does not correspond to the `@id ` of the target in the output:

`<xref href="child-topic-2.dita#child-topic-2"/>` where _child-topic-2.dita_ is under a chunked topic, outputs as `<a class="xref" href="head-topic-chunked.html#child-topic-2">`.

Whereas _child-topic-2.dita_ outputs as `<article class="topic nested1" aria-labelledby="ariaid-title3" id="head-topic-chunked__child-topic-2">`.

Note the original `@id` concatenated with the chunked topic `@id`.

The same issue is true with a keyref instead of an href.

See samples for more info. I used DITA-OT 2.4.6 and develop produce the output.
[DITA.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/1024668/DITA.zip)
[HTML5.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/1024665/HTML5.zip)

title: DITA-OT Issue #2704: Avoid renaming non-DITA resources used in branch filtering with dvrResourceSuffix or dvrResourcePrefix specified
content:
Let's say I have in the DITA Map a portion like this:

 <topicref href="topics/introduction.dita">
 <ditavalref href="test.ditaval">
 <ditavalmeta>
 <dvrResourceSuffix>stuff</dvrResourceSuffix>
 </ditavalmeta> 
 </ditavalref>
 <topicref href="test.pdf" format="pdf" navtitle="THIS IS MY PDF"/>
 </topicref>

Right now (even with latest DITA OT 2.x built from the develop branch) when you generate XHTML, the table of contents will have a broken reference to "teststuff.pdf".
In my opinion the dvrResourceSuffix and dvrResourcePrefix should only act upon topic references made to DITA resource, and not topic references made to non-DITA ones.

content:
In the RNG file "plugins\org.oasis-open.dita.v1_3\rng\base\rng\topicMod.rng" search for:

 <attribute name="dita:DITAArchVersion" a:defaultValue="1.2"/>

content:
Based on this [DITA Users List feedback](https://groups.yahoo.com/neo/groups/dita-users/conversations/messages/42339):

> I have tried text rotation in cells using `<entry rotate=”1”>` No rotation occurred. Does anyone have any suggestions as to why this might not be working?

As a possible solution in the XSLT stylesheet:

 DITA-OT\plugins\org.dita.pdf2\xsl\fo\tables.xsl

the template with mode "processTableEntry" could be modified as such:
<xsl:template match="*" mode="processTableEntry">
 <xsl:call-template name="commonattributes"/>
 <xsl:call-template name="applySpansAttrs"/>
 <xsl:call-template name="applyAlignAttrs"/>
 <xsl:call-template name="generateTableEntryBorder"/>
 <fo:block-container reference-orientation="{if (@rotate eq '1') then 90 else 0}"> 
 <fo:block xsl:use-attribute-sets="tbody.row.entry__content">
 <xsl:apply-templates select="." mode="ancestor-start-flag"/>
 <xsl:call-template name="processEntryContent"/>
 <xsl:apply-templates select="." mode="ancestor-end-flag"/>
 </fo:block>
 </fo:block-container>
</xsl:template>
Only Antenna House seems to have decent support for this from what I tested. Both XEP and Apache FOP do not properly render the table.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2729: maplink generating additional, spurious links from keydef entries
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2729: maplink generating additional, spurious links from keydef entries
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2729: maplink generating additional, spurious links from keydef entries
content:
Xhtml pages produced with a collection-type="sequence" attribute on the map have been creating navigation links with multiple parents and next entries, as shown in the picture. I would expect a single entry for next previous and parent. 

![dita_map_links_incorrect](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1036831/27276133-7a391a10-54da-11e7-8fa3-b2e520cb82b4.png)

The extract is produced from a large map, and I haven't been able to isolate the exact conditions that create it. However I have manage to trace the issue to what I think is a problem in the match condition being used to generate the links in maplinkImpl.xsl. 

For example, for the parent link, maplinkImpl.xsl currently uses the following test (around line 210):
` <!--parent-->
 <xsl:template match="*[contains(@class, ' map/topicref ')][not(ancestor::*[contains(concat(' ', @chunk, ' '), ' to-content ')])]" mode="link-to-parent" name="link-to-parent">`

The problem arises because the generated map used from temp also includes keydefs, which have the class " map/topicref mapgroup-d/keydef ". The match is picking these up too, creating the spurious links.

Enhancing the match condition to exclude the keydef entries as shown below appears to cure the problem:
`<xsl:template match="*[contains(@class, ' map/topicref ') and not(contains(@class, ' mapgroup-d/keydef ')) ][not(ancestor::*[contains(concat(' ', @chunk, ' '), ' to-content ')])]" mode="link-to-parent" name="link-to-parent">`
The generated output for the same map as above is now as I would expect:

![dita_map_links_correct](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1036831/27276160-99e8db7a-54da-11e7-9d33-37a213dcab9d.png)

The correction would be required on at least the matches for parent and next/previous (around line 260), but probably on others too (sibling friend etc.). 

The only problem might be that anybody using the current implementation might have got used to seeng the current, incorrect implementation...

content:
According to this email exchange on the [DITA TC list](https://lists.oasis-open.org/archives/dita-comment/201707/msg00001.html), according to [DITA 1.3 spec](http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3/errata01/os/complete/part1-base/archSpec/base/processing-keyref-for-text.html):

> For empty `<image>` elements, effective content is used as alternate text, equivalent to creating an `<alt>` sub-element to hold that content.

If in my DITA Map I have a key definition:
and in a DITA topic I have a keyref to it:
the image `<alt>` element should be computed automatically from the `<linktext>` set on the keydef `<topicmeta>`.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2756: DL indentation issue.
content:
In one of our topics we need to have a DL inside a LI (which belongs to an OL). The DL should be indented at the same depth as the LI where the DL is included.

We expect to see something like this:
1 - "This is a LI"
 "This is a DT"
 "This is a DD"
2 - "This is a LI"

When the DL is long enough, coming to the end of the page, the expected behaviour is that the DL should break, continuing on the next page. Or the whole DL, or the LI, should be pushed into the next page.
<!-- Tell us what happens instead of the expected behavior. -->
The DL breaks from the LI indentation. Instead of having something like:

1 - "This is a LI"
 "This is a DT"
 "This is a DD"
2 - "This is a LI"

We get:

1 - "This is a LI"
"This is a DT"
"This is a DD"
2 - "This is a LI"

Another issue is that if I build a longer DL (which I need to for another topic) the DL inside the LI doesn't work well with the page break. The DL never goes to the next page. Instead it overwrites my footer and then disappears from the PDF.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2770: Make it easier to convert @outputclass attribute value to another attribute in PDF output
content:
In the XSLT stylesheet `plugins\org.dita.pdf2\xsl\fo\topic.xsl` there is a `commonattributes` template.
I would propose rewriting it to:
<xsl:template name="commonattributes">
 <xsl:apply-templates select="@id"/>
 <xsl:apply-templates select="*[contains(@class,' ditaot-d/ditaval-startprop ')] |
 *[contains(@class,' ditaot-d/ditaval-endprop ')]" mode="flag-attributes"/>
 <xsl:apply-templates select="@outputclass"/>
</xsl:template>
 
<xsl:template match="@outputclass"/>
so that in my custom XSL I could just override the `@outputclass` template match and do my thing, generate those corresponding `xsl:attributes`.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2774: Add Markdown plugin to distribution package
content:
The [DITA-OT Markdown](https://github.com/jelovirt/dita-ot-markdown) plugin should be added to the default distribution to support lightweight authoring and publishing workflows.
This would allow users to include [Markdown](https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/) files as topics and generate Markdown output from DITA source without having to install additional plugins.

content: Issue #2775 is closed with labels feature. Retrieval signals: map, dita-ot, plugin.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2775: Add normalization plugin to distribution package
content:
The **DITA to DITA plugin** [org.dita.normalize](https://github.com/dita-ot/org.dita.normalize) should be added to the default distribution.

This would provide access to normalized topics and maps from DITA input without having to install additional plugins or copy files from the `temp` folders created during builds.

Since normalized output includes the results of the pre-processing operations that resolve references, it can be used to access the DITA output generated from [Markdown input](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2774), or feed DITA content into less sophisticated authoring tools which may not support certain features from the latest DITA versions.

Normalized output can also be used during plugin development to troubleshoot the results of preprocessing routines.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2781: Separate configuration to own directory
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2781: Separate configuration to own directory
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2781: Separate configuration to own directory
content:
Currently configuration files that are modified by integration are located in `src/main/resources` and they will end up in `dost.jar`; some configuration files are also bundled into `dost-configuration.jar` by the integration process. This will cause unstable behaviour because classpath order will define which will take precedence.

All configuration files that are generated or modified by integration or user should be located in a separate `config` directory and only static configuration should be kept in `resources` directory.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2790: Case sensitivity problem in PDF2 customization override string files.
content:
I expect that [customization.dir]/cfg/common/vars/zh_CN.xml will be found when doing a string lookup for xml:lang="zh-cn".
Here are two possible solutions:
1) Change org.dita.dost.pdf2.VariableFileTask.java so that the language portion of the filename is mapped to lowercase.
Change: lang.setAttributeNS(XML_NS_URI, "xml:lang", n.substring(0, i).replace('_', '-'));
To: lang.setAttributeNS(XML_NS_URI, "xml:lang", n.substring(0, i).replace('_', '-').toLowerCase());
2) Change the findString template in dita-utilities.xsl so that the stringfile variable's select statement uses the matches() function, with the ignore case flag active, rather than the = operator within the predicate portion of the XPath.
Change: <xsl:variable name="stringfile" select="$stringFiles[@xml:lang = $l]/@filename" as="xs:string*"/>
To: <xsl:variable name="stringfile" select="$stringFiles[matches(@xml:lang, $l, 'i')]/@filename" as="xs:string*"/>
<!-- Test case, Gist, set of files or steps required to reproduce the issue. -->

1. Add a language file to a customization for any of the following languages: pt-br, zh-cn, or zh-tw using file names pt_BR.xml, zh_CN.xml, or zh_TW.xml (these are the same names used in the org.dita.pdf2 plugin).
2. Change the graphic for the caution icon.
3. Run the dita-ot for one of the above languages and watch it ignore the customization file.

content: Issue #2793 is closed with labels enhancement, preprocess/keyref, stale. Retrieval signals: error, conref, keyref, html, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2793: Check for missing @href for undefined keys
content:
We sometimes link to images by key. There's an error of type `info` that checks, whether the key is undefined:
DOTJ047I Unable to find key definition for key reference "%1"
in root scope. The href attribute may be used as fallback if it exists
* Remove **[DOTJ047I](www.dita-ot.org/dev/user-guide/DITA-messages.html#msgs__DOTJ047I)** from the DITA-OT, keep it in the docs for reference * Split the error in the following 2 new errors:
[INFO] Unable to find key definition for key reference "%1"
 in root scope. A href attribute is found and will be used as fallback
 [ERROR] Unable to find key definition for key reference "%1"
 in root scope. No href attribute is found as fallback
**[keyref] [DOTJ046E](www.dita-ot.org/dev/user-guide/DITA-messages.html#msgs__DOTJ046E)** is of type `[ERROR]`. For us, a broken key reference without a fallback `@href` is as bad as a broken content key reference. So I'd recommend to use `[ERROR]` as the error level for the suggested error type.
[echo] [keyref] [DOTJ046E][ERROR] Conkeyref="TOPIC/ID" can not be resolved
because it does not contain a key or the key is not defined. The build will use 
the conref attribute for fallback, if one exists.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2815: Support relative paths for HTML headers/footers
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2815: Support relative paths for HTML headers/footers
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2815: Support relative paths for HTML headers/footers
content:
Currently several HTML parameters require absolute path values, which prevents portable cross-platform builds with the `dita` command:

* `args.ftr`
* `args.hdf`
* `args.hdr`

If absolute paths for these parameters are defined on one system, the same command/value may not work on other operating systems or machines where paths differ.

Allowing the `dita` command to interpret relative paths in these cases would reduce the need for Ant or other build scripts to set paths with variables that resolve to the correct local path when the build runs. 

These parameter values could then be passed in `.properties` files that work on multiple systems, which is apparently not possible at the moment per [comments](https://github.com/dita-ot/docs/pull/163#issuecomment-337163323) in https://github.com/dita-ot/docs/pull/163:

> WRT the absolute paths and properties file: cannot be fixed so that it will work every[w]here and will not break OT itself.

Various toolkit parameters currently use different approaches to path resolution. Perhaps the resolution mechanism for the HTML header/footer files could be aligned with one of these other approaches:

* `args.filter`

 > Relative paths are resolved against the DITA-OT base directory (for backwards compatibility) and internally converted to absolute paths.

* `args.input`

 > The path can be absolute, relative to `args.input.dir`, or relative to the directory where your project's Ant build script resides if `args.input.dir` is not defined.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2816: Improper conkeyref resolution

DITA-OT Issue #2816: Improper conkeyref resolution
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

content: Issue #2816 is closed with labels bug, priority/medium, stale. Retrieval signals: keyref, map, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2816: Improper conkeyref resolution
content:
I attached a ZIP with the samples.
Let's say I have a glossgroup containing multiple glossentries:

 <!DOCTYPE glossgroup PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Glossary Group//EN" "glossgroup.dtd">
 <glossgroup id="glossgroup">
 <title>GlossGroup</title>
 <glossentry id="genus">
 <glossterm>Genus</glossterm>
 <glossdef>Def text</glossdef>
 </glossentry>
 </glossgroup>

and in the main DITA Map a keydef pointing to the glossgroup:

 <keydef keys="testK" href="topics/glossgroup.dita"/>

and I have another glossgroup in which there is a conkeyref to the glossentry:

 <!DOCTYPE glossgroup PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Glossary Group//EN" "glossgroup.dtd">
 <glossgroup id="g2">
 <title>G2</title>
 <glossentry id="ddl" conkeyref="testK/genus">
 <glossterm></glossterm>
 <glossdef></glossdef>
 </glossentry>
 </glossgroup>

I consider that conkeyref to be invalid because the key name must be followed by an element ID, not by a topic (glossentry in this case) ID. Despite this, the published output resolves the conkeyref instead of reporting it as a problem.

[inproperConkeyref.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/1394321/inproperConkeyref.zip)
