title: DITA-OT Issue #2818: Task Module RNGs do not allow for easy domain attribute substitution
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2818: Task Module RNGs do not allow for easy domain attribute substitution
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2818: Task Module RNGs do not allow for easy domain attribute substitution
content:
If you look at this RNG file:

https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/develop/src/main/plugins/org.oasis-open.dita.v1_3/rng/technicalContent/rng/taskMod.rng

at some point it contains something like:

 <optional>
 <attribute name="domains"
 a:defaultValue="(topic task) (topic hi-d) (topic ut-d) (topic indexing-d) (topic hazard-d) (topic abbrev-d) (topic pr-d) (topic sw-d) (topic ui-d) "
 />
 </optional>

which should probably be replaced with:

 <ref name="domains-att"/>

because the "domains-att" is defined in the "task.rng" and this also allows for easier substitution of the attribute default value when creating a specialization of the task which for example adds a new profiling attribute which needs to be defined also in the domains attribute.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2824: Rendering problem in PDF when depth of the nested 'ul' elements is greater than 4
content:
A normal bullet should be rendered for the list items with nested depth greater than 4.
A possible solution would be to change the `plugins/org.dita.pdf2/xsl/fo/lists.xsl` resource to use the bullet symbol for depth=4 in case when current nested depth is greater than 4.

Modify the template:
``
<xsl:template match="*[contains(@class, ' topic/ul ')]/*[contains(@class, ' topic/li ')]">
``
to add:
<xsl:variable name="depth">
 <xsl:choose>
 <xsl:when test="$depth > 4">4</xsl:when>
 <xsl:otherwise>
 <xsl:value-of select="$depth"/>
 </xsl:otherwise>
 </xsl:choose>
</xsl:variable>

title: DITA-OT Issue #2842: Copy-to with key links to original rather than to copy
content:
<topicref href="alsocopykey.dita" keys="also1"/>
<topicref href="alsocopykey.dita" copy-to="alsocopykey-newname.dita" keys="also2"/>
Key references to `also1` should resolve to `alsocopykey.dita`, while key references to `also2` should resolve to the copied version, `alsocopykey-newname.dita`.
Key references to both `also1` and `also2` resolve to the original topic, `alsocopykey.dita`. When I generate HTML5, two topics are generated but all links are to the original; when I generate PDF, the topic appears twice but all links are to the original.

I also have a reference that appears *only* with copy-to, and is never referenced without the copy-to:
`<topicref href="onlycopykey.dita" copy-to="onlycopykey-newname.dita" keys="only"/>`

For that case, the HTML5 build generates both `onlycopykey.html` and `onlycopykey-newname.html`, but all uses of `keyref="only"` resolve to the original name. In the PDF, `<xref keyref="only"/>` results in blue text but no link, because the original file `onlycopykey.dita` is not in the PDF to provide a link destination.
When the `keyref` value is resolved for key definitions that set `@copy-to`, the link should go to the copy specified in `@copy-to`. At this point don't yet know if that change is simple or would require a giant architectural change.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2845: Define new attribute sets for block and inline images for pdf2
content:
This template is called for block _and_ inline images. As you can see, the `<fo:external-graphic>` element uses the same attribute set `image` for inline and block images.
So currently you cannot easily set attributes for the block and inline images separately, only for its wrapping block element. That's no good. The template should be refactored to set an additional `blockImage` (or something like that) attribute set, if the image is a block image (defined by `placement="break"`) or otherwise set the additional attribute set `inlineImage`.
If you agree, please upvote. Then I'll create a PR for **3.x**.

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2847: Add new pdf.image.dpi parameter
content:
1. The specified dimensions in the DITA file, or 2. The DPI setting saved in the image file itself, or 3. The fallback DPI set by the renderer for images with no DPI information.
For image formats that _do_ specify DPI information (most), in order to scale images consistently in a PDF, you must either set the dimensions for each image manually in the DITA topics or save all images using a fixed DPI setting.
The proposed parameter, when set, would:
1. Get the pixel dimensions of each image after preprocessing using the existing `org.dita.dost.module.ImageMetadataModule`.
2. If no image dimensions are set by the DITA topic, compute the effective dimensions using the specified DPI and set them in the FO file.
3. If the dimensions in the DITA topic are specified in pixels, or if `@scale` is used, compute the effective dimensions of the image in inches using the specified DPI and set them in the FO file.

This has the effect of overriding the DPI setting in the image files and applying a consistent DPI anywhere the DITA source doesn't specify different sizing for the rendered image.

For example, if you set `pdf.image.dpi=150` an image that is 300x600px would be rendered in the PDF at 2inx4in regardless of the DPI setting in the image file itself — unless the DITA topic specified a different size.

The existing behaviors would be retained if you didn't use this parameter.

DITA-OT Issue #2850: The image alternative text is not used when generating PDF with Apache FOP formatter
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2850: The image alternative text is not used when generating PDF with Apache FOP formatter
content:
The image alternate text is not processed by the PDF transformation when generate the `XSL-FO` file. I've used the `Apache FOP` processor.
Conforming with `Apache FOP` documentation, images must have an alternate text `fox:alt-text` extension attribute (in the fox namespace) on `fo:external-graphic` and `fo:instream-foreign-object` to specify a short text describing the image.
Override the next template:
`<xsl:template match="*" mode="placeImage">`
Location: `org.dita.pdf2/xsl/fo/topic.xsl`

from `org.dita.pdf2.fop` plugin:

title: DITA-OT Issue #2850: The image alternative text is not used when generating PDF with Apache FOP formatter
content:
<!--
 Override the original XSLT template to make images accessible.
 
 Conforming with Apache FOP documentation, images must have an alternate text fox:alt-text 
 extension attribute (in the fox namespace) on fo:external-graphic and fo:instream-foreign-object to 
 specify a short text describing the image.
 
 See: https://xmlgraphics.apache.org/fop/2.2/accessibility.html
-->
<xsl:template match="*" mode="placeImage">
 <xsl:param name="imageAlign"/>
 <xsl:param name="href"/>
 <xsl:param name="height" as="xs:string?"/>
 <xsl:param name="width" as="xs:string?"/>
 
 <!--
 Call the default processing to get an fo:external-graphic. 
 -->
 <xsl:variable name="external-graphic">
 <xsl:next-match>
 <xsl:with-param name="imageAlign" select="$imageAlign"/>
 <xsl:with-param name="href" select="$href"/>
 <xsl:with-param name="height" select="$height"/>
 <xsl:with-param name="width" select="$width"/>
 </xsl:next-match> 
 </xsl:variable>
 
 <!--
 Add fox:alt-text attribute if alt attribute or element is present. 
 -->
 <xsl:apply-templates select="$external-graphic" mode="fix-image-alt">
 <xsl:with-param name="ctx" select="." tunnel="yes"/>
 </xsl:apply-templates>
</xsl:template>

<!--
 Add 'fox:alt-text' attribute if image has an alternative text.
-->
<xsl:template match="fo:external-graphic" mode="fix-image-alt">
 <xsl:param name="ctx" tunnel="yes"/> 
 <xsl:copy>
 <xsl:choose>
 <xsl:when test="$ctx/@alt">
 <xsl:attribute name="fox:alt-text" 
 select="$ctx/@alt"/> 
 </xsl:when>
 
 <xsl:when test="$ctx/alt">
 <xsl:attribute name="fox:alt-text" 
 select="$ctx/alt"/> 
 </xsl:when>
 </xsl:choose> 
 
 <xsl:apply-templates select="node() | @*" mode="fix-image-alt"/>
 </xsl:copy>
</xsl:template>

<xsl:template match="node() | @*" mode="fix-image-alt">
 <xsl:copy>
 <xsl:apply-templates select="node() | @*" mode="fix-image-alt"/> 
 </xsl:copy>
</xsl:template>

content: Issue #2862 is closed with labels bug, preprocess, preprocess2, priority/high. Retrieval signals: error, exception, crash, xref, map, pdf, html, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2862: xref to web page kills PDF, hangs HTML5 for a while
content:
One of my customers had this link in a topic -- it's missing `@scope="external"` but is otherwise normal and worked in the past:
Expected: the link works. Based on the specification, processing default for links beginning with http, https, ftp, and mailto should be treated as external, so my customers shouldn't be forced to add it (though I tend to encourage adding it), and certainly shouldn't get failing builds because of it: https://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3/errata01/os/complete/part1-base/langRef/attributes/thescopeattribute.html
With a simple one-topic map, and that link in the topic, HTML5 hangs for an extended period at `topicpull`.

In 2.5.4, the HTML5 build otherwise works locally on my Windows machine, but when I run it on a Linux machine I get this error from the `topic-fragment` step -- I don't know why only there: 
`Error: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Only file URI scheme supported: http://www-01.ibm.com/common/ssi/ShowDoc.wss?docURL=/common/ssi/rep_ca/0/897/ENUS217-240/index.html`

I don't have 3.0 on that machine to test HTML5 there. But locally, with PDF and `preprocess2`, that link now kills the build in the merge step:

title: DITA-OT Issue #2862: xref to web page kills PDF, hangs HTML5 for a while
content:
map2pdf2:
[topic-merge] Processing C:\Users\IBM_AD~1\AppData\Local\Temp\temp20171204144909813\e17ddccb7429a132b18bfa84b28d3bed6f844f1a.ditamap
[topic-merge] Processing C:\Users\IBM_AD~1\AppData\Local\Temp\temp20171204144909813\b7e631acad95a349a712d265a6b2a2d6792ac95e.dita
[topic-merge] null
Error: Failed to run pipeline: Failed to process merged topics: Supplied element name is a zero-length string
Per the specification, treat the 4 known prefixes as "external" when no other scope is specified or inherited (should be relatively straightforward for `xref` as in this case but not sure how this will affect cascading in maps).

Apart from the crash, which is obviously a bug itself -- not treating this as external is also a bug because the spec says it should be treated as external; the spec also allows other prefixes to be treated as external, but implementing this as some sort of configuration option seems more like a new feature.
Build this map to PDF or HTML5 for the different behaviors described: [scopes.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/1528742/scopes.zip)

content: Issue #2872 is closed with labels feature, stale. Retrieval signals: map, pdf, html.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2872: Add "Related terms" category for related links to glossentries
content:
When the relationship table defines links between a topic and others, those links are automatically grouped in the published output at the end of the topic HTML content in various categories: "Related topics", "Related tasks", "Related concepts" and "Related information".
Our particular end user would like to have a particular category for related links to glossentry topic types, category which could be called "Related terms". 

So for example in the translation files like "xsl/common/strings-en-us.xml" we would need a new mapping like:

 <str name="Related glossentrys">Related terms</str> 

which would be used in the XSLTs for HTML and PDF based outputs similar to the ones for concepts, tasks and references for the category labels when a topic has related links to glossary entries.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2874: strictTaskbodyConstraintMod.xsd refers to taskMod.xsd unversioned
content:
The reference to `taskMod.xsd` should be versioned as with all other references in the schema files.
It references `taskMod.xsd` without version qualifier and it causes problems when running transformations that are based on versioned schema references with version tied to 1.2
The following command shows pretty well how `strictTaskbodyConstraintMod.xsd` is different from all other files:
find src/main/plugins/org.oasis-open.dita.v1_2/ -name *.xsd | xargs grep "redefine schemaLocation"
Run a transformation on a map that contains a task with `xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:oasis:names:tc:dita:xsd:task.xsd:1.2"`.
Copy of the error message, log file or stack trace
The relevant log output line is:
src-resolve: Cannot resolve the name 'tasktroubleshooting' to a(n) 'group' component.
* DITA-OT version: 2.5.4, possibly all others that support both DITA 1.2 and 1.3
* Operating system and version: independent of
* How did you run DITA-OT? `dita` command
* Transformation type: custom on top of PDF2

title: DITA-OT Issue #2887: Upgrade to Saxon-HE 9.8.0.7 to restore XSLT 1.0 support
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2887: Upgrade to Saxon-HE 9.8.0.7 to restore XSLT 1.0 support
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2887: Upgrade to Saxon-HE 9.8.0.7 to restore XSLT 1.0 support
content:
Saxon has apparently backtracked on their decision to abandon XSLT 1.0 support in Saxon-HE:

> **From 9.8.0.7, XSLT 1.0 backwards-compatibility mode is reinstated in Saxon-HE.** 
> In earlier versions of 9.8, this mode requires Saxon-PE or higher 
> _(that is, Saxon-HE will reject stylesheets that specify version=“1.0”)_.

— https://www.saxonica.com/html/documentation/conformance/xslt30.html

We currently ship Saxon-HE 9.8.0.5 in DITA-OT 3.0.1, but we could spare users some update grief by upgrading to 9.8.0.7 for DITA-OT 3.0.2.

This would make it easier for users with custom plug-ins that still use XSLT 1.0 syntax to upgrade to 3.x.

content:

content: Issue #2904 is closed with labels bug, plugin/pdf. Retrieval signals: map, pdf, html.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2904: PDF ignores titlealts/navtitle unless locked in map
content:
Navigation titles defined in topics via `<titlealts>`/`<navtitle>` should be used in PDF bookmarks unless explicitly overridden with other navtitles that are defined and locked in the map.

In HTML this works as intended: navtitles from topic `<titlealts>` are honored without any map modifications.
In PDF output, navtitles from topic `<titlealts>` are ignored unless the `@locktitle` attributes are set to `yes` in the map — even though the map doesn’t set any navtitles at all.

But this shouldn't be necessary: the locking mechanism should *only* be required to force-apply navtitles that are defined in the map. 

— If the map doesn't define one but the topic does, use the one from the topic.

Observed with the latest code on the `hotfix/3.0.3` branch — possibly related to recent changes in #2897.

content:
This is again a topic I thought I had created an issue for long time ago, but it does not seem so. I would like to have a `depend.process.post` (after everything) extension point.
**Why** I extract metadata from the map using the `depend.preprocess.post` extension point, so after all keys have been resolved. This metadata is stored in properties, because I use [OOPS xmltask](http://www.oopsconsultancy.com/software/xmltask/). These properties are cleared, when the processing is done. title: DITA-OT Issue #2931: con(key)ref shall use caller's ditaval specifications (flagging)
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2931: con(key)ref shall use caller's ditaval specifications (flagging)
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2931: con(key)ref shall use caller's ditaval specifications (flagging)
content:
The present **conrefImpl.xsl** uses the _target's ditaval flagging properties_ which isn't optimal if more places feed content from the target and suffer from it's ditaval flagging. Instead ... the source's (caller's) ditaval flagging should determine the actual ditaval-flagging which would make the idea more versatile.
see above ... I did all the changes and tested them for conref / conkeyref situations. The demand came from our professional writer team which needed the feature to ditaval-based highlighting(flag) different release versions even on conref'ed content.
There are a few changes to be made in **conrefImpl.xsl** and I marked all my changes with **<!--HSX ...** comments. If there is a strong reason to keep the target's dominance, it is very easy to allow both alternatives using an **@outputclass='useLocal'** definition. I just didn't go that far to do miminal changes to the existing code.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2943: Ignore links specified in reltable if topics are filtered out
content:
DITA-OT Issue #2943: Ignore links specified in reltable if topics are filtered out
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2943: Ignore links specified in reltable if topics are filtered out
content:
Let's say that in the DITA Map I refer to a topic with a profiling attribute set on the topicref:

 <map title="Growing Flowers">
 <topicref href="topics/introduction.dita" audience="expert"/>
 <topicref href="topics/care.dita"/>
 <reltable>
 <relrow>
 <relcell><topicref href="topics/introduction.dita"/></relcell>
 <relcell><topicref href="topics/care.dita"/></relcell>
 </relrow>
 </reltable>
 </map>

I then publish using a DITAVAL to filter out the "audience=expert" value. But there is still a reference to the "introduction.dita" in the reltable and this particular reference does not have the same profiling attribute set on it.
Because of this, the HTML generated for the other topic "care.dita" will contain a reference to "introduction.html".
So maybe a topic referenced in a reltable should be ignored if it is explicitly excluded in the DITA Map.

I added a sample project here:
[ignoreLinksInReltable.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/1960547/ignoreLinksInReltable.zip)

title: DITA-OT Issue #2954: build preprocess target name="copy-files" unless="preprocess.copy-files.skip" does not work as expected.
content:
<!-- copy-files
 Copy files to the output directory. -->
 <target name="copy-files"
 dita:depends="{depend.preprocess.copy-files.pre},copy-image,copy-html,copy-flag"
 dita:extension="depends org.dita.dost.platform.InsertDependsAction"
 unless="preprocess.copy-files.skip" />
You would expect that the copy-files target is skipped if you set preprocess.copy-files.skip, right?
But the preprocess.copy-files.skip skips only the contents of the copy-files target. But it is an empty target anyway. Because the copy-flag has a more detailed skip, it also influences copy-flag. But copy-image and copy-html are executed anyway.
Imitate <target name="copy-flag-check"> for copy-image and copy-html

The XSLT stylesheet "job-helper.xsl" does not specify an encoding to write the text output and on Windows the default platform encoding is not UTF-8 (although it is UTF-8 for Linux and Mac), it's more restrictive. So maybe we can force specify an "UTF-8" encoding on it's xsl:output.

The Ant build script for the DITA-OT docs was replaced with a Gradle build for 3.1 in DITA-OT/docs#178, but the [generateDocs task](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/develop/build.gradle#L245-L258) in the distribution build still calls the obsolete Ant build `docsrc/build.xml`.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2979: Default vertical alignment for table cells should be top in the HTML5 output similar to the XHTML output
content:
For the same tables one expects similar output for XHTML and HTML5.
There is an inconsistency between the XHTML and HTML5 outputs. The table entries that do not have set a valign attribute are aligned to the top in XHTML, as DITA 1.0 recommended, while in HTML5 they are aligned to the middle.
There are two ways of solving this:
1. Add a td {vertical-align:top} in the commonltr.css and commonrtl.css. If the table entries have an explicit valign attribute then this is translated to a class name and other selectors will match.
2. Invoke the "doEntry" template from the org.dita.html5/xsl/tables.xsl. This template is currently not used. (You should either use it or remove it from the stylesheet.)
1. Use a simple dita map with a single topic.
2. Add a table with one row and two cells. In the first cell put a small text, in the second one a bigger one.
3. Transform to HTML5
4. Check the vertical alignment. The small text should remain top when the second one wraps.

title: DITA-OT Issue #2983: Build result when @conkeyref attribute to reference external content is possibly incorrect for the html5 transform
content:
DITA builds using the html5 transform do not handle @conkeyref attribute references outside of the directory hierarchy underneath the map referenced by args.input. The path to this file is miscalculated. This problem has few follow-on consequences: - Content in t-prompt.dita is not pulled in to the output. - @conkeyref references for shared content in a file in the same directory as the map is not pulled into the output. - Paths to the CSS file are miscalculated.
Below is an overview of the content source setup. File src/shared_content/t-prompt.dita will not be seen if this is built:
src/
 shared_content/ 
 t-prompt.dita
 topicset/
 m-map.ditamap
 c-top_doc.dita
 t-conkeyref-test.dita
 to-data.dita
In the example, m-map.ditamap has keyrefs:

 <keyref keys="prompts" href="../shared_content/t-prompt.dita" processing-role="resource-only"/>
 <keyref keys="ts" href="to-data.dita" processing-role="resource-only"/>

The file t-conkeyref-test.dita has a @conkeyref set like this:

 <systemoutput conkeyref="prompts/python"/>

The result is that the path to shared content calculated by the transform appears to be incorrect. Impacts include path to to-data.dita being miscalculated, path to CSS file being miscalculated as well as path to t-prompt.dita being miscalculated.

Given a single topic that is bound to a resource-only key and then used by two or more normal-role topicrefs, each with a distinct key, xrefs to the navigation keys should resolve to the uses identified by the referenced keys.

For PDF there is only one possible correct result. 

For HTML, when "force unique" is false then the topic may have as many parents as there are uses. When force unique is true then each use should result in a unique HTML result and the xrefs should resolve to the corresponding result HTML file.
All xrefs resolve to first use of the topic.
I think the issue is in KeyrefModule.java but inspecting the code it's difficult to see what's going on. Would require more investigation and deeper understanding of how key references are resolved to be able to suggest a solution. [keyref-xref-to-multi-use-topic.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/2084721/keyref-xref-to-multi-use-topic.zip)
Test case zip is attached.

1. Generate PDF output from the map.ditamap map
2. Go to last topic (titled "TEST THE LINKS")
3. Observe that all three links resolve to the first use (page 3). They should resolve to each different use.
Copy of the error message, log file or stack trace

title: DITA-OT Issue #3003: Windows Help (CHM) HTML files have transitional DOCTYPE but contain HTML5 element
content:
Tested with DITA OT 3.1 and 2.5.4.
Publishing a DITA Map to CHM, if you open one of the HTML documents which will be part of the CHM, the DOCTYPE declaration is:

 <!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01 Transitional//EN" "http://www.w3.org/TR/html4/loose.dtd">

but inside it contains elements like "main" and "article" which are HTML5 specific.
The XSLT which does the HTML5 elements cleanup "plugins\org.dita.xhtml\xsl\dita2xhtml-util.xsl" is not used in the "plugins\org.dita.xhtml\xsl\dita2html.xsl".

Two possibilities:

1) Filter out those HTML 5 elements from the CHM output.
2) Change DOCTYPE declaration of those obtained HTML files to be HTML5, maybe also add this:

 <meta http-equiv="X-UA-Compatible" content="IE=edge" /> 

to allow for some more flexible CSS matchings (support for CSS :before, :after).

Several indications show that something is wrong, here are the observations

2. Processing a simple .ditamap generates the log ... T:\Dita-OT3\plugins\org.dita.pdf2\xsl\fo\bookmarks.xsl:42:31: Warning! Stylesheet module bookmarks.xsl is included or imported more than once.

I have done more than 20 integrations, always following the latest version, so I don't believe that I'm doing a typical beginner's fault.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3008: NPE when adding a keyref on a DITA element which does not allow one

title: DITA-OT Issue #3008: NPE when adding a keyref on a DITA element which does not allow one
content:
This is also a question related to the DITA 1.3 specs, so maybe @robander can help a little bit here. Let's say someone creates a DITA DTD specialization and adds a new element which extends the DITA

element. But their new element is allowed to have the keyref attribute on it. The DITA OT processing only expects the keyref attribute to be defined on specific DITA elements, see "org.dita.dost.writer.KeyrefPaser.keyrefInfos". But I do not see anything in the DITA 1.3 specification stating that only certain element types can have the keyref attribute specified on them. So right now the publishing breaks with a NullPointerException when you have a DITA element with an unexpected keyref set on it. As a quick experiment, let's say that inside a DITA topic somewhere in a paragraph I add this non-existing DITA element: and then I publish to HTML5 setting the "validate=false" parameter, I will get a NullPointerException reported with DITA OT 3.1 (but also with older DITA OTs): org.dita.base\build_preprocess.xml:280: java.lang.NullPointerException at org.dita.dost.writer.KeyrefPaser.processElement(KeyrefPaser.java:478) at org.dita.dost.writer.KeyrefPaser.startElement(KeyrefPaser.java:468) at org.xml.sax.helpers.XMLFilterImpl.startElement(Unknown Source) at org.dita.dost.writer.TopicFragmentFilter.startElement(TopicFragmentFilter.java:79) at org.dita.dost.writer.ConkeyrefFilter.startElement(ConkeyrefFilter.java:83) at org.apache.xerces.parsers.AbstractSAXParser.startElement(Unknown Source)

title: DITA-OT Issue #3022: Dita-OT 3.1 and 3.1.1 do not process xmlelement / xmlatt
content:
The elements `xmlelement `and `xmlatt `should be processed appropriately.
A warning is produced [topic-reader] [DOTJ030I][INFO] No 'class' attribute for was found for element `xmlatt`. The element will be processed as an **unknown or non-DITA element**. [topic-reader] [DOTJ030I][INFO] No 'class' attribute for was found for element `xmlelement`. The element will be processed as an **unknown or non-DITA element**.
Appeared with version 3.1 / 3.1.1, the version 3.0.3 does not show that behavior. That's no solution but a hint.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3026: Coderefs to C-sharp regions does not allow whitespace in tokens
content:
Token handling in coderef resolver does not accept whitespace in pattern. `coderef href="sample.cs#token=marker1,marker2"`
Create a file sample.cs, containing only:
`#token=%23region,%23endregion` will return the expected single block, so character encoding does work: ` // Body A`
Observations: - We only have to tokenize a uri-decoded fragment string into: 'token=' marker1 (',' marker2) - marker1 is terminated on comma and/or (multiple)space. Aha! This way you can never specify a search on a pattern containing space (and a comma too) in a text file.
In C# it is perfectly sensible to even have nested regions. If you don't expect it, it causes weird results. But by keeping code samples simple, the token-fragment feature should do nicely.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3052: Properly detect format attribute if missing
content:
The DITA 1.3 specs says that when the @format attribute is missing:

>(no value)
>The processing default is used. The processing default for the `@format` attribute is determined by inspecting the value of the `@href` attribute. If the `@href` attribute specifies a file extension, the processing default for the `@format` attribute is that extension, after conversion to lower-case and with no leading period. The only exception to this is if the extension is "xml", in which case the default format is "dita". If there is no extension, but the `@href` value is an absolute URI whose scheme is "http" or "https", then the processing default is "html". In all other cases where no extension is available, the processing default is "dita".

There are two cases:

1. ```xml
 <keydef keys="imageKey" href="images/Gardeniaflower.jpg"/>
according to the specification, you do not need to set "format="jpg"" on it as it will be detected from the @href value. So any image with keyref to "imageKey" should work find.
The PDF output works and shows the image (but it issues a warning at some point). The HTML output does not show the keyreffed image.

2. ```xml
 <topicref href="test.ditamap"/>

title: DITA-OT Issue #3063: Default PDF layout: extra indent on shortdesc in abstract
content:
DITA-OT Issue #3063: Default PDF layout: extra indent on shortdesc in abstract
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3063: Default PDF layout: extra indent on shortdesc in abstract
content:
When a `<shortdesc>` element is nested in `<abstract>` along with other elements and PDF output is generated with the default (MiniTOC) chapter layout, the short description is indented further than its siblings:

![shortdesc-in-abstract_minitoc](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/129995/44961243-67c27400-af0e-11e8-85e1-3e13cce31cba.png)

When the MiniTOC is disabled with `args.chapter.layout=BASIC`, the short description is aligned with the remaining abstract content as expected, with no excess indentation:

![shortdesc-in-abstract_basic](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/129995/44961248-7a3cad80-af0e-11e8-8676-e59cdf5d18df.png)

This is because the basic chapter layout uses the [`format-shortdesc-as-inline`](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/3.1.2/src/main/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/xsl/fo/topic.xsl#L578-L586) template mode (which applies the "[shortdesc](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/3.1.2/src/main/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/cfg/fo/attrs/topic-attr.xsl#L189-L190)" attribute set), whereas MiniTOC layout calls the [`format-shortdesc-as-block`](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/3.1.2/src/main/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/xsl/fo/topic.xsl#L562-L576) template mode, which uses the "[topic__shortdesc](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/3.1.2/src/main/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/cfg/fo/attrs/topic-attr.xsl#L192-L193)" attribute set.

Both attribute sets are empty, but the latter applies "[body](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/3.1.2/src/main/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/cfg/fo/attrs/topic-attr.xsl#L182-L184)" attributes that set the "start-indent" property to the value of the $side-col-width. This is responsible for the extra indentation, as the "start-indent" property is already applied via the "[abstract](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/3.1.2/src/main/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/cfg/fo/attrs/topic-attr.xsl#L186-L187)" attribute set.

Changing the `format-shortdesc-as-block` template mode to also use the "shortdesc" attribute set (without "body" attributes) solves the indentation issue for MiniTOC layout (regardless of where the short description appears):

diff --git a/src/main/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/xsl/fo/topic.xsl b/src/main/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/xsl/fo/topic.xsl

--- a/src/main/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/xsl/fo/topic.xsl
+++ b/src/main/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/xsl/fo/topic.xsl
@@ -564,7 +564,7 @@ See the accompanying LICENSE file for applicable license.
 <xsl:apply-templates/>
 </fo:block-->
 <!--compare the length of shortdesc with the got max chars-->
- <fo:block xsl:use-attribute-sets="topic__shortdesc">
+ <fo:block xsl:use-attribute-sets="shortdesc">
 <xsl:call-template name="commonattributes"/>
 <!-- If the shortdesc is sufficiently short, add keep-with-next. -->

title: DITA-OT Issue #3078: Errors caused by link to topic with xref in shortdesc
content:
When I have the following condition:

1. Topic contains `<xref>` to another topic `xref-in-shortdesc.dita`
1. The referenced topic has a short description, *and* that short description also contains an `<xref>` to `finaltarget.dita`
1. The xref inside that short description is missing link text or `<desc>`

The `topicpull` step ends up grabbing the short description from the middle file `xref-in-shortdesc.dita`, putting that in a variable, and then processing the variable. The result is that the `<xref>` to `finaltarget.dita` is processed again but in the context of that variable, which causes the processor to look for it in our XSLT directory, and ends with errors. Happens with both `preprocess` and `preprocess2`, here is the error log from `preprocess`:
C:\DCS\test\apiref>\dita-ot\dita-ot-3.1.2\bin\dita -i in.ditamap -f html5
[topicpull] I/O error reported by XML parser processing file:/C:/DITA-OT/dita-ot-3.1.2/xsl/preprocess/finaltarget.dita: C:\DITA-OT\dita-ot-3.1.2\xsl\preprocess\finaltarget.dita (The system cannot find the file specified.)
[topicpull] file:/C:/DCS/test/apiref/xref-in-shortdesc.dita:5:68: [DOTX031E][ERROR]: The file finaltarget.dita is not available to resolve link information.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3078: Errors caused by link to topic with xref in shortdesc
content:
C:\DCS\test\apiref>\dita-ot\dita-ot-3.1.2\bin\dita -i in.ditamap -f pdf
[topicpull] I/O error reported by XML parser processing file:/C:/DITA-OT/dita-ot-3.1.2/xsl/preprocess/dd3f451dd1448c00ddc872728d9573466227ad65.dita: C:\DITA-OT\dita-ot-3.1.2\xsl\preprocess\dd3f451dd1448c00ddc872728d9573466227ad65.dita (Thesystem cannot find the file specified.)
[topicpull] file:/C:/DCS/test/apiref/xref-in-shortdesc.dita:5:68: [DOTX031E][ERROR]: The file dd3f451dd1448c00ddc872728d9573466227ad65.dita is not available toresolve link information.
Once everything is in the variable context, I'm not sure how easy it is to get away from this. Most likely, the only way around it is to update the `copy-shortdesc` mode so that when it finds an xref, it actually goes to process the file, but I'm not sure yet.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3083: copy-to ignored in preprocess2
content:
Using `@copy-to` should result in an extra copy of the referenced topic. If file names are relevant for output, the specified names will be used.
The `@copy-to` attribute is not processed, so a copy is not created.

In PDF output, this results in a broken link and missing file. There are several errors when different steps try to read the copy that does not exist. In 3.1.2 this ends in a build failure caused by the missing file; #3082 removes the build failure and replaces it with an error like the other steps.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3083: copy-to ignored in preprocess2
content:
The error comes from this line: https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/develop/src/main/java/org/dita/dost/module/CopyToModule.java#L148

In an HTML build with `preprocess`, the file listed in `.job.xml` does not have `@src` until after `copy-to` is evaluated. That listing immediately before copy-to:
`<file uri="copyto.dita" path="copyto.dita" result="file:/C:/DITA-OT/TESTGITHUB/copyto/copyto.dita">`
and after:
`<file src="file:/C:/DITA-OT/TESTGITHUB/copyto/original.dita" uri="copyto.dita" path="copyto.dita" result="file:/C:/DITA-OT/TESTGITHUB/copyto/copyto.dita" format="dita" target="true">`

In a PDF build with `preprocess2`, that same file has `@src` after the first step (`map-reader`). That line in `preprocess2` assumes that if `@src` is listed, the file was referenced as a source file, so we shouldn't copy anything to it. That listing before copy-to:
`<file src="file:/C:/DITA-OT/TESTGITHUB/copyto/original.dita" uri="f7ac72d7ff9763eb29f90236b7c20b67fce3a84a.dita" path="f7ac72d7ff9763eb29f90236b7c20b67fce3a84a.dita" result="file:/C:/DITA-OT/TESTGITHUB/copyto/original.dita" format="dita" target="true">
</file>`

I'm not yet sure where in `map-reader` the `@src` attribute is set up, otherwise this would be coming in as a pull request. I _suspect_ that if we just leave off `@src` for the copies at this point, it will give the correct results, but I haven't been able to test that so I'm not sure if it would affect other map steps.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3083: copy-to ignored in preprocess2
content:
Build this to PDF - it will result in the build failures with 3.1.2, but you can see in temp that the copies are not created, and other steps will warn when trying to access them. The map has commented out copies of the `<files>` section from HTML (before/after copy-to runs), and PDF (before `copy-to` runs). With the fix for #3082 in place, it will produce a PDF that has 1 topic instead of 3.

content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3109: Provide CLI feedback for plug-in installation
content:
The `dita --install` option currently provides no confirmation when plug-ins are successfully installed (or removed). 

This is consistent with the typical "no news is good news" approach for basic UNIX utilities, and tolerable enough when installing or removing a single plug-in.

However, the current behavior is less helpful in situations when the `plugins` directory is manually modified to add/remove multiple plug-ins at once, ~or install multiple plug-ins from a single .zip file~.
Since DITA-OT maintains a list of currently installed plug-ins and updates this configuration during the integration process, it would be helpful to compare the before/after states and print a summary to the console upon completion, for example:
It might also be useful to conclude the integration process by printing the current list of available plug-ins to the console via the `dita --plugins` option. 

Since the plug-in registry changes for #3028 also permit the installation of plug-ins by alias, this would also serve to confirm the user's intent by displaying the plug-in ID that was actually installed via the alias.

This would be more consistent with the feedback provided by other CLI-based package managers.

_(See related enhancement #3070)._

title: DITA-OT Issue #3112: Temporary plugin installation locations
content:
DITA-OT Issue #3112: Temporary plugin installation locations
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3112: Temporary plugin installation locations
content:
When running CI build machines, these machines often have to render lots of projects in parallel. For each render job, the set of needed plugin differs. There is no point in time when it is kown to the administrator of the machine, which plugins all those render jobs might need. Also, due to the nature of CI, plugins and plugin versions will change it fast pace, i. e. a job which needed plugin-v1 in build #n might need plugin-v2 in build #n+1, but a second job might still need plugin-v1.
Render jobs should be able to use plugins without the need to install them on the build machine. The optimal solution would be that a render job has a dependency which is a plugin-ZIP. Maven unpacks the ZIP to the project's target folder, and DITA-OT uses that folder as an additional plugin source. All plugins found there are used, even if not registered in DITA-OT.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3128: HTML5 @border must not use "0" (zero) value
content:
Tables that have no border should either omit the @border attribute set the value to an empty string.

From the HTML5 spec:

"The border content attribute may be specified on a table element to explicitly indicate that the table element is not being used for layout purposes. If specified, the attribute’s value must either be the empty string or the value "1". The attribute is used by certain user agents as an indication that borders should be drawn around cells of the table."

https://www.w3.org/TR/html52/tabular-data.html#the-table-element

Epubcheck applied to EPUBs reports border="0" as an error, which is how I noticed this.

Two of our clients complained that when using the stock DITA OT 3.2 sometimes their XSLT customizations are no longer taken into account, latest report is here:

https://www.oxygenxml.com/forum/topic17977.html

Basically if their "custom.xsl" imports a "front-matter.xsl" placed relative to it, Saxon somehow skips over this import and uses the "front-matter.xsl" specified in the base PDF folder.

I have a plugin with which I can reproduce the problem on my side, with Saxon 9.1 the problem with the XSLT imports precedence cannot be reproduced but unfortunately I'm having trouble putting together a small XML + XSLT package to open an issue on the Saxonica list.
My first idea would be to update to Saxon 9.9 and see if the problem is fixed, unfortunately the DITA OT 3.2 Java code needs to be updated in order to work with Saxon 9.9:

title: DITA-OT Issue #3158: Plugin not called for all pre-process extension points for PDF transform
content:
I'm attempting to update an old job we have - we have a custom Python script which converts textual instances of `@@VAR:SomeTextHere` into `<keyword keyref="SomeTextHere_first">` the first time the keyword is seen and `<keyword keyref="SomeTextHere_other">` for subsequent uses. These keywords are defined in the ditamap.

I don't want to modify the real source files, and ideally I don't want to have a 2-stage process of:

- Parse ditamap, copy all referred ditas to a temporary location and modify those files
- Run dita over the new files.

So I thought I could hook into the dependency points once the dita files have been copied across to the temporary directory, and modify them there.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3158: Plugin not called for all pre-process extension points for PDF transform
content:
- PDF transforms are provided by org.dita.pdf2. 
- https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/3.2/src/main/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/build_template.xml defines the build template used for a transformation. 
- It has `preprocess2` as a target. 
- As far as I can see, https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/3.2/src/main/plugins/org.dita.base/build_preprocess2_template.xml doesn't have the same dita:depends targets as https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/3.2/src/main/plugins/org.dita.base/build_preprocess_template.xml.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3167: Support <required-cleanup>, <unknown>, and <foreign> in more elements
content:
I'm working on FrameMaker-to-DITA migration for our team. There are places where I need `<foreign>`, `<unknown>`, or `<required-cleanup>` elements to preserve external information for later review, but the OASIS content models do not allow them.

Two real-world examples are:

- allow `<required-cleanup>` in `<uicontrol>` (for unsupported nested styles)
- allow `<foreign>` in `<cmdname>` (for links to external interactive help systems)

This enhancement requests that these three tags be supported in more places.
I am attaching a perl script (cm.pl) that dumps a content model for a given document-type shell. It requires jing/trang, perl, and the XML::Twig perl CPAN library.

I ran it as follows to find the elements that allow text **but not** each of the three tags, and I'm attaching those results as well. (Note that f.txt and u.txt are identical, which is expected as they're allowed similarly.)
cd plugins/org.oasis-open.dita.v1_3/rng/technicalContent/rng
fgrep -v required-cleanup cm | fgrep -v 'ns1:' | egrep -v -E '_[0-9]' | fgrep text > rq.txt
fgrep -v unknown cm | fgrep -v 'ns1:' | egrep -v -E '_[0-9]' | fgrep text > u.txt
fgrep -v foreign cm | fgrep -v 'ns1:' | egrep -v -E '_[0-9]' | fgrep text > f.txt

title: DITA-OT Issue #3192: keyref in mapref can not access key when both are defined in a keyscope
content:
The root.ditamap defines keys with hrefs to the `featureXX.dita` files. Then maprefs reference a `template_xxxxx_feature.ditamap` in which the keys shall be used to set the href of the included topicrefs. Since the `template_xxxxx_feature.ditamap` files can be referenced multiple times, with different values for the same keynames topicgroups around the keydef and mapref define a keyscope. See "Steps to reproduce" for example files.
Expected output behavior without keyscopes (first occurance of key "feature" counts so Feature 2.1 shows twice) ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47040897/51771558-ae954e00-20e9-11e9-9c49-740031f9bc30.png)
Expected output behaviour with keyscopes set to prevent double keydef in same scope ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47040897/51771543-99b8ba80-20e9-11e9-86fa-03e81ca37ef4.png)
None of the topics get referenced in the output when keyscopes are defined ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47040897/51771581-be149700-20e9-11e9-989a-bd968d26df6e.png)

title: DITA-OT Issue #3192: keyref in mapref can not access key when both are defined in a keyscope
content:
<!-- Optional suggestions on how to fix the issue, or implement the changes. -->
<!-- If you know how to fix the issue, please create a pull request instead. -->
The Open Toolkit should support the behaviour correctly as defined in the specification:

_"...Map authors define the boundaries for key scopes by specifying the `@keyscope` attribute on `<map>` elements, `<topicref>` elements, or elements that are specializations of `<map>` or `<topicref>`. Such elements, their contents, and any locally-scoped content referenced from within the element, are considered to be part of the scope...."_
http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3/errata02/os/complete/part3-all-inclusive/langRef/attributes/the-key-scope-attribute.html#keyscope-attribute

The example in the linked spec shows how keyscopes are defined in topicgroups. The mapref is a specialisation of topicref and a child in the keyscope defined by the group. Thus the referenced map should be able to us the keys defined in the keyscope.
[example.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/2797759/example.zip)

This Classification DITA Map based on the XML Schema should be considered valid:

 <map xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
 xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:oasis:names:tc:dita:spec:classification:xsd:classifyMap.xsd">
 <title></title>

but it's not. 
In the XML Schema "org.oasis-open.dita.v1_3\schema\subjectScheme\xsd\classifyMap.xsd" next to this group reference:

there should be another one:

 <xs:group ref="classify-d-topicref"/>

content: Issue #3218 is closed with labels enhancement, plugin-integration, stale. Retrieval signals: error, dita-ot, plugin.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3218: Improve error message for installed plug-ins
content:
If you try to install a plug-in that already exists, the toolkit throws an error that points to the location of the existing plug-in installation:
Error: Plug-in org.lwdita already installed: /path/to/dita-ot/plugins/org.lwdita
Since #3120 landed in version 3.2, the `--force` option can be used to overwrite existing plug-ins with new versions, but since this is a relatively recent addition, many users may not be aware it exists.

To make this option more discoverable, we could mention it in the error message.

> Error: Plug-in `{pluginID}` already installed: `/path/to/dita-ot/plugins/{pluginID}`
> To update it, add the `--force` option: `dita --install {pluginID} --force`.

https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/pull/2880

There was recently a discussion on the Saxon mailing list started by @drmacro:
https://sourceforge.net/p/saxon/mailman/saxon-help/?viewmonth=201902&viewday=18

and one of the posters there had some feedback that I will summarize below:

1.

> If a dita-ot feature, was there some coordination with Saxonica on
the use of net.sf.saxon.lib.ExtensionFunctionDefinition as the name
of the service? I wonder if that could lead to complications should Saxonica later
decide to use such a ServiceLoader in Saxon itself. I haven't played
much with multiple ServiceLoaders looking for the same service ...
I suppose if called in different class loader contexts they could
end up finding different providers, but maybe that's not a big deal.

2.

> P.S.: This test

https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/0b3e3d221fe8e78286f88ad81ce30a872beaf3fc/src/main/java/org/dita/dost/module/XsltModule.java#L218

> looks as if the simpler (tf instanceof
net.sf.saxon.TransformerFactoryImpl) would test exactly the condition
wanted, without the potential to NPE (if a null tf is passed) or
ClassCastException (in the unlikely case a tf is passed of some type
<T super net.sf.saxon.TransformerFactoryImpl>; unlikely because it
may be that no other such instantiable T exists anyway). Sometimes
the simplest ways are still the best.

3.

> I also wondered why

https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/0b3e3d221fe8e78286f88ad81ce30a872beaf3fc/src/main/java/org/dita/dost/module/XsltModule.java#L233

> takes the ExtensionFunctionDefinition instance that the ServiceLoader
just gave it, gets its class, then makes a new instance.

According to the [documentation](https://www.dita-ot.org/dev/parameters/parameters-base.html#base__args.rellinks), the `args.rellinks` parameter should default to `nofamily` for PDF output:
> • `nofamily` – Parent, child, next, and previous links are not included. > For PDF output, the default value is `nofamily`. For all other formats, the default value is `all`.
Family links are included in PDF output regardless of this parameter setting.
Run the `dita` command on the DITA-OT documentation bookmap and generate default PDF output:
In both cases, family links are included in the output, for example in _“[Customizing HTML output](https://www.dita-ot.org/dev/topics/html-customization.html)”_, which defines [family collections](https://github.com/dita-ot/docs/blob/develop/topics/html-customization.ditamap#L7-L8).

title: DITA-OT Issue #3241: Modules that Use XSLT do not pass parameters
content:
<!-- Tell us what happens instead of the expected behavior. -->

Modules that use XSLT, such as MaprefModule, do not completely configure the Transformer or the transform. 

For example, parameters configured by plugins are not passed as they are for XsltModule-based transforms.
I think the solution is to factor the transformer configuration and setup code to a common superclass used by all transform-running pipeline modules so that the setup processing is centralized and consistent.

Alternative would be to provide a helper class that provides a properly-configured Transformer instance that is then used by the module-specific code that runs the transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3242: Non-dita resources copied to incorrect folder when performing the PDF transformation
content:
Using the latest DITA OT "develop" branch with the first sample project attached here: https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2620
I publish the PDF from the command line, at the end of the transformation I get this extra folder created on disk:

 dita-ot\src\main\${_dita.map.output.dir}\resources

and inside it contains the "Particles.mp4".
Also for the PDF output I looked inside the _MERGED.xml file and it contains this reference:
<object datakeyref="shining_dots" outputclass="video" class="- topic/object " xtrf="file:/C:/Users/radu_coravu/Desktop/datakeyrefProblem/space-multimedia/topics/movies.dita" xtrc="object:1;20:15" data="99dc317f2c89406f64f6ccb34a8be40f53de63cc.mp4" format="mp4"/>
But that "99dc317f2c89406f64f6ccb34a8be40f53de63cc.mp4" file is not present next to the merged file.
Of course for the PDF output the DITA object element makes little sense, ideally it could get converted to a plain link to the video in this case.
So there are two problems:

1) Video is copied to wrong location because the ANT parameter "_dita.map.output.dir" is not properly defined.
2) The final PDF gets a link to the hashed video file name instead of linking to the original video file name.

I cannot reproduce the problem with DITA OT 3.2.1 so this may be an unwanted side effect of: https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/pull/3234

title: DITA-OT Issue #3254: Report template plug-in suggestion
content:
After seeing this thread: [Generating a reference report](https://groups.yahoo.com/neo/groups/dita-users/conversations/topics/44509), I wondered how a plug-in might generate such a report. I've looked at the impressive list of plug-ins, but none stood out as a starting point for a report.
I suppose the obvious way to generate a report would be with a transformation that 'kills off' the majority of elements, leaving only the desired elements. The equally obvious drawback is the maintenance overhead with any specialisation, or new versions of DITA.
The thread mentions the use of an XPath query, and this seems a whole lot more sensible. Filter out only the desired elements. So the question / suggestion is: "Is it possible to build an XPath query into a plug-in?" If so, would it be reasonable to have a plug-in that demonstrates this?

title: DITA-OT Issue #3255: Allow specifying a DITA OT plugin extension as optional
content:
Let's say I create a DITA OT plugin.xml which adds an XSLT custom stylesheet for HTML-based outputs:

 <feature extension="dita.xsl.html5" value="xsl/xhtmlSVG.xsl" type="file"/>
 <feature extension="com.oxygenxml.pdf.css.xsl.merged2html5" value="xsl/xhtmlSVG.xsl" type="file"/>

The extension point "com.oxygenxml.pdf.css.xsl.merged2html5" is for a plugin which may or may not be installed in the DITA OT where my plugin is placed. Somehow I want to signal to the DITA OT Integrator to avoid failing if the extension point "com.oxygenxml.pdf.css.xsl.merged2html5" is not found in the DITA OT. Some kind of:

 <feature extension="com.oxygenxml.pdf.css.xsl.merged2html5" value="xsl/xhtmlSVG.xsl" type="file" optional="true"/>

Otherwise, I would need to have two plugin.xml's, one for the case when my plugin is installed in the standard DITA OT and one for the case when it's installed in a DITA OT which has that extra plugin installed.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3263: Conref to element within a topic incorrectly requires same element type
content:
<xsl:when test="exists($elemid)">
 <xsl:sequence select="key('id', $elemid)[local-name() = $element][ancestor::*[contains(@class, ' topic/topic ')][1][@id = $topicid]]"/>
</xsl:when>
The `[local-name() = $element]` predicate means that valid conrefs to specializations of the referencing element will not be correctly resolved.

The fix is to do an is-specialization-of check in place of this predicate.

Not sure what the best way to do that check is--is there an existing function to do that check?

title: DITA-OT Issue #3272: Integrator class uses method not defined in "xml-apis-1.4.01.jar"
content:
DITA-OT Issue #3272: Integrator class uses method not defined in "xml-apis-1.4.01.jar"
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3272: Integrator class uses method not defined in "xml-apis-1.4.01.jar"
content: It uses this method "XMLInputFactory.newFactory()" which is defined in the JRE 1.8 default classes but is not defined in the similar implementation from "xml-apis-1.4.01.jar". Publishing probably works because the Java default classes are usually stronger than the extra JAR libraries from the classpath. But when compiling the "dos.jar" if for example the compilation classpath favors "xml-apis-1.4.01.jar" instead of the runtime libraries, you get a compilation error. I suggest replacing "newFactory()"=>"newInstance()" which does the same thing.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3280: Provide option to retain submap details in cleaned merged map
content:
As of 3.3.1 the Clean Map preprocess stage removes the topicgroup elements introduced in earlier phases to capture details about submaps.

This this has the effect of losing key scope definition boundaries, making it impossible to use the final merged map to resolve references to scoped keys.

ideally the the clean map process would simply retain the submap-reflecting topicgroups but that could break processes that make assumptions about the markup structure (e.g., tools that don't account for the possibility of an additional layer of containment around Bookmap chapters managed as submaps or something).

So would like a runtime option to retain the submap topicgroups in the final merged map.

Alternatively, provide an extension point in the clean map transform so that this kind of functionality can be added by plugins.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3292: Uninstalling plug-in that provides transformer factory fails
content: Issue #3292 is closed with labels bug, plugin-integration, priority/medium, stale. Retrieval signals: error, dita-ot, plugin, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3292: Uninstalling plug-in that provides transformer factory fails
content:
The DITA Community plugin includes a jar that provides a custom transformer factor that configures the collators that the i18n code uses.

This is reflected in the services entry in the jar.

The failure on uninstall is:
./bin/dita --uninstall org.dita-community.i18n
Error: The following error occurred while executing this line:
/Users/ekimber/workspace-ditaot/dita-ot-wek-dev/src/main/integrator.xml:45: javax.xml.transform.TransformerFactoryConfigurationError: Provider for class javax.xml.transform.TransformerFactory cannot be created

title: DITA-OT Issue #3292: Uninstalling plug-in that provides transformer factory fails
content:
I'm sure the issue is that the jar is in the classpath at the time the uninstall starts, but then the plugin directory is removed, making the jar with the transformer factory unavailable.

I can't reproduce this failure when running Main from Eclipse, presumably because the jar is still in the class path somewhere.

I tried debugging through the Integrator code to see where this was happening and see if there was a way to recover from it but I couldn't find the place where the failure occurs.

I have no idea how we might work around this particular issue--I don't know if there's a way to play tricks with class loaders or something during the uninstall process or just fork a new execution environment.

The end result is that the plugin is not completely uninstalled--the directory gets removed but the entries from the plugin.xml and so on do not get removed, so the plugin is still listed as existing.

Running --install does complete the uninstallation.

content:
I'm using the Apache HTTP Client libraries with the DITA OT and lately starting with DITA OT 3.3.1 my console started getting flooded with debug messages coming from the library:

 [gen-list] [DEBUG] http-outgoing-0 >> GET http://devel-new.sync.ro/webdav-qa/DITA/flowers/topics/introduction.xml HTTP/1.1
 [gen-list] [DEBUG] http-outgoing-0 >> Accept: application/xml,*/*

title: DITA-OT Issue #3314: PDF index <index-see-also> and <index-see> issues

title: DITA-OT Issue #3314: PDF index <index-see-also> and <index-see> issues
content: Issue #3314 is closed with labels bug, index, plugin/pdf, plugin/pdf/fop. Retrieval signals: map, pdf, dita-ot, plugin.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3314: PDF index <index-see-also> and <index-see> issues
content:
PDF FOP index produces the following issues related to `<index-see-also>`:
1. If there are multiple `<index-see-also>` elements as children of `<indexterm>` only the first one (alphabetically, after sorting occurs between *_MERGED.xml and stage1.xml) appears in the index. In the example below, only "See also DTD" is emitted. Both "RELAX NG" and "schema" are suppressed.
Note: Changing the markup to put each `<index-see-also>` as a lone child of `<indexterm>` had no effect on the final "see also" entries; it does however create extra page number entries for "grammar files" in the index, which is likely related to the next issue.
<indexterm>grammar files<index-see-also>schema</index-see-also></indexterm>
<indexterm>grammar files<index-see-also>RELAX NG</index-see-also></indexterm>
<indexterm>grammar files<index-see-also>DTD</index-see-also></indexterm>

title: DITA-OT Issue #3314: PDF index <index-see-also> and <index-see> issues
content:
2. When emitting multiple "see also" entries, they should be separated by a comma. I don't see any processing in index.xsl or index_fop.xsl that would account for that currently.

3. The `<index-see-also>` entries show their page number twice (e.g., "schema 3, 3") -- once for each time the term is used in my test files. Only one entry per page should be emitted. Because the page number is emitted once for each time that a term appears in `<indexterm>` or `<index-see-also>` leads me to believe that each `<index-see-also>` is being processed, but there is no logic to remove duplicated page numbers.

Removing `[1]` from from certain `opentopic-index:index.entry[1]` in plugins\org.dita.pdf2\xsl\fo\index.xsl does emit all of the "see also" entries, albeit the linking is wrong (only to the alphabetically first ID) and there is no comma. 

I'm not sure if anything in plugins\org.dita.pdf2.fop\xsl\fo\index_fop.xsl is implicated.

Tested using
* The attached files
* DITA-OT 3.3.1 with no custom plugins
* Generated from oXygen.

The attached .zip file contains a DITA map and one topic file to demonstrate the issues.

Edit: I also confirmed that `<index-see>` is also affected. 

[see-also.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/3238413/see-also.zip)

content: Issue #3320 is closed with labels bug, index, plugin/pdf, plugin/pdf/fop. Retrieval signals: error, pdf, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3320: Index entries missing if child entries exist
content:
The DITA specification is clear that an `<indexterm>` with children should not create locators (i.e., links or page numbers). 

> In the case of nested <indexterm> elements, each <indexterm> with no <indexterm> children (the "leaves") contributes a page number to the generated index; the ancestral <indexterm> elements for each leaf <indexterm> provide the higher levels for the multilevel entry.

But the specification appears to make an assumption that the index entries are all in the same file. That distinction is not clear when multiple files are involved. 

garagetaskoverview.xml & wwfluid.xml
`<indexterm>garage</indexterm>`

shelving.xml
`<indexterm>garage<indexterm>shelving</indexterm></indexterm>`

title: DITA-OT Issue #3360: Possible NPE in ANT Invoker
content:
Using the latest DITA OT development branch, I'm passing to the "dita" command line some params which are not quite appropriate and I get:

 Caused by: java.lang.NullPointerException
 at org.dita.dost.invoker.Main.handleLogfile(Main.java:234)
 at org.dita.dost.invoker.Main.startAnt(Main.java:165)
 ... 7 more

so while processing the arguments a RuntimeException occurs. This means that the "args" variable is null so you end up with a NPE in the "handleLogfile" which hides the original stack trace of the exception. So the "handleLogfile" method needs to check also if the "args" variable is null.
I will add another issue with the original exception once I figure out what it is.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3376: NullPointerException in Saxon when using ANT XMLCatalog implementation
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3376: NullPointerException in Saxon when using ANT XMLCatalog implementation
content:
When the DITA OT is placed in a folder containing spaces and French accents, Saxon throws a NullPointerException. I originally added the issue on the Saxonica issues list:

https://saxonica.plan.io/issues/4326

I think this can be fixed from the Saxon side but I consider it would be better if our XsltModule code would not use the ANT "XMLCatalog" implementation for anything and always use the Apache Xerces Resolver instead.

Maybe on the method "org.dita.dost.module.XsltModule.setXMLCatalog(XMLCatalog)" we could just get the catalog path from the ANT XMLCatalog (which has various bugs) and create a Xerces Catalog Resolver over that path.
Or remove the method "org.dita.dost.module.XsltModule.setXMLCatalog(XMLCatalog)" completely because the "org.dita.dost.module.XsltModule.init()" method already sets the proper XML catalog resolver to the class.

content:
DITA-OT Issue #3380: Are incremental builds a possibility?
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3380: Are incremental builds a possibility?
content:
I'm investigating the Dita OT and would like to know if it's possible to have incremental builds. What I mean is after building a deliverable, subsequent builds will only process files that have changed (changes including things like content changes to the topic itself, conref changes, changes in links, etc.). 

The goal is to speed up builds and provide feedback on content that has changed.

My group is considering transitioning our content to Dita and need some speed metrics on Dita OT. Processing the Dita 1.3 standard as HTML5 took about 5 minutes on my machine, and that's a very small deliverable compared to the documentation we need to process. It's one thing if an initial build takes a while, but we can't have builds that take the same amount of time when one topic changes.

Is it possible to implement this kind of functionality to Dita OT?

title: DITA-OT Issue #3384: Allow adding extra attributes in extra namespaces in plugin.xml
content:
We are working on a feature in our product so that we mark certain DITA OT parameters as important in the plugin.xml and for those important parameters we can promote the parameters in the "Parameters" editing list and show them as separate entries above the list.
For this ideally the plugin.xml would be valid against the "plugin.rng" even if there would be attributes in custom namespaces defined on each parameter like:

 <transtype name="abc">
 <param name="args.css" oxy:promoted="true" oxy:promotedLabel="CSS Path" xmlns:oxy="httpL//someNamespace"/>
 </transtype>

This snippet above could mean for our application that above the table of parameters we could show a label called "CSS Path" followed by an URL chooser in which the end user would choose the CSS. 
So would making the "plugin.rnc" more flexible make sense to you?
The information from the plugin.xml gets collected to a plugins.xml, I'm not sure if that file gets also validated in some way.

content:

 <xsl:template name="insertTocOddFooter">

content:
Let's say I have a DITA topic with an element inside:

This is changed text.

and a DITAVAL file containing these rules: Right now if I publish to HTML the element is displayed and flagged as yellow. But according to the specification: http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3/errata02/os/complete/part3-all-inclusive/archSpec/base/flagging.html#flagging When the same element evaluates as both flagged and filtered (for example, flagged because of a value for the @audience attribute and filtered because of a value for the @product attribute value), the element should be filtered. content: Issue #3431 is closed with labels none. Retrieval signals: map, pdf, dita-ot, plugin.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3431: Cannot properly expand abbreviated-form
content:
Based on this message:

https://groups.io/g/dita-users/message/44956

I'm attaching this sample project, when converted to PDF the warning appears and the abbreviated form reference is not properly expanded:

 [DOTX060W][WARN]: Key 'key_g_dccs' was used in an abbreviated-form element, but the key is not associated with a glossary entry. Abbreviated-form should ONLY be used to reference to a glossary entry.

[abbrevform-not-resolving.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/3954354/abbrevform-not-resolving.zip)

I looked inside this XSLT stylesheet:

 plugins\org.dita.pdf2\xsl\fo\abbrev-domain.xsl

in this template:

 <xsl:template match="*[contains(@class,' abbrev-d/abbreviated-form ')]" name="topic.abbreviated-form">

this variable:

 <xsl:variable name="target" select="key('id', substring(@href, 2))[1]" as="element()?"/>

seems to match the topicref to the glossentry instead of the glossentry. Looking at the _MERGED.xml file, both the topicref to the glossentry and the glossentry element have the same @id attribute value which is wrong in my opinion. Also even if I manually set an @id attribute value on the glossref in the DITA Map:

 <glossref keys="key_g_dccs" href="glossary/g_dccs.dita#g_dccs" print="yes" id="test"/>

the @id attribute will not be preserved in the _MERGED.xml document.

A possible easy fix for this would be to rewrite the "target" variable as:

 <xsl:variable name="target" select="key('id', substring(@href, 2))[self::*[contains(@class,' glossentry/glossentry ')]]" as="element()?"/>

but the problem with the @id attribute set on two different elements with the same value in the _MERGED.xml document would remain.

content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3440: DITA 2.0: allow for new "specializations" attribute
content: Issue #3440 is closed with labels DITA 2.0, enhancement. Retrieval signals: map.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3440: DITA 2.0: allow for new "specializations" attribute
content:
With DITA 2.0, the `@domains` attribute is going away, along with most tokens that go in it -- https://github.com/oasis-tcs/dita/issues/217

The `@specializations` attribute is added to replace it, and only used for specialized attributes.

For DITA 2.0, we need to:

- Stop issuing this message when `@domains` is missing: `[DOTJ029I][INFO] No 'domains' attribute was found for element '<map>'. This generally indicates that your DTD or Schema was not developed properly according to the DITA specification.`
- Allow the new syntax for specialized attribute tokens when determining which attributes can be used for filtering
I'm not sure that the `DOTJ029I` is even needed.

If we want to keep supporting 1.3 while looking ahead to 2.0, we could possibly:

- Drop that message (not really needed)
- If a topic or map has `@specializations`, create `@domains` along side it with the right syntax
- If a topic or map has `@domains`, create `@specializations` with tokens for specialized attributes
- Steps that follow (core steps or extensions) will then work with either variant, and can be switched over in the future to be based on DITA 2.0 syntax

title: DITA-OT Issue #3475: Row separator is applied incorrectly in pdf output with merged cells
content:
Hello,

I use the DITA-OT 2-5-4 pdf2 plugin and I have noticed an error in the processing of entry row separators.
From what I have seen this error is still present in the current version.

Given the following DITA table:

title: DITA-OT Issue #3475: Row separator is applied incorrectly in pdf output with merged cells
content: Lorem Lorem Lorem Lorem Lorem Lorem dolor Lorem dolor Lorem dolor Lorem dolor Lorem dolor Lorem dolor Lorem Lorem Lorem dolor Lorem dolor Lorem Lorem Lorem dolor Lorem dolor Lorem dolor No bottom border Lorem No top border Lorem Lorem Lorem dolor Lorem dolor Lorem dolor Lorem dolor Lorem dolor Lorem dolor Lorem Lorem Lorem dolor Lorem dolor Lorem Lorem Lorem dolor Lorem dolor Lorem dolor Lorem dolor

title: DITA-OT Issue #3475: Row separator is applied incorrectly in pdf output with merged cells
content:
The entry "No bottom border" should have no bottom border in the output, because the default rowsep value on table is "0" and the entry has no rowsep attribute.
However a bottom border is generated in the output.

I have identified the problem in the xslt code. 

When looking at **dita-ot/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/xsl/fo/tables.xsl**, on line 694, inside the variable "needTopBorderOnBreak" :
<xsl:when test="../parent::node()[contains(@class, ' topic/tbody ')]">
 <xsl:variable name="entryNum" select="count(preceding-sibling::*[contains(@class, ' topic/entry ')]) + 1"/>
 <xsl:variable name="prevEntryRowsep" as="xs:string?">
 <xsl:for-each select="../preceding-sibling::*[contains(@class, ' topic/row ')][1]/*[contains(@class, ' topic/entry ')][$entryNum]">
 <xsl:call-template name="getTableRowsep"/>
 </xsl:for-each>
 </xsl:variable>
 <xsl:choose>
 <xsl:when test="$prevEntryRowsep != '0'">
 <xsl:sequence select="true()"/>
 </xsl:when>
 <xsl:otherwise>
 <xsl:sequence select="false()"/>
 </xsl:otherwise>
 </xsl:choose>
 </xsl:when>

title: DITA-OT Issue #3475: Row separator is applied incorrectly in pdf output with merged cells
content:
The variable "entryNum" does not take into account the possibility of merged entries in the row. The variable needTopBorderOnBreak determines whether an entry needs a top border based on the @rowsep value of the entry with the same position in the preceding row. But in this case, there is an entry that spans accross three columns. So the following entry ("No top border") has the position **2** but it should actually take the rowsep value of the entry with position **4** in the preceding row.

I propose to use the value of @dita-ot:x instead:
<xsl:when test="../parent::node()[contains(@class, ' topic/tbody ')]">
 <xsl:variable name="entryNum" select="@dita-ot:x" as="xs:integer"/>
 <xsl:variable name="prevEntryRowsep" as="xs:string?">
 <xsl:for-each select="../preceding-sibling::*[contains(@class, ' topic/row ')][1]/*[contains(@class, ' topic/entry ')][@dita-ot:x = $entryNum]">
 <xsl:call-template name="getTableRowsep"/>
 </xsl:for-each>
 </xsl:variable>
 <xsl:choose>
 <xsl:when test="$prevEntryRowsep != '0'">
 <xsl:sequence select="true()"/>
 </xsl:when>
 <xsl:otherwise>
 <xsl:sequence select="false()"/>
 </xsl:otherwise>
 </xsl:choose>
 </xsl:when>

title: DITA-OT Issue #3492: Improve CLI help for subcommands
content:
--install [<file>] install plug-in from a local ZIP file
 --install [<url>] install plug-in from a URL
 --install [<id>] install plug-in from plugin registry
 --install reload plug-ins
 --uninstall <id> uninstall plug-in with the ID
 --plugins print list of installed plug-ins
 --transtypes print list of installed transtypes
 --deliverables print list of deliverables in project
 -h, --help print this message
 --version print version information and exit
To help users understand the purpose of each subcommand, it would be good if a basic description could be presented alongside each subcommand in the `dita --help` output, and find a place to indicate that details are available for each via `dita <subcommand> --help`:
$ dita --help
Usage:
 dita -i <file> -f <name> [options]
 dita --project=<file> [options]
Subcommands:
 deliverables Print list of deliverables in project file
 install Install or reload plug-ins
 plugins Print list of installed plug-ins
 transtypes Print list of installed transformation types (output formats)
 uninstall Remove and delete plug-in
 version Print version information and exit

 See 'dita <subcommand> --help' for details about a specific subcommand.

content: Issue #3495 is closed with labels enhancement, i18n. Retrieval signals: error, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3495: Extract user-facing text to strings file(s)
content:
Currently, user-facing text in error messages, CLI help and parameter descriptions are embedded in various places in the Java code and elsewhere, which makes it difficult to find and review.
If these strings were extracted to dedicated .properties files (or another suitable format), it would make it much easier to review them all at once to ensure consistency and align the tone of messages that were created years apart by different authors.

_(This would also provide a foundation for localization, if that were ever considered for the CLI itself.)_

It would be ideal if all user-facing text could be consolidated in a single format, but given the extensible plug-in–based architecture, and variety of source code formats, I'm not sure that's practical.

As a first step, extracting strings from the core Java code would certainly be a significant improvement.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3533: Chunk="to-content" generates java.lang.NullPointerException error message
content:
In attached you find a bookmap with a chapter ditamap containing a couple of topics. All topics have unique @keys added in the topicref. Chunk="to-content" is added in the first topic of the DITAMAP.
Generate output with chunked="to-content" topics in webhelp.
When I publish this BOOKMAP, I get the following error message: Generates java.lang.NullPointerException

Keys attribute seems to cause this issue.
When I remove all keys, I can publish without problems.
<!-- Test case, Gist, set of files or steps required to reproduce the issue. -->

1. Create a BOOKMAP with a DITAMAP added as chapter and add key. 
It's importat you add a DITAMAP as chapter, not a topic. There is not bug when the chapter references to a DITA file.
2. In the DITAMAP, add a topic with a couple of child topics.
3. Add a key to all topics.
4. Add the attribute @chunk="to-content" to the first topic in the DITAMAP
5. Try to generate a OxygenXML webhelp or PDF

title: DITA-OT Issue #3536: Avoid parsing all key definition topics if only a couple of the keys are actually used
content:
I have a DITA sub-Map which defines about 10 keys using "keydef" and I have a parent DITA Map which has keyrefs only to 2 of those topics in its table of contents:
<map>
 <title>Test</title>
 <mapref href="keydefs.ditamap"/>
 <topicref keyref="topicKeyDef1"/>
 <topicref keyref="topicKeyDef2"/>
</map>
But the majority of the publishing stages will still process all those 10 topics although only two of them are actually referenced and appear in the published output.
This means that if I keep all my key definitions in a single map and I want to publish a map which has only a couple of key references, all the keys defined in the DITA Map will get processed and thus increase the publishing delay.

[profiling.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/4779652/profiling.zip)

title: DITA-OT Issue #3546: @keyref isn't resolved when contained in @conref
content:
Using DITA-OT versions 3.5 through 3.5.2, @keyrefs contained within @conrefs aren't resolved.

In the attached sample, there are two keys defined: a product name (product-name) and a web site (web-site). The myproduct.dita topic directly references the product-name key and conrefs a <ph> element which references the product-name key.

Similarly, the mysite.dita topic directly references the web-site key and conrefs a <ph> element which references the web-site key.
The file test.txt in the attached zip is how I run the dita command.

Examining the contents of the temp directory shows that the key references through the conref <ph> elements aren't being resolved, so this is definitely a preprocess bug.
