title: DITA-OT Issue #3565: Reltable: Keyref to Topic in Other Keyscope Resolves to Wrong Instance of Linked Topic
content:
I’ve got two submaps, both of which reference a unique concept and the topic _t_topic.dita_ with a key defined in a separate _keydefTopic.ditamap_. Both submaps also have a ditaval to filter the content of _t_topic.dita_. Both submaps have their own keyscope. The navigational topicref in each submap is also assigned a unique key, as in `<topicref keys="uniqueKey" keyref="previouslyDefinedKey"/>`. 
The unique key is then used in a reltable (in map one) to create links between the concept of map one and the specific instance of _t_topic.dita_ from map two. The topicref for the specific instance from map two uses the keyscope and the unique key, as in `<topicref keyref="map2.uniqueKey"/>`. 
I expect the concept from map one to be linked to the map two-instance of _t_topic.dita_ and vice versa.
DITA-OT 3.5.2: The concept from map one is linked to the map one-instance of _t_topic.dita_ instead of the expected instance from map two. I get no output from DITA-OT 3.4.1. 
I used [@jelovirt’s fix of mapreflmpl.xsl](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/hotfix/3.5.4/src/main/plugins/org.dita.base/xsl/preprocess/maprefImpl.xsl) for both DOT-versions.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3571: href="-dita-use-conref-target" is broken in PDF2 in 3.5.2
content: Issue #3571 is open with labels none. Retrieval signals: conref, xref, pdf, html, dita-ot, plugin, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3571: href="-dita-use-conref-target" is broken in PDF2 in 3.5.2
content:
In the PDF2 plugin, during preprocessing <xref href="-dita-use-conref-target" conref="..."/> should be replaced by the referenced element's href by the time the pipeline produces stage1.xml.
In the PDF2 plugin in 3.5.2, what you see in stage1.xml is still <xref href="-dita-use-conref-target"/>.
In the HTML5 plugin in 3.5.2, you **do** get the correct result.
Also in the PDF2 plugin in **3.0.4**, you **do** get the correct result.
I did a quick pass comparing preprocess/conrefImpl.xsl in 3.0.4 and 3.5.2, but I couldn't find anything obvious. I'm also not sure the problem is there, as I am not that familiar with all the targets in the PDF2 pipeline. So I don't really have a possible solution.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3576: relative path doesn't work for args.hdr, args.hdf specified in project XML file
content:
Project file allows you to specify paths relative to the project file, even for parameters that require absolute paths, such as:

 - args.cssroot
 - args.ftr
 - args.hdf
 - args.hdr

However, only the first (cssroot) works!
$ ls navbar.xml 
navbar.xml
$ dita --project website.xml
[DOTA008E][ERROR] Cannot find the running-header file "navbar.xml". Please double check the value to ensure it is specified correctly.
the document clearly stated that all of the hdr, hdf and cssroot accept relative path:
https://www.dita-ot.org/dev/topics/using-project-files.html

But in reality dita have no problem processing relative path specified for css and cssroot, only args.hdr, args.hdf has problems. So wherever the problem is, it might be found by observing the difference in handling hdr and css.

The other point to start researching this problem, is to find out why project file works in `docsrc/samples/project-files` works but not when the project file is written as I described and placed in the same directory as the ditamap

 /Users/..dita-ot/plugins/org.dita.base/build_preprocess.xml:194: java.lang.NullPointerException

title: DITA-OT Issue #3614: sectiondiv element should accept child title OR default XSL should transform sectiondiv/data/title
content:
<!-- If you're describing a bug, tell us what should happen. -->
When I author a sectiondiv, I expect to add a title for that. I should be able to add a title element, but this is not allowed. That title element should also be transformed by default XSL to an appropriate level heading in HTML output (for example)
<!-- Tell us what happens instead of the expected behavior. -->
- In sectiondiv, a title element is not allowed, but I can add a data/title element.
- In default XSL, sectiondiv/data/title is not processed to output.
<!-- Optional suggestions on how to fix the issue, or implement the changes. -->
<!-- If you know how to fix the issue, please create a pull request instead. -->
As a workaround, I use custom XSL to transform sectiondiv/data/title to output HTML heading based on the section/title template use:

title: DITA-OT Issue #3614: sectiondiv element should accept child title OR default XSL should transform sectiondiv/data/title
content:
<!-- Pass through to get sectiondiv title -->
 <xsl:template match="*[contains(@class, ' topic/data ')]" >
 <xsl:apply-templates/>
 </xsl:template>

 <xsl:template match="*[contains(@class, ' topic/sectiondiv ')]/*[contains(@class, ' topic/data ')]/*[contains(@class, ' topic/title ')]">
 <!-- Add 1 extra for parent section -->
 <xsl:param name="headLevel">
 <xsl:variable name="headCount" select="count(ancestor::*[contains(@class, ' topic/topic ')])+2"/>
 <xsl:choose>
 <xsl:when test="$headCount > 6">h6</xsl:when>
 <xsl:otherwise>h<xsl:value-of select="$headCount"/></xsl:otherwise>
 </xsl:choose>
 </xsl:param>
 <xsl:element name="{$headLevel}">
 <xsl:attribute name="class">sectiontitle</xsl:attribute>
 <xsl:call-template name="commonattributes">
 <xsl:with-param name="default-output-class" select="'sectiontitle'"/>
 </xsl:call-template>
 <xsl:apply-templates/>
 </xsl:element>
 </xsl:template>

content:
DITA-OT Issue #3633: Table border is partially missing after page break
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3633: Table border is partially missing after page break
content: Issue #3633 is open with labels enhancement, plugin/pdf, priority/medium. Retrieval signals: pdf, dita-ot, plugin, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3633: Table border is partially missing after page break
content:
The table border should be drawn correctly for all table cells.
The issue appears from the following code - https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/develop/src/main/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/xsl/fo/tables.xsl#L698-L711
Say we have 1 cell in the row on the previous page and 2 cells in the row on the following page. Then entryNum will be 2 for the second cell but it will not find the second cell in the previous row. Hence, prevEntryRowsep will be '0'.

Possible (not ideal) solution is to use `min(($entryNum, last()))` to pick the last cell if we cannot find the cell by number:
<xsl:variable name="prevEntryRowsep" as="xs:string?">
 <xsl:for-each select="../preceding-sibling::*[contains(@class, ' topic/row ')][1]/*[contains(@class, ' topic/entry ')][min(($entryNum, last()))]">
 <xsl:call-template name="getTableRowsep"/>
 </xsl:for-each>
</xsl:variable>
However, this code will work incorrectly if we have different column spanning in both rows and finding a cell by number might return the wrong cell. For example, if table contains more than 2 columns and in the first row columns are spanned in the beginning but in the second row columns are spanned in the end, we will need to actually take spanning into account to find the right cell. Quite tricky. The above code works for me though but probably does not fit into the public codebase.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3641: Add RELAX NG schemas to catalog
content:
DITA-OT Issue #3641: Add RELAX NG schemas to catalog
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3641: Add RELAX NG schemas to catalog
content: Issue #3641 is closed with labels enhancement. Retrieval signals: map, html, dita-ot, plugin, validation.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3641: Add RELAX NG schemas to catalog
content:
We currently ship 2 RELAX NG schemas that can be used to validate plug-ins and project files:

- `resources/project.rnc`
- `resources/plugin.rnc`

When these schemas are referenced in files with **relative** URIs as in our own docs [/samples/project-files/html.xml](https://github.com/dita-ot/docs/blob/develop/samples/project-files/html.xml#L2), validation may fail if these files are opened or maintained outside the toolkit directory _(as is common in many custom development projects)_.
In discussion with @raducoravu, he commented:

> if for example the `catalog-dita.xml` would have had an URI mapping
> for the `project.rnc` schema like:
>
> <uri name="http://www.dita-ot.project.com/project.rnc
> <http://www.dita-ot.project.com/project.rnc>"
> uri="../../resources/project.rnc"/>
>
> you could have used that absolute URI when referencing the
> `project.rnc` from your XML and Oxygen would have found the target
> by going through the XML catalog support.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3641: Add RELAX NG schemas to catalog
content:
> So the RNC file is located in `dita-ot/resources/project.rnc`.
>
> The `dita-ot/catalog-dita.xml` is deprecated and should not be modified further by adding an extra mapping in our case.
>
> The `dita-ot/plugins/org.dita.base/catalog-dita.xml` seems to be intended to map schemas or plugin IDs, XSLTs. Adding in it a reference to a folder 2 levels up 
> `../../resources/project.rnc` seems ugly to me.
>
> So I do not know where that catalog entry should be added, maybe an extra `catalog.xml` could be added to `dita-ot/resources` with some mappings for `plugin.rnc` and `project.rng`?

The catalog approach seems like the right way to handle this in a vendor-neutral way, as any XML editor with catalog support _(at least those aware of DITA-OT catalogs)_ would then be able to validate files based on these schemas regardless of file location.

The `project.rnc` file [declares a namespace](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/develop/src/main/resources/project.rnc#L1), so we might want to do something similar for the plugin schema:

 default namespace = "https://www.dita-ot.org/project"

@jelovirt @robander Any thoughts?

Currently (OTK 3.5) when I have this: When the referenced topic is not in the map and its title is "Topic not in map", the generated HTML looks like this: This paragraph has an xref to Topic not in map. This would be the same as `true` but additionally would not render xrefs as links when the topic is not in the map, but would still use the title when available. If there is no title available, throw a warning (or maybe even an error, though warning feels more right).

Exporting all DITA-OT jars as Maven artifact would help a lot in building Maven projets that are using DITA-OT for building their documentation by removing the dependencies on DITA jars with <scope>system</scope>. Publishing DITA-OT maven artifacts on Central should be linked to the distribution of a parent pom in the DITA-OT release folder

title: DITA-OT Issue #3661: Add schema caching when parsing RNG-based maps and topics
content:
If I have a DITA Map with 5 RNG-based topics referenced in it, the method `org.ditang.relaxng.defaults.RelaxNGDefaultsComponent.loadDefaults()` is called by the pre-processing stage 5 times and the RNG schemas are loaded 5 times. To avoid this we need to cache the loaded RNG defaults obtained for the `topic.rng`and re-use them.
I propose passing the XML grammar pool on the `RelaxNGDefaultsComponent` constructor and having a grammar pool implementation which can cache also RNG defaults.
We already have something like this in Oxygen and use it when running "Validate and check for completeness" on RNG-based map and topics.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3663: Changes to .job.xml file are sometimes not detected and handled
content:
I have a DITA-OT plugin that excludes `<draftintro>` topics (unless `args.draft==true`). This exclusion is performed before `mapref` processing by doing the following three things:

1. Delete `<draftintro>` elements from the map
2. Delete `*_draftintro*.dita` files from `$tempdir`
3. Delete `*_draftintro*.dita` file entries from `$tempdir/.job.xml`

The expectation is that this effectively removes the `<draftintro>` topics from the transformation.
Starting with the 3.5 release and continuing through 3.6, this fails roughly 20% of the time as follows:

content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3682: Allow a PDF deliverable to specify its output file name
content: Issue #3682 is closed with labels feature, priority/medium, project. Retrieval signals: map, pdf, html, dita-ot, transform, publishing.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3682: Allow a PDF deliverable to specify its output file name
content:
When a shared map is published to PDF in multiple profiling conditions, then each output PDF file must have a different name according to its condition.

`<deliverable>` elements allow the output _directory_ to be specified (great for HTML5!), but not the output _basename_ (needed for PDF).

As a result, the output PDF files derive their basename from the input map, resulting in duplicate PDF file names:

![3682_1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50950969/152381770-f437b3ca-a35e-45d0-ab87-7a29cdd2ac50.svg)

title: DITA-OT Issue #3682: Allow a PDF deliverable to specify its output file name
content:
One approach would be to support `<param>` directly inside `<deliverable>`:

![3682_2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50950969/152381808-1cf78e2a-5e49-4e6b-8079-9aa8f0d35def.svg)

If this is too philosophically different from what `<deliverable>` was intended to contain, another approach is to allow `<param>` inside an `idref`'ed `<publication>` inside the `<deliverable>`

![3682_3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50950969/152381817-818c49d1-b4fa-4a94-af33-0cb35c42d029.svg)

This second approach is very RelaxNG-like in its method of applying overrides to a refererence, which is quite nice!

Some workarounds (and their deficiencies) are:

* Uniquify the PDF `<publication>` definition.
 * In our case, we would need to uniquify our `<publication>` definitions by the hundreds, which is not ideal because then we must update _all_ of them whenever our PDF transformation changes.
* Rename the PDF files using a post-processing script.
 * Isn't the goal of DITA-OT project files to be able to replicate -- in a structured way -- what is normally performed on the `dita` command line (where the basename is normally specified), without the need for post-processing scripts?
 * If all PDFs go in the same directory, then they collide with themselves during full publication before such a script could run.
* Place the PDF files in different output directories.
 * This avoids file collisions, but it does not solve the duplicate file name issue (which would confuse our customers).

title: DITA-OT Issue #3682: Allow a PDF deliverable to specify its output file name
content: To reproduce, you can try using the following project file (copied to `<DITA-OT>/docsrc/samples/project-files/pdf-test.xml`, perhaps):

title: DITA-OT Issue #3682: Allow a PDF deliverable to specify its output file name
content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<?xml-model href="https://www.dita-ot.org/rng/project.rnc" type="application/relax-ng-compact-syntax"?>
<project xmlns="https://www.dita-ot.org/project">

 <!-- single map to be published in two flavors -->
 <context id="context-ug1" name="User Guide 1">
 <input href="../../userguide-book.ditamap"/>
 <!-- pretend we have DITAVAL 1 applied here -->
 </context>

 <context id="context-ug2" name="User Guide 2">
 <input href="../../userguide-book.ditamap"/>
 <!-- pretend we have DITAVAL 2 applied here -->
 </context>

 <!-- single shared publication definition -->
 <publication id="pub-pdf2" transtype="pdf2">
 <param name="args.chapter.layout" value="BASIC"/>
 <param name="args.gen.task.lbl" value="YES"/>
 <param name="include.rellinks" value="friend"/>
 <param name="processing-mode" value="strict"/>
 </publication>

 <!-- publish book flavors with two different output base names -->
 <deliverable id="del-pdf-ug1">
 <context idref="context-ug1"/>
 <output href="."/>
 <publication idref="pub-pdf2">
 <param name="outputFile.base" value="userguide1"/>
 </publication>
 </deliverable>

 <deliverable id="del-pdf-ug2">
 <context idref="context-ug2"/>
 <output href="."/>
 <publication idref="pub-pdf2">
 <param name="outputFile.base" value="userguide2"/>
 </publication>
 </deliverable>

</project>

I have two books, bookA and bookB. bookA references bookB as a `@scope=peer` map:

In a topic in bookA, I would like to reference a "Product" variable from bookB:

This enhancement requests that keyscoped `@scope="peer"` maps pull their keys (but not topics) from the referenced map into the current map.

To test this, unarchive the following testcase:

[ditaot_keys_from_peer_books.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/5852619/ditaot_keys_from_peer_books.zip)

then run

title: DITA-OT Issue #3685: Allow variables to be referenced from @scope="peer" maps
content:
I tried implementing a proof-of-concept solution, which you can see in the testcase directory as follows:

`diff maprefImpl.xsl.ORIG maprefImpl.xsl.NEW`

The attempt was to remember when we're in a `@scope="peer-with-keys"` context, that would keep all `mapref` contents *except* topic references. Unfortunately, even this naive attempt did not work - the variables still did not resolve, and bookB topics still showed up in the bookA output directory. (You will need to change `@scope="peer"` to `@scope="peer-with-keys"` to try this proof-of-concept on the provided testcase.)
I am aware of warehouse topics, shared key definition files, etc. However, those are not a good fit for this need. This enhancement is for the case where we're *already referencing a peer book* and that book *already defines the variables we want* (for its own use), and we simply want to access them as well.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3690: In DITA-OT project files, apply both <context> and <publication> DITAVAL filtering

DITA-OT Issue #3690: In DITA-OT project files, apply both <context> and <publication> DITAVAL filtering
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3690: In DITA-OT project files, apply both <context> and <publication> DITAVAL filtering
content:
(This is a more educated follow-up to #3474.)

For DITA-OT project files, if a `<context>` applies a DITAVAL and a `<publication>` applies a DITAVAL, then a `<deliverable>` using both of them should apply both DITAVAL files:

![3690_1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50950969/152367300-f7a0d755-6414-437b-833f-1df573cd0998.svg)
Both `<context>` and `<publication>` DITAVAL files should be applied. The need for this is demonstrated by replacing the `<context>` and `<publication>` definitions above with their respective DITAVAL files:

![3690_2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50950969/152367787-dcdedff1-f64d-4ea1-81c7-b71360b959c9.svg)

In this example, the `<context>` DITAVAL is filtering on `@product`, while the `<publication>` DITAVAL is filtering on `@audience` (and applying `@rev` highlighting). These filtering aspects are orthogonal.
In the attached testcase:

[dita_project_file.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/5920276/dita_project_file.zip)

run the following command:

`dita --project=books.xml --deliverable="del-pdf-review-prodA_ug" --verbose`

then note in the output log that the publication `flag_review.ditaval` DITAVAL is not applied.

The image hrefs in the XSL-FO should always point to the correct files (same as in original DITA files). It works fine for images in DITA topics but not in DITAMAP. This is reproducible in DITA-OT 3.x (checked with 3.0-3.6). In 3.0 there is an NullPointerException, in 3.1+ the image is simply not rendered in PDF. The same DITA worked fine in DITA-OT 2.5.4.
<xsl:variable name="main-visual" select="/*/opentopic:map/*[contains(@class, ' map/topicmeta ')]/*[contains(@class, ' topic/data ') and @name = 'main-visual']/image/@href"/>
<fo:block>
 <fo:external-graphic max-width="30mm"
 src="url({if (opentopic-func:isAbsolute($main-visual)) then $main-visual else concat($input.dir.url, $main-visual)})"/>
</fo:block>

It seems to be somehow related to the following ticket - https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2828 As far as I understood, it was intentionally implemented in DITA-OT 3.x to not allow image hrefs in ditamaps. The motivation is not clear to me. I could not find how to properly fix it.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3711: Map-level conkeyref-push of a topic does not work
content:
According to the DITA spec at

https://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3/os/part2-tech-content/archSpec/base/conref-overview.html

a conref/conkeyref can target:

- A referenced element within a DITA map
- A referenced element within a DITA topic
- **An entire DITA map**
- **An entire DITA topic**

Thus, I expect that this mechanism would work on an entire topic within a map:
<!-- attempt to replace topic 2 by topic key -->
<topicref href="topic_2_replacement.dita" processing-role="resource-only" conaction="pushreplace" conkeyref="topic_2"/>
<topicref href="topic_2.dita" keys="topic_2"/>
The DITA-OT issues the following error:
`[conref-push] [DOTJ041E][ERROR] The attribute conref="topic_2.dita" uses invalid syntax. The value should contain '#' followed by a topic or map ID, optionally followed by '/elemID' for a sub-topic element.`
`dita -i map.ditamap -f html5`

title: DITA-OT Issue #3713: Make it possible to add Saxon features in pipeline + XSLT task
content:
DITA-OT Issue #3713: Make it possible to add Saxon features in pipeline + XSLT task
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3713: Make it possible to add Saxon features in pipeline + XSLT task
content:
Recent DITA-OT customization after `preprocess` forces developers to use XSLT + pipeline elements because many of the files that DITA-OT generated in temporary folder or properties are now obsolete. 

[https://www.dita-ot.org/dev/topics/plugin-coding-conventions.html](https://www.dita-ot.org/dev/topics/plugin-coding-conventions.html)

> Use custom <pipeline> elements
> In Ant scripts, use the XSLT module from DITA-OT instead of Ant’s built-in <xslt> or <style> tasks.
> 
> The XSLT module allows access to DITA-OT features like using the job configuration to select files in the temporary folder based on file metadata and custom XSLT extension functions.
> 

 <pipeline>
 <xslt style="${dita.plugin.example.dir}/custom.xsl"
 destdir="${dita.output.dir}">
 <ditafileset format="dita" />
 </xslt>
 </pipeline>

However this element combination does not allow to add Saxon feature settings via `factory` element inside `xslt` element.

 <factory name="net.sf.saxon.TransformerFactoryImpl">
 <attribute name="http://saxon.sf.net/feature/timing" value="true"/>
 <attribute name="http://saxon.sf.net/feature/suppressXsltNamespaceCheck" value="true"/>
 <attribute name="http://saxon.sf.net/feature/enableAssertions" value="true"/>
 <attribute name="http://saxon.sf.net/feature/traceListenerClass" value="net.sf.saxon.trace.XSLTTraceListener"/>
 </factory>

Using Saxon feature setting is very important to debug XSLT stylesheets for stylesheet developers. 
As a result I want to submit a request to allow `factory` element in `xslt` element.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3713: Make it possible to add Saxon features in pipeline + XSLT task
content:
None! As described above, using raw `xslt` task is not possible due to DITA-OT generated files in temporary folder or properties that exist in older version are now removed.

[https://www.dita-ot.org/3.5/topics/migrating-to-3.5.html](https://www.dita-ot.org/3.5/topics/migrating-to-3.5.html)

> 9.2. Legacy constructs removed
> DITA-OT 3.5 no longer includes the following legacy properties, list files, and targets, which were deprecated in previous releases. These constructs were no longer used in recent releases, and have now been removed entirely.
>

title: DITA-OT Issue #3729: Incremental publishing to decrease processing time
content:
DITA-OT Issue #3729: Incremental publishing to decrease processing time
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3729: Incremental publishing to decrease processing time
content: Issue #3729 is open with labels feature. Retrieval signals: conref, keyref, map, pdf, html, publishing.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3729: Incremental publishing to decrease processing time
content:
A place holder for ideas about how subsequent publishing DITA content could be instrumented to take less time than the first publishing.
Feedback from John Kirkiris on the DITA OT Slack Channel:

> The subject of incremental builds came up again with some of our writing groups that product large deliverables with about 40K topics in all. Given DITA's reuse features, there can easily be both direct and indirect dependencies all over the place. I'm assuming that to even begin to answer the question of what's the minimum that needs to be re-rendered compared to a prior build, a dependency graph of some type would be necessary. To answer the question, "does this topic or map need to be re-rendered?", the pipeline would need to analyze the dependencies.
>
>It's entirely possible that the time it would take to perform such an analysis could take as much time as just rendering the entire docset, but that only works for relatively small collections. As OT is traversing its way across a docset's web of intrigue during a build, could it build such a list, even it was just a set of tuples indicating that a dependency exists and perhaps the nature of the dependency, conref, keyref, internal link, external link, etc.? It would need to consider changes to other resources like a referenced image or anything else.
>
>Oxygen can show incoming and outgoing references from the currently selected file on a micro scale. I'm asking what's the best way to do this in a CI/CD pipeline. Has anyone else tried to do this or something similar to optimize builds? It would be a code-optimizer, but for DITA. We used to have build optimizers decades ago, so prior art exists. I'm just curious if anyone has done so for DITA. Perhaps it's sitting under my nose.

Answer from @raducoravu :

> Looking at how fast we process topics for the Oxygen validate and check for completeness (about 100 a second with DTD caching) going once through the entire 40k topics project to create some kind of dependency graph might take about 6 minutes. So this would probably be worth it comparing 6 minutes to the entire amount of time it takes to re-publish 40 k topics which probably takes close to an hour to publish.
>
>We looked into this once but encountered various problems. For example:
When the title of a topic changes, all topics which link to it must be processed again. But the table of contents also contains the topic titles so that would need again to be re-published. For our WebHelp output we keep inside each HTML topic a small simplified TOC with its siblings and parent topics. So the sibling topics would need to be published as well.
In reality we will not really know what changed inside a topic, we will just know that it has changed since the last time it was processed.
>
>So any topic which has a link to the modified topic should be processed. And any topic which has a conref to it would need to be processed as well, same for topics which have indirect conrefs to it. The table of contents would need to be re-processed and in our case (WebHelp) also would sibling topics.
>
>But you cannot send the DITA OT incomplete content to publish, so this would need to be built into the DITA OT, maybe allow the DITA OT to perform the pre-processing and filtering stages as it does right now, on the entire project and then look to see what pre-processed topics changed so that we would create new HTML files only for them.
>
>Of course this would not work for outputs like PDF which rely on creating a single large XML document from the DITA Map which is processed to PDF.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3733: Key reference in content referenced content not properly expanded when using key scopes
content:
I'm attaching a sample project file, the main DITA Map is "hzm1617899793683.ditamap" and it can be published to PDF:
[keyscope-conkeyref-keyword-fail-1.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/6355677/keyscope-conkeyref-keyword-fail-1.zip)

There is a topic named "xge1617899981044.xml" referenced as resource-only in multiple key scope contexts.
Paragraphs from this topic are reused in other topics via conkeyref, for example in "jxk1617900527138.xml".

Key references are expanded by the DITA OT before content references. The "org.dita.dost.module.KeyrefModule.processTopic(FileInfo, KeyScope, boolean)" method considers that it should not create unique files for each reference to the "xge1617899981044.xml" topic because it is resource-only:

 final int increment = isResourceOnly ? 0 : 1;

In my opinion the condition should be something like:

 final int increment = isResourceOnly && ! ditaFormat ? 0 : 1;

During the [debug-filter] pre-processing, we found that all file path names are renamed with an error message.

> [DOTJ083E][ERROR] The resource referenced as file:/d:/P1/re/276570932/b/projects/en/sample_project/trans_picts/play_mode/play_mode_midi_instance.png is capitalized differently on disk, using file:/**D**:/P1/re/276570932/b/projects/en/sample_project/trans_picts/play_mode/play_mode_midi_instance.png.

This only happens on our Windows integration server with a standard Windows installation when our custom Ant build script is run. The developer who is responsible for this server has also tested on his own Windows client and had the same issue. 
It does not happen on my client and also not on my team member's client. We both use Windows installations.

When this pre-processing step is done, in the [map-ref] pre-processing step, all maps that contain submaps show another error, which, we hope, is based on the capitalization issue.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3740: Change CLI default logging level
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3740: Change CLI default logging level
content:
Change `dita` command (CLI) default logging level from _warning_ to _info_ and add option `-q, --quiet` to enable _warning_ level logging.
To retain previous behaviour, add configuration option to choose which logging level should be treated as default.
The traditional UNIX command line convention has been to not print anything to standard out if there are not errors. DITA-OT CLI logging levels have been:

| logging option | Ant logging levels |
|---|---|
| _default_ | warning + error|
| `-v` | info + warning + error|
| `-d` | verbose +info + warning + error||

Given that most of our users are likely not tranditional UNIX command line users and we should prioritize clarity, a more user friendly logging levels would be:

| logging option | Ant logging level |
|---|---|
| `-q` | warning + error| |
| _default_ | info + warning + error| |
| `-v`, `-d` | verbose + info + warning + error||

Ant has a very low level logging level _debug_, but we should not enable that in CLI output because it's intended and used only by Ant for debugging and behaviour. Thus, `-v` and `-d` should become synonyms.

Current DITA-OT documentation refers about <ditafileset> features and it is described in the following URL:
https://www.dita-ot.org/dev/topics/plugin-coding-conventions.html#ariaid-title1

Add `<ditafileset format="ditamap-main"/>` to select the main ditamap file.
This is only my idea. This should be discussed in DITA-OT developers.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3750: Reconsider how force-unique works with references to separate topics inside the same file
content:
I'm attaching a DITA Map which references a glossary.ditamap with the following content:

 <map>
 <glossref href="concepts/glossary.dita#flowers.genus" print="yes" keys="genus"/>
 <glossref href="concepts/glossary.dita#flowers.pollination" print="yes" keys="pollination"/>
 ....
 </map>

so we have multiple references to multiple glossentry elements located in the same file.
If I publish to PDF setting the "force-unique=true" parameter the PDF output will contain the glossary entries multiplied a number if times because the ForceUniqueFilter adds copy-to attributes to each reference.

I think the ForceUniqueFilter should not consider that references like "glossary.dita#flowers.genus" or "glossary.dita#flowers.pollination" are identical and thus avoid setting extra copy-to attributes on them.

[force-unique-flowers.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/6458775/force-unique-flowers.zip)

title: DITA-OT Issue #3755: Cannot run integrator on Windows and then use the DITA-OT on Linux
content:
Let's say I have a DITA-OT folder on Windows and run the DITA-OT integrator in it, it re-generates various resources among which the `config/org.dita.dost.platform/plugin.properties`. All references in the re-generated resources contain Windows-style `\` separators.
Then I take the entire DITA-OT, copy it on a Linux or Mac machine and try to use it to publish a small DITA Map, it will not work, I get an error that the public ID of the DITA Map cannot be mapped through the XML catalogs.
I need to run the DITA-OT integrator again on Linux to make the DITA-OT work again.

In my opinion all resources generated by the DITA-OT integrator process should use `/` style path separators which work both on Windows and on Linux/Mac.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3767: Keyscope processing issue when set on *ref element (mapref or topicref)

content: Issue #3795 is open with labels bug, preprocess/keyref, priority/medium. Retrieval signals: map, html, dita-ot, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3795: Variable references inside <navtitle> do not resolve inside a multiple-value @keyscope region
content:
If the current `@keyscope` region has multiple values (1) and a variable is defined (2), that variable should resolve both in a `<navtitle>` element (3) as well in topic content (4).

![multiple_value_keyscope](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50950969/130520837-5650c03c-600c-493b-8ef2-873b1c484945.png)
The variable does not resolve in the `<navtitle>` element (3). The HTML output is as follows:
Map Title
- Navigation Title for ""
 - Topic Title for "My Product"
This issue occurs when there are multiple space-separated values in `@keyscope`, whether they are the same value (`"top top"` or `"local local"`) or different (`"top local"`).

This testcase might seem improbable, but it is reduced for simplicity. In our production environment, a top-level `<mapref>` with a top-level scope instantiates a submap's `<map>` with its own local scope. The `@keyscope` values are concatenated during `mapref` preprocessing per ["2.3.4.2 Key scopes"](http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3/errata02/os/complete/part3-all-inclusive/archSpec/base/keyScopes.html), thus triggering this bug and causing a product variable to fail evaluation in a `<navtitle>` within the submap.
Command: `dita -i map.ditamp -f html5`

[TestTMElement.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/7119290/TestTMElement.zip) Feedback from one of our end users: > Recently we bumped into this issue in DITA-OT 3.6.1 where the tm superscript is not printed when there is a repeated value use for trademark attribute and element data. No vulnerabilities should be present in DITA-OT.
Copy of the error message, log file or stack trace
The logback-core package is vulnerable to XML eXternal Entity (XXE) attacks. The buildSaxParser() method in the SaxEventRecorder class processes malicious external entities by default due to an unsafe XML parser configuration. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by supplying XML data with a Document Type Definition (DTD) that contains malicious external entity references. These references may be leveraged by the attacker to exfiltrate sensitive information, cause a Denial of Service (DoS) condition, or to perform other XXE related attacks.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3815: A <mapref> with a @keys attribute is processed incorrectly
content:
DITA-OT Issue #3815: A <mapref> with a @keys attribute is processed incorrectly
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3815: A <mapref> with a @keys attribute is processed incorrectly
content: Issue #3815 is open with labels bug. Retrieval signals: error, keyref, map, pdf, dita-ot, transform, publishing.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3815: A <mapref> with a @keys attribute is processed incorrectly
content:
If `<mapref>` elements have the `@keys` attribute defined:

![3815_1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50950969/155891353-86719e9f-f6cf-454f-9514-2b6d93581a27.svg)

then publishing should yield the same results as if `@keys` was not defined.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3815: A <mapref> with a @keys attribute is processed incorrectly
content:
The content is published incorrectly in the `preprocess2` pipeline, as described below. (`preprocess` is also affected when `force-unique` is used - see comments below this description.)

During the `mapref` preprocessing stage, the presence of the `@keys` attribute causes a `<keydef>` element to be created in addition to a `<submap>` element for the referenced map contents:

![3815_2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50950969/155891359-27ca8176-1903-40c4-b7c9-0cbb979fbc65.svg)

During the `branch-filter` preprocessing stage, the profiled "Product" key values are correctly pruned to reflect the `<ditavalref>`:

![3815_3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50950969/155891367-9a422db7-0a5e-4a82-82c5-22e662fae6d2.svg)

During the `keyref` preprocessing stage, the `<keydef>` element is **incorrectly processed to insert a redundant (and unfiltered) `<submap>`** of "Product" values:

![3815_4](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50950969/155891374-c37dba78-04bb-4c51-a152-a01f05079d45.svg)

When `preprocess2` is used, because topics are processed after maps, the unfiltered "Product" key values are incorrectly used to resolve the key reference in the topic file, causing the `***ERROR***` value to be used in the output.

(Note that an extra `preprocessing-only` topic reference to preface.dita is also created, but it does not affect output in this testcase.)

title: DITA-OT Issue #3815: A <mapref> with a @keys attribute is processed incorrectly
content:
Somehow the second insertion of the `<submap>` (due to the `<keydef>`) must be prevented. I don't know enough about the `keyref` stage to know what element structures should/should not be created.
1. Unarchive the following testcase: [ditaot_mapref_keys_bug.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/8149031/ditaot_mapref_keys_bug.zip) 2. Run the `pdf2` transformation: `dita -i map.ditamap -f pdf2`

title: DITA-OT Issue #3826: Remove support for Customization directory in PDF2
content:
Remove support for [`Customization` directory and `custom.xsl` files referenced with `cfg` URI scheme](https://www.dita-ot.org/dev/topics/pdf-plugin-structure.html) in PDF2.
The legacy extensibility API to PDF2 adds overhead and makes PDF2 more complex with limited benefits. By removing the legacy extensibility we can simplify PDF2 configuration code and offer users a one way to customization.
With legacy extensibility removed, we should offer a migration guide from `Customization` directory to plug-in based extensibility.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3827: Replace attribute reflection in PDF2
content:
Remove [attribute reflection](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/develop/src/main/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/xsl/common/attr-set-reflection.xsl#L319) and replace it with utility function that extracts attributes generated from attribute sets. This is related to #3826 because attribute reflection has support for the legacy customization `cfg` URIs.
<xsl:template name="get-attributes" as="attribute()*">
 <xsl:param name="element" as="element()"/>
 <xsl:sequence select="$element/@*"/>
</xsl:template>
<xsl:call-template name="get-attributes">
 <xsl:with-param name="element" as="element()">
 <dummy xsl:use-attribute-sets="topic.topic.topic.title"/>
 </xsl:with-param>
</xsl:template>
<xsl:variable name="element" as="element()">
 <dummy xsl:use-attribute-sets="topic.topic.topic.title"/>
</xsl:variable>
<xsl:apply-templates select="$element" mode="get-attributes"/>

title: DITA-OT Issue #3845: Need better design for "skip" properties
content:
DITA-OT Issue #3845: Need better design for "skip" properties
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3845: Need better design for "skip" properties
content: Issue #3845 is closed with labels enhancement, preprocess, priority/medium. Retrieval signals: conref, keyref, map, html, dita-ot, plugin.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3845: Need better design for "skip" properties
content:
Many of our Ant targets in the preprocess code have "skip" properties that allow you to skip running part of our build pipeline. These are considered internal properties and subject to change, but available to advanced users who understand the code. There are several problems:

* They are not documented, even for advanced users (this has come up in Slack a few times).
* The naming is inconsistent, with most based on Ant target names rather than on function. You can disable the code that cascades map metadata, but you have to know the Ant target is `move-meta-entries` making the property name `preprocess.move-meta-entries.skip`. Some do not use the Ant target name, such as `preprocess.clean-map-check.skip`. Where preprocess and preprocess2 have overlapping targets, preprocess2 uses the name from preprocess; where they do not, it creates a property with the Ant target name. An odd one is `clean-temp.skip` which is outside of preprocess.
* Property names based on Ant target name makes it hard to split or combine steps
* You have to set the property to disable something, which is not intuitive; setting `preprocess.keyref.skip=true` disables keyref resolution.
* Because of how Ant works, setting the variable to *anything* disables the target, it just checks if the property is set. So, setting `preprocess.keyref.skip=false` also disables keyref. This is likely familiar to people with a lot of Ant experience, but many of those trying to tweak DITA-OT builds do not have that background.

List of current skip properties in base plugin:

- `clean-temp.skip`
- `preprocess.branch-filter.skip`
- `preprocess.chunk.skip`
- `preprocess.clean-map-check.skip`
- `preprocess.clean-preprocess.skip`
- `preprocess.coderef.skip`
- `preprocess.conref.skip`
- `preprocess.conrefpush.skip`
- `preprocess.copy-files.skip`
- `preprocess.copy-flag.skip`
- `preprocess.copy-html.skip`
- `preprocess.copy-image.skip`
- `preprocess.debug-filter.skip`
- `preprocess.gen-list.skip`
- `preprocess.keyref.skip`
- `preprocess.map-profile.skip`
- `preprocess.maplink.skip`
- `preprocess.mapref.skip`
- `preprocess.move-meta-entries.skip`
- `preprocess.normalize-codeblock.skip`
- `preprocess.profile.skip`
- `preprocess.topic-profile.skip`
- `preprocess.topicpull.skip`

Note that not all are used in `target/@unless`. Some are used e.g.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3845: Need better design for "skip" properties
content:
Ideally, in a 4.0 major release we could:
* Create a consistent pattern for all of the current "skip" properties.
* The property names should be based entirely on function, not connected to the Ant target, so that even if we split a single `chunk` target into 5 targets, the "process chunking" property does not change and works to disable all 5.
* The property be set to "false" to disable a step. Ant has `istrue` condition that maps case-insensitive "true", "yes", and "on" to `true`; otherwise `false`.
* The actual Ant property used to skip a target is internal-only, and our build should fail if someone tries to set it; going forward this ensures we do not break anyone if those properties have to change
* All of this makes it possible to document the properties in a straightforward manner - "Set X to false to disable conref resolution" - without going into detail about why it's "enable this property to disable this feature", or why "disable this property" also disables it, etc.

I'm not sure of the best pattern for these or I'd have started with a PR that updated one step. Adding some ideas, using conref as an example; I like having `run` or `buildstep` or `build-step` in there, but am not attached to anything. I do like having the feature name last so all of these have the same prefix:
* `run.conref.step=true`
* `run.step.conref=true`
* `run.buildstep.conref=true`
* `build-step.conref=true`

title: DITA-OT Issue #3845: Need better design for "skip" properties
content:
We could simply document the properties that exist today, but we've intentionally avoided this:
* It locks in the properties like an external API, making them hard to change
* The issues above all make it hard to document, requiring an explanation of Ant and of the "enable to disable" naming
This has come up twice in Slack over the last few months, both times about the `preprocess.clean-map-check.skip` property as a way to skip that step and retain information added by preprocessing.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3848: related-links scope is not cascaded

The example source for the related-links element should build without errors
`scope="external"` from the `<related-links>` element is not cascaded to child `<link>` elements, causing issues in gen-list / topic-reader steps. Adding `scope="external"` to each `<link>` element solves the issue, but isn't required by the specification.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3861: PDF2 i18n-postprocess extension point not working
content:
A DITA-OT plugin wing XSL for the `i18n-postprocess` extension point should be able to override default XSLT in `plugin:org.dita.pdf2:xsl/fo/i18n-postprocess.xsl`.
Overrides do not happen because `plugin:org.dita.pdf2:xsl/fo/i18n-postprocess_template.xsl` includes both the extension point and the XSLT templates that might be overridden.
1. Create and integrate a plugin with the `i18n-postprocess` extension point.
2. Observe that the templates in `plugin:org.dita.pdf2:xsl/fo/i18n-postprocess.xsl` override those in the imported XSL.

Motivation for using this extension point is to enable a plugin to point to a font mapping file using another mechanism than the old customization directory.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3867: Child navigation links to nested topics are incorrect/missing if there is a <ph keyref/>
content:
When all of the following are true:

- A topic file that has nested subtopics in the same file.
- This topic file is included in two different submaps (content reuse).
- Both submaps are included (in different keyscopes) in the same top-level map.
- The topic file contains a `<ph keyref="..."/>` reference.

then if I run the `html5` transformation, the child navigation links for the second submap's topic instance are missing, which causes all child links to point to the top-level topic instead of the nested topics:

- Feature Topic
 - Concepts
 - Configuration
 - Option 1
 - Option 2
 - Limitations
- Feature Topic
 - Feature Topic (incorrect)
 - Feature Topic (incorrect)
 - Feature Topic (incorrect)
 - Feature Topic (incorrect)
 - Feature Topic (incorrect)

If I run the `pdf2` transformation instead of the `html5` transformation (which uses `preprocess2` instead of `preprocess`), then I get an even weirder result of recursively nested links that are a mix of correct and incorrect links.
Child links should resolve correctly, whether there is a `<ph keyref="..."/>` or not.

If the `<ph keyref="..."/>` element is deleted, then the child navigation links are gathered correctly:

- Feature Topic
 - Concepts
 - Configuration
 - Option 1
 - Option 2
 - Limitations
- Feature Topic

title: DITA-OT Issue #3870: Curly quotes in files produce misleading ANT topic-fragment log messages
content:
Curly quotes (and possibly other characters) are supported in files referenced by `coderef` and no topic-fragment errors are present in the log.
When building the DITA-OT docs using the [site transform](https://github.com/dita-ot/website/blob/master/README.md#building-documentation-output), I get the following errors when building on Windows using the command line.
[ant:topic-fragment] Failed to process include D:\dita-ot\dita-ot-docs\resources\dita-ot-doc.css
[ant:topic-fragment] Failed to process include D:\dita-ot\dita-ot-docs\resources\dita-ot-doc.css
The `dita-ot-doc.css` includes curly quotes (lines [1014](https://github.com/dita-ot/docs/blob/develop/resources/dita-ot-doc.css#L1014) and [1019](https://github.com/dita-ot/docs/blob/develop/resources/dita-ot-doc.css#L1019))
These are parsed without error on Mac (and presumably Linux), but not on Windows.
Change the curly quotes to straight quotes and the errors are no longer present. The [glossary](https://www.dita-ot.org/dev/reference/glossary.html#gloss-dita-open-toolkit) is one place where curly quotes are used in the DITA-OT docs.
Build the `site` output of the DITA-OT docs on Windows.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3873: args.filter does not support multiple relative paths in DITA-OT project file
content:
Per [the documentation](https://www.dita-ot.org/3.7/topics/using-project-files.html), DITA-OT project files promise to convert relative paths to absolute paths when `path="..."` is used:

> Use `path` for parameters that require an absolute value, like `args.cssroot`. Paths may be defined relative to the project file, but are always expanded to an absolute system path.

If I specify multiple relative paths for `args.filter` in a DITA-OT project file:
<publication transtype="html5">
 <!-- this does not work -->
 <param name="args.filter" path="flag_final.ditaval:filter_B.ditaval"/>
</publication>
then all paths in the list should be resolved to absolute paths.
Only the first path is resolved to a full path, leaving the second path to fail as follows:
$ dita --project project.xml
[ditaval-merge] [DOTJ071E][ERROR] Cannot find the specified DITAVAL 'file:/home/chrispy/dita-ot/filter_B.ditaval'.
<publication transtype="html5">
 <!-- this works, but it is not portable across compute environments -->
 <!-- (as evidenced by the fact that you'll have to modify this to run it yourself -->
 <param name="args.filter" path="/mnt/c/nobackup/project_file_experiments/ditaval/flag_final.ditaval:/mnt/c/nobackup/project_file_experiments/ditaval/filter_B.ditaval"/>
</publication>

title: DITA-OT Issue #3875: Branch filtering does not handle nested subtopics properly
content:
If I have nested subtopics, and the same topic is used in two different DITAVAL contexts:
<topicgroup keyscope="A">
 <ditavalref href="filter_A.ditaval"/>
 <topicref href="topic.dita"> <!-- reused topic -->
 <topicref href="topic.dita#subtopic1_id"/>
 <topicref href="topic.dita#subtopic2_id"/>
 <topicref href="topic.dita#subtopic3_id"/>
 </topicref>
 </topicgroup>

 <topicgroup keyscope="B">
 <ditavalref href="filter_B.ditaval"/>
 <topicref href="topic.dita"> <!-- reused topic -->
 <topicref href="topic.dita#subtopic1_id"/>
 <topicref href="topic.dita#subtopic2_id"/>
 <topicref href="topic.dita#subtopic3_id"/>
 </topicref>
 </topicgroup>
then branch filtering should uniquify the topic and its nested subtopics properly.
After the `branch-filter` preprocessing stage, the map looks like this:

title: DITA-OT Issue #3875: Branch filtering does not handle nested subtopics properly
content:
<topicgroup keyscope="A">
 <topicref href="topic.dita">
 <topicref href="topic.dita#subtopic1_id"/>
 <topicref href="topic.dita#subtopic2_id"/>
 <topicref href="topic.dita#subtopic3_id"/>
 </topicref>
 <ditavalref href="filter_A.ditaval"/>
 </topicgroup>

 <topicgroup keyscope="B">
 <topicref href="topic-1.dita">
 <topicref href="topic.dita#subtopic1_id" filter-copy-to="topic-1.dita#subtopic1_id"/>
 <topicref href="topic.dita#subtopic2_id" filter-copy-to="topic-1.dita#subtopic2_id"/>
 <topicref href="topic.dita#subtopic3_id" filter-copy-to="topic-1.dita#subtopic3_id"/>
 </topicref>
 <ditavalref href="filter_B.ditaval"/>
 </topicgroup>
(I used the `ditaot_save_preprocessing.pl` script from [here](https://github.com/chrispy-snps/DITA-ditaot-utilities) to easily obtain the preprocessing results.)

In the "B" branch, note that the top-level topic is correctly uniquified to `@href="topic-1.dita"`, but the nested subtopics are left in an unfinished state with the original `@href` and lingering `@filter-copy-to` attributes that were never used.

Because of this, the child navigation links in the final HTML output are incorrect:

* Topic in A
 * Subtopic 1 in A
 * Subtopic 2 in A
 * Subtopic 3 in A
* Topic in B <-- correct
 * Subtopic 1 in A <-- incorrect, should be B
 * Subtopic 2 in A <-- incorrect, should be B
 * Subtopic 3 in A <-- incorrect, should be B

title: DITA-OT Issue #3875: Branch filtering does not handle nested subtopics properly
content:
The `@filter-copy-to` on the nested subtopics should also be applied.

I think this might be follow-up work to #3680 (Transformation fails with "URI has a fragment component" when calling a `<mapref>` with a `<ditavalref>`).

title: DITA-OT Issue #3896: Further support for DITA 2.0 specializations attribute
content:
Continuation of #3440
Look in all the XSLTs where the @domains attribute is still used.

I created a small sample in which I manually added the @specializations attribute on the root of a topic:
[flowers.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/8183243/flowers.zip)

For example here: "plugins/org.dita.normalize/xsl/normalize.xsl" there is a template which should match also the new attribute:

 <xsl:template match="@class | @domains | @xtrf | @xtrc | @ditaarch:DITAArchVersion"
 priority="10"/>

so that the normalized content is valid.

There are also a couple of places where the @domains attribute is used for flagging like "plugins/org.dita.html5/xsl/topic.xsl"

 <xsl:when test="exists($passthrough-attrs[empty(@att) and empty(@value)])">
 <xsl:variable name="specializations" as="xs:string*">
 <xsl:for-each select="ancestor-or-self::*[@domains][1]/@domains">
 .........

From what I understood from @jelovirt the Java pre-processing code should automatically create a @domains attribute on the topic root element from the original @specializations attribute. This indeed seems to work, so for an original topic content like this:

 <topic id="t1" specializations="@props/hello">

the temporary topic file looks like that:

 <topic specializations="@props/hello" domains="a(props hello)" .....>

so I think this should work fine.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3903: Branch filtering processes nested-topic topic files multiple times
content:
When branch filtering is applied to a topic with nested subtopics:
<map>
 <title>Test Map</title>

 <ditavalref href="filter-A.ditaval"/>

 <topicref href="topic.dita">
 <topicref href="topic.dita#id_1">
 <topicref href="topic.dita#id_1_1"/>
 <topicref href="topic.dita#id_1_2"/>
 </topicref>
 <topicref href="topic.dita#id_2">
 <topicref href="topic.dita#id_2_1"/>
 <topicref href="topic.dita#id_2_2"/>
 </topicref>
 </topicref>

</map>
the `branch-filter` step should process each topic file a single time:
[branch-filter] Filtering file:/tmp/temp20220319114445274/topic.dita
The `branch-filter` step processes each topic file multiple times:
[branch-filter] Filtering file:/tmp/temp20220319114445274/topic.dita
[branch-filter] Filtering file:/tmp/temp20220319114445274/topic.dita#id_1
[branch-filter] Filtering file:/tmp/temp20220319114445274/topic.dita#id_1_1
[branch-filter] Filtering file:/tmp/temp20220319114445274/topic.dita#id_1_2
[branch-filter] Filtering file:/tmp/temp20220319114445274/topic.dita#id_2
[branch-filter] Filtering file:/tmp/temp20220319114445274/topic.dita#id_2_1
[branch-filter] Filtering file:/tmp/temp20220319114445274/topic.dita#id_2_2

title: DITA-OT Issue #3903: Branch filtering processes nested-topic topic files multiple times
content:
I confirmed that the first branch filtering operation processes the entire file; thus, the subsequent operations perform unnecessary read-modify-write operations.

On small testcases, the effect on runtime is negligible.

But on a production online help map with many nested topics, branch filtering takes 66% of the `html5` transformation runtime (1050 seconds for branch filtering, out of 1590 seconds total).

#3875 is likely related - see the bottom of [this comment](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/3875#issuecomment-1044208535).
`BranchFilterModule.java` should be updated to process each file a single time. The solution should handle both omitted root topic `@id` values:
<topicref href="topic.dita"> <!-- root topic @id omitted -->
 <topicref href="topic.dita#id_1"/>
 <topicref href="topic.dita#id_2"/>
 </topicref>
as well as explicit root topic `@id` values:
<topicref href="topic.dita#root_topic_id"> <!-- @id explicitly included -->
 <topicref href="topic.dita#id_1"/>
 <topicref href="topic.dita#id_2"/>
 </topicref>

title: DITA-OT Issue #3904: OT 4.0 Idea: Provide an option to produce a dependency graph representation between all objects used in a build
content:
DITA-OT Issue #3904: OT 4.0 Idea: Provide an option to produce a dependency graph representation between all objects used in a build
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3904: OT 4.0 Idea: Provide an option to produce a dependency graph representation between all objects used in a build
content:
For optimizing builds and to provide the data for a visual graph of dependencies, enable OT to produce a text representation of the relationships between all objects referenced in a build in a form such as: <object1> <relationship> <object2>, where each object at a minimum is a file, but ideally can go down to element-level granularity.
Use cases may exist as two different options that could be independently enabled. Dependencies could be identified at the
1. DITA source level (pre-pre-processing)
2. After preprocessing where all conditions are applied and references resolved (post-pre-processing)

The data should be complete enough to answer questions, such as:
- What other objects could be affected by a change to a given object, directly or indirectly?
- What relationships have changed, been added, or deleted between dependency-graph-1 and dependency-graph-2? This could help optimize doc builds by identifying the only parts of a document set that need rendering.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3904: OT 4.0 Idea: Provide an option to produce a dependency graph representation between all objects used in a build
content:
Possible object representation formats include DITA addressing and perhaps optionally XPath references. It could be similar to RDF (subject–predicate–object), but optimized for DITA. There are multiple serialization formats for RDF https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resource_Description_Framework#Serialization_formats, including XML and JSON. There is also an W3C standard querying language https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SPARQL, which might be useful for running queries on such relationships. The Apache Jena project is an example of an implementation that supports SPARQL. 

An XQuery alternative might be another avenue to explore.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3910: Arabic corrupted in PDFs created with DITA OT 3.7.1 and FOP 2.6
content:
Generate correct Arabic text in PDFs using DITA OT 3.7.1 and FOP 2.6.
We had an issue with generating Arabic text in PDFs with DITA OT and FOP. Words are not correctly formed with the proper intermediate letter forms and connections. We were able to fix this with our custom PDF plugin for DITA OT 3.6.1 by overriding the attributes of fo:root to remove xml:lang. This introduced other issues like warnings about missing language attributes and there is no language specified in the PDF, but it generated correct Arabic text.

We upgraded to DITA OT 3.7.1 with the provided FOP 2.6, and the Arabic text problem is happening again. The override in our plugin to remove xml:lang no longer works. The xml:lang attribute still appeared in fo:root. As a workaround, we attempted to set xml:lang to ar for Arabic (because using language and locale, like ar-eg, often prevented complex scripts from working with Arabic) and adding script=arab and language attributes to for:root. These also didn't fix the problem. We also notice that the text direction in the PDF isn't correctly set to right-to-left even though we specified it in fo:root.

As it stands now, we cannot create valid Arabic PDFs with DITA OT 3.7.1 and FOP 2.6.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3910: Arabic corrupted in PDFs created with DITA OT 3.7.1 and FOP 2.6
content:

2. Build PDF using our plugin for DITA OT 3.7.1 with FOP 2.6. In the dita command, set -Dclean.temp to no to preserve temporary folder.
3. Open the PDF and notice that the Arabic words contain initial forms and are disconnected. This is not valid Arabic.
4. Open topic.fo from the temporary folder. Notice the fo:root contains xml:lang, even when we override it in the plugin. Adding script and language attributes to fo:root do not show any changes.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3914: In DITA-OT project files, allow subsets of deliverables to be published
content:
Currently, DITA-OT project file publishing is limited to publishing one deliverable or all deliverables.

To publish subsets of deliverables, the `<deliverable>` definitions must be split into multiple files, with subsets built using a hierarchy of `<include>` directives:

![files](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50950969/163050643-a1296063-e3c8-4b04-98ca-5e140ba0e2f6.svg)

This has the following drawbacks:

* Many files can be required.
 * We have 100+ contexts, shared by dozens of products, organized into several help collections.
 * Our deliverable definitions are resistant to grouping in fewer files, due to being shared where products overlap.
* It is difficult to know what a particular file publishes without tracing through multiple files.
* It is difficult to explore the evolution of project file content over time in a revision control system.
* Maintenance operations (search-and-replace, adjusting collections) are more complex.
* `<context>` and `<publication>` information must be replicated in every deliverable file to allow individual publishing (inelegant, but technically harmless).

title: DITA-OT Issue #3914: In DITA-OT project files, allow subsets of deliverables to be published
content:
When a collection is published, its deliverables should be published in the order resulting from expanding the references. This provides support for order-dependent deliverables (such as HTML online help that cleans its output directory first, followed by PDF deliverables written to that same output directory).

If the reference expansion includes a deliverable multiple times, the deliverable should only be published once (the first occurrence seems reasonable).

Detection for circular collection reference loops would be needed.
I considered having a deliverable declare its dependencies via a new `<depends>` element, but this made it difficult to specify whether to publish a deliverable alone or with its dependencies, plus there was no intuitive way to describe order dependency.
A testcase is included:

[ditaot_project_file_collections.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/8476477/ditaot_project_file_collections.zip)

The `project.xml` file in the testcase uses the format proposed above, although other implementations are possible.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3928: ImageMetadataFilter should take into account case in which the image metadata is null
content:
Based on this issue https://github.com/jelovirt/com.elovirta.ooxml/issues/94

If in the method `org.dita.dost.writer.ImageMetadataFilter#readBitmapMetadata(URI)` the `r.getImageMetadata(0)` returns `null`, it should be taken into account as the method is documented as being able to return `null`. And if it is `null` the image could be fully loaded to a bufferedimage to get the width and height. Because third party libraries which implement the ImageIO API sometimes do not implement the API for obtaining the image metadata.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3931: DITA 2.0: Use resourceid for result HTML file when appid-role is "deliverable-anchor"

title: DITA-OT Issue #3931: DITA 2.0: Use resourceid for result HTML file when appid-role is "deliverable-anchor"
content: Issue #3931 is open with labels DITA 2.0, feature, priority/medium. Retrieval signals: map, pdf, html, dita-ot, plugin, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3931: DITA 2.0: Use resourceid for result HTML file when appid-role is "deliverable-anchor"
content:
When a topicref contains a resourceid element with an @appid-role of "deliverable-anchor" the @appid value should be used to construct the name of the result, similar to the behavior of @copy-to, with these refinements:

For multi-file outputs, i.e., HTML, EPUB, CHM

* If the @appid value looks like a filename with no extension, i.e., appid="result-file", use the value as the base name of the result file, i.e., resulting in "result-file.html" for the deliverable file.
* If the @appid value looks like a filename with an extension use that value as the name of the result file, i.e., appid="result-file.json" results in "result-file.json" as the deliverable file.
* If the topicref element is a topic head (navtitle but no referenced resource), a result file should be generated as though the navigation title was the title of a title-only topic.

Note that the 2.0 spec restricts @appid values to single URI components when @appid-role is "deliverable-anchor".

For single-file outputs, i.e., PDF: Use the @appid value as the base for a generated anchor, where the anchor is made as unique as required to avoid duplicate anchors (i.e., combining the anchors of ancestors to construct a globally-unique result anchor.

These behaviors should be applied when no @appname value is specified (implying that that appid applies to all outputs).

When @appname is specified, the following values should be recognized:

* "html" - Applies to all HTML-based outputs: HTML5, XHTML, EPUB, etc.
* "pdf", "print", "paged" - Applies to all paginated outputs (PDF2, Miramo, Oxygen Chemistry, etc.)
* "csh", "help" - Applies to all help-generating outputs (CHM, WebHelp, etc.)

In addition, when @appname matches the name of the transformation type, it should be applied. I.e., an @appname value of "html5" would apply to the html5 transform but not to the xhtml transform.

It might make sense to provide a way to specify @appname values that plugins will recognize in the plugin.xml.

When multiple <resourceid> elements would be recognized by a processor, use the first one recognized in document order.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3932: Publishing speed slower with Java 17 than with Java 1.8 [Windows]
content:
I publish on Windows a large (about 2000 topics) DITA Map to HTML5 with default settings: https://github.com/oxygenxml/userguide/blob/master/DITA/UserManual.ditamap With both Java 17 and 1.8 they should get published in about the same time.
- Set the **-Dsun.io.useCanonCaches=true** system property in the dita script file which starts the Java process. There was a [change in Java 12](https://bugs.openjdk.java.net/browse/JDK-8207005 ) which changed default for the cache to `false`. As the DITA OT works intensively with files, enabling this property seems to make a big difference and remove this large publishing time difference between Java 1.8 and 17.. - Setting `store-type=memory` as a parameter also helps as a workaround to reduce the publishing time with Java 17.
1. Download https://github.com/oxygenxml/userguide 2. Publish "DITA/UserManual.ditamap" to HTML5 using default params and Java 17 3. Publish "DITA/UserManual.ditamap" to HTML5 using default params and Java 8 4. Compare publishing times

and when I use it in the command line with `--propertyfile=x.properties` the `args.draft` parameter is not set as enabled in the DITA OT code.
This happens because after that `yes` value in the properties file there is an extra space which is not removed by the DITA OT code in `org.dita.dost.invoker.Arguments.BooleanArgument.getValue(String)` when comparing the value with various constants.
So that switch expression there could also trim the value `switch (value.trim().toLowerCase())`.
Such a problem is quite hard to figure out once present, I had to add logging in the DITA OT code in various classes.

content: Issue #3950 is open with labels bug. Retrieval signals: error, map, pdf, dita-ot, plugin, transform, publishing.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3950: Fix broken key issue by raising severity of DOTJ047I
content:
The severity of DOTJ047I should be raised to `ERROR`, because content is missing (e.g. an image) when a key is not defined, e.g. for images.
The severity of DOTJ047I is `INFO`. The problem is, that this does not fail a build and this severe issue is not detected.
Change severity from `INFO` to `ERROR` in [messages_template.xml](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/blob/develop/src/main/config/messages_template.xml). This is the only solution, because the DITA-OT does not allow to override the severity of messages with a plugin.
The build should fail with a severe error, because a key to an image is not defined, but it does not. The image is, of course, missing in the output. Missing content errors should always have the severity `ERROR`.

title: DITA-OT Issue #3957: Include `@keyscope` and `@outputclass` in the rewrite-rules file list
content:
I just discovered rewrite rules and they are amazing! However, we need some additional functionality to use them.

Consider the following DITA content and HTML5 output structure:

![rewrite1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50950969/177048767-8279a6f3-c71f-476c-a077-a19c32b84705.svg)

I would like to do the following:

* Move content-reuse files in `_warehouse/` to their relevant book directory (red).
 * We do not want internal path components like `_warehouse` exposed in customer-visible URLs.
 * We follow a convention of matching book map file, directory, and `@keyscope` names, which can be used here.
 * I need `@keyscope` to know what directory name to replace `_warehouse/` with.
* Move topics with `@outputclass="root"` to the root of the output directory (green).
 * This could be done by hardcoded file name matches, but writer-driven directives via `@outputclass` are more flexible.
If `@keyscope` and `@outputclass` were propagated to the `<file>` entries, then I can make use of them in the rewrite rules:

title: DITA-OT Issue #3957: Include `@keyscope` and `@outputclass` in the rewrite-rules file list
content:
<!-- rename _warehouse/... to {@keyscope}/... -->
 <xsl:template match="file[@keyscope]/@result[starts-with(., '_warehouse/')]">
 <xsl:attribute name="{local-name()}" select="replace(., '_warehouse', ../@keyscope)"/>
 <!-- ^^^^^^^^^ -->
 </xsl:template>

 <!-- move @outputclass="root" topics to root directory -->
 <xsl:template match="file[contains-token(@outputclass, 'root')]/@result">
 <!-- ^^^^^^^^^^^^ -->
 <xsl:attribute name="{local-name()}" select="replace(., '.*/', '')"/>
 </xsl:template>
resulting in the following HTML5 output structure:
Multiple `@keyscope` values from the map ancestry should be combined into a token list. `@outputclass` should be simply copied on a per-file basis.
I considered writing a Perl post-processing script, but this approach cannot be shared across Windows-based publishing from Oxygen on writer laptops and Linux-based publishing on a back-end production machine. Plus, rewrite rules already implement all the clever reference-remapping machinery, and the best solution is to make use of it.
To run it, publish the `project.xml` file:

content:
I publish the DITA map from this zip file [sample.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/9198045/sample.zip) to HTML and the conref to topic element is not resolved into the output.

In the console I have the following messages:

I checked into the "plugin:org.dita.base:xsl/preprocess/conrefImpl.xsl" file and the problem seems to be into the template that matches '*[@conref:orig-id]'. In my case the "orig-id" variable is the id of a topic and the content ('content' variable) where this id is searched contains a list of elements that skips the topic elements.
So, it seems to work if I change the "first" variable with this:
`<xsl:variable name="first" select="($topic//@conref:orig-id[. = $orig-id])[1]" as="attribute()"/>`

title: DITA-OT Issue #3983: For `--project` publishing, `dita.temp.dir` should default to /tmp/<tempdir> in linux
content:
In linux, when a map is published directly, `dita.temp.dir` defaults to a unique directory in /tmp:
$ dita -i map.ditamap -f html5 -verbose
...omitted...
 [echo] dita.temp.dir=/tmp/temp20220803100015319
Our DITA-OT installation is in a shared network filesystem. It would be much better for the default temporary directory to be in /tmp (which is a local solid-state disk) instead of in a shared network filesystem.
Change the default `dita.temp.dir` behavior in linux.
We can use the `--temp` command-line option to specify a temporary directory, but then we must also take responsibility for directory name uniqueness when there are concurrent runs on the same machine.
A small testcase is included: [ditaot-default-project-tmpdir.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/9252082/ditaot-default-project-tmpdir.zip)

title: DITA-OT Issue #3991: Relax possibility for named template to return an empty sequence
content:
I have quite a large project containing a large chunk of topicrefs.
At some point during processing the large chunked topic in the "html5.topics.common.inner" stage I get in the console the error:

 [xslt] An empty sequence is not allowed as the result of template related-links:result.reference
 [xslt] Failed to transform document: Failed to transform document: An empty sequence is not allowed as the result of template related-links:result.reference
 [xslt] Processing

and afterwards the HTML topic corresponding to the chunked file is incomplete, it's not even valid, it's missing most of its contents.

In this file `DITA-OT/plugins/org.dita.html5/xsl/reference.xsl` there is a template:
<xsl:template match="*[contains(@class, ' topic/link ')][@type='reference']" mode="related-links:result-group"
 name="related-links:result.reference" as="element()">
If I relax the `as="element()?"` to specify an optional element, the processing works and produces a large HTML document from the chunked topic, as it should. Looking in all other XSLTs, all other templates named `related-links:result.reference` have `as="element()?"`

title: DITA-OT Issue #4001: Should HTML Images be lazily loaded by default?
content:
DITA-OT Issue #4001: Should HTML Images be lazily loaded by default?
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4001: Should HTML Images be lazily loaded by default?
content: Whilst fixing a chunking issue in a custom plugin, I discovered a more generic issue related to the rendering of `` elements. The issue can be seen here: https://jason-fox.github.io/dita-bootstrap/Chunk1343199979.html I have a page which contains a side-toc and lots of content. In this particular case, one image is failing to load, but that doesn't really matter, what does matter is that the DOM is only fully rendered once the whole page is loaded. In this case it takes 45 seconds for the bottom half of the DOM after the slow image to complete rendering. In the meantime the side-toc remains unusable. When loading on mobile, for a massive full of images, all images would need to be downloaded (wasting bandwidth) before the page is rendered. This would also improve rendering speed of longer documents throughout. [Lazy loading](https://blog.hubspot.com/website/lazy-loading-eager-loading) has been implemented across many browsers. The suggestion is to add [`loading="lazy`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/img#attr-loading) to rendered images: When should `loading="lazy"` be added?

title: DITA-OT Issue #4001: Should HTML Images be lazily loaded by default?
content:
Looking at the DITA spec, I can see that [`<image>`](https://www.oxygenxml.com/dita/1.3/specs/langRef/base/image.html) has an [`@scope`](https://www.oxygenxml.com/dita/1.3/specs/langRef/attributes/thescopeattribute.html) attribute, the suggestion would be to add `loading="lazy"` when `scope="external"` or defaults to external because the `@href` begins with `http` and `@scope` is not defined.
When should `loading="eager"` be added?
If the `@scope` attribute of an `<image>` is deliberately set to `scope="local"`, it should probably be set to `loading="eager"`
This behaviour could added as a custom plugin, but seems too trivial to warrant one. I think it would make a better PR request, but I'd like feedback before I spend more time looking at it and work out if the proposed categories of lazy/eager are correct. Furthermore, a properly implemented XSL template could still be applied to override the defaults - e.g. set lazy for all images or none.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4006: Setting output.dir and dita.temp.dir in a DITA-OT project file
content:
As a user I'm expecting to set all params in the DITA-OT project file. As I have learned now (thanks @raducoravu and @chrispy-snps) the **`<output>`** element and the **`output.dir`** parameter are two different things and they are relative to each other. But I cannot set **`output.dir`** in the project file.
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project>
 
 <deliverable name="Output Dir" id="output-dir">
 <context name="Output Dir" id="output-dir-context">
 <input href="output-dir.ditamap"/>
 </context>
 <output href="./output-dir"/>
 <publication transtype="pdf2">
 <param name="clean.temp" value="no"/>
 <param name="dita.temp.dir" value="./temp"/>
 <param name="output.dir" value="./new-out"/>
 </publication>
 </deliverable>
 
</project>
But it fails with something like this:
Developers-MacBook-Pro:bin raducoravu$ sh dita -p /Users/raducoravu/Desktop/output-dir/output-dir.xml
Error: [DOTJ085E][ERROR] The 'output.dir' parameter cannot be set with 'param' in project files. Use 'output' instead.
Just publish the DITA-OT file.
[output-dir.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/9573958/output-dir.zip)
