title: DITA-OT Issue #4013: Unresolved keyref, duplicate output topic when `<mapref>` and referenced `<map>` both have `@keyscope`
content:
When a `<mapref>` and its referenced `<map>` both have `@keyscope` defined:

![4013](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50950969/193274087-604ca527-f0bf-4481-9570-f2210dc9b74c.svg)

I expected the transformation to behave as described in [2.3.4.2 Key scopes](http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3/errata02/os/complete/part2-tech-content/archSpec/base/keyScopes.html) in the DITA 1.3 specification:

> If the `@keyscope` attribute is specified on both a reference to a DITA map and the root element of the referenced map, only one scope is created; the submap does not create another level of scope hierarchy. The single key scope that results from this scenario has multiple names; its names are the union of the values of the `@keyscope` attribute on the map reference and the root element of the submap. This means that processors can resolve references to both the key scopes specified on the map reference and the key scopes specified on the root element of the submap.

and keys locally defined and referenced within the submap should work.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4013: Unresolved keyref, duplicate output topic when `<mapref>` and referenced `<map>` both have `@keyscope`
content:
For an HTML-based transformation, the following issues occur:

* An unresolved key message is emitted:

 `[keyref] file:/.../submap.ditamap:15:29: [DOTJ047I][INFO] Unable to find key definition for key reference "Product" in root scope. The href attribute may be used as fallback if it exists`

 This message is caused by the key reference in the submap `<topicmeta>`; the key reference in the topic resolves correctly.

* Two copies of any topic with a key reference are created:
$ ls out/
 commonltr.css commonrtl.css empty.html index.html topic-1.html topic.html
 ^^^^^^^^^^^^ ^^^^^^^^^^
This issue is caused by the key reference in the topic.
1. Download the following testcase: [4013.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/9684347/4013.zip) 2. Run the following command: `dita -i map.ditamap -f html5 -verbose`

title: DITA-OT Issue #4015: Property 'args.html5.toc.class' does not work in HTML5 transformation
content:
Adding the property `args.html5.toc.class` to the properties file that I use when generating HTML5 output produces no corresponding @class attribute on the TOC <body> element.

I have the following line in my properties file:
`args.html5.toc.class = top_toc`

In the output log, the property is recognized and associated with the OUTPUTCLASS parameter:
html5.map.toc:
 ...
 [xslt] Set parameter OUTPUTCLASS to 'top_toc'
The XSL transforms appear to be looking for @outputclass on the <map> element, but the intermediate <map> element in the temp directory contains no such attribute:
<map xmlns:dita-ot="http://dita-ot.sourceforge.net/ns/201007/dita-ot"
 xmlns:ditaarch="http://dita.oasis-open.org/architecture/2005/" 
 cascade="merge" 
 class="- map/map " 
 ditaarch:DITAArchVersion="1.3" 
 domains="(map mapgroup-d) (topic abbrev-d) (topic delay-d) a(props deliveryTarget) (map ditavalref-d) (map glossref-d) (topic hazard-d) (topic hi-d) (topic indexing-d) (topic markup-d) (topic pr-d) (topic relmgmt-d) (topic sw-d) (topic ui-d) (topic ut-d) (topic markup-d xml-d)" 
 specializations="@props/deliveryTarget" 
 xml:lang="ja" 
 xtrc="map:1;5:20" 
 xtrf="file:/***.ditamap">
In the meantime, we can just manually add a @class attribute since it's just one file, but I hope this can be addressed in a future update.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4017: PDF2 renders index entries in link text
content:
When a link target includes index entries, PDF2 adds the text of the index entries to `<xref>` link text, whereas HTML5 output does not.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4032: URI scheme is not "file" `IllegalArgumentException` is thrown if `scope` is not resolved.
content:
When copying over images during preprocessing, only images with a `file` URI scheme should be copied to the output location. Images which are defined using `scope="external"` or which have a HTTP URI scheme should be ignored
<files>
 <file src="file:/.../in/document.ditamap" uri="document.ditamap" path="document.ditamap" 
 result="file:/.../in/document.ditamap" format="ditamap" input="true">
 </file>
 <file src="file:/.../in/markdown.dita" uri="markdown.dita" path="markdown.dita"
 result="file:/.../in/markdown.dita" format="dita" has-link="true" target="true">
 </file>
 <file src="https://example.com/image.png" uri="https://example.com/image.png" 
 path="https:/example.com/image.png" result="https://example.com/image.png" 
 format="image">
 </file>
</files>
In this case `https://example.com/image.png` is added to the `<files>` list. I think it is only excluded if `scope="external"` is set - I also have a use case with a custom processor and even when I hardcode `scope` debug complains about the missing attribute somehow.

The failure is here in `build_process.xml` because the ANT `copy` task can't handle HTTP which is in the `<fileset>`
<copy todir="${copy-image.todir}" failonerror="false" overwrite="true">
 <ditafileset format="image" />
 <jobmapper/>
</copy>

title: DITA-OT Issue #4036: NullPointerException when using the root-chunk-override with the new DITA 2.0 "combine" value
content:
Using the sample project in the related #4019 if I were out of curiosity to change the DOCTYPE declaration of the DITA Map to make it 2.0:
<!DOCTYPE map PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA 2.x Map//EN" "map.dtd">
and then publish to HTML5 using the "root-chunk-override" param set to "combine", I get a NullPointerException instead:

 java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "java.net.URI.resolve(java.net.URI)" because "chunk.src" is null
 at org.dita.dost.chunk.ChunkModule.rewriteLinks(ChunkModule.java:230)
 at org.dita.dost.chunk.ChunkModule.lambda$9(ChunkModule.java:193)
 at java.base/java.util.ArrayList$ArrayListSpliterator.forEachRemaining(ArrayList.java:1625)
 at java.base/java.util.stream.ReferencePipeline$Head.forEach(ReferencePipeline.java:762)
 at org.dita.dost.chunk.ChunkModule.generateChunks(ChunkModule.java:188)
 at org.dita.dost.chunk.ChunkModule.processCombine(ChunkModule.java:85)
 at org.dita.dost.chunk.ChunkModule.execute(ChunkModule.java:52)

This NPE comes probably from `org.dita.dost.chunk.ChunkModule.collectChunkOperations(URI, Element, List)` which has a commented out `//.src(href)` when chunk is combine.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4048: Warn about profiled DITA content that is not affected by any DITAVAL filtering rule
content:
A new message could be implemented that works as follows:

* The check is always applied, even if neither global or branch filtering is used.
* The check considers a default exclusion rule in a user-applied DITAVAL file to be intentional filtering.
* The check considers the final effect after both global and branch filtering are applied. 
* The check has a warning severity.

Or, DOTJ031I could be repurposed and improved in these ways.
Each run tests content profiled in the following ways:

* Within a topic file (`dita-topic-condition/`)
 ![topic](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50950969/201549484-eef6f048-b000-49a9-8bb0-97a39c6a5549.svg)

* Topic references in a map file (`dita-topicref-condition/`)
 ![topicref](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50950969/201549499-f7f1fdee-98e0-43b9-8c2c-f5f3f103de3f.svg)

* Submap references in a map file (`dita-mapref-condition/`)
 ![mapref](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50950969/201549509-69818be4-c854-4a17-bc2b-d770be03f5a7.svg)

Note that I included all cases in a single issue because I think the solution must be architected with all cases in mind.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4068: DOTJ047I (unresolved key reference) should not be issued for references into declared peer maps
content:
If there are scoped keyrefs into a declared, keyscoped peer map, then a new **information** message (not DOTJ047I) should be issued because the peer map could possibly define those keys:
An unresolved key message (DOTJ047I) is displayed for correctly defined keyrefs into peer maps, making it different to separate correct references from bad references (undefined keyscopes, missing map files, etc.):
Implement a new check that detects whether the keyref's scope reaches into any declared keyscoped peer map. Subsequent nested scope levels "inside" the peer map can be ignored, as we don't know what scope structures exist inside that map.

Also implement #3950 to increase the severity of bad keyrefs with bad scopes.

content: Issue #4069 is open with labels bug. Retrieval signals: xref, map, pdf, html, dita-ot, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4069: DOTX028E (missing link target) should not be satisfied by linktext
content:
If there are `<link>` elements that do not resolve, DOTX028E should be issued regardless of whether `<linktext>` is included or not:

![DOTX028E_linktext_expected](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50950969/205107892-c1768b6e-1030-450f-95ac-a879c0c6b28d.svg)

This is because `<linktext>` is cosmetic rendering information that does not affect whether the underlying reference is valid and can be followed.
No DOTX028E message is issued for `<link>` elements with `<linktext>` (highlighted in blue):

![DOTX028E_linktext_actual](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50950969/205107923-f115591f-408e-452e-90e3-f49cee12a7d8.svg)
The fix must not complain about links into declared peer maps. Such links are not resolvable to an `@href` in the current transformation, due to the peer scope's nature of deferred resolution. (This tricky problem is quite possibly why the current DOTX028E behavior exists.)
1. Download the following testcase:
 [4069.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/10134256/4069.zip)
2. Run the following command:
 `dita --project project.xml -verbose`

Note that matching `<xref>` content is included for completeness of consideration, although the `<xref>` behavior is affected by #4067.

content:
Defer the DOTJ031I check until after both global and/or branch filtering are performed. This would resolve both limitations 1 and 3 in now-closed issue #4048.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4086: Go through all DITA OT information messages, avoid reporting some and increase severity of others
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4086: Go through all DITA OT information messages, avoid reporting some and increase severity of others
content:
In general the DITA OT should in my opinion not show information messages and if there are information messages which are very useful, like a missing keyref, it could be presented as a warning maybe.
Because I'm looking in "/DITA-OT/config/messages.xml" at "INFO" messages, some of them are like this:

 <message id="DOTX029I" type="INFO">
 <reason>The type attribute on a %1 element was set to %3, but the reference is to a more specific %4 %2. This may cause your links to sort incorrectly in the output.</reason>
 <response/>
 </message>

which in my opinion should be a warning.

Other messages make up part of the usual functionality:

 <message id="DOTX077I" type="INFO">
 <reason>Resolving content references results in duplicate ID '%1'.</reason>
 <response>Rewriting resolved version to '%2'.</response>
 </message>

and in my opinion should not be output at all because end user start asking if this is a problem and if not how they can avoid such messages from being presented.

Or an info message like this:

 <message id="DOTJ047I" type="INFO">
 <reason>Unable to find key definition for key reference "%1" in root scope.</reason>
 <response>The href attribute may be used as fallback if it exists</response>
 </message>

which should be a warning.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4094: Cascaded DITAVAL filtering is not properly applied to multiple-condition profiled content
content:
DITA-OT Issue #4094: Cascaded DITAVAL filtering is not properly applied to multiple-condition profiled content
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

content: Issue #4094 is open with labels bug. Retrieval signals: map, html, dita-ot, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4094: Cascaded DITAVAL filtering is not properly applied to multiple-condition profiled content
content:
This is a follow-up issue from discussion in #4085.

In [3.5.4.1 `<ditavalref>`](https://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3/os/part2-tech-content/langRef/base/ditavalref.html), I interpret the paragraph about cascaded `<ditavalref>` elements as follows:

* If a "condition" (attribute name and value) is excluded at a higher level, that condition cannot be reenabled for inclusion at a lower level.
* Processing-wise, `<ditavalref>` is applied from top to bottom, with higher levels removing conditions from consideration by lower levels.
* It is the exclusions, not the inclusions, that combine in an OR-like way from top to bottom.

As an industrial DITA user, I would expect this behavior so that sensitive content excluded from a higher level cannot unexpectedly be re-included at a lower level, such as when reusing common submaps. (However, we have yet to hit this scenario in practice, so there is no urgency from us.)
In addition to removing content elements that are excluded, perhaps the global and branch filtering code can also remove the excluded keywords themselves from attribute values when only some keywords in the value are excluded. This would more accurately reflect the propagation of exclusions described in section 3.5.4.1.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4105: Cascading of metadata elements from submap
content:
DITA-OT Issue #4105: Cascading of metadata elements from submap
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4105: Cascading of metadata elements from submap
content:
<div type='discussions-op-text'>

<sup>Originally posted by **lief-erickson** May 17, 2022</sup>
What is the expected behavior for element metadata cascading from submaps?

**root-map.ditamap**
<map id="root-map">
 <topicmeta>
 <category>one</category>
 </topicmeta>
 <mapref href="submap.ditamap"/>
</map>
<map id="submap">
 <topicmeta>
 <category>two</category>
 </topicmeta>
 <topicref href="topic.dita"/>
</map>
**topic.dita**
<concept>
 <prolog>
 <metadata>
 <category>three</category>
 </metadata>
 </prolog>
 ...
</concept>
According to the [specification](http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3/errata02/os/complete/part3-all-inclusive/archSpec/base/cascading-of-metadata-elements-from-map-to-map.html#cascading-of-metadata-elements-from-map-to-map), `<category>` should be additive. And it kinda is. Using the `html5` and normalized `dita` transtypes, the output for **topic.dita** in **temp.dir** is:
<concept>
 <prolog>
 <metadata>
 <category>one</category>
 <category>three</category>
 </metadata>
 </prolog>
 ...
</concept>
The `<audience>two</audience>` element is discarded and nowhere to be found. Is this expected behavior?

This alternative construct using the root map produces the same results.

**root-map-alternative.ditamap**

title: DITA-OT Issue #4105: Cascading of metadata elements from submap
content:
<map id="root-map-alt">
 <topicmeta>
 <category>one</category>
 </topicmeta>
 <mapref href="submap.ditamap">
 <topicmeta>
 <category>two</category>
 </topicmeta>
 </mapref>
</map>

title: DITA-OT Issue #4106: DITA OT enables full debug logging for all Java packages
content:
The logback.xml file "config/logback.xml" enables by default full debug logging for all Java packages. This means it interferes with Java packages from other plugins as well. I think it should enable full debug logging only on the "org.dita.dost" and "com.idiominc" packages and leave the default debug level as "INFO" instead of DEBUG.
For example we have some indexing Java code in our Oxygen WebHelp plugins, once the plugins are added to a stock DITA OT distribution, the end user will see all our debug messages in the console.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4123: Use some XSLT 3.0 features
content:
This enhancement provides an XSLT stylesheet that can update XSLT files as follows:

* Update all XSLT stylesheet versions to `version="3.0"`
* Replace `contains(@att, " keyword ")` with `contains-token(@att, "keyword")`
* Replace identity templates with `<xsl:mode on-no-match="shallow-copy">`
* Use `mode="#current"` where possible
 * This was done in #3974, but I am including it for completeness.

I created this issue to capture the idea and the approach when we are ready.
1. Download the following testcase: [4123.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/10713446/4123.zip)
2. In Oxygen, run the "XSLT optimizer" refactoring operation on all *.xsl files in the DITA-OT repository.

I recommend using Oxygen because it is quite good at preserving the original document formatting to minimize revision control differences.

Unfortunately, newlines in attribute values are not preserved. These instances must be reformatted manually.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4153: `<?ditaot usershortdesc?>` and `<?ditaot usertext?>` PIs are not inserted consistently during `topicpull`
content:
The following XML processing instructions should be inserted consistently for `<xref>` and `<link>` elements during `topicpull` preprocessing:

* `<?ditaot gentext?>` - indicates OT-computed link text
* `<?ditaot usertext?>` - indicates user-supplied link text
* `<?ditaot genshortdesc?>` - indicates OT-computed `<desc>` text
* `<?ditaot usershortdesc?>` - indicates user-supplied `<desc>` text

For example, this link element:
<link keyref="topic" type="topic">
 <linktext>LINKTEXT</linktext>
 <desc>DESCTEXT</desc>
</link>
should have the following PIs inserted during `topicpull` preprocessing:
<link keyref="topic" type="topic" href="topic.dita">
 <?ditaot usertext?><linktext>LINKTEXT</linktext>
 <?ditaot usershortdesc?><desc>DESCTEXT</desc>
</link>

title: DITA-OT Issue #4170: Force unique behavior with keyrefs
content:
Tested with DITA OT 4.0.2. I have a DITA Map which maps two keys to the same referenced topic:
<topicref href="step.dita" keys="step_a"/>
<topicref href="step.dita" keys="step_b"/>
<topicref href="target.dita" keys="target"/>
<reltable>
 <relrow>
 <relcell>
 <topicref keyref="step_a"/>
 <topicref keyref="step_b"/>
 </relcell>
 <relcell>
 <topicref keyref="target"/>
 </relcell>
 </relrow>
</reltable>
and then the reltable adds references between both keys and the `target` key.
I'm using `fource-unique=true` to publish to HTML5.
As force-unique generates two HTML files `step.html` and `step-2.html` on disk from the original `step.dita`, both these generated HTML files should have a related link to `target.html`. But only the first `step.html` does.

Looking at the console output, the copy-to processing which generates the `step-2.dita` takes place after the keyrefs are resolved so the `step_b` key remains mapped to `step.dita`.
But I'm not sure how this could be fixed.

[test_force-unique.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/11273404/test_force-unique.zip)

title: DITA-OT Issue #4175: The entity "nbsp" was referenced, but not declared
content:
I have 2 DITA tasks, both using the nbsp entity, please see the attached project. I publish to HTML5 using the default settings. For the second task I get this error reported and the task is no longer parsed:

 [gen-list] [DOTJ013E][ERROR] Failed to parse the referenced file ../flowers/t2.dita'.: ../flowers/t2.dita Line 12:The entity "nbsp" was referenced, but not declared.

[flowers.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/11309148/flowers.zip)

The problem is caused by the "args.grammar.cache" param set to "yes" and the fact that the Xerces parser has a grammar caching bug:

title: DITA-OT Issue #4184: Circular `<xref>` references inside `<shortdesc>` causes infinite XSLT recursion during `topicpull` target text computation
content:
According to the DITA content models, an `<xref>` inside a `<shortdesc>` is allowed and thus should not interfere with publishing:
<!-- topic1.dita -->
<topic>
 <title>Feature 1</title>
 <shortdesc>This is feature 1, which works together with <xref keyref="feature2"/>.</shortdesc>
 ...
</topic>

<!-- topic2.dita -->
<topic>
 <title>Feature 2</title>
 <shortdesc>This is feature 2, which works together with <xref keyref="feature1"/>.</shortdesc>
 ...
</topic>
If there is a circular reference loop across topic `<shortdesc>` elements (such as in the example above), infinite XSLT recursion occurs when `topicpull` attempts to resolve the `<xref>` target text:
[topicpull] Too many nested template or function calls. The stylesheet may be looping.
[topicpull] Failed to transform document: Failed to transform document: Too many nested template or function calls. The stylesheet may be looping.

[topicpull] Too many nested function calls. May be due to infinite recursion.
[topicpull] Failed to transform document: Failed to transform document: [topicpull] Too many nested function calls. May be due to infinite recursion.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4184: Circular `<xref>` references inside `<shortdesc>` causes infinite XSLT recursion during `topicpull` target text computation
content:
We found this issue when converting our specialized topic-summary element into `<shortdesc>` elements. Some of our summaries mentioned related features using `<xref>` elements.

Even when the references aren't circular, unnecessarily nested `<desc>` elements can result. Given the following linear sequence of `<shortdesc>` references:
<!-- topicW.dita -->
<shortdesc>This is feature W, which works together with <xref keyref="featureX"/>.</shortdesc>

<!-- topicX.dita -->
<shortdesc>This is feature W, which works together with <xref keyref="featureY"/>.</shortdesc>

<!-- topicY.dita -->
<shortdesc>This is feature W, which works together with <xref keyref="featureZ"/>.</shortdesc>

<!-- topicZ.dita -->
<shortdesc>This is feature Z.</shortdesc>
<shortdesc>This is feature W, which works together with
 <xref keyref="featureX" href="topicX.dita" type="topic">Feature X
 <desc>This is feature X, which works together with
 <xref keyref="featureY" href="topicY.dita" type="topic">Feature Y
 <desc>This is feature Y, which works together with
 <xref keyref="featureZ" href="topicZ.dita" type="topic">Feature Z
 <desc>This is feature Z.</desc>
 </xref>.
 </desc>
 </xref>.
 </desc>
 </xref>.
</shortdesc>
1. Download and extract the following testcase: [4184.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/11401087/4184.zip) 2. Run a transformation on map.ditamap (any type).

content: Issue #4207 is open with labels none. Retrieval signals: map, html, dita-ot, plugin.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4207: Replace `call-template` with `apply-templates` where possible
content:
In the DITA-OT XSLT stylesheets, some named templates are marked as deprecated with a note that the equivalent moded templates should be used instead. However, some existing code still uses `<xsl:call-template>` to named templates in some places.

Perhaps opportunities for future XSLT code improvement are (in this order):

1. Convert `<xsl:call-template name="...">` to `<xsl:apply-templates mode="..."/>` where possible.
2. Remove deprecated named templates in some future major release where compatibility is not guaranteed (DITA-OT 5.0?).

title: DITA-OT Issue #4207: Replace `call-template` with `apply-templates` where possible
content:
To help identify these improvements, I wrote an XSLT stylesheet that does the following:

1. Identifies each top-level XSLT stylesheet.
 * A "top-level stylesheet" is an .xsl file that is not imported or included by any other stylesheet.
2. Flattens each stylesheet into a single document by inlining any included/imported sub-stylesheets.
 * This allows template references across included files to be considered properly.
3. For each "name-to-mode" remapping template (in which no processing is performed except calling the equivalent mode),
 * Report the named remapping template (for opportunity 2 in the "Description" section).
 * Report any calls to the named remapping template (for opportunity 1 in the "Description" section).

Here is the stylesheet: [report-named-templates.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/11592561/report-named-templates.zip)

In linux, the usage is as follows:
Here is an example of the output (blank lines added for clarity):

title: DITA-OT Issue #4207: Replace `call-template` with `apply-templates` where possible
content:
<top-stylesheet uri="file:/path/to/dita-ot/plugins/org.dita.html5/xsl/dita2html5.xsl">
 ...
 <templates name="generateChapterTitle">

 <xsl:template xml:base="file:/path/to/dita-ot/plugins/org.dita.html5/xsl/topic.xsl"
 name="generateChapterTitle">
 <xsl:apply-templates select="." mode="generateChapterTitle"/>
 </xsl:template>

 <xsl:call-template xml:base="file:/path/to/dita-ot/plugins/org.dita.html5/xsl/topic.xsl"
 name="generateChapterTitle"/>

 </templates>
 ...
 </top-stylesheet>
Note the following:

* The `<templates>` element specifies the `@name` being reported.
* The `<xsl:template>` and `<xsl:call-template>` elements indicate the file that contains them via the `@xml:base` attribute.

Any conversions from named template calls to moded template calls should verify that the `@match` expression of the moded template(s) maintains the desired behavior.
* The stylesheet uses the DITA-OT catalog to resolve URN-based references in the XSLT files. * The DITA-OT catalog does not seem to be functional in the src/main/ directory of a DITA-OT development directory, but it does seem to work in distribution directories. * For top-level stylesheets with *_template.xsl variants, both versions are processed (template and installed). * The stylesheet could be enhanced to process one or the other in such cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4223: Sometimes chunking is not done correctly when using copy-to (or the "force-unique" parameter)
content:
When using force-unique, sometimes child topicrefs which contain chunks should be processed.
In the Java class ChunkMapReader.processChildTopicref(Element) replace:
 
 final URI href = toURI(getValue(currentElem, ATTRIBUTE_NAME_HREF));

with:

 URI href = toURI(getValue(currentElem, ATTRIBUTE_NAME_COPY_TO));
 if(href == null) {
 href = toURI(getValue(currentElem, ATTRIBUTE_NAME_HREF));
 }
The DITA Map structure looks like this:

 <topicref href="topics/index.dita" collection-type="sequence">
 <topicref href="concepts/summerFlowers.dita" collection-type="sequence">
 <topicref href="topics/flowers/gardenia.dita" chunk="to-content"> </topicref>
 </topicref>
 </topicref>
 <topichead navtitle="New Chapter" collection-type="sequence">
 <topicref href="concepts/summerFlowers.dita" collection-type="sequence">
 <topicref href="topics/flowers/gardenia.dita" chunk="to-content"> </topicref>
 </topicref>
 </topichead>

[Uploading chunk-force-unique.zip…]()

1. Publish the attached DITA project to HTML5 setting the force-unique=true parameter.
2. In the generated index.html the last reference should be to a "gardenia_2.html". But it is to the "gardenia.html"

title: DITA-OT Issue #4254: HTML5: Teletype output contains inline style attributes
content:
When MDITA source contains text wrapped in backticks, the generated HTML output should contain either `<span>` elements with appropriate class attributes, or `<tt>` elements as described in the release notes.
in the HTML output. This appears to contradict the explanation in the release notes, which goes like this:

> Standard Markdown syntax can now be used to indicate a span of code by wrapping it with backtick quotes (`). In Markdown DITA input, these constructs are converted to DITA \<codeph\> elements on import, and rendered as \<code\> elements in HTML output. In MDITA input, this syntax is converted to teletype \<tt\> elements to align with LwDITA, which supports teletype highlighting in XDITA.
The attached [`demo.zip`](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/12215053/demo.zip) file contains source and output that demonstrates the problem.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4256: DITAVAL with conditions for group default values
content:
If we have a conditional attribute group such as `groupA(a b)` and we set the group to **exclude** in a ditaval file using `<prop action="exclude" att="audience" val="groupA"/>` it should set the default values for `a` and `b` to **exclude** and the entire group should evaluate to **exclude**, according to [DITA Specification](https://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3/os/part1-base/langRef/ditaval/ditaval-val.html).
The default values of `a` and `b` are not changed and the group evaluates to **include**.

2. Publish main_map.ditamap to PDF
3. Open the PDF. Chapter1 contains the word `product1`, but the keydef element containing that keyword should have been excluded from the ditamap and instead we should see `product2`

content: Issue #4260 is open with labels bug, preprocess/keyref. Retrieval signals: keyref, map, pdf, html, dita-ot, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4260: Key definition with key reference
content:
<!-- If you're describing a bug, tell us what should happen. -->
If we have a keydef element with a keyref to another key, the first key should pull resources from the second.
<keydef keys="product" keyref="product_aux">
 <topicmeta>
 <keywords>
 <keyword>product1</keyword>
 </keywords>
 </topicmeta>
</keydef>
<keydef keys="product_aux">
 <topicmeta>
 <keywords>
 <keyword>product_aux</keyword>
 </keywords>
 </topicmeta>
</keydef>
According to [DITA Specification](https://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3/os/part1-base/archSpec/base/example-keydef-with-keyref.html), if a resource is already present in the first key, it won't be pulled from the second. If the initial keydef has a topicmeta element containing a keyword and the second one has a topicmeta with a keyword as well, the first keydef should keep the first keyword.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4269: Footnote in <title>, footnote text appears in <xref>
content:
<!-- If you're describing a bug, tell us what should happen. -->
An xref to a title element should show the content of <title> without the <fn> text. When published, the <fn> text should only appear in a footnote.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4269: Footnote in <title>, footnote text appears in <xref>
content:
<!-- Optional suggestions on how to fix the issue, or implement the changes. -->
<!-- If you know how to fix the issue, please create a pull request instead. -->
I fixed this in version 2.5.4, so I will refrain from doing a PR. But I tested it with DITA OT 4.0.2 and the bug is still there. Here is my fix in OT 2.5.4 in links.xsl (see "markg" changes):

 <xsl:template match="*[contains(@class,' topic/xref ')]" name="topic.xref">
 <xsl:variable name="destination" select="opentopic-func:getDestinationId(@href)"/>
 <xsl:variable name="element" select="key('key_anchor',$destination, $root)[1]"/>
 
 <!-- markg: change $element variable to remove <fn> elements -->
 <xsl:variable name="element2">
 <xsl:apply-templates select="$element" mode="removefn"/>
 </xsl:variable>

 <xsl:variable name="referenceTitle" as="node()*">
 <xsl:apply-templates select="." mode="insertReferenceTitle">
 <xsl:with-param name="href" select="@href"/>
 <xsl:with-param name="titlePrefix" select="''"/>
 <xsl:with-param name="destination" select="$destination"/>

 <!-- markg: change from $element to $element2 -->
 <xsl:with-param name="element" select="$element2"/>
 </xsl:apply-templates>
 </xsl:variable>
 [...]
 </xsl:template

 <!-- markg: get rid of fn elements -->
 <xsl:template match="fn" mode="removefn" />
 <xsl:template match='@* | node()' mode="removefn">
 <xsl:copy>
 <xsl:apply-templates select='@* | node()' mode="removefn"/>
 </xsl:copy>
 </xsl:template>

title: DITA-OT Issue #4281: Add DITA-OT version to generated metadata
content:
When DITA-OT generates output, it adds metadata to output indicating that content was generated by DITA-OT:

- HTML: `<meta name="generator" content="DITA-OT">`
- PDF2: `Content creator: DITA Open Toolkit`

— but this info does not include the **version** of DITA-OT, which could be useful for future reference, or when debugging differences in output from different toolkit versions.
Let's add the DITA-OT version to both of these metadata instances.

While we're at it, perhaps we should align them to either spell out the name _(or abbreviate it)_ in both places:

- HTML: `<meta name="generator" content="DITA Open Toolkit 4.1.1">`
- PDF2: `Content creator: DITA Open Toolkit 4.1.1`

_or_ 

- HTML: `<meta name="generator" content="DITA-OT 4.1.1">`
- PDF2: `Content creator: DITA-OT 4.1.1`

content: Issue #4293 is open with labels bug. Retrieval signals: error, exception, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4293: XSL Messages with termination are presented as unhandled internal errors
content:
I publish with the DITA OT and the console output contains an error like this:

 [pipeline] net.sf.saxon.s9api.SaxonApiUncheckedException: THIS IS IT...
 [pipeline] at org.dita.dost.util.XMLUtils.lambda$toMessageListener$0(XMLUtils.java:209)
 [pipeline] at net.sf.saxon.s9api.AbstractXsltTransformer.lambda$setMessageListener$0(AbstractXsltTransformer.java:302)
 [pipeline] at net.sf.saxon.expr.instruct.MessageInstr$MessageInstrElaborator.lambda$elaborateForPush$0(MessageInstr.java:351)
 [pipeline] at net.sf.saxon.expr.instruct.Block$BlockElaborator.lambda$elaborateForPush$1(Block.java:851)
 [pipeline] at net.sf.saxon.expr.instruct.TemplateRule.applyLeavingTail(TemplateRule.java:393)
 [pipeline] at net.sf.saxon.trans.Mode.handleRuleNotNull(Mode.java:587)
 [pipeline] at net.sf.saxon.trans.Mode.applyTemplates(Mode.java:521)
 [pipeline] at net.sf.saxon.trans.XsltController.applyTemplates(XsltController.java:684)
 [pipeline] at net.sf.saxon.s9api.AbstractXsltTransformer.applyTemplatesToSource(AbstractXsltTransformer.java:427)
 [pipeline] at net.sf.saxon.s9api.XsltTransformer.transform(XsltTransformer.java:356)
 [pipeline] at org.dita.dost.store.StreamStore.transformUri(StreamStore.java:235)
 [pipeline] at org.dita.dost.store.StreamStore.transform(StreamStore.java:212)
 [pipeline] at org.dita.dost.module.XsltModule.transform(XsltModule.java:307)
 [pipeline] at org.dita.dost.module.XsltModule.transform(XsltModule.java:280)
 [pipeline] at org.dita.dost.module.XsltModule.execute(XsltModule.java:170)
 [pipeline] at org.dita.dost.ant.ExtensibleAntInvoker.execute(ExtensibleAntInvoker.java:210)
 ...
 [pipeline] at org.apache.tools.ant.launch.Launcher.main(Launcher.java:101)
 [pipeline] Caused by: net.sf.saxon.expr.instruct.TerminationException: THIS IS IT...
 [pipeline] at org.dita.dost.util.XMLUtils.lambda$toMessageListener$0(XMLUtils.java:207)
 [pipeline] ... 57 more
 [31mError: java.lang.RuntimeException: Internal error evaluating template rule at line 125 in module file:/.../com.oxygenxml.webhelp.responsive/xsl/dita2webhelp/dita2webhelpImpl.xsl[0m

Looking at this console log as a developer it looks more ike a bug in the Saxon processor, not like an `xsl:message` which terminated the processing.
Maybe in the `XMLUtils MessageListener2.message(XdmNode, QName, boolean, SourceLocator)` when the terminate flag comes enabled we could just issue a message and let Saxon terminate the process in the class `net.sf.saxon.expr.instruct.MessageInstr.MessageInstrElaborator` instead of us throwing an unhandled error.

Maybe we could also create a custom exception class which extends `net.sf.saxon.s9api.SaxonApiUncheckedException`, named something like `org.dita.dost.TerminateMessage` and throw that when we want to forcefully terminate a "FATAL" error which does not have terminate = yes.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4298: HTML output uses removed HTML5 attribute: @compact
content:
HTML output should use standard HTML markup supported by major browsers. @compact is no longer supported by Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge, Opera.
HTML output for html5 and xhtml uses @compact attribute, which was removed from HTML5. It was deprecated in HTML 4 about 20 years ago.
HTML5 spec, section 16.2 Non-conforming features: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#non-conforming-features Paraphrase of the spec: >The following attributes are obsolete (though the elements are still part of the language), and must not be used by authors: >compact on dl elements >compact on menu elements >compact on ol elements >compact on ul elements
1. In DITA 1.3 XML topic, add @compact to the root element of a list like `<ul>`:
2. Run the html5 or xhtml transtype on it. 3. The HTML output uses @compact. html5:

title: DITA-OT Issue #4304: Dita-OT 4.1.2 fails with unresolved XREF if using PDF themes
content:
When using PDF output with --theme, xrefs with undefined keys are skipped.
When using PDF output with --theme, xrefs with undefined keys are reported as errors in the topic.fo,
leaving the user clueless where this comes from:

` [fop] [ERROR] Anttask - Error rendering fo file: /home/hcw/work/Deuta/generic-gateway/modules/dita-plugins/com.deuta.deuta-pdf/test/tmp/topic.fo <org.apache.fop.apps.FOPException: net.sf.saxon.trans.XPathException: org.apache.fop.fo.ValidationException: Missing attribute on fo:basic-link: Either external-destination or internal-destination must be specified. (Siehe Position 18:61)
`

It is caused by every `<xref keyref="undefined-key"/>` reference.
That leads to the error, but only if --theme is given.
Without --theme, that gives no warnings / errors, it just renders an empty xref.
<!-- Test case, Gist, set of files or steps required to reproduce the issue. -->

1. Use any topic which contains a `<xref keyref="undefined-key"/>`
2. Render with`dita -f pdf --theme docsrc/samples/themes/dita-ot-docs-theme.yaml ...`
3. You get an error as above.
4. Omit `--theme`
5. PDF renders ok
Copy of the error message, log file or stack trace

title: DITA-OT Issue #4319: Apache FOP cannot access the .fop/fop-fonts.cache anymore
content:
Since a few days, I cannot publish no PDFs anymore with Apache FOP. It started crashing and I don't know why. Not sure, if this is related to the DITA-OT, but I don't know where else to search for a solution.
The build crashes because the FOP fonts cache cannot be accessed anymore `.fop\fop-fonts.cache (Access is denied)`. I can delete the entire directory. It is re-created when I publish something, so this is quite strange. Also the cache is filled with data during the transformation, so I absolutely do not understand why FOP is failing a few seconds later. And I cannot disable font caching, because then the publishing fails with a stack-overflow.
Can only repruce this on my computer, unfortunately.

content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4321: Release new patch version to fix plugin org.dita.pdf2.fop security issues
content:
Plugin `org.dita.pdf2.fop` included in the latest 4.1.2 release includes `batik-all-1.16.jar` dependency, which has 2 security issues:
* [CVE-2022-44730](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-44730) (4.4 medium severity)
* [CVE-2022-44729](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-44729) (7.1 high severity)

Both of these can be solved by updating `batik` dependency to version 1.17, which is already fixed in `develop` branch.

Could a patch version be released with this change included to fix the security issues?

title: DITA-OT Issue #4323: Add a warning in console when chunking is present on multiple levels
content:
When the chunking attribute is present on nested topicrefs only the last topic will have the chunking. This is not a problem but we could alert the user with a warning in the console.
Only the last topic has the chunking but nothing appear in the console. The DITA structure is valid, but as the result will only have the chunking on topic2.dita, a warning could be nice.
1. Create a ditamap with the following content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE map
 PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Map//EN" "map.dtd">
<map>
 <title>Map</title>
 <topicref href="topic1.dita" chunk="to-content">
 <topicref href="topic2.dita" chunk="to-content">
 <topicref href="topic3.dita"/>
 <topicref href="topic4.dita"/>
 <topicref href="topic5.dita"/>
 </topicref>
 </topicref>
</map>
2. Generate the HTML5 output and check the console, nothing is present.

content: Issue #4325 is open with labels CLI, feature, priority/medium. Retrieval signals: pdf, dita-ot, plugin.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4325: Add 'update' functionality to the dita install subcommand
content:
It could be useful to have an `update` option use with the plugin registry. This would simply function similar to PIP or NPM, in which an additional optional (or different subcommand; update instead of install) is used to quickly update.
This might just be a synonym command for the `--force` option, but perhaps with some notes regarding the current and latest versions and a confirmation. E.g., Are you sure you want to update the com.elovirta.pdf plugin from 0.7.0 to the latest available version (0.7.1)? [y/N]
- a `--info` option here could be used to show the current installed version of all registry plugins along with the latest available (com.elovirta.pdf@0.7.0 -> 0.7.1) - a `--all` option could be used to update all registry plugins to the latest available version. - a `--version` option could take a specific version to download and install, rather than just the latest available (would not work with an `--all` option, I would think)
The benefit of having a specific update command would bring the dita CLI in-line with many modern package managers. While I realize the plugin registry isn't really trying to be a package manager, it seems like a minor yet useful improvement for those used to this style of CLI.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4339: dita2markdown Tables are malformatted when cells contain multiple paragraphs or lists
content:
Tables rendered in a dita2markdown conversion should be well formatted regardless of whether cells contain paragraphs or lists.
Tables with even relatively simple content are rendered in markdown output poorly and often don't conform to general markdown requirements.

For example, the generated markdown output for a table that contains a list, might appear as follows:
Perhaps the easiest solution to this problem is to provide an option to render tables in HTML format, which most markdown renderers and parsers respect.

Table formats are notoriously problematic in Markdown, particularly for more complex tables, so providing an option to output tables in HTML format could help work around these problems.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4351: Generate HTML5 metadata attributes in the `index.html` TOC file
content: Issue #4351 is closed with labels bug, plugin/html5. Retrieval signals: map, html, dita-ot, validation, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4351: Generate HTML5 metadata attributes in the `index.html` TOC file
content:
This is an enhancement request for the `index.html` TOC file produced by the HTML5 transformation to include map metadata.
Given a root map file with lots of metadata:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<?xml-model href="urn:oasis:names:tc:dita:rng:map.rng" schematypens="http://relaxng.org/ns/structure/1.0"?>
<map>
 <title>My Root Map</title>
 <topicmeta>
 ...lots and lots of metadata elements...
 </topicmeta>
 ...
</map>
the `<head>` element of the resulting `index.html` file does not contain any of the metadata in the root-map `<topicmeta>` element:
<html lang="en">
 <head>
 <meta charset="UTF-8">
 <meta name="generator" content="DITA-OT">
 <title>My Root Map</title>
 <link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="commonltr.css">
 </head>
It would be useful for the TOC file to include root-map metadata because the TOC file is a reliable, filename-invariant file that can be referenced in automated content processing flows. For example, the tool version of a documentation collection could be stored in the root-map metadata:
<map>
 <title>Online Help for My Product</title>
 <topicmeta>
 <prodinfo>
 <prodname>My Product</prodname>
 <vrmlist>
 <vrm version="2023.12"/>
 </vrmlist>
 </prodinfo>
 </topicmeta>
 ...
</map>
then reliably extracted from metadata fields in the `index.html` file:

title: DITA-OT Issue #4351: Generate HTML5 metadata attributes in the `index.html` TOC file
content:
<html lang="en">
 <head>
 <meta charset="UTF-8">
 <meta name="generator" content="DITA-OT">
 <meta name="prodname" content="My Product"> <!-- HERE -->
 <meta name="version" content="2023.12"> <!-- HERE -->
 <title>Online Help for My Product</title>
 <link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="commonltr.css">
 </head>
Update the metadata templates in `get-meta.xsl` to also consider map metadata elements.

Currently, most of the templates are hardcoded to look inside the `<prolog>` element of topic files, even though the `<topicmeta>` element of map files can contain most of the same fields:
<xsl:apply-templates select="*[contains(@class,' topic/prolog ')]/*[contains(@class,' topic/metadata ')]/*[contains(@class,' topic/prodinfo ')]/*[contains(@class,' topic/vrmlist ')]/*[contains(@class,' topic/vrm ')]/@version |
 self::dita/*[1]/*[contains(@class,' topic/prolog ')]/*[contains(@class,' topic/metadata ')]/*[contains(@class,' topic/prodinfo ')]/*[contains(@class,' topic/vrmlist ')]/*[contains(@class,' topic/vrm ')]/@version" mode="gen-metadata"/>
The following testcase contains both a map file and a topic file that have lots of metadata information:

[4351.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/13760055/4351.zip)

To run:
dita -i map.ditamap -f html5 --verbose -Dvalidate=no

title: DITA-OT Issue #4351: Generate HTML5 metadata attributes in the `index.html` TOC file
content: Validation must be disabled to relax the schema rules for some test structures, such as disabling one-of-list attribute value checks and allowing both `<abstract>` and `<shortdesc>` in the topic file.

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4374: Allow defining artifacts and have DITA projects which depend on other projects
content:
Based on an older idea @georgebina, but today I also had a client with such needs. 
In computer programming we split a larger project in subprojects. Those subprojects may have code which refers to other subprojects. We use for example Maven to pack each subproject as an artifact which can be used in a larger project.

Assume we have a team working on documenting a specific part of a product. They could have their own DITA XML project hosted on Git/SVN. So maybe you have multiple teams, each working on a specific DITA XML project which documents a part of the product. And each team has their own GitHub repo.
Then you have another DITA XML project which incorporates in its DITA Map references to the submaps developed in those smaller projects. 
How does that work today? I need to check out all those subprojects locally and the "main.ditamap" needs to have references like "mapref href="../../chapter.ditamap"".
Maybe I do not want to checkout all those subprojects locally as I am not making changes to them, I'm just using their content to build a larger publication

title: DITA-OT Issue #4374: Allow defining artifacts and have DITA projects which depend on other projects
content:
Maybe the DITA OT project file for a certain project could specify on what other project artifacts it depends. Those artifacts would already be published somewhere. So when the DITA OT project file is run, those artifacts it depends on would be unpacked and used. Probably this would mean the entire sources would need to be moved to a temporary files folder and the published output built from that.
This particular client uses as a workaround in the DITA Map of the main project a mapref to the HTTP location of the submap in the Subversion repository. So they have a mapref like this:

 <topicref
 href="https://.../samples/dita/garage/garage.ditamap"
 format="ditamap" scope="external"/> 

and they rely on the HTTP connection to retrieve the content of the submap.

content: Issue #4397 is closed with labels feature. Retrieval signals: error, map, plugin, validation.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4397: Add validate subcommand
content:
Add dedicated subcommand for validation. The process will run pre-processing to discover error or warnings. Instead of producing output, it would only log issues and return with non-zero exit code.

There will be a new extension point that plug-ins can use to run custom Ant targets for additional validation. If there are multiple plugins that use the extension point, then multiple validation steps are run in _some_ order. Each should just log warnings and errors, not product any output.

The validation subcommand could also produce a list of all error and warnings in some format. However, you can output the normal log into an XML file or using a custom build listener you can generate any output you want.
$ dita validate -i userguide.ditamap
$ dita validate -i userguide.ditamap --processing-mode=strict
Open items
- [ ] Should the default processing mode be strict or lax? For conversion the default is lax.

content: Issue #4405 is closed with labels bug, plugin/html5. Retrieval signals: map, html, dita-ot, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4405: Variable definition values should not be included in `index.html` file
content:
If I publish the following:

![4405-1](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/assets/50950969/582c6d08-aa71-4e39-abf2-85f867b30cc1)

the `<meta name="keywords">` element in `index.html` file should contain only keywords intended to be metadata.
In #4352, the HTML5 transformation was updated to include map-level metadata in the `index.html` file. In `get-meta.xsl`, `<keyword>` values in map metadata blocks were added for consideration ([link to code here](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/pull/4352/files#diff-44db18c4206d6b9300448634510cdbe6599828f7db24ce6f7ca2a330ee55d3e1R250-R252)):
topic/prolog/metadata/keywords/descendant-or-self::*
map//topicmeta/keywords/descendant-or-self::*
map//topicmeta/metadata/keywords/descendant-or-self::*
However, this inadvertently matched `<keyword>` elements used in variable definitions:

![4405-2](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/assets/50950969/1ba71da2-f746-4dd0-a8ba-f9870c1b0981)

which unintentionally and undesirably includes all variable definitions in the metadata:
<html lang="en">
 <head>
 ...
 <meta name="keywords" content="keyword1, variable1, variable2">
 ^^^^^^^^^ ^^^^^^^^^
 <title>My Map</title>
(Side note: the non-variable submap metadata is saved in a temporary submap metadata container, but that is deleted before the HTML5 output is generated.)

title: DITA-OT Issue #4405: Variable definition values should not be included in `index.html` file
content:
The `<keywords>` paths should be updated to exclude variable definitions in a robust and reliable way.
1. Download and extract this testcase: [4405.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/14268116/4405.zip) 2. Run the following command: `dita -i map.ditamap -f html5`

title: DITA-OT Issue #4448: Error in nested DITA-OT project file is not properly reported.
content:
The DITA-OT build should fail, when there is a problem with the DITA-OT project file. The error message should help me to determine the position of the error.
I get an error like this:
Error: Failed to read project file file:/home/runner/work/foo/foo/bar.xml:3:122: 
text not allowed here; expected the element end-tag or element 
"context", "deliverable", "include" or "publication"
First problem is, that the build does not fail at all on GitHub Actions. This should be fixed.
The reported line (3) and character (122) position is misleading, because the `bar.xml` file contains only **`<include>`** elements. Probably the message is triggered, when the includes were resolved. This makes it hard to determine the position of the error.
It would be nice, if the DITA-OT build would fail immediately, if the project file is invalid. It would be nice, if the error message would echo the ID/name of the deliverable. This would help a lot to nail down the error.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4454: preprocess2 fails when topicref is missing regardless of processing-mode
content:
For a missing DITA topic file referenced by a `<topicref>` element in a map, the DITA OT should not fail when processing-mode="lax" (defualt) or "skip"; only when set to "strict". This was the behavior in the original preprocess.

A warning should (and is) generated, but the processing should be able to proceed and simply skip over any missing files.

It is not uncommon for a file reference to be removed in one place but missed in others (e.g., a `<xref>` in a topic or `<topicref>` in a relationship table). Providing output for the "lax" or "skip" values allows users to still review the output.
In preprocess2, _regardless_ of the value for processing-mode, the DITA OT fails with a Java NullPointerException.
When the processing-mode is set to "lax" (default) or to "skip", then any files flagged as missing should just be ignored. The warning is already generated in the preprocess2 step of reading the files and generating a temporary copy.
1. Include `<topicref href="dummy.dita"/>` within a map of any project; where dummy.dita does not exist.
2. Publish this output to a HTML5 output format with the parameter processing-mode="skip"

title: DITA-OT Issue #4468: Should be able to change severity for Java based messages
content:
DITA-OT Issue #4468: Should be able to change severity for Java based messages
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4468: Should be able to change severity for Java based messages
content: Issue #4468 is open with labels feature. Retrieval signals: error, dita-ot, validation.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4468: Should be able to change severity for Java based messages
content:
With DITA-OT 4.2, I'm able to override message severities. My use case for that is to set up a build gate as part of validation for documentation commits; issues that are allowed as warnings or errors for local / in-progress builds should be treated as fatal for pull request purposes. (We already use processing-mode strict, but this doesn't catch everything.)

When I change the severity of an XSLT message to Fatal, the message templates pick it up, and the build will fail if I throw the message. However the Java code will not do the same; because Java messages are thrown using `logger.warn` or `logger.error`, the message severity is part of the code itself, and modifying the severity in the message definition will have no effect.

For example, the Java code throws DOTX008E for missing images; I would like to set the severity of that to FATAL and use that to prevent merging any content with missing image references.
It would be nice if the Java code was able to read the severity as well as the message text, so that when throwing an error, it could use that to determine error level.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4474: PDF Theme not Obeying Heading title-numbering
content: Issue #4474 is open with labels bug. Retrieval signals: conref, map, pdf, dita-ot, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4474: PDF Theme not Obeying Heading title-numbering
content:
When applying a pdf theme with the title-numbering style key I expect the headings to be numbered regardless of the fact of how the topic hierarchy is defined in the dita/ditamap source.
Headings are only numbered when I use the ditamap to define the topic hierarchy (shown in test-case-a). Headings are not numbered when the hierarchy is the result of nested topics, whether they be native (shown in test-case-b) or via conref (shown in test-case-c).
1. Extract the [attached compressed tarball](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/15382680/test-cases.tar.gz).
2. Execute the run.sh script.
3. Observe the fact that in the pdf output test-case-a/out/test-case-a.pdf correctly adds all heading numbering but 
 test-case-b/out/test-case-b.pdf and test-case-c/out/test-case-c.pdf do not (they are missing numbering for 
 the "World" heading).

title: DITA-OT Issue #4475: Dita 2.0 chunk="combine" on root element produces incorrect output
content:
With chunk="combine" at the root of the map, all content is ouput in a single file and only topics content is present.
There is a single output file but maps content and resource topics are present in this file.
Comparison of html5 output between dita 1.3 chunk="to-content" and dita 2.0 chunk="combine":
1. With given test case : 
[test_chunk.zip](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/files/15416911/test_chunk.zip)

2. run `dita -i content/guide.bookmap -o out -f dita --root-chunk-override=combine`
3. you can see in the output that the map content and the keydef topic content are present in the output

With the same test case with dita 1.3 sources and --root-chunk-override=to-content, the output is correct

title: DITA-OT Issue #4480: foreign xlink:href attributes are processed, resulting into NullPointer exception
content:
Hey! I am setting up a Dita OT plugin that (among other things) includes some elements in a foreign element that I specialized and I place in a `map`.
This `<foreign />` contains some element that has an xlink:href attribute on it.
I would expect Dita OT to not process the contents of `<foreign />` elements. Just copy over the contents.
1. Take the map at https://gist.github.com/DrRataplan/ded9a31559cceb5188f74c53e980c59a

title: DITA-OT Issue #4489: Fatal XSLT error does not show location of problem in XSLT and does not immediately stop processing
content:
Based on this report:
https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox/FMfcgzQVxRGDprPblXHkwdbSjfdVHQbg

I added in the XSLT stylesheet something which breaks it like:

 <xsl:if test="xs:int('hello')"/>

I would expect that when the DITA OT breaks I get for the "Cannot convert string "hello" to an integer" error message the line/column and XSLT system ID where the problem occurs.
The "Cannot convert string "hello" to an integer" is reported in the console but not as a [DOT] error. The transformation continues on to the next task where it breaks because the "stage2.fo" was not produced, in my case the console looks like this:
[pipeline] Processing file:/Users/../samples/dita/flowers/temp/pdf/oxygen_dita_temp/stage1.xml to file:/.../samples/dita/flowers/temp/pdf/oxygen_dita_temp/stage2.fo [pipeline] Cannot convert string "hello" to an integer [pipeline] Failed to transform document: Failed to transform document: Cannot convert string "hello" to an integer
transform.topic2fo.i18n.filter: [i18n-preprocess] Processing file:/../dita/flowers/temp/pdf/oxygen_dita_temp/stage2.fo to file:/../samples/dita/flowers/temp/pdf/oxygen_dita_temp/topic.fo [i18n-preprocess] [Fatal Error] :-1:-1: Premature end of file.
Somehow attempt to see where that exception is caught, try to obtain more details from it and see if we can stop the DITA OT processing instead of proceeding to the next stage.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4489: Fatal XSLT error does not show location of problem in XSLT and does not immediately stop processing
content:
Open the "DITA-OT/plugins/org.dita.pdf2/xsl/fo/root-processing.xsl" and add in one of the templates like this one:

 <xsl:template match="*[contains(@class, ' map/topicref ')]" mode="topicref-validation">

this line to break the processing:

 <xsl:if test="xs:int('hello')"/>

title: DITA-OT Issue #4518: Conditions not respected in content conref'd into bookmap
content:
In several previous releases of DITA-OT (I've been doing this for at least 5 years across various companies), I have configured my bookmaps to reference a quantity of <bookmeta> data via conrefs. This way I can maintain version numbers, release dates, for however many documents in one centralized location.
I have used <vrmlist conref="anotherbookmap.ditamap#vrmlistid"/> and <bookchangehistory conref="anotherbookmap.ditamap#bookchangehistoryid"/>. "anotherbookmap.ditamap" contains a <vrmlist> and a <bookchangehistory> with however many <vrm> and <bookevent> elements I need, all conditioned using @otherprops for each release. This way I can maintain version numbers, release dates, for however many documents in one centralized location. 

I'm currently trying to upgrade from DITA-OT 3.6.1 to DITA-OT 4.2.3 and that behavior is no longer working.

When I generate using DITA-OT 4.2.3, I get all the version numbers or all the dates on my cover page. 

Now, if I take a bookmap, and have the conditions in the bookmap, the ditaval filtering works. When it's pulled in via a conref, it doesn't.

My guess is something regarding order of operations of when ditavals are evaluated has changed. That's deep in the guts of the DITA-OT that I don't understand.

I've created bookmapConrefDitaval.zip to show what used to work.

- com.bookmapconref.pdf - an extension of the pdf2 plugin that puts the version and date on the cover page. You can put this in your plugins directory
- out - contains the PDFs I generated locally as an example.
 - bookmapConrefDitaval_bookmap.pdf shows how it's not working
 - bookmapDitaval_bookmap.pdf shows the output I expect, but it's using a bookmap without conrefs.
- bookmapConrefDitaval_bookmap.ditamap - This is the type of bookmap I want to use, with the <vrmlist> and <bookchangehistory> using @conref.
- bookmapDitaval_bookmap.ditamap - A bookmap with the <vrmlist> and <bookchangehistory> set up without the conrefs to confirm that bookmaps could still handle conditions. This gives me the output I'd like, but I don't want to have to update versions across dozens of books.
- BuildPDF.bat - dinky batch script to build both pdfs. you'll have to edit the path to the DITA-OT for your environment.
- sharedversions_bookmap.ditamap - the "shared" bookmap that contains all the version info in one place that is referenced by the conref.
- topic.dita - bookmaps need some content, and it has some details in it.
- version100.ditaval - Includes @otherprops=version100
- version211.ditaval - Includes @otherprops=version211

title: DITA-OT Issue #4524: InputStream cannot be null when running Main class with no config/plugins.xml file
content:
The Main class should execute without any issue.
The process fails with "InputStream cannot be null".
The problem is located in `PluginInstall.init()` when calling `Plugins.getInstalledPlugins()`. This calls `Plugins.getPluginConfiguration()` which creates a null InputStream when getting the resource `Plugins.class.getClassLoader().getResourceAsStream(PLUGIN_CONF)`.
As `PluginInstall.execute()` calls `integrator.execute()` (which will generate the file) after calling `init()`, it should be possible to continue the init without getting installed plugins.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4528: HTML meta don't contain indexterms
content:
The HTML output should contain `<meta name="keywords" content="myKeyword, myIndexterm">`.
If we change `*[contains(@class,' topic/keyword ')]` by `descendant::*` in get-meta.xsl the output will contain all <keywords> children.
1. Create a ditamap with a topic having the folowing metadata:
<metadata> 
 <keywords>

title: DITA-OT Issue #4532: Add missing HTML5 metadata placeholder templates for `<data>`, `<data-about>`, and `<resource-id>` elements

</topic>
This means that third-party plugins have no template to override to process these elements.

According to the specification: http://docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3/errata02/os/complete/part3-all-inclusive/archSpec/base/processing-keyref-for-text.html#processing_key_references

Empty elements that include a key reference with a defined key might get their effective content from the key definition. Empty elements are defined as elements that meet the following criteria:

So I would expect XML such as `<ph keyref='key'> </ph>` to display empty text.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4557: Allow specifying custom path for plugin directory
content:
Currently, plugins are always installed to `$(pwd)/plugins`, where `$(pwd)` points to the installation directory. I want to be able to specify a custom path for the folder of the plugins (e.g., `~/.config/dita-ot/plugins.`).
Add the possibility to have a file `$(pwd)/plugins/location.txt` that points to a location, e.g., `~/.config/dita-ot/plugins/`. Everytime a plugin should be installed, first the existence of the special file is checked and used if existing. Otherwise keep previous behavior.
I'm requesting this, as I want to allow installing plugins to an immutable file system (NixOS). Currently, the package for [dita-ot on the Nix package manager](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/pkgs/by-name/di/dita-ot/package.nix) does not allow using `dita install <plugin>` as this tries to write to the immutable folder in the Nix file system. If there was a prepopulated file, it could be used to redirect installs to the mutable file system.

<!-- If you're describing a bug, tell us what should happen. -->

1. A DITA 1.3 map that contains valid MDITA topics (`format="mdita"`)

3. One or more MDITA topics contain a keyref: `[key]`
4. Apache FOP is used for the PDF transform
5. A PDF theme file (even the base sample one bundled with DITA-OT) is specified for the PDF transform

content: Issue #4566 is open with labels feature. Retrieval signals: general issue behavior.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4566: Add setting to control limits in security manager set to protect against billion laughs attack
content:
As a side effect of #4542, we received a few days ago a valid DITA DTD specialization. If an XML document uses this specialization and is parsed by an XML parser with the default SecurityManager set on it, the parsing fails because of the entity expansion limit. It seems Xerces in the method "XMLEntityManager.getParamEntityRefCount(String)" also adds parameter references count and in this case the "%univ-atts" parameter is used a lot in the DTD specialization and overflows the org.apache.xerces.util.SecurityManager.DEFAULT_ENTITY_EXPANSION_LIMIT which is 100k.
I'm not sure if I can get permission from the client to share their DTD specialization, the specialization does not seem particular in any way. The "%univ-atts" parameter is used in about 150 entity params and those entity params are used in other places as well so the limit is reached.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4567: File extension for DITA-OT project files
content:
In my test I would like to verify, if - for instance - **B.xml** includes **BA.xml**, **BB.xml**, and **BC.xml**. Only if this is the case, I can build the **root.xml** file and can be sure that all deliverables are properly build, because the dependency tree is intact.

My problem is, that technical writers forget to add their DITA-OT project file to the dependency tree. The consequence is, that the CI worker does not build those deliverables and the errors are not found. Further on, when the dependencies are missing, Oxygen XML refactoring operations do not work properly.

I think I can write a Schematron validation which tests a file collection. This would be quite simple. But there might be other XML files. So, it would help me to identify DITA-OT project files, when then would have their own file extension, something like `.dotp`.

content:
DITA-OT should pass HTML `<video>` elements in Markdown source files straight to HTML output, with no modification.
When a Markdown topic contains a `<video>` element, the `dita` command runs successfully and reports no errors - there's nothing in the log. However, the `<video>` element in the output contains no information.

DITA-OT Issue #4582: Branch filtering and key definition issues
GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

content: Issue #4582 is open with labels bug. Retrieval signals: error, pdf, dita-ot, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4582: Branch filtering and key definition issues
content:
> **INFO** This is similar to https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2096.

We get **DOTJ045I** messages, when keys are defined and branch filtering is used. Probably the reason is that keys are resolved before branches are filtered. @jelovirt explained it in [this comment (2015-10-10)](https://github.com/dita-ot/dita-ot/issues/2096#issuecomment-147039056) almost ten years ago. We handle **DOTJ045I** as an error and **fail the build** when it occurs, because we use extensive filtering and do not want to fall-back to defaults, because this leads to non-deterministic results.

> We still read keys without scope information in the beginning of processing, because subject schemes use that. To implement both subject scheme filtering and key scopes, we'd need to move subject scheme filtering to take place after key resolution. But, this means normal filtering will take place after that too. 

> **INFO** Setting the parameter `filter-stage` to either `early` or `late` does not make a difference.

content: Issue #4633 is open with labels bug. Retrieval signals: error, xref, map, pdf, html, dita-ot, transform.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4633: Scoped indirect xrefs to nested keyscopes fail
content:
My test case contains four **nested** keyscopes _**English.Diana**_, _**English.Thierry**_, _**French.Diana**_, and _**French.Thierry**_. Each references the same CV-skeleton.dita topic, rendered differently in each keyscope, as an effect of transcluding variables from distinct collections. Even the titles are rendered differently as they contain variables. An introduction topic in the frontmatter, outside of the four keyscopes, contains four **indirect scoped** cross-references, one to each instance of the CV-skeleton.dita topic. In the output, these cross-references are expected to render different titles and navigate, upon clicking, to the four different instances of the CV-skeleton.dita topic.
The enclosed ZIP also contains a bookmap with flat keyscopes that does not exhibit this issue.
The two enclosed PDFs show the output for flat and for nested keyscopes, respectively. Refer to the comments inside. The same PDFs are also inside the ZIP, without comments.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4633: Scoped indirect xrefs to nested keyscopes fail
content:
In oXygen Author, each of the four cross-references directs to its corresponding topic instance and displays correctly its title. This holds for both flat and nested keyscopes. However, while the PDF resulting from the bookmap with flat keyscopes is as expected, the one resulting from the bookmap with nested keyscopes is not correct. All four cross-references default to the first instance of the topic, that is, the one corresponding to the first of the four nested keyscopes. As a result, they all render the same title and direct to the same place upon clicking.
This looks like a DITA-OT bug that needs correction. When using flat keyscopes instead of nested, the scoped indirect cross-references direct to the respective topic instances as expected and they display the expected topic instance titles. In the package, I also provide the bookmap "CV_FlatKeyscopes.ditamap" with flat keyscopes, for reference and comparison, as well as the resulting PDF.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4692: dita.conductor.lib.import resolves library class paths incorrectly
content:
When extending via dita.conductor.lib.import in my plugin, I expect the path given in the "file" attribute to be resolved relative to $dita.dir and placed in the base plugin's build.xml.
instead, the path in build.xml has a dita.dir variable prepended to it, but the rest of the path is not resolved relative to dita.dir. Using the example above, you would get:

`${dita.dir}${file.separator}../foo-plugin/lib/blah.jar`
Should probably resolve the path relative to dita.dir, rather than resolving it relative to the template file and then trying to insert an Ant property in front of it.
1. Install dita-ot from zip
2. Run `dita install`
3. Look in plugins/org.dita.base/build.xml

You don't need to create your own plugin, you can demonstrate the issue with some of the plugins that come with the distribution:

title: DITA-OT Issue #4713: Using ditavalref in a map results in no content
content:
The map has structure:
<map>
 <topicref>
 ...
 <ditavalref>
</map>
The result should be a PDF document with some filtering applied. Using DITA-OT versions up to 4.3.2 the file is generated correctly. The <...>_MERGED.xml file contains the map plus all topics.
Starting with version 4.3.3 all content of the map is gone. The <...>_MERGED.xml only contains the map.
The problem is inside the "dost.jar" file. When copied this file from 4.3.3 to the 4.3.2 version the problem also appears in the 4.3.2 version. So this is explicitly introduced with the update of the DOST file.

No error message at all just a PDF with a front/back page and no content. It looks like all content is filtered out.
Create a map with topics and add a ditaval file using the <ditavalref> element to the map. And create a PDF.
Without the <ditavalref> element the complete PDF is created, with the ditavalref it is only a one or two pager.
The ditaval need not have much content. Added the "cascade" attribute on the map element, but did not change the behavior (used both "merge" and "nomerge" values).
Windows 11, OpenJDK version 19.0.1. DITA-OT version 4.3.2 and version 4.3.3 (also 4.3.4) with custom PDF plugins.
Started using ant with a dedicated build.xml file using a dedicated PDF transformation that uses the standard preprocessing steps.

Since I'm able to run it with the above workaround, I can run `uname -m` within the container, confirming that the `aarch64` image loads, not the `amd64` one:
<!-- Optional suggestions on how to fix the issue, or implement the changes. -->

I haven't discovered any possible solutions, other than than running the `aarch64` image on x86_64 hosts via the Qemu workaround linked above. It seems like the `amd64` image isn't actually there.

content:

title: DITA-OT Issue #4766: Hierarchical filtering: emit WARN diagnostic when child include/flag conflicts with excluded parent
content:

GitHub issue evidence from dita-ot/dita-ot for DITA-OT behavior, defects, regressions, and edge cases.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4766: Hierarchical filtering: emit WARN diagnostic when child include/flag conflicts with excluded parent
content: Issue #4766 is open with labels ai-generated, bug, needs reproduction. Retrieval signals: error, keyref, map, html, dita-ot.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4766: Hierarchical filtering: emit WARN diagnostic when child include/flag conflicts with excluded parent
content:
When a subject scheme map defines a parent→child hierarchy (e.g., `linux → redhat`) and a DITAVAL file both excludes the parent (`linux=exclude`) **and** explicitly includes or flags a child (`redhat=include` or `redhat=flag`), this is an **error condition** per the DITA 1.3 specification. Neither DITA-OT nor Oxygen WebAuthor currently emits any warning or error for this conflict.
This request asks for a **WARN-level diagnostic** (similar to `DOTJ049W`) when DITA-OT detects this hierarchy conflict, consistent with the spec's "applications **may** recover by generating an error message" language.
> "Excluded. This is an error condition, because if all 'linux' content is excluded, 'redhat' also is excluded. **Applications may recover by generating an error message.**"
The key detail: if `linux=exclude`, then `redhat` content is also excluded (it is a subtype of `linux`). An explicit `redhat=include` or `redhat=flag` rule in the same DITAVAL is therefore a contradiction — the parent's exclusion takes precedence, yet the child's rule misleadingly suggests content will appear.
The phrase "may recover" is a **SHOULD-level** requirement, not a SHALL. This means DITA-OT is not strictly required to emit the warning, but doing so would greatly aid authoring correctness.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4766: Hierarchical filtering: emit WARN diagnostic when child include/flag conflicts with excluded parent
content:
- DITA-OT processes without error or warning. - Content with `platform="redhat"` is **not excluded** in some DITA-OT versions, or behavior is inconsistent across `FilterModule` vs `BranchFilterModule` paths. - No diagnostic is generated, leaving authors unaware of the content modeling error.
DITA-OT should detect the conflict during DITAVAL + subject scheme resolution and emit a warning such as:
[WARN][DOTJXXX] DITAVAL conflict: attribute "platform" value "redhat" has action "include",
but its subject scheme ancestor "linux" has action "exclude".
The child value will be excluded. Review your DITAVAL and subject scheme hierarchy.
This warning would: 1. Alert authors to a likely content modeling mistake before publication. 2. Clarify which behavior wins (parent exclude takes precedence). 3. Be consistent with the existing `DOTJ049W` warning for attribute values not compliant with the subject scheme.
1. Create a subject scheme map with a `linux → redhat` hierarchy bound to `@platform`:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE subjectScheme PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Subject Scheme Map//EN" "subjectScheme.dtd">
<subjectScheme>
 <hasKind>
 <subjectdef keys="linux">
 <subjectdef keys="redhat"/>
 </subjectdef>
 </hasKind>
 <enumerationdef>
 <attributedef name="platform"/>
 <subjectdef keyref="linux"/>
 </enumerationdef>
</subjectScheme>
2. Create `case1.ditaval`:

title: DITA-OT Issue #4766: Hierarchical filtering: emit WARN diagnostic when child include/flag conflicts with excluded parent
content:
3. Create a topic `test.dita`: Hierarchical filtering test – Case 1

This is linux content (should be excluded).

This is redhat content (should be excluded — error condition).

This is generic content (should be included).

 4. Create `test.ditamap` referencing both files. dita --input=test.ditamap --format=html5 \ --filter=case1.ditaval \ --output=out/case1/ --verbose **Expected:** A `WARN`-level message in the console/log indicating the `redhat=include` rule conflicts with `linux=exclude` in the subject scheme hierarchy. **Actual:** No warning. Output is inconsistent (redhat content may or may not be excluded depending on filter path used). --- - `DOTJ049W` — already emitted when a `@platform` attribute value in content does not match the enumeration in the subject scheme. A similar check at DITAVAL-loading time (when resolving `` elements against the loaded subject scheme) would be the natural place to add this new diagnostic. - The subject scheme tree is available to the `FilterModule` at processing time — it can be walked to verify that no included/flagged child value has an excluded ancestor. ---

title: DITA-OT Issue #4766: Hierarchical filtering: emit WARN diagnostic when child include/flag conflicts with excluded parent
content:
Without this diagnostic, content modeling errors of this type are **silent**: authors may write DITAVAL files believing `redhat` content is being included for review, while actually the `linux=exclude` rule silently voids the child rule. This leads to unexpected omissions in publications.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4768: Hierarchical filtering: child explicit include drops inherited parent flag action
content:
Per DITA 1.3 spec (conditional processing with subject scheme, linux/redhat hierarchy):

> When `platform="linux"` is set to `flag` and `platform="redhat"` is set to `include`, content with `platform="redhat"` should be **included AND flagged with the linux flag** — because `redhat` is a type of `linux`, the parent's flag is inherited even when the child is explicitly included.

Elements with `platform="redhat"` should appear in the output **with the linux flag applied**.

---

 <hasKind>
 <subjectdef keys="linux">
 <subjectdef keys="redhat"/>
 </subjectdef>
 </hasKind>

 <subjectdef keyref="linux"/>
 </enumerationdef>
</subjectScheme>

3. Create a topic `test.dita`:

Open `out/case4/test.html` — the paragraph `This is redhat content` appears but has **no flag**, while the spec requires it to carry the `linux` flag. --- | Element | Expected | Actual (OT 4.4) | Actual (oXygen XML Editor 28.0) | |---|---|---|---| | `platform="linux"` | Flagged | ✅ Flagged | ✅ Flagged | | `platform="redhat"` | **Included + flagged (linux flag)** | ❌ Included, not flagged | ❌ Included, not flagged | > **Note:** Both DITA-OT 4.4 and Oxygen XML Editor 28.0 fail this case.

title: DITA-OT Issue #4768: Hierarchical filtering: child explicit include drops inherited parent flag action
content:
DITA-OT's filtering module resolves the child's action first and, on finding an explicit `include`, considers resolution complete without consulting the parent's flag. The spec requires that an inherited `flag` from an ancestor is **additive** to the child's action when the child is `include` or `unspecified`.

[WARN][DOTJXXX] DITAVAL conflict: attribute "platform" value "redhat" has action "include",
but its subject scheme ancestor "linux" has action "exclude".
The child value will be excluded. Review your DITAVAL and subject scheme hierarchy.
This warning would: 1. Alert authors to a likely content modeling mistake before publication. 2. Clarify which behavior wins (parent exclude takes precedence). 3. Be consistent with the existing `DOTJ049W` warning for attribute values not compliant with the subject scheme.
1. Create a subject scheme map with a `linux → redhat` hierarchy bound to `@platform`:

<subjectScheme>
 <hasKind>

 </subjectdef>
 </hasKind>
 <enumerationdef>
 <attributedef name="platform"/>
 <subjectdef keyref="linux"/>
 </enumerationdef>
</subjectScheme>

A similar check at DITAVAL-loading time (when resolving `` elements against the loaded subject scheme) would be the natural place to add this new diagnostic. - The subject scheme tree is available to the `FilterModule` at processing time — it can be walked to verify that no included/flagged child value has an excluded ancestor. ---

title: DITA-OT Issue #4769: Hierarchical filtering: child include/flag does not propagate upward to unspecified parent
content:
Without this diagnostic, content modeling errors of this type are **silent**: authors may write DITAVAL files believing `redhat` content is being included for review, while actually the `linux=exclude` rule silently voids the child rule. This leads to unexpected omissions in publications. repro-case1/ ├── subjectScheme.ditamap ← linux → redhat hierarchy with wrapper key (platformKey) ├── topic.dita ← 3 paragraphs: generic, linux, redhat ├── test.ditamap ← root map ├── case1.ditaval ← linux=exclude, redhat=include ← this issue └── README.md ← expected vs. actual with validated output dita --input=test.ditamap --format=html5 --filter=case1.ditaval --output=out **Validated output (DITA-OT 4.4.0):**

Generic content — always included (no @platform).

RedHat content — ...

title: DITA-OT Issue #4774: Hierarchical filtering: child include/flag does not propagate upward to unspecified parent
content:
Subject scheme: `redhat` IS-A `linux` bound to `@platform`. When the DITAVAL default is `exclude` and only the child value (`redhat`) has an explicit `include` or `flag` rule, DITA-OT does not include the unspecified parent (`linux`). Per DITA 1.3 §5.2.4, a child's explicit action should propagate upward to ancestors with no explicit rule. **Topic** (`topic.dita`):

Generic.

Linux content.

RedHat content.
